# Env Vault, Plan B (orgs): Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A person can join their company's organisations in Dots. An org's variables come from the org's own OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault, Infisical, or a SOPS file encrypted with age, under a policy the org's admin signs. A dot belongs to one org, chosen when it is made. Its variables resolve in that org under the policy's rules, and it keeps working offline from an encrypted copy of the last fetch until the copy runs out. The admin can cut a person off and rotate a leaked value. `dots-admin` makes the admin's key, policy and join codes, and `docs/vault-admin.md` tells the admin how to set it all up.

**Architecture:** A new core module `vault::org`:

- the org's signed policy: `policy`, `signed`
- the join code: `join`
- its database row: `row`, plus `store/orgs.rs` and migration `0013_orgs.sql`
- the offline copy, encrypted with DPAPI: `offline`
- the source trait and one adapter per service: `sources/{mod,openbao,infisical,sops}`
- the `Orgs` service (join, update, remove, refresh, status, expiry): `service`
- one refresh timer per org: `timers`

`Vault` gains the orgs. Resolution takes the dot's scope (`DotScope`), MCP catalogs are kept per scope, and an http server whose URL reads `${VAR}` sends a scope's values only to an origin confirmed in that scope. `vault::status` gives each grant's status for the dot editor. The app gains ten commands (`org_*`, `confirm_origin`, `dot_variables`), and `library_check`, `library_accept` and `create_dot` gain a scope or an org. The UI gains Settings → Organisations, the Library's org sections, per-scope tool lists and **Check as**, the dot editor's org picker and per-grant status, and the "org removed" refusals. A new crate, `crates/dots-admin`, is the admin's command line.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.95, sqlx 0.8 on SQLite, tokio, reqwest 0.12 (rustls); new: `minisign-verify` 0.3, `minisign` 0.10 (dev, and `dots-admin`), `age` 0.12.1, `aes-gcm` 0.10.3, `subtle` 2.6; `windows-sys` 0.61.2 (DPAPI); Tauri 2.12; Bun 1.3, React 19.3, TypeScript 6.0, TanStack Query 5.104, zod 4.6, Vitest 5.0.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-env-vault-design.md` at `eeda3ee`, the base of this plan (master, with plan A, PR #18, and dot memory, PR #20). This plan is **plan B** of three, as the spec's §14 records:

- **A** (merged): Personal, grants, resolution and the base environment, the Env tab and a dot's Variables, redaction, migration.
- **B** (this plan): orgs, sources, policy, the offline copy, per-scope catalogs, origin pinning, the org picker and `dots-admin`.
- **C:** audit (records, the outbox, `dots-admin audit verify`).

Task 16 adds the spec's §16, "Changes made while building (plan B)", which the table "Deviations" below lists.

**Previous plans:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-env-vault-a.md` built the vault this plan extends: `Vault`, `SecretStore`, grants, `Vault::resolve`, `child_env::start_clean` and the redactor.

**Where the tasks come from:** spec §6.3 and §6.1 (Tasks 1, 2), §5.2 and §6.4 (Tasks 3, 4), §6.1 and §6.2 (Tasks 5 to 7), §6.4 (Task 8), §8 (Tasks 9 to 11), §9 (Tasks 12 to 15), §12 (Tasks 2, 16), §13 (Task 17).

**How this plan's code was checked:** the code blocks of Tasks 1 to 16 were generated from a throwaway worktree of `eeda3ee`, one commit per task (branch `proto/env-vault-b`), where each compiled and passed on Windows 11. A script then replayed the plan onto `eeda3ee`, applying every block and comparing the tree with each task commit. All 16 tasks matched, and the tree after Task 16 equals the prototype's last commit. `Cargo.lock` and the contract fixture were taken from the task commits, since the plan's commands write them.

- Toolchain: Rust 1.95 stable; Bun 1.3 (`bun x`, not `bunx`, which is not on the PATH in Git Bash); WebView2 runtime. Windows 11, Git Bash.
- Branch `feat/env-vault-b`, in the worktree `C:\Users\aksha\dots\.claude\worktrees\env-vault-b`, based on `eeda3ee`. All commands run from the repository root unless a step says otherwise. Never commit to `master`. `git add` names its files: never `git add -A` or `git add .` (a `.memsearch/` folder in a worktree is not ours).
- Every cargo command runs with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/aksha/dots/target` (the shared build folder): `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/aksha/dots/target` once per shell. Add `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` when another session is building.
- Dependencies (each added by the step that needs it; the first build writes `Cargo.lock`; do not run `cargo add` as well):

- **One migration, `0013_orgs.sql`**, made in Task 3 and extended in Tasks 10 and 11. It follows master's `0012_memories.sql`. Appending to it changes its checksum, so a data folder migrated by an earlier task of this branch will not open ("previously applied but has been modified"). Run every build of this branch on a temp `DOTS_DATA_DIR`, never on the real data folder.
- The subscription rule: Dots only spawns the official `claude` CLI and never reads, copies or sends its credentials or calls an Anthropic API. No agent runs the real `claude` CLI; tests and smokes use `fake-claude`.
- **No secret in clear on disk or in a test's output.** Tests use made-up values, and every error, summary and listing test checks that no value is in its `Display`, `Debug` or JSON. A test that touches Credential Manager uses an install id `test-<ULID>` and deletes what it wrote; DPAPI tests use temp folders. The two age identities in `crates/dots-core/tests/fixtures/sops/` are test-only and say so in their first line; a secret scanner may flag them.
- The SOPS fixtures need no tool to run. One test, `vault_org_sops_test::the_age_cli_reads_a_new_identity`, runs `age-keygen` from `DOTS_TEST_AGE_KEYGEN` or the PATH, and prints "skipped" and passes when it finds neither. winget installs it to `/c/Users/aksha/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/FiloSottile.age_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/age`.
- Values the spec fixes, or the prototype settled (spec §16 after Task 16):
  - An org id is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, and `personal` is refused: "'personal' is reserved for your own keys; choose another org id".
  - The signed policy is `{"v":1,"policy":"<policy JSON text>","signature":"<minisign signature box>"}`; the policy key is `DOTS_POLICY`.
  - Sign-in details are stored at `org/<org_id>/source` (Credential Manager target `Dots/<install_id>/org/<org_id>/source`), at most 2,560 bytes. The offline copy is `<data>/vault/<org_id>.bin`.
  - Every source: one reqwest client, 20 s per request (`FETCH_TIMEOUT`), no redirects, answers at most 1 MiB; 401 and 403 are Denied, every 5xx and 429 Unreachable, anything else Invalid.
  - `RETRY_AFTER` is 5 minutes; `DEFAULT_REFRESH_MINUTES` is 15; a policy's defaults are `personal: "deny"`, `shell_secrets: false`, `refresh_minutes: 15`, `offline_hours: 24`.
  - `PERSONAL_SCOPE` is `"personal"`.
  - The run texts, status texts, notices and UI copy that the tests below quote.
- No agent installs or runs an installer, runs a release build, or touches the installed Dots (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Dots`), the real data folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dots`, or the person's own Credential Manager entries. Smokes use a debug build with a fresh `DOTS_DATA_DIR`.
- How the code blocks are written. A step changes files in two ways, and its blocks are applied in the order given:
  - **Create `path`:** the block is the whole new file.
  - **In `path`, replace:** … **with:** … The first block is a passage of the file as it stands at that moment, and it occurs there exactly once; the second block takes its place. Lines above and below the change are in both blocks, so that the place is unambiguous.
- A step that says "Replace" must find its passage once. If it does not (an earlier fix round changed the file), stop and compare with the prototype's intent before changing anything; do not paste over a fix.
- Files are LF with a final newline, and valid UTF-8. Check with `git diff --cached --check`, `git ls-files --eol <files>` and `iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 <file> > /dev/null` before each commit (the blocks hold `§`, `—`, `→`, `⚙` and `…`). The working copies may be CRLF (`core.autocrlf`); the index must hold LF. The SOPS fixtures are written exactly as given: their MACs cover the values, not the line ends, but a changed byte inside a value breaks them.
- Write Rust with the Write and Edit tools, not a Bash heredoc: heredocs in this shell turn `\\` into `\`, which breaks string continuations. Scan each staged `.rs` file with `grep -nE '[^ ] {8,}[^ ]'`; a hit inside a string literal is a lost line continuation.
- The UI reaches the backend only through `ui/src/api/commands.ts` and `ui/src/api/events.ts`. No `fetch`, no other plugin.
- Live data is parsed, not cast, with strict schemas: a type the UI parses changes only together with the contract fixture and `ui/src/api/types.ts`, in the same commit (Tasks 3, 12 to 15). The fixture `ui/src/api/__fixtures__/contract.json` is written by `UPDATE_CONTRACT=1 cargo test -p dots-app contract` and never by hand. `contract.rs`'s `samples()` is at the `json!` macro's recursion limit: a new sample is added after the macro (`samples["X"] = ...`).
- Before each commit:
  - the task's own tests
  - then, as the change requires: `cargo test` of the crates touched (`--no-fail-fast` for `dots-core`), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` with no warnings, `cargo fmt --check`, `DEBUG_PRINT_LIMIT=0 bun run --cwd ui test`, and `bun run --cwd ui typecheck`

  Test output must be free of warnings. `cargo test -p dots-app` and clippy need `ui/dist`: in a fresh checkout run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, then `bun x vite build` in `ui`, first. The UI files have no formatter; keep new lines within 100 columns where the file does. Compare the UI run's file count with `find ui/src -name '*.test.ts*' | wc -l`: a run that hit a worker timeout reports fewer files.
- Known on this machine: a `vitest` run started right after an install, a `tsc` run or a cargo build, or beside another session's build, can fail with `[vitest-pool-runner]: Timeout waiting for worker to respond` or "Failed to start forks worker", or report fewer files. Run it again on its own, with `-- --maxWorkers=2` while another build runs; do not change the pool settings. Run the UI tests before the typecheck.
- Known to be flaky under load (rerun the test binary alone before treating one as a failure):
  - `worktree_review_test::a_follow_up_fails_before_the_engine_starts_when_its_row_names_no_dots_worktree` and `discard_finds_the_repository_from_the_worktree_when_the_dot_moved`
  - `browser_call_test::a_live_approval_on_a_page_that_moved_is_not_performed`
  - `runtime_test::chat_follow_up_restores_a_removed_worktree_at_the_same_path`
  - `approvals_test::ask_approved_within_window_is_live`
  - `runtime_local_test::live_approval_lets_the_command_run`, `local_tools_test::shell_stops_at_its_timeout_and_on_cancel`
  - clippy's "error finalizing incremental compilation session directory … Access is denied" is a lock in the shared target folder, not a lint: run it again.
- Fact-Forcing Gate (a hook of this machine): the first Edit or Write of each file, the first Bash command after a task notification, and `rm`, `git commit --amend` or a rebase are blocked until the facts it asks for are stated (callers, affected API, data shapes, the instruction, or for a destructive command what changes and how to undo it); then retry the identical call. For a large new file, write a one-line stub first.

## Deviations from the spec

Task 16 records each of these in the spec's new §16, with the reason.

| Spec at `eeda3ee` | This plan | Why |
|---|---|---|
| §6.3: "the signed text" | A JSON envelope `{v, policy, signature}`, verified over the exact bytes of `policy`, prehashed signatures only | One string fits an OpenBao key, an Infisical secret and the SOPS `policy` field |
| §6.3: unknown fields at the top level are refused | Nested unknown fields, a field given twice and a `v` other than 1 are refused too; an empty `allow` allows nothing | Fail closed throughout |
| §6.1: the `org_id` is not specified | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, and `personal` is refused | The id is in file names and Credential Manager targets, and `personal` is the Personal scope's key |
| §6.2: `Unreachable` is offline | Every 5xx and 429 is Unreachable; TLS also trusts the Windows certificate store; no redirects | Server or rate-limit trouble keeps the copy; a company CA must connect; a redirect would carry the token elsewhere |
| §6.4: expiry once `offline_hours` pass since the last good fetch | A Connected org's values expire only after a failed fetch | A policy with `refresh_minutes` above `offline_hours` would expire an org that works |
| §6.4: fetch before a run if the copy is older than `refresh_minutes` | Not within 5 minutes of a failed attempt (`RETRY_AFTER`) | A source that hangs would make every run start wait 20 s |
| §6.4: a removed org's dots "are disabled and labelled 'org removed'" | They are not disabled: a run fails at start by every trigger, `update_dot` refuses, and the UI's card, menu, editor and Home composer refuse with the text | Switching them off or deleting them keeps working, and a re-join needs no step |
| §6.1: the SOPS join shows the key and the person waits | A join refused for lack of a recipient answers `pending` (an `OrgSummary`), kept in memory only; the key is stored at once | The person sends the key and presses **Try again**, with no error shown |
| §8: pinning when a variable sits in a URL's scheme, host or port | Pinned when the URL reads `${VAR}` anywhere; a header-only variable is not pinned; confirmations only grow | A fixed URL can't move, and today's dialog already names it with its header variables |
| §8: Check resolves every variable in the scope | It also refuses an origin not confirmed in that scope; the app then asks the native dialog naming the org | A Check must not send an org's values somewhere never confirmed |
| §11: upgrade steps run in `Store::open` | `finish_0013` runs at `Runtime::start`, after the literals move | An origin needs Personal's values, which live in the secret store |
| §9: Remove asks for confirmation | In the UI, not a native dialog; a new policy key on Update is asked in a native dialog | Remove only takes access away; a new key changes whom Dots trusts |
| §9 and plan A §14: "used by" and "value missing" deferred | Built, per section | With orgs, the Env tab needs them |

The spec leaves these to the builder, and the plan settles them:

- **The module layout** in "Architecture" above, and `store/orgs.rs`.
- **The test harnesses** in `crates/dots-core/tests/common/`: `fake_openbao`, `fake_infisical`, `fake_files` (an http file server) and `orgs` (`OrgsHarness`, `Scripted`, a source a test drives).
- **`dots-admin`** parses its arguments by hand, writes results to stdout and notes to stderr, and exits 0, 1 for a failure, 2 for a wrong command line. `OrgPolicy::summary` moves into core in Task 8, so the admin and the person read the same words.
- **The SOPS reader** keeps the file's key order with a small tree of its own, since `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` would reorder every JSON map in the app.

## Review Focus

These are the inputs and conditions most likely to bite a person that the spec implies, each pinned to the tests that cover it:

1. **The org's source goes down or hangs during the day.** Expected: dots keep running on the saved copy until `offline_hours` run out, the status says "offline (…); using the saved copy until …", and run starts don't each wait for the timeout. Tests:
   - `vault_orgs_test::an_unreachable_refresh_keeps_the_copy_until_offline_hours`, `the_copy_expires_offline_hours_after_the_last_good_fetch` and `refresh_if_stale_fetches_only_after_refresh_minutes` (Task 8)
   - `vault_org_resolve_test::an_offline_org_resolves_from_its_copy` (Task 9)
2. **The admin cuts a person off**: a revoked token, a removed identity, or a SOPS file re-encrypted without their key. Expected: the next fetch wipes the copy and the values, the status reads "access revoked (…)", and runs get "Acme Engineering: access revoked". Tests:
   - `vault_org_sops_test::a_key_that_is_not_a_recipient_is_denied` (Task 7)
   - `vault_orgs_test::a_denied_refresh_wipes_the_copy_and_the_values` (Task 8)
   - `vault_org_resolve_test::a_revoked_org_gives_nothing` (Task 9)
3. **A tampered, re-signed or rolled-back policy or file.** Expected: refused with the reason, the last good copy kept until it runs out, no new value taken. Tests:
   - `vault_org_policy_test::a_policy_changed_after_signing_is_refused`, `a_policy_signed_by_another_key_is_refused` (Task 1)
   - `vault_org_sops_test::a_file_with_two_values_swapped_in_a_list_fails_the_mac` (Task 7)
   - `vault_orgs_test::an_invalid_answer_or_a_bad_signature_keeps_the_last_good_copy`, `a_rolled_back_policy_is_refused_and_the_copy_kept` (Task 8)
4. **An org's value moves an http MCP server to another host.** Expected: the server does not start in that org's runs, with "github: <origin> is not a confirmed origin; open the server in the Library to confirm it", nothing is sent, Personal runs are unaffected, and a Check asks before sending. Tests:
   - `vault_org_origin_test::the_orgs_value_moving_the_host_is_refused_while_personal_stays_confirmed` (Task 11)
   - `vault_org_origin_test::a_check_is_refused_until_the_origin_is_confirmed_in_its_scope` (Task 12)
5. **The person leaves an org while its dots remain**, and a schedule, webhook or chat reply fires. Expected: the run fails at start with "dot 'D': its org 'acme-eng' was removed", nothing is spawned, and the UI marks the dot and refuses Save, Run now and the composer. Tests:
   - `runtime_org_test::a_run_of_a_dot_whose_org_was_removed_fails_at_start_and_spawns_nothing`, `saving_a_dot_whose_org_was_removed_is_refused` (Task 9)
   - `DotOrgs.test.tsx` "is marked on its card at home, and can't be run from there" and "can't be sent a message from the chat at home, which says why" (Task 15)

### Task 1: The org's policy, its signed text and the join code

Spec §6.3 and §6.1: the policy parsed and checked so that it fails closed, its minisign signature verified against the join code's key, and the join code read and written.

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/policy.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/signed.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/join.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/Cargo.toml`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/mod.rs`
- Create: `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_policy_test.rs`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `vault::entries::check_variable_name`, `crate::{Error, Result}`, `str_enum!`.
- Produces, re-exported from `dots_core::vault::org`:
  - `policy::{POLICY_VERSION = 1, PersonalMode { Deny, Fallback, Override } (default Deny), UseRules { allow (default ["*"]), deny }, AuditTarget { endpoint, token_entry }, OrgPolicy { org_id, issued_at, plain, use_rules, personal, shell_secrets, refresh_minutes, offline_hours, audit }, PolicyError { Envelope, Key, Signature, Invalid, WrongOrg { found, expected }, RolledBack { issued_at, last } }, parse_policy(&str) -> Result<OrgPolicy, PolicyError>}`. `OrgPolicy` has a private parsed instant, so only `parse_policy` makes one; `may_use(name)`, `is_plain(name)` and `check_not_rolled_back(Option<&str>) -> Result<(), PolicyError>`.
  - `signed::{ENVELOPE_VERSION = 1, envelope(policy_text, signature_box) -> String, verify_policy(signed, policy_key, org_id) -> Result<OrgPolicy, PolicyError>}`: envelope, key, signature (`allow_legacy` off), then `parse_policy`, then the org.
  - `join::{JOIN_CODE_VERSION = 1, MAX_ORG_ID = 63, JoinCode { v, org_id, name, source, policy_key } with encode(), SourceSettings { OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings), Infisical(InfisicalSettings), Sops(SopsSettings) } (tag "kind") with kind(), address(), check(), OpenBaoSettings { address, mount = "secret", path, auth = Token, auth_mount, namespace } with login_mount(), BaoAuth { Token, Userpass, Ldap }, InfisicalSettings { site_url, project_id, environment, secret_path = "/" }, SopsSettings { location }, parse_join_code(&str) -> Result<JoinCode>, check_org_id(&str) -> Result<()>, key_fingerprint(&str) -> Result<String>}` (16 upper-case hex). Crate-private: `join::org_id_rule`, `policy::plain_serde`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_policy_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! An org's policy, the signed text that carries it and the join code (env vault spec §6.1,
//! §6.3): defaults, fail-closed parsing, minisign verification and the join code's checks.

use std::io::Cursor;

use base64::engine::general_purpose::{STANDARD, URL_SAFE_NO_PAD};
use base64::Engine;
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    envelope, key_fingerprint, parse_join_code, parse_policy, verify_policy, AuditTarget, BaoAuth,
    InfisicalSettings, JoinCode, OpenBaoSettings, OrgPolicy, PersonalMode, PolicyError,
    SopsSettings, SourceSettings, UseRules,
};
use dots_core::Error;
use minisign::KeyPair;
use serde_json::{json, Value};

/// The example policy of spec §6.3, as written there.
const SPEC_POLICY: &str = r#"{
  "v": 1,
  "org_id": "acme-eng",
  "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z",
  "plain": ["LOG_LEVEL", "API_BASE_URL"],
  "use": { "allow": ["*"], "deny": ["PROD_*"] },
  "personal": "fallback",
  "shell_secrets": false,
  "refresh_minutes": 15,
  "offline_hours": 24,
  "audit": { "endpoint": "https://audit.acme.internal/dots", "token_entry": "DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN" }
}"#;

fn keys() -> KeyPair {
    KeyPair::generate_unencrypted_keypair().unwrap()
}

/// The `.minisig` text over `text`, as `minisign -S` or `dots-admin policy sign` writes it.
fn signature(keys: &KeyPair, text: &str) -> String {
    minisign::sign(Some(&keys.pk), &keys.sk, Cursor::new(text), None, None)
        .unwrap()
        .to_string()
}

fn signed(keys: &KeyPair, text: &str) -> String {
    envelope(text, &signature(keys, text))
}

/// A policy with only the required fields, plus `extra`.
fn policy_with(extra: Value) -> String {
    let mut policy = json!({"v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"});
    for (k, v) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
        policy[k] = v.clone();
    }
    policy.to_string()
}

fn invalid(text: &str) -> String {
    match parse_policy(text) {
        Err(PolicyError::Invalid(why)) => why,
        other => panic!("expected an invalid policy, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

fn parsed(extra: Value) -> OrgPolicy {
    parse_policy(&policy_with(extra)).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn the_spec_example_policy_parses_exactly() {
    let p = parse_policy(SPEC_POLICY).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.org_id, "acme-eng");
    assert_eq!(p.issued_at, "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z");
    assert_eq!(p.plain, ["LOG_LEVEL", "API_BASE_URL"]);
    assert_eq!(
        p.use_rules,
        UseRules {
            allow: vec!["*".into()],
            deny: vec!["PROD_*".into()],
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(p.personal, PersonalMode::Fallback);
    assert!(!p.shell_secrets);
    assert_eq!(p.refresh_minutes, 15);
    assert_eq!(p.offline_hours, 24);
    assert_eq!(
        p.audit,
        Some(AuditTarget {
            endpoint: "https://audit.acme.internal/dots".into(),
            token_entry: "DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN".into(),
        })
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_with_only_the_required_fields_takes_every_default() {
    let p = parsed(json!({}));
    assert!(p.plain.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(p.use_rules, UseRules::default());
    assert_eq!(p.use_rules.allow, ["*"]);
    assert!(p.use_rules.deny.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(p.personal, PersonalMode::Deny);
    assert!(!p.shell_secrets);
    assert_eq!(p.refresh_minutes, 15);
    assert_eq!(p.offline_hours, 24);
    assert_eq!(p.audit, None);

    // A `use` that gives only `deny` still allows everything else.
    let p = parsed(json!({"use": {"deny": ["PROD_*"]}}));
    assert_eq!(p.use_rules.allow, ["*"]);
    // `offline_hours: 0` means no offline copy, and is allowed.
    assert_eq!(parsed(json!({"offline_hours": 0})).offline_hours, 0);
    assert_eq!(
        parsed(json!({"personal": "override"})).personal,
        PersonalMode::Override
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_required_fields_are_required() {
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(r#"{"org_id": "acme-eng", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"}"#),
        "missing field 'v'"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(r#"{"v": 1, "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"}"#),
        "missing field 'org_id'"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(r#"{"v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng"}"#),
        "missing field 'issued_at'"
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_unknown_top_level_field_is_refused() {
    let err = parse_policy(&policy_with(json!({"foo": true}))).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err, PolicyError::Invalid("unknown field 'foo'".into()));
    assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "unknown field 'foo'");
    // Inside `use` and `audit` too: the policy fails closed throughout.
    assert!(
        invalid(&policy_with(json!({"use": {"allow": ["*"], "except": []}})))
            .contains("unknown field 'except'")
    );
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(
        json!({"audit": {"endpoint": "https://a.example", "token_entry": "T", "x": 1}})
    ))
    .contains("unknown field 'x'"));
}

#[test]
fn a_version_other_than_1_is_refused_before_its_fields_are_read() {
    let v2 = json!({"v": 2, "org_id": "acme-eng", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z",
                    "new_v2_field": true});
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(&v2.to_string()),
        "policy version 2 is not supported; this Dots reads version 1"
    );
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"v": "1"}))).contains("version \"1\" is not supported"));
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_that_is_not_a_json_object_or_repeats_a_field_is_refused() {
    assert!(invalid("not json").starts_with("not JSON: "));
    assert!(!invalid("{\"v\": 1,").contains("line"));
    assert_eq!(invalid("[1]"), "the policy must be a JSON object");
    let twice = r#"{"v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng", "org_id": "evil",
                    "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"}"#;
    assert_eq!(invalid(twice), "duplicate field 'org_id'");
}

#[test]
fn refresh_minutes_below_1_is_refused() {
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(&policy_with(json!({"refresh_minutes": 0}))),
        "refresh_minutes must be at least 1"
    );
    assert_eq!(parsed(json!({"refresh_minutes": 1})).refresh_minutes, 1);
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"refresh_minutes": -5}))).contains("invalid value"));
}

#[test]
fn a_glob_with_anything_but_name_characters_and_star_is_refused() {
    for bad in ["PROD_?", "PROD_[0-9]", "", "A B", "PROD-*", "A**{B}"] {
        let why = invalid(&policy_with(json!({"use": {"deny": [bad]}})));
        assert!(
            why.starts_with(&format!("use.deny: '{bad}' ")),
            "{bad}: {why}"
        );
    }
    let why = invalid(&policy_with(json!({"use": {"allow": ["GITHUB_?"]}})));
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        "use.allow: 'GITHUB_?' may hold only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '_' and '*'"
    );
    assert!(
        invalid(&policy_with(json!({"use": {"allow": ["A".repeat(129)]}})))
            .contains("must be 1 to 128 characters")
    );
}

#[test]
fn every_value_is_checked() {
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(&policy_with(json!({"plain": ["LOG LEVEL"]}))),
        "plain: 'LOG LEVEL' is not a variable name"
    );
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"personal": "sometimes"})))
        .contains("unknown variant 'sometimes'"));
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"shell_secrets": "yes"}))).contains("invalid type"));
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(&policy_with(json!({"issued_at": "21 Oct 2026"}))),
        "issued_at '21 Oct 2026' is not an RFC 3339 time, like 2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"
    );
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"issued_at": "2026-10-21"}))).contains("RFC 3339"));
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(json!({"org_id": "Acme Eng"})))
        .starts_with("org id 'Acme Eng': use 1 to 63 characters"));
}

#[test]
fn the_audit_target_needs_an_https_endpoint_and_an_entry_name() {
    let audit = |endpoint: &str, token_entry: &str| {
        policy_with(json!({"audit": {"endpoint": endpoint, "token_entry": token_entry}}))
    };
    for bad in [
        "http://audit.acme.internal/dots",
        "audit.acme.internal",
        "https://",
        "",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            invalid(&audit(bad, "DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN")),
            format!("audit.endpoint '{bad}' must be an https:// URL")
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(&audit("https://audit.acme.internal", "DOTS-AUDIT")),
        "audit.token_entry 'DOTS-AUDIT' is not a variable name"
    );
    assert!(invalid(&policy_with(
        json!({"audit": {"endpoint": "https://a.example"}})
    ))
    .contains("missing field 'token_entry'"));
    assert_eq!(parsed(json!({"audit": null})).audit, None);
}

#[test]
fn may_use_applies_allow_then_deny_without_regard_to_case() {
    let p = parse_policy(SPEC_POLICY).unwrap();
    assert!(p.may_use("GITHUB_TOKEN"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("PROD_DB"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("prod_db"), "the deny glob ignores case");
    assert!(!p.may_use("Prod_Db_Password"));
    assert!(p.may_use("PROD"), "PROD_* needs the underscore");

    let p = parsed(json!({"use": {"allow": ["github_*", "LOG_LEVEL"], "deny": ["GITHUB_ADMIN*"]}}));
    assert!(p.may_use("GITHUB_TOKEN"));
    assert!(p.may_use("log_level"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("GITHUB_ADMIN"), "deny wins over allow");
    assert!(!p.may_use("github_admin_token"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("OTHER"), "a name no allow glob matches");

    let p = parsed(json!({"use": {"allow": ["*_TOKEN", "A*B*C"], "deny": []}}));
    assert!(p.may_use("_TOKEN"), "a star matches an empty run");
    assert!(p.may_use("NPM_TOKEN"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("NPM_TOKEN_2"));
    assert!(p.may_use("AxxBxxC"));
    assert!(p.may_use("ABBC"));
    assert!(!p.may_use("ABCD"));

    let none = parsed(json!({"use": {"allow": []}}));
    assert!(!none.may_use("ANY"), "an empty allow list allows nothing");
}

#[test]
fn is_plain_reads_plain_without_regard_to_case() {
    let p = parse_policy(SPEC_POLICY).unwrap();
    assert!(p.is_plain("LOG_LEVEL"));
    assert!(p.is_plain("api_base_url"));
    assert!(!p.is_plain("DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN"));
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_signed_by_the_org_key_verifies() {
    let keys = keys();
    let text = signed(&keys, SPEC_POLICY);
    let policy = verify_policy(&text, &keys.pk.to_base64(), "acme-eng").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(policy, parse_policy(SPEC_POLICY).unwrap());
    // The envelope is the documented shape, with the policy text unchanged.
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(value["v"], 1);
    assert_eq!(value["policy"], SPEC_POLICY);
    assert!(value["signature"]
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .starts_with("untrusted comment: "));
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_changed_after_signing_is_refused() {
    let keys = keys();
    let sig = signature(&keys, SPEC_POLICY);
    let tampered = SPEC_POLICY.replace(r#""deny": ["PROD_*"]"#, r#""deny": []"#);
    assert_ne!(tampered, SPEC_POLICY);
    let err =
        verify_policy(&envelope(&tampered, &sig), &keys.pk.to_base64(), "acme-eng").unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err, PolicyError::Signature);
    assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "signature does not match");
    // Even a change in white space only.
    let spaced = format!("{SPEC_POLICY}\n");
    assert_eq!(
        verify_policy(&envelope(&spaced, &sig), &keys.pk.to_base64(), "acme-eng"),
        Err(PolicyError::Signature)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_signed_by_another_key_is_refused() {
    let (org, other) = (keys(), keys());
    let text = signed(&other, SPEC_POLICY);
    assert_eq!(
        verify_policy(&text, &org.pk.to_base64(), "acme-eng"),
        Err(PolicyError::Signature)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_signature_relabelled_as_legacy_is_refused() {
    // Turn the `ED` (prehashed) algorithm tag into legacy `Ed`, which signs the raw bytes: only
    // prehashed signatures are accepted.
    let keys = keys();
    let sig = signature(&keys, SPEC_POLICY);
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = sig.lines().map(String::from).collect();
    let mut bytes = STANDARD.decode(&lines[1]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(&bytes[..2], b"ED");
    bytes[1] = b'd';
    lines[1] = STANDARD.encode(&bytes);
    let legacy = lines.join("\n") + "\n";
    assert_eq!(
        verify_policy(
            &envelope(SPEC_POLICY, &legacy),
            &keys.pk.to_base64(),
            "acme-eng"
        ),
        Err(PolicyError::Signature)
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_policy_for_another_org_is_refused() {
    let keys = keys();
    let err = verify_policy(
        &signed(&keys, SPEC_POLICY),
        &keys.pk.to_base64(),
        "other-org",
    )
    .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        err,
        PolicyError::WrongOrg {
            found: "acme-eng".into(),
            expected: "other-org".into(),
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "for org 'acme-eng', not 'other-org'");
}

#[test]
fn a_signed_policy_that_is_invalid_is_refused_after_its_signature() {
    let keys = keys();
    let text = policy_with(json!({"refresh_minutes": 0}));
    assert_eq!(
        verify_policy(&signed(&keys, &text), &keys.pk.to_base64(), "acme-eng"),
        Err(PolicyError::Invalid(
            "refresh_minutes must be at least 1".into()
        ))
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_bad_envelope_or_key_is_refused() {
    let keys = keys();
    let key = keys.pk.to_base64();
    let sig = signature(&keys, SPEC_POLICY);
    let envelope_error = |text: &str| match verify_policy(text, &key, "acme-eng") {
        Err(PolicyError::Envelope(why)) => why,
        other => panic!("expected a bad envelope, got {other:?}"),
    };
    // The bare policy, not wrapped.
    assert!(envelope_error(SPEC_POLICY).contains("unknown field 'org_id'"));
    assert!(!envelope_error("{").contains("line"));
    assert!(
        envelope_error(&json!({"v": 1, "policy": SPEC_POLICY}).to_string())
            .contains("missing field 'signature'")
    );
    assert!(envelope_error(
        &json!({"v": 1, "policy": SPEC_POLICY, "signature": sig, "by": "admin"}).to_string()
    )
    .contains("unknown field 'by'"));
    assert_eq!(
        envelope_error(&json!({"v": 2, "policy": SPEC_POLICY, "signature": sig}).to_string()),
        "version 2 is not supported; this Dots reads version 1"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        envelope_error(&envelope(SPEC_POLICY, "not a minisig")),
        "the signature is not a minisign signature"
    );
    let err = verify_policy(&envelope(SPEC_POLICY, &sig), "RWQnot-a-key", "acme-eng").unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err, PolicyError::Key);
    assert_eq!(
        err.to_string(),
        "the org's policy key is not a minisign public key"
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_older_policy_is_rolled_back_and_the_same_or_newer_is_accepted() {
    let at = |issued_at: &str| parsed(json!({"issued_at": issued_at}));
    let last = Some("2026-10-21T09:00:00Z");

    assert_eq!(
        at("2026-10-21T09:00:00Z").check_not_rolled_back(last),
        Ok(())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        at("2026-10-22T09:00:00Z").check_not_rolled_back(last),
        Ok(())
    );
    let err = at("2026-10-21T08:59:59Z")
        .check_not_rolled_back(last)
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        err,
        PolicyError::RolledBack {
            issued_at: "2026-10-21T08:59:59Z".into(),
            last: "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z".into(),
        }
    );
    assert!(err
        .to_string()
        .starts_with("issued before the last accepted policy"));

    // The comparison is of instants, not text: 10:00 at +01:00 is 09:00Z.
    assert_eq!(
        at("2026-10-21T10:00:00+01:00").check_not_rolled_back(last),
        Ok(())
    );
    assert!(at("2026-10-21T09:59:59+01:00")
        .check_not_rolled_back(last)
        .is_err());
    // As text "2026-10-21T08:30:00-01:00" sorts first, but it is later.
    assert_eq!(
        at("2026-10-21T08:30:00-01:00").check_not_rolled_back(last),
        Ok(())
    );

    // No policy accepted yet; and a damaged last value never turns the check off.
    assert_eq!(
        at("2020-01-01T00:00:00Z").check_not_rolled_back(None),
        Ok(())
    );
    assert!(at("2026-10-22T09:00:00Z")
        .check_not_rolled_back(Some("yesterday"))
        .is_err());
}

fn spec_join_code(policy_key: &str) -> JoinCode {
    JoinCode {
        v: 1,
        org_id: "acme-eng".into(),
        name: "Acme Engineering".into(),
        source: SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
            address: "https://bao.acme.internal".into(),
            mount: "secret".into(),
            path: "dots".into(),
            auth: BaoAuth::Token,
            auth_mount: None,
            namespace: None,
        }),
        policy_key: policy_key.into(),
    }
}

/// The join code text for any JSON, so a test can write one Dots would refuse.
fn code_for(value: &Value) -> String {
    URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(value.to_string())
}

fn join_value(key: &str, source: Value) -> Value {
    json!({"v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng", "name": "Acme Engineering", "source": source,
           "policy_key": key})
}

fn refused(text: &str) -> String {
    match parse_join_code(text) {
        Err(Error::Invalid(why)) => why,
        other => panic!("expected a refused join code, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_spec_join_code_reads_with_its_defaults() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let text = code_for(&json!({
        "v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng", "name": "Acme Engineering",
        "source": { "kind": "openbao", "address": "https://bao.acme.internal", "path": "dots" },
        "policy_key": key
    }));
    let code = parse_join_code(&text).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(code, spec_join_code(&key));
    assert_eq!(code.source.kind(), "openbao");
    assert_eq!(code.source.address(), "https://bao.acme.internal");
    let SourceSettings::OpenBao(bao) = &code.source else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    assert_eq!(bao.login_mount(), None);
}

#[test]
fn a_join_code_round_trips_without_padding_and_reads_with_whitespace_or_padding() {
    let code = spec_join_code(&keys().pk.to_base64());
    let text = code.encode();
    assert!(!text.contains('='));
    assert!(
        !text.contains('+') && !text.contains('/'),
        "base64url, not base64"
    );
    assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&text).unwrap(), code);

    // Pasted with white space around it, and wrapped across lines as an email might.
    let wrapped = text
        .as_bytes()
        .chunks(40)
        .map(|c| std::str::from_utf8(c).unwrap())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\r\n");
    assert_eq!(
        parse_join_code(&format!("  \n{wrapped}\n\t")).unwrap(),
        code
    );

    // With `=` padding, as a base64 tool that pads would write it.
    let padded = format!("{text}{}", "=".repeat((4 - text.len() % 4) % 4));
    assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&padded).unwrap(), code);
    let padded = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode("x") + "==";
    assert!(refused(&padded).starts_with("join code: no JSON inside"));
}

#[test]
fn every_source_kind_round_trips_with_its_defaults_spelled_out() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let infisical = parse_join_code(&code_for(&join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "infisical", "site_url": "https://app.infisical.com",
               "project_id": "p-1", "environment": "prod"}),
    )))
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        infisical.source,
        SourceSettings::Infisical(InfisicalSettings {
            site_url: "https://app.infisical.com".into(),
            project_id: "p-1".into(),
            environment: "prod".into(),
            secret_path: "/".into(),
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&infisical.encode()).unwrap(), infisical);

    let bao = parse_join_code(&code_for(&join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://bao.acme.internal", "mount": "kv",
               "path": "teams/dots", "auth": "ldap", "auth_mount": "corp-ldap",
               "namespace": "eng"}),
    )))
    .unwrap();
    let SourceSettings::OpenBao(settings) = &bao.source else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    assert_eq!(settings.auth, BaoAuth::Ldap);
    assert_eq!(settings.login_mount(), Some("corp-ldap"));
    assert_eq!(settings.namespace.as_deref(), Some("eng"));
    assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&bao.encode()).unwrap(), bao);

    let userpass = parse_join_code(&code_for(&join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "http://127.0.0.1:8200", "path": "dots",
               "auth": "userpass"}),
    )))
    .unwrap();
    let SourceSettings::OpenBao(settings) = &userpass.source else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    assert_eq!(settings.login_mount(), Some("userpass"));

    for location in [
        r"C:\Shared\acme\dots.sops.json",
        "https://files.acme.example/dots.json",
    ] {
        let sops = parse_join_code(&code_for(&join_value(
            &key,
            json!({"kind": "sops", "location": location}),
        )))
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            sops.source,
            SourceSettings::Sops(SopsSettings {
                location: location.into()
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(sops.source.address(), location);
        assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&sops.encode()).unwrap(), sops);
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_join_code_with_an_unknown_version_is_refused() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let mut value = join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://a.example/f"}),
    );
    value["v"] = json!(2);
    value["new_field"] = json!(true);
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&code_for(&value)),
        "join code: version 2 is not supported; update Dots"
    );
    value.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("v");
    assert_eq!(refused(&code_for(&value)), "join code: no version 'v'");
}

#[test]
fn a_join_code_with_a_bad_org_id_is_refused() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let long = "a".repeat(64);
    for bad in [
        "Acme",
        "-acme",
        "",
        "acme_eng",
        "acme eng",
        "acme.eng",
        long.as_str(),
    ] {
        let mut value = join_value(
            &key,
            json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://a.example/f"}),
        );
        value["org_id"] = json!(bad);
        let why = refused(&code_for(&value));
        assert!(
            why.starts_with(&format!("org id '{bad}': use 1 to 63 characters")),
            "{bad}: {why}"
        );
    }
    for good in ["0", "a", "acme-eng", "9-lives-", &"a".repeat(63)] {
        let mut value = join_value(
            &key,
            json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://a.example/f"}),
        );
        value["org_id"] = json!(good);
        assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&code_for(&value)).unwrap().org_id, good);
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_join_code_whose_policy_key_is_not_a_minisign_key_is_refused() {
    let keys = keys();
    let pub_file = keys.pk.to_box().unwrap().into_string();
    for bad in [
        "RWQ-not-a-key".to_string(),
        String::new(),
        pub_file,
        format!(" {}", keys.pk.to_base64()),
    ] {
        let value = join_value(
            &bad,
            json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://a.example/f"}),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            refused(&code_for(&value)),
            "join code: its policy_key is not a minisign public key (the RW… line of the .pub \
             file)",
            "{bad:?}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_source_address_that_is_not_https_is_refused() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let bao = |address: &str| {
        code_for(&join_value(
            &key,
            json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": address, "path": "dots"}),
        ))
    };
    let not_https = "must start with https:// (http:// only for localhost or 127.0.0.1)";
    for bad in [
        "http://bao.acme.internal",
        "http://10.0.0.5:8200",
        "ftp://bao.acme.internal",
        "http://localhost.acme.example",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            refused(&bao(bad)),
            format!("join code: the source's address '{bad}' {not_https}")
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&bao("bao.acme.internal")),
        "join code: the source's address 'bao.acme.internal' is not a URL"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&bao("https://admin:hunter2@bao.acme.internal")),
        "join code: the source's address 'https://admin:hunter2@bao.acme.internal' must not \
         hold a user name or password"
    );
    for local in [
        "http://localhost:8200",
        "http://127.0.0.1:8200",
        "https://bao.acme.internal",
    ] {
        assert!(parse_join_code(&bao(local)).is_ok(), "{local}");
    }

    let infisical = code_for(&join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "infisical", "site_url": "http://infisical.acme.internal",
               "project_id": "p", "environment": "prod"}),
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&infisical),
        format!("join code: the source's site_url 'http://infisical.acme.internal' {not_https}")
    );
    let sops = code_for(&join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "http://files.acme.example/dots.json"}),
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&sops),
        format!(
            "join code: the source's location 'http://files.acme.example/dots.json' {not_https}"
        )
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_join_code_missing_what_a_fetch_needs_is_refused() {
    let key = keys().pk.to_base64();
    let refused_for = |source: Value| refused(&code_for(&join_value(&key, source)));
    assert_eq!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "sops", "location": r"shared\dots.json"})),
        "join code: the source's location 'shared\\dots.json' must be a full path or an \
         https:// URL"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://b.example", "path": " "})),
        "join code: the source's path is empty"
    );
    assert!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://b.example"}))
            .contains("missing field 'path'")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "infisical", "site_url": "https://i.example",
                           "project_id": "p", "environment": "prod", "secret_path": "dots"})),
        "join code: the source's secret_path 'dots' must start with '/'"
    );
    assert!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "dropbox", "location": "https://d.example"}))
            .contains("unknown variant 'dropbox'")
    );
    assert!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://d.example", "key": "x"}))
            .contains("unknown field 'key'")
    );
    assert!(
        refused_for(json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://b.example",
                               "path": "dots", "auth": "oidc"}))
        .contains("unknown variant 'oidc'")
    );

    let mut value = join_value(
        &key,
        json!({"kind": "sops", "location": "https://d.example"}),
    );
    value["name"] = json!("  ");
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&code_for(&value)),
        "join code: the org's name is empty"
    );
    value["name"] = json!("Acme");
    value["admin"] = json!("me");
    assert!(refused(&code_for(&value)).contains("unknown field 'admin'"));
}

#[test]
fn text_that_is_not_a_join_code_is_refused() {
    assert_eq!(refused("not a join code!"), "join code: not base64url text");
    assert_eq!(refused(""), "join code: no JSON inside");
    assert_eq!(
        refused(&URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode("[1, 2]")),
        "join code: no version 'v'"
    );
}

#[test]
fn the_key_fingerprint_is_the_minisign_key_id() {
    let keys = keys();
    let fingerprint = key_fingerprint(&keys.pk.to_base64()).unwrap();
    let keynum: [u8; 8] = keys.pk.keynum().try_into().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fingerprint, format!("{:016X}", u64::from_le_bytes(keynum)));
    assert_eq!(fingerprint.len(), 16);
    // The id `minisign` writes in the .pub file's comment.
    let pub_file = keys.pk.to_box().unwrap().into_string();
    assert!(
        pub_file.starts_with(&format!(
            "untrusted comment: minisign public key: {fingerprint}\n"
        )),
        "{pub_file}"
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        key_fingerprint("RWQ-not-a-key"),
        Err(Error::Invalid(_))
    ));
}
```

```rust
//! The join code (env vault spec §6.1): what an admin hands each person to join an org. It is
//! base64url JSON naming the org, its source and the key its policy is signed with. It holds no
//! secrets: the person gives their own credential for the source.

use std::path::Path;

use base64::engine::general_purpose::{STANDARD, URL_SAFE_NO_PAD};
use base64::Engine;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;

use super::policy::plain_serde;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The only join code version this Dots reads.
pub const JOIN_CODE_VERSION: u32 = 1;

/// The longest org id. It appears in file names and Credential Manager targets.
pub const MAX_ORG_ID: usize = 63;

/// What a person pastes, or reads from a `.dotsorg` file, to join an org.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct JoinCode {
    pub v: u32,
    pub org_id: String,
    /// The org's name as the person sees it, "Acme Engineering".
    pub name: String,
    pub source: SourceSettings,
    /// The minisign public key the org's policy is signed with, the bare `RW…` base64 line.
    pub policy_key: String,
}

/// Where an org's entries and signed policy come from, and how to reach them. It holds no
/// secrets, so it is stored as JSON in the `orgs` row.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum SourceSettings {
    /// OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault, KV v2.
    OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings),
    /// Infisical, self-hosted or cloud.
    Infisical(InfisicalSettings),
    /// A SOPS JSON file encrypted to age recipients.
    Sops(SopsSettings),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct OpenBaoSettings {
    pub address: String,
    /// The KV v2 mount.
    #[serde(default = "default_mount")]
    pub mount: String,
    /// Entries are read from `<mount>/data/<path>/env`, the policy from `…/<path>/policy`.
    pub path: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub auth: BaoAuth,
    /// The auth mount for `userpass` or `ldap`. `None` means the method's own name.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub auth_mount: Option<String>,
    /// Sent as `X-Vault-Namespace`; Vault Enterprise and HCP only.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub namespace: Option<String>,
}

str_enum!(BaoAuth {
    Token => "token",
    Userpass => "userpass",
    Ldap => "ldap",
});

impl Default for BaoAuth {
    /// A token, unless the join code names a login method.
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::Token
    }
}

impl OpenBaoSettings {
    /// The mount to log in through, `auth/<mount>/login/<user>`: `None` for a token.
    pub fn login_mount(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self.auth {
            BaoAuth::Token => None,
            BaoAuth::Userpass | BaoAuth::Ldap => {
                Some(self.auth_mount.as_deref().unwrap_or(self.auth.as_str()))
            }
        }
    }
}

fn default_mount() -> String {
    "secret".into()
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct InfisicalSettings {
    pub site_url: String,
    pub project_id: String,
    /// The environment slug, `dev` or `prod`.
    pub environment: String,
    /// Entries are read from this folder, the policy from its `policy` sub-folder.
    #[serde(default = "default_secret_path")]
    pub secret_path: String,
}

fn default_secret_path() -> String {
    "/".into()
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct SopsSettings {
    /// An absolute local path, synced by git or IT, or an `https://` URL.
    pub location: String,
}

impl SourceSettings {
    /// The kind as the join code spells it: `openbao`, `infisical` or `sops`.
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::OpenBao(_) => "openbao",
            Self::Infisical(_) => "infisical",
            Self::Sops(_) => "sops",
        }
    }

    /// Where the source is, for the UI: the address, the site or the file location.
    pub fn address(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Self::OpenBao(s) => &s.address,
            Self::Infisical(s) => &s.site_url,
            Self::Sops(s) => &s.location,
        }
    }

    /// Checks the addresses and the fields a fetch needs.
    pub fn check(&self) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Self::OpenBao(s) => {
                check_address("address", &s.address)?;
                check_not_blank("mount", &s.mount)?;
                check_not_blank("path", &s.path)?;
                if let Some(mount) = &s.auth_mount {
                    check_not_blank("auth_mount", mount)?;
                }
                if let Some(namespace) = &s.namespace {
                    check_not_blank("namespace", namespace)?;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            Self::Infisical(s) => {
                check_address("site_url", &s.site_url)?;
                check_not_blank("project_id", &s.project_id)?;
                check_not_blank("environment", &s.environment)?;
                if !s.secret_path.starts_with('/') {
                    return Err(refused(format!(
                        "the source's secret_path '{}' must start with '/'",
                        s.secret_path
                    )));
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            Self::Sops(s) if s.location.contains("://") => check_address("location", &s.location),
            Self::Sops(s) => {
                if !Path::new(&s.location).is_absolute() {
                    return Err(refused(format!(
                        "the source's location '{}' must be a full path or an https:// URL",
                        s.location
                    )));
                }
                Ok(())
            }
        }
    }
}

impl JoinCode {
    /// The code as the admin hands it out: base64url of the JSON, without padding.
    pub fn encode(&self) -> String {
        let json = serde_json::to_string(self).expect("a join code serializes");
        URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(json)
    }
}

/// Reads a join code as pasted or read from a `.dotsorg` file. Whitespace anywhere is ignored,
/// so a code wrapped in an email still reads, and `=` padding is optional. Every field is
/// checked: an unknown version, a bad org id, a policy key that is not a minisign public key, or
/// a source that is not `https://` is refused.
pub fn parse_join_code(text: &str) -> Result<JoinCode> {
    let compact: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
    let bytes = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(compact.trim_end_matches('='))
        .map_err(|_| refused("not base64url text"))?;
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_| refused("no JSON inside"))?;
    match value.get("v").map(Value::as_u64) {
        Some(Some(v)) if v == u64::from(JOIN_CODE_VERSION) => {}
        Some(Some(v)) => {
            return Err(refused(format!(
                "version {v} is not supported; update Dots"
            )))
        }
        _ => return Err(refused("no version 'v'")),
    }
    let code: JoinCode = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| refused(plain_serde(&e)))?;
    check_org_id(&code.org_id)?;
    if code.name.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(refused("the org's name is empty"));
    }
    if minisign_verify::PublicKey::from_base64(&code.policy_key).is_err() {
        return Err(refused(
            "its policy_key is not a minisign public key (the RW… line of the .pub file)",
        ));
    }
    code.source.check()?;
    Ok(code)
}

/// An org id: 1 to 63 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. It
/// appears in file names and Credential Manager targets.
pub fn check_org_id(org_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    org_id_rule(org_id).map_err(Error::Invalid)
}

/// `check_org_id`'s rule, its message without the `Error` around it, for the policy's errors.
pub(crate) fn org_id_rule(org_id: &str) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    let bytes = org_id.as_bytes();
    let ok = !bytes.is_empty()
        && bytes.len() <= MAX_ORG_ID
        && (bytes[0].is_ascii_lowercase() || bytes[0].is_ascii_digit())
        && bytes
            .iter()
            .all(|&b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'-');
    if !ok {
        return Err(format!(
            "org id '{org_id}': use 1 to {MAX_ORG_ID} characters of a-z, 0-9 or '-', starting \
             with a letter or digit"
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The policy key's minisign key id, as 16 upper-case hex digits: what `minisign` prints in the
/// `.pub` file's comment, and what the UI shows so the person can compare it with the admin's.
pub fn key_fingerprint(policy_key: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let not_a_key = || Error::Invalid("the policy key is not a minisign public key".into());
    minisign_verify::PublicKey::from_base64(policy_key).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    // `Ed` (2 bytes), the key id (8 bytes, little-endian), the Ed25519 key (32 bytes).
    let bytes = STANDARD.decode(policy_key).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    let id: [u8; 8] = bytes
        .get(2..10)
        .and_then(|b| b.try_into().ok())
        .ok_or_else(not_a_key)?;
    Ok(format!("{:016X}", u64::from_le_bytes(id)))
}

/// A source address: `https://`, or `http://` only to `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`, for test
/// servers. It must name a host and hold no user name or password.
fn check_address(field: &str, address: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let refuse = |why: &str| refused(format!("the source's {field} '{address}' {why}"));
    let url = reqwest::Url::parse(address).map_err(|_| refuse("is not a URL"))?;
    let host = url.host_str().unwrap_or_default();
    if host.is_empty() {
        return Err(refuse("names no host"));
    }
    let local = matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1");
    if !(url.scheme() == "https" || url.scheme() == "http" && local) {
        return Err(refuse(
            "must start with https:// (http:// only for localhost or 127.0.0.1)",
        ));
    }
    if !url.username().is_empty() || url.password().is_some() {
        return Err(refuse("must not hold a user name or password"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn check_not_blank(field: &str, value: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if value.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(refused(format!("the source's {field} is empty")));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn refused(why: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Error {
    Error::Invalid(format!("join code: {why}"))
}
```

```rust
//! Orgs (env vault spec §6): entries an admin's service holds for a team, under a policy signed
//! with the org's minisign key, joined with a join code.

pub mod join;
pub mod policy;
pub mod signed;

pub use join::{
    check_org_id, key_fingerprint, parse_join_code, BaoAuth, InfisicalSettings, JoinCode,
    OpenBaoSettings, SopsSettings, SourceSettings,
};
pub use policy::{parse_policy, AuditTarget, OrgPolicy, PersonalMode, PolicyError, UseRules};
pub use signed::{envelope, verify_policy};
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/policy.rs`:**

```rust
//! An org's policy (env vault spec §6.3): which of its entries are plain, which names dots may be
//! granted, how Personal entries mix in, and how often to refresh. It fails closed: an unknown
//! field, an unknown version or a value out of range makes the whole policy invalid.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::Deserialize;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::vault::entries::{check_variable_name, MAX_VARIABLE_NAME};

str_enum!(PersonalMode {
    Deny => "deny",
    Fallback => "fallback",
    Override => "override",
});

impl Default for PersonalMode {
    /// Only the org's entries resolve unless the admin says otherwise.
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::Deny
    }
}

/// The only policy version this Dots reads.
pub const POLICY_VERSION: u32 = 1;

const FIELDS: &[&str] = &[
    "v",
    "org_id",
    "issued_at",
    "plain",
    "use",
    "personal",
    "shell_secrets",
    "refresh_minutes",
    "offline_hours",
    "audit",
];

/// Why a policy, or the signed text that carries it, was refused. The text names what failed in
/// plain words, for "Acme Engineering: policy invalid: <error>".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum PolicyError {
    /// The signed text is not the `{"v":1,"policy":…,"signature":…}` envelope.
    #[error("the signed policy is not readable: {0}")]
    Envelope(String),
    /// The join code's `policy_key` is not a minisign public key.
    #[error("the org's policy key is not a minisign public key")]
    Key,
    /// The signature is not by the org's key, or not over this policy text.
    #[error("signature does not match")]
    Signature,
    /// The policy text itself: bad JSON, an unknown field, a value out of range.
    #[error("{0}")]
    Invalid(String),
    /// The policy names another org than the join code.
    #[error("for org '{found}', not '{expected}'")]
    WrongOrg { found: String, expected: String },
    /// The policy is older than the last one accepted for this org.
    #[error("issued before the last accepted policy ({issued_at}, last {last})")]
    RolledBack { issued_at: String, last: String },
}

/// Which org entry names dots may be granted. A name must match an `allow` glob and no `deny`
/// glob: deny wins.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct UseRules {
    #[serde(default = "allow_all")]
    pub allow: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub deny: Vec<String>,
}

impl Default for UseRules {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            allow: allow_all(),
            deny: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

fn allow_all() -> Vec<String> {
    vec!["*".into()]
}

/// Where audit records go (plan C sends them). `token_entry` names an org entry sent as
/// `Authorization: Bearer`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct AuditTarget {
    pub endpoint: String,
    pub token_entry: String,
}

/// A policy that parsed and passed every check. It is only made by `parse_policy`, so it is
/// always valid.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OrgPolicy {
    pub org_id: String,
    /// The `issued_at` text as the admin wrote it, for display and for `orgs.last_issued_at`.
    pub issued_at: String,
    pub plain: Vec<String>,
    pub use_rules: UseRules,
    pub personal: PersonalMode,
    pub shell_secrets: bool,
    pub refresh_minutes: u32,
    pub offline_hours: u32,
    pub audit: Option<AuditTarget>,
    /// `issued_at` as an instant, so `+01:00` and `Z` spellings compare right.
    issued: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct RawPolicy {
    /// Checked to be 1 before this struct is parsed.
    #[serde(rename = "v")]
    _v: u64,
    org_id: String,
    issued_at: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    plain: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, rename = "use")]
    use_rules: UseRules,
    #[serde(default)]
    personal: PersonalMode,
    #[serde(default)]
    shell_secrets: bool,
    #[serde(default = "default_refresh_minutes")]
    refresh_minutes: u32,
    #[serde(default = "default_offline_hours")]
    offline_hours: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    audit: Option<AuditTarget>,
}

fn default_refresh_minutes() -> u32 {
    15
}

fn default_offline_hours() -> u32 {
    24
}

/// Parses and checks a policy's JSON text. The version and the top-level field names are checked
/// before anything else, so a newer policy says it is newer instead of naming a field.
pub fn parse_policy(text: &str) -> Result<OrgPolicy, PolicyError> {
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(text)
        .map_err(|e| invalid(format!("not JSON: {}", plain_serde(&e))))?;
    let Value::Object(fields) = &value else {
        return Err(invalid("the policy must be a JSON object"));
    };
    match fields.get("v") {
        None => return Err(invalid("missing field 'v'")),
        Some(v) if v.as_u64() == Some(u64::from(POLICY_VERSION)) => {}
        Some(v) => {
            return Err(invalid(format!(
                "policy version {v} is not supported; this Dots reads version {POLICY_VERSION}"
            )))
        }
    }
    if let Some(unknown) = fields.keys().find(|k| !FIELDS.contains(&k.as_str())) {
        return Err(invalid(format!("unknown field '{unknown}'")));
    }
    // Parsed again from the text, not the `Value`, so a field given twice is refused.
    let raw: RawPolicy = serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| invalid(plain_serde(&e)))?;

    super::join::org_id_rule(&raw.org_id).map_err(invalid)?;
    let issued = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&raw.issued_at)
        .map_err(|_| {
            invalid(format!(
                "issued_at '{}' is not an RFC 3339 time, like 2026-10-21T09:00:00Z",
                raw.issued_at
            ))
        })?
        .with_timezone(&Utc);
    for name in &raw.plain {
        check_variable_name(name)
            .map_err(|_| invalid(format!("plain: '{name}' is not a variable name")))?;
    }
    for (list, globs) in [
        ("use.allow", &raw.use_rules.allow),
        ("use.deny", &raw.use_rules.deny),
    ] {
        for glob in globs {
            check_glob(glob).map_err(|why| invalid(format!("{list}: '{glob}' {why}")))?;
        }
    }
    if raw.refresh_minutes < 1 {
        return Err(invalid("refresh_minutes must be at least 1"));
    }
    if let Some(audit) = &raw.audit {
        check_audit(audit)?;
    }

    Ok(OrgPolicy {
        org_id: raw.org_id,
        issued_at: raw.issued_at,
        plain: raw.plain,
        use_rules: raw.use_rules,
        personal: raw.personal,
        shell_secrets: raw.shell_secrets,
        refresh_minutes: raw.refresh_minutes,
        offline_hours: raw.offline_hours,
        audit: raw.audit,
        issued,
    })
}

impl OrgPolicy {
    /// Whether dots may be granted the org entry `name`: an `allow` glob matches and no `deny`
    /// glob does. Case is ignored, as names compare that way.
    pub fn may_use(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        let matches = |globs: &[String]| globs.iter().any(|g| glob_matches(g, name));
        !matches(&self.use_rules.deny) && matches(&self.use_rules.allow)
    }

    /// Whether the org entry `name` is plain, shown with its value. Every other entry is secret.
    pub fn is_plain(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.plain.iter().any(|p| p.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
    }

    /// The rollback check (§6.3): refuses this policy when it was issued before `last_issued_at`,
    /// the `issued_at` of the last policy accepted for the org. The same instant is a re-fetch of
    /// the same policy and passes. `None`, no policy accepted yet, always passes. A `last` that is
    /// not RFC 3339 is refused too, so a damaged row never turns the check off.
    pub fn check_not_rolled_back(&self, last_issued_at: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), PolicyError> {
        let Some(last) = last_issued_at else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        let rolled_back = || PolicyError::RolledBack {
            issued_at: self.issued_at.clone(),
            last: last.to_string(),
        };
        let last_at = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(last).map_err(|_| rolled_back())?;
        if self.issued < last_at {
            return Err(rolled_back());
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn check_audit(audit: &AuditTarget) -> Result<(), PolicyError> {
    let url = reqwest::Url::parse(&audit.endpoint);
    let https = url
        .as_ref()
        .is_ok_and(|u| u.scheme() == "https" && u.host_str().is_some_and(|h| !h.is_empty()));
    if !https {
        return Err(invalid(format!(
            "audit.endpoint '{}' must be an https:// URL",
            audit.endpoint
        )));
    }
    check_variable_name(&audit.token_entry).map_err(|_| {
        invalid(format!(
            "audit.token_entry '{}' is not a variable name",
            audit.token_entry
        ))
    })
}

/// A glob is a variable name in which `*` may stand for any run of characters, `*` alone
/// included. Nothing else is special.
fn check_glob(glob: &str) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    if glob.is_empty() || glob.len() > MAX_VARIABLE_NAME {
        return Err("must be 1 to 128 characters");
    }
    if !glob
        .bytes()
        .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_' || b == b'*')
    {
        return Err("may hold only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '_' and '*'");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Matches `name` against `glob`, where `*` is any run of characters, without regard to case.
/// Both are ASCII by the name and glob rules. The classic two-pointer match: on a mismatch,
/// retry from the last `*`, letting it take one more character.
fn glob_matches(glob: &str, name: &str) -> bool {
    let (g, n) = (glob.as_bytes(), name.as_bytes());
    let (mut gi, mut ni) = (0, 0);
    let mut star: Option<(usize, usize)> = None;
    while ni < n.len() {
        if gi < g.len() && g[gi] == b'*' {
            star = Some((gi, ni));
            gi += 1;
        } else if gi < g.len() && g[gi].eq_ignore_ascii_case(&n[ni]) {
            gi += 1;
            ni += 1;
        } else if let Some((sg, sn)) = star {
            gi = sg + 1;
            ni = sn + 1;
            star = Some((sg, sn + 1));
        } else {
            return false;
        }
    }
    g[gi..].iter().all(|&b| b == b'*')
}

fn invalid(message: impl Into<String>) -> PolicyError {
    PolicyError::Invalid(message.into())
}

/// A serde error as plain words: no "at line 1 column 9", and 'quotes' for serde's backticks.
pub(crate) fn plain_serde(e: &serde_json::Error) -> String {
    let text = e.to_string();
    let suffix = format!(" at line {} column {}", e.line(), e.column());
    text.strip_suffix(&suffix)
        .unwrap_or(&text)
        .replace('`', "'")
}
```

```rust
//! The signed policy text (env vault spec §6.3): one JSON string holding the policy text and a
//! minisign signature over its exact UTF-8 bytes, so it fits an OpenBao key, an Infisical secret
//! and the SOPS `policy` field alike.
//!
//! `{"v":1,"policy":"<policy JSON text>","signature":"<the whole .minisig text>"}`

use minisign_verify::{PublicKey, Signature};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::policy::{parse_policy, plain_serde, OrgPolicy, PolicyError};

/// The only envelope version this Dots reads.
pub const ENVELOPE_VERSION: u32 = 1;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Envelope {
    v: u32,
    policy: String,
    signature: String,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct EnvelopeRef<'a> {
    v: u32,
    policy: &'a str,
    signature: &'a str,
}

/// Wraps a policy text and its minisign signature box into the signed text, for `dots-admin`.
/// `policy_text` goes in unchanged: the signature is over its exact bytes.
pub fn envelope(policy_text: &str, signature_box: &str) -> String {
    serde_json::to_string(&EnvelopeRef {
        v: ENVELOPE_VERSION,
        policy: policy_text,
        signature: signature_box,
    })
    .expect("an envelope serializes")
}

/// Verifies the signed text fetched from an org's source against the join code's `policy_key`
/// and `org_id`, in this order: the envelope, the signature (prehashed `ED` only), the policy,
/// then the org. The policy is not read until its signature checks out. Rollback is the
/// caller's check, `OrgPolicy::check_not_rolled_back`, since it needs the `orgs` row.
pub fn verify_policy(
    signed: &str,
    policy_key: &str,
    org_id: &str,
) -> Result<OrgPolicy, PolicyError> {
    let envelope: Envelope =
        serde_json::from_str(signed).map_err(|e| PolicyError::Envelope(plain_serde(&e)))?;
    if envelope.v != ENVELOPE_VERSION {
        return Err(PolicyError::Envelope(format!(
            "version {} is not supported; this Dots reads version {ENVELOPE_VERSION}",
            envelope.v
        )));
    }
    let key = PublicKey::from_base64(policy_key).map_err(|_| PolicyError::Key)?;
    let signature = Signature::decode(&envelope.signature)
        .map_err(|_| PolicyError::Envelope("the signature is not a minisign signature".into()))?;
    key.verify(envelope.policy.as_bytes(), &signature, false)
        .map_err(|_| PolicyError::Signature)?;

    let policy = parse_policy(&envelope.policy)?;
    if policy.org_id != org_id {
        return Err(PolicyError::WrongOrg {
            found: policy.org_id,
            expected: org_id.to_string(),
        });
    }
    Ok(policy)
}
```
