```rust
//! `dots-admin` (env vault spec §12, §13): keys, policies and join codes made here are what
//! `dots-core` accepts, and what it would refuse is refused here first.

use std::cell::RefCell;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command;

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use dots_admin::keys::{keygen, read_public_key};
use dots_admin::policy::{new_policy, sign_policy, verify_signed};
use dots_admin::{run, AdminError, Ask, Io};
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    parse_join_code, parse_policy, verify_policy, BaoAuth, InfisicalSettings, JoinCode,
    OpenBaoSettings, PersonalMode, PolicyError, SopsSettings, SourceSettings, UseRules,
};
use serde_json::Value;
use tempfile::TempDir;

/// What one `run` wrote, and how it ended.
struct Ran {
    out: String,
    err: String,
    result: Result<(), AdminError>,
    asked: Vec<Ask>,
}

/// Runs a command line with `password` as the only password, recording what was asked.
fn run_with(args: &[&str], password: Option<&str>) -> Ran {
    let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|a| a.to_string()).collect();
    let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    let asked = RefCell::new(Vec::new());
    let mut source = |ask: Ask| {
        asked.borrow_mut().push(ask);
        password
            .map(str::to_string)
            .ok_or_else(|| AdminError::Failed("no password in this test".into()))
    };
    let result = run(
        &args,
        &mut Io {
            out: &mut out,
            err: &mut err,
            password: &mut source,
        },
    );
    Ran {
        out: String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(),
        err: String::from_utf8(err).unwrap(),
        result,
        asked: asked.into_inner(),
    }
}

/// Runs a command line that needs no password and must succeed.
fn ok(args: &[&str]) -> Ran {
    let ran = run_with(args, None);
    assert!(ran.result.is_ok(), "{args:?}: {:?}", ran.result);
    assert!(ran.asked.is_empty(), "{args:?} asked for a password");
    ran
}

/// The message of a command line that must fail.
fn failure(args: &[&str]) -> AdminError {
    let ran = run_with(args, None);
    ran.result.expect_err("the command should fail")
}

fn path(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> String {
    dir.join(name).to_str().unwrap().to_string()
}

fn no_password(_: Ask) -> dots_admin::Result<String> {
    panic!("an unprotected key needs no password")
}

fn at(text: &str) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(text)
        .unwrap()
        .with_timezone(&Utc)
}

/// A policy with the required fields and `extra`.
fn policy_with(extra: &str) -> String {
    format!(r#"{{"v": 1, "org_id": "acme-eng", "issued_at": "2026-10-21T09:00:00Z"{extra}}}"#)
}

/// An unprotected key pair in a new folder.
fn keys() -> (TempDir, String, String) {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let keys = keygen(dir.path(), None).unwrap();
    let secret = std::fs::read_to_string(&keys.secret_path).unwrap();
    (dir, secret, keys.public_key)
}

#[test]
fn round_trip_from_keygen_to_a_join_code_that_dots_accepts() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let keygen = ok(&[
        "keygen",
        "--out",
        dir.path().to_str().unwrap(),
        "--no-password",
    ]);
    assert!(keygen
        .err
        .contains("warning: policy.key is not password-protected"));
    let public = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("policy.pub")).unwrap();
    let public_key = read_public_key(&public).unwrap();
    assert!(keygen.out.contains(&public_key));

    let policy_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.json");
    ok(&[
        "policy",
        "new",
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
        "--out",
        &policy_file,
    ]);
    // The admin's edit: two fields, and an old issued_at that signing replaces.
    let edited: String = std::fs::read_to_string(&policy_file)
        .unwrap()
        .lines()
        .map(|line| match line {
            l if l.starts_with(r#"  "issued_at": "#) => {
                r#"  "issued_at": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","#.to_string()
            }
            l => l
                .replace(r#""plain": []"#, r#""plain": ["LOG_LEVEL"]"#)
                .replace(r#""personal": "deny""#, r#""personal": "fallback""#),
        })
        .map(|line| line + "\n")
        .collect();
    assert!(edited.contains("LOG_LEVEL") && edited.contains("fallback") && edited.contains("2020"));
    std::fs::write(&policy_file, &edited).unwrap();

    let before = Utc::now();
    let signed_file = path(dir.path(), "signed.json");
    let key_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.key");
    let sign = ok(&[
        "policy",
        "sign",
        &policy_file,
        "--key",
        &key_file,
        "--out",
        &signed_file,
    ]);
    assert!(sign.out.contains("store its text as DOTS_POLICY"));

    let signed = std::fs::read_to_string(&signed_file).unwrap();
    let policy = verify_policy(&signed, &public_key, "acme-eng").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(policy.plain, ["LOG_LEVEL"]);
    assert_eq!(policy.personal, PersonalMode::Fallback);
    let issued = at(&policy.issued_at);
    assert!(issued >= before - chrono::Duration::seconds(1) && issued <= Utc::now());
    // The policy file itself is left as the admin wrote it.
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(&policy_file).unwrap(), edited);

    let pub_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.pub");
    let verify = ok(&["policy", "verify", &signed_file, "--pub", &pub_file]);
    assert!(verify
        .out
        .starts_with("ok: a Dots client in org 'acme-eng' accepts this policy"));
    assert!(verify
        .out
        .contains("plain entries, shown with their values: LOG_LEVEL"));
    let verify = ok(&[
        "policy",
        "verify",
        &signed_file,
        "--pub",
        &pub_file,
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
    ]);
    assert!(verify.out.starts_with("ok"));

    let join = ok(&[
        "join-code",
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
        "--name",
        "Acme Engineering",
        "--source",
        "openbao",
        "--address",
        "https://bao.acme.internal",
        "--path",
        "dots",
        "--pub",
        &pub_file,
    ]);
    let code = parse_join_code(&join.out).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(code.policy_key, public_key);
    // What Dots does on joining: the fetched policy verifies against the join code.
    verify_policy(&signed, &code.policy_key, &code.org_id).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn a_password_protected_key_signs_and_verifies() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let out = dir.path().to_str().unwrap();
    let keygen = run_with(&["keygen", "--out", out], Some("correct horse"));
    assert!(keygen.result.is_ok(), "{:?}", keygen.result);
    assert_eq!(keygen.asked, [Ask::NewKey]);
    assert!(
        keygen.err.is_empty(),
        "no warning for a protected key: {}",
        keygen.err
    );
    let secret = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("policy.key")).unwrap();
    assert!(!keygen.out.contains(secret.lines().nth(1).unwrap()));

    let policy_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.json");
    ok(&[
        "policy",
        "new",
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
        "--out",
        &policy_file,
    ]);
    let key_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.key");
    let sign = run_with(
        &["policy", "sign", &policy_file, "--key", &key_file],
        Some("correct horse"),
    );
    assert!(sign.result.is_ok(), "{:?}", sign.result);
    assert_eq!(sign.asked, [Ask::Unlock]);
    assert!(sign.err.contains("signed the policy for org 'acme-eng'"));

    let public = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("policy.pub")).unwrap();
    let policy = verify_signed(&sign.out, &public, Some("acme-eng")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(policy.org_id, "acme-eng");

    let policy_text = std::fs::read_to_string(&policy_file).unwrap();
    let wrong = sign_policy(
        &policy_text,
        &secret,
        &mut |_| Ok("battery staple".into()),
        Utc::now(),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        wrong.unwrap_err(),
        AdminError::Failed("wrong password for the policy key".into())
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_empty_password_is_refused() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let ran = run_with(&["keygen", "--out", dir.path().to_str().unwrap()], Some(""));
    let message = ran.result.unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(
        message.contains("an empty password does not protect the key"),
        "{message}"
    );
    assert!(!dir.path().join("policy.key").exists());
}

#[test]
fn policy_new_has_every_field_at_its_default() {
    let text = new_policy("acme-eng", at("2026-10-23T08:30:00Z")).unwrap();
    let policy = parse_policy(&text).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(policy.org_id, "acme-eng");
    assert_eq!(policy.issued_at, "2026-10-23T08:30:00Z");
    assert!(policy.plain.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(policy.use_rules, UseRules::default());
    assert_eq!(policy.personal, PersonalMode::default());
    assert!(!policy.shell_secrets);
    assert_eq!(policy.refresh_minutes, 15);
    assert_eq!(policy.offline_hours, 24);
    assert_eq!(policy.audit, None);
    // Every field is spelled out, so the admin sees what can be set.
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
    let mut fields: Vec<&str> = value
        .as_object()
        .unwrap()
        .keys()
        .map(String::as_str)
        .collect();
    fields.sort_unstable();
    let mut expected = [
        "v",
        "org_id",
        "issued_at",
        "plain",
        "use",
        "personal",
        "shell_secrets",
        "refresh_minutes",
        "offline_hours",
        "audit",
    ];
    expected.sort_unstable();
    assert_eq!(fields, expected);
    assert!(
        text.starts_with("{\n  \"v\": 1,\n  \"org_id\": \"acme-eng\","),
        "{text}"
    );

    let stdout = ok(&["policy", "new", "--org-id", "acme-eng"]);
    parse_policy(&stdout.out).unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn policy_new_refuses_a_bad_org_id_and_an_existing_file() {
    let message = failure(&["policy", "new", "--org-id", "Acme Eng"]).to_string();
    assert!(
        message.starts_with("org id 'Acme Eng': use 1 to 63 characters"),

#[test]
fn policy_check_says_ok_with_a_summary() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let file = path(dir.path(), "policy.json");
    std::fs::write(
        &file,
        policy_with(
            r#", "plain": ["LOG_LEVEL", "API_BASE_URL"],
            "use": {"allow": ["*"], "deny": ["PROD_*"]}, "personal": "override",
            "shell_secrets": true, "refresh_minutes": 1,
            "offline_hours": 0, "audit": {"endpoint": "https://audit.acme.internal/dots",
            "token_entry": "DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN"}"#,
        ),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let check = ok(&["policy", "check", &file]);
    let expected = "\
ok
  org: acme-eng
  issued at: 2026-10-21T09:00:00Z
  plain entries, shown with their values: LOG_LEVEL, API_BASE_URL; every other org entry is a secret
  dots may be granted: every org entry except names matching PROD_*
  personal entries: win over the org's entry of the same name
  secrets in the shell: allowed
  refresh: every 1 minute
  offline copy: none; offline, the org's entries are not available
  audit: records go to https://audit.acme.internal/dots, with the token in entry DOTS_AUDIT_TOKEN
";
    assert_eq!(check.out, expected);
}

#[test]
fn policy_check_refuses_an_unknown_field_and_a_zero_refresh() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let file = path(dir.path(), "policy.json");
    for (extra, message) in [
        (r#", "foo": 1"#, "policy invalid: unknown field 'foo'"),
        (
            r#", "refresh_minutes": 0"#,
            "policy invalid: refresh_minutes must be at least 1",
        ),
    ] {
        std::fs::write(&file, policy_with(extra)).unwrap();
        let error = failure(&["policy", "check", &file]);
        assert_eq!(error, AdminError::Failed(message.into()));
        assert_eq!(error.exit_code(), 1);
    }
}

#[test]
fn policy_sign_refuses_an_invalid_policy() {
    let (dir, _, _) = keys();
    let policy_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.json");
    let signed_file = path(dir.path(), "signed.json");
    std::fs::write(&policy_file, policy_with(r#", "refresh_minutes": 0"#)).unwrap();
    let key_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.key");
    let ran = run_with(
        &[
            "policy",
            "sign",
            &policy_file,
            "--key",
            &key_file,
            "--out",
            &signed_file,
        ],
        Some("unused"),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        ran.result,
        Err(AdminError::Failed(
            "policy invalid: refresh_minutes must be at least 1".into()
        ))
    );
    assert!(
        ran.asked.is_empty(),
        "no password is asked for a policy that is refused"
    );
    assert!(!Path::new(&signed_file).exists());
}

#[test]
fn policy_sign_rewrites_only_issued_at() {
    let (_dir, secret, public_key) = keys();
    // Odd layout, an escaped key and look-alikes that are not the top-level issued_at.
    let text = concat!(
        "{ \"use\" : {\"allow\":[\"issued_at\"]},\n",
        "\t\"issued\\u005fat\":\"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z\" ,",
        "\"v\":1, \"org_id\":\"acme-eng\",\"plain\" : [ \"ISSUED_AT\" ] }",
    );
    let signed = sign_policy(text, &secret, &mut no_password, at("2026-10-23T10:00:00Z")).unwrap();
    let envelope: Value = serde_json::from_str(&signed.text).unwrap();
    let expected = text.replace(
        "\"issued\\u005fat\":\"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z\"",
        "\"issued\\u005fat\":\"2026-10-23T10:00:00Z\"",
    );
    assert_eq!(envelope["policy"], expected);
    assert_eq!(signed.policy.issued_at, "2026-10-23T10:00:00Z");
    let signature = envelope["signature"].as_str().unwrap();
    assert!(signature.contains("trusted comment: dots policy acme-eng 2026-10-23T10:00:00Z\n"));
    verify_policy(&signed.text, &public_key, "acme-eng").unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn a_signature_by_another_key_fails_verify() {
    let (dir, secret, _) = keys();
    let (_other_dir, _, other_public) = keys();
    let policy = new_policy("acme-eng", Utc::now()).unwrap();
    let signed = sign_policy(&policy, &secret, &mut no_password, Utc::now()).unwrap();
    let signed_file = path(dir.path(), "signed.json");
    std::fs::write(&signed_file, &signed.text).unwrap();
    let other_pub = path(dir.path(), "other.pub");
    std::fs::write(&other_pub, &other_public).unwrap();

    let error = failure(&["policy", "verify", &signed_file, "--pub", &other_pub]);
    assert_eq!(
        error,
        AdminError::Failed("a Dots client would refuse it: signature does not match".into())
    );
    assert_eq!(error.exit_code(), 1);
    assert_eq!(
        verify_policy(&signed.text, &other_public, "acme-eng").unwrap_err(),
        PolicyError::Signature
    );
}

#[test]
fn policy_verify_checks_the_org() {
    let (dir, secret, public_key) = keys();
    let policy = new_policy("acme-eng", Utc::now()).unwrap();
    let signed = sign_policy(&policy, &secret, &mut no_password, Utc::now()).unwrap();
    let error = verify_signed(&signed.text, &public_key, Some("other-org")).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        error,
        AdminError::Failed(
            "a Dots client would refuse it: for org 'acme-eng', not 'other-org'".into()
        )
    );
    let error = verify_signed("not signed", &public_key, None)
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
    assert!(error.starts_with("a Dots client would refuse it: the signed policy is not readable"));
    let not_a_key = verify_signed(&signed.text, "RWnope", None)
        .unwrap_err()
        .to_string();
    assert!(
        not_a_key.contains("is not a minisign public key"),
        "{not_a_key}"
    );
    drop(dir);
}

#[test]
fn join_code_for_each_source_kind_reads_back_in_dots() {
    let (dir, _, public_key) = keys();
    let pub_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.pub");
    let common = [
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
        "--name",
        "Acme Engineering",
        "--pub",
        &pub_file,
    ];
    let cases: Vec<(Vec<&str>, SourceSettings)> = vec![
        (
            vec![
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "https://bao.acme.internal",
                "--path",
                "dots",
            ],
            SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
                address: "https://bao.acme.internal".into(),
                mount: "secret".into(),
                path: "dots".into(),
                auth: BaoAuth::Token,
                auth_mount: None,
                namespace: None,
            }),
        ),
        (
            vec![
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "https://vault.acme.internal:8200",
                "--mount",
                "kv",
                "--path",
                "teams/eng",
                "--auth",
                "ldap",
                "--auth-mount",
                "corp-ldap",
                "--namespace",
                "eng",
            ],
            SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
                address: "https://vault.acme.internal:8200".into(),
                mount: "kv".into(),
                path: "teams/eng".into(),
                auth: BaoAuth::Ldap,
                auth_mount: Some("corp-ldap".into()),
                namespace: Some("eng".into()),
            }),
        ),
        (
            vec![
                "--source",
                "infisical",
                "--site-url",
                "https://app.infisical.com",
                "--project-id",
                "p-123",
                "--environment",
                "prod",
                "--secret-path",
                "/dots",
            ],
            SourceSettings::Infisical(InfisicalSettings {
                site_url: "https://app.infisical.com".into(),
                project_id: "p-123".into(),
                environment: "prod".into(),
                secret_path: "/dots".into(),
            }),
        ),
        (
            vec![
                "--source",
                "infisical",
                "--site-url",
                "https://infisical.acme.internal",
                "--project-id",
                "p-9",
                "--environment",
                "dev",
            ],
            SourceSettings::Infisical(InfisicalSettings {
                site_url: "https://infisical.acme.internal".into(),
                project_id: "p-9".into(),
                environment: "dev".into(),
                secret_path: "/".into(),
            }),
        ),
        (
            vec![
                "--source",
                "sops",
                "--location",
                "https://files.acme.internal/eng.sops.json",
            ],
            SourceSettings::Sops(SopsSettings {
                location: "https://files.acme.internal/eng.sops.json".into(),
            }),
        ),
    ];
    for (i, (source_args, source)) in cases.into_iter().enumerate() {
        let expected = JoinCode {
            v: 1,
            org_id: "acme-eng".into(),
            name: "Acme Engineering".into(),
            source,
            policy_key: public_key.clone(),
        };
        let mut args = vec!["join-code"];
        args.extend(common);
        args.extend(&source_args);
        let printed = ok(&args);
        assert_eq!(
            parse_join_code(&printed.out).unwrap(),
            expected,
            "{source_args:?}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            printed.out.lines().count(),
            1,
            "only the code goes to stdout"
        );
        assert!(
            printed.err.contains("policy key fingerprint: "),
            "{}",
            printed.err
        );

        let file = path(dir.path(), &format!("org{i}.dotsorg"));
        args.extend(["--file", &file]);
        let written = ok(&args);
        assert!(written.out.starts_with(&format!("wrote {file}")));
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parse_join_code(&text).unwrap(), expected, "{source_args:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn join_code_on_a_local_sops_file() {
    let (dir, _, _) = keys();
    let pub_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.pub");
    let location = path(dir.path(), "eng.sops.json");
    let printed = ok(&[
        "join-code",
        "--org-id",
        "acme-eng",
        "--name",
        "Acme",
        "--source",
        "sops",
        "--location",
        &location,
        "--pub",
        &pub_file,
    ]);

}

#[test]
fn join_code_refuses_what_dots_would_refuse() {
    let (dir, _, _) = keys();
    let pub_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.pub");
    let key_file = path(dir.path(), "policy.key");
    let base = ["join-code", "--org-id", "acme-eng", "--name", "Acme"];
    let cases: [(&[&str], &str); 8] = [
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--site-url",
                "https://x.example",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "--site-url is for --source infisical",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "https://x.example",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "--source openbao needs --path",
        ),
        (
            &["--source", "dropbox", "--pub", &pub_file],
            "--source must be openbao, infisical or sops, not 'dropbox'",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "https://x.example",
                "--path",
                "d",
                "--auth",
                "kerberos",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "--auth must be token, userpass or ldap, not 'kerberos'",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "https://x.example",
                "--path",
                "d",
                "--auth-mount",
                "corp",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "--auth-mount is for --auth userpass or ldap",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "openbao",
                "--address",
                "http://x.example",
                "--path",
                "d",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "join code: the source's address 'http://x.example' must start with https://",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "sops",
                "--location",
                "relative/eng.json",
                "--pub",
                &pub_file,
            ],
            "join code: the source's location 'relative/eng.json' must be a full path",
        ),
        (
            &[
                "--source",
                "sops",
                "--location",
                "https://x.example/a.json",
                "--pub",
                &key_file,
            ],
            "the --pub file is not a minisign public key",
        ),
    ];
    for (extra, message) in cases {
        let mut args = base.to_vec();
        args.extend(extra);
        let error = failure(&args).to_string();
        assert!(error.starts_with(message), "{args:?}: {error}");
    }
    let bad_org = failure(&[
        "join-code",
        "--org-id",
        "-acme",
        "--name",
        "Acme",
        "--source",
        "sops",
        "--location",
        "https://x.example/a.json",
        "--pub",
        &pub_file,
    ]);
    assert!(
        bad_org.to_string().starts_with("org id '-acme'"),
        "{bad_org}"
    );
}

#[test]
fn keygen_refuses_to_overwrite_existing_files() {
    for existing in ["policy.key", "policy.pub"] {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.path().join(existing), "old").unwrap();
        let ran = run_with(
            &["keygen", "--out", dir.path().to_str().unwrap()],
            Some("pw"),
        );
        let message = ran.result.unwrap_err().to_string();
        assert!(
            message.contains(&format!("{existing} already exists")),
            "{message}"
        );
        assert!(
            ran.asked.is_empty(),
            "no password is asked for a key that won't be written"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join(existing)).unwrap(),
            "old"
        );
        let other = if existing == "policy.key" {
            "policy.pub"
        } else {
            "policy.key"
        };
        assert!(!dir.path().join(other).exists());
        assert!(keygen(dir.path(), None).is_err());
    }
}

#[test]
fn keygen_writes_a_minisign_key_pair() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let keys = keygen(&dir.path().join("new-folder"), None).unwrap();
    let public = std::fs::read_to_string(&keys.public_path).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        public,
        format!(
            "untrusted comment: minisign public key: {}\n{}\n",
            keys.fingerprint, keys.public_key
        )
    );
    let secret = std::fs::read_to_string(&keys.secret_path).unwrap();
    assert!(secret.starts_with("untrusted comment: dots-admin policy secret key"));
    assert_eq!(read_public_key(&keys.public_key).unwrap(), keys.public_key);
}
```

Expected: FAIL: the package ID specification `dots-admin` did not match any packages.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the crate**

`crates/dots-admin` joins both `members` and `default-members`: it needs no UI, so a plain `cargo test` still runs it. Its dependencies are all in `Cargo.lock` already; the lock gains only the `dots-admin` entry.

**In `Cargo.toml`, replace:**

```toml
resolver = "2"
members = ["crates/dots-core", "apps/dots-app"]
# `cargo test` and `cargo build` without `-p` stay headless: the app needs the built UI
```

**with:**

```toml
resolver = "2"
members = ["crates/dots-core", "crates/dots-admin", "apps/dots-app"]
# `cargo test` and `cargo build` without `-p` stay headless: the app needs the built UI
```

**In `Cargo.toml`, replace:**

```toml
# and, on Linux, WebKitGTK.
default-members = ["crates/dots-core"]
```

**with:**

```toml
# and, on Linux, WebKitGTK.
default-members = ["crates/dots-core", "crates/dots-admin"]
```

**Create `crates/dots-admin/src/args.rs`:**

```rust
//! A small command line parser: positional words, `--name value` (or `--name=value`) options
//! and `--name` switches. Each command names the options it takes; any other is refused.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

use crate::{usage, Result};

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub(crate) struct Args {
    positional: Vec<String>,
    values: BTreeMap<&'static str, String>,
    switches: BTreeSet<&'static str>,
}

impl Args {
    /// Parses a command's arguments. `values` are the options that take a value, `switches`
    /// the ones that don't. An option given twice, or one the command doesn't take, is refused.
    pub(crate) fn parse(
        args: &[String],
        values: &[&'static str],
        switches: &[&'static str],
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let mut parsed = Self::default();
        let mut args = args.iter();
        while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
            let Some(option) = arg.strip_prefix("--") else {
                if arg.len() > 1 && arg.starts_with('-') {
                    return Err(usage(format!("unknown option '{arg}'")));
                }
                parsed.positional.push(arg.clone());
                continue;
            };
            let (name, inline) = match option.split_once('=') {
                Some((name, value)) => (name, Some(value.to_string())),
                None => (option, None),
            };
            if let Some(&name) = switches.iter().find(|s| **s == name) {
                if inline.is_some() {
                    return Err(usage(format!("--{name} takes no value")));
                }
                if !parsed.switches.insert(name) {
                    return Err(usage(format!("--{name} is given twice")));
                }
            } else if let Some(&name) = values.iter().find(|s| **s == name) {
                let value = match inline {
                    Some(value) => value,
                    None => args
                        .next()
                        .filter(|v| !v.starts_with("--"))
                        .cloned()
                        .ok_or_else(|| usage(format!("--{name} needs a value")))?,
                };
                if parsed.values.insert(name, value).is_some() {
                    return Err(usage(format!("--{name} is given twice")));
                }
            } else {
                return Err(usage(format!("unknown option '--{name}'")));
            }
        }
        Ok(parsed)
    }

    pub(crate) fn value(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.values.get(name).map(String::as_str)
    }

    pub(crate) fn required(&self, name: &str) -> Result<&str> {
        self.value(name)
            .ok_or_else(|| usage(format!("--{name} is required")))
    }

    pub(crate) fn switch(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.switches.contains(name)
    }

    /// The names of the value options given, in name order.
    pub(crate) fn given(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> + '_ {
        self.values.keys().copied()
    }

    /// The one positional word, `what` naming it for the error.
    pub(crate) fn one(&self, what: &str) -> Result<&str> {
        match self.positional.as_slice() {
            [word] => Ok(word),
            [] => Err(usage(format!("give {what}"))),
            [_, extra, ..] => Err(usage(format!("unexpected argument '{extra}'"))),
        }
    }

    /// Refuses any positional word, for commands that take none.
    pub(crate) fn none(&self) -> Result<()> {
        match self.positional.first() {
            None => Ok(()),
            Some(extra) => Err(usage(format!("unexpected argument '{extra}'"))),
        }
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-admin/src/join.rs`:**

```rust
//! Join codes (env vault spec §6.1): what the admin hands each person. A code names the org, its
//! source and the policy key, and holds no secrets.

use dots_core::vault::org::join::JOIN_CODE_VERSION;
use dots_core::vault::org::{key_fingerprint, parse_join_code, BaoAuth, JoinCode, SourceSettings};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::args::Args;
use crate::keys::read_public_key;
use crate::{core_failed, failed, read_file, say, usage, write_file, Io, Result};

/// A source kind's options, named after its `SourceSettings` fields with `-` for `_`.
struct Kind {
    name: &'static str,
    required: &'static [&'static str],
    optional: &'static [&'static str],
}

const KINDS: &[Kind] = &[
    Kind {
        name: "openbao",
        required: &["address", "path"],
        optional: &["mount", "auth", "auth-mount", "namespace"],
    },
    Kind {
        name: "infisical",
        required: &["site-url", "project-id", "environment"],
        optional: &["secret-path"],
    },
    Kind {
        name: "sops",
        required: &["location"],
        optional: &[],
    },
];

/// The options `join-code` takes besides the source's.
const OPTIONS: &[&str] = &["org-id", "name", "source", "pub", "file"];

/// Builds the join code and reads it back with `parse_join_code`, as Dots will, so a code Dots
/// would refuse is never handed out. `public_key` is the bare `RW…` key.
pub fn join_code(
    org_id: &str,
    name: &str,
    source: SourceSettings,
    public_key: &str,
) -> Result<JoinCode> {
    let code = JoinCode {
        v: JOIN_CODE_VERSION,
        org_id: org_id.to_string(),
        name: name.to_string(),
        source,
        policy_key: public_key.to_string(),
    };
    let read_back = parse_join_code(&code.encode()).map_err(core_failed)?;
    if read_back != code {
        return Err(failed("the join code does not read back as written"));
    }
    Ok(code)
}

/// `join-code --org-id <id> --name <name> --source <kind> [source options] --pub <policy.pub>
/// [--file <out.dotsorg>]`. Without `--file` the code alone goes to stdout and the notes to
/// stderr, so the code can be redirected.
pub(crate) fn join_code_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let mut options = OPTIONS.to_vec();
    for kind in KINDS {
        options.extend(kind.required.iter().chain(kind.optional));
    }
    let args = Args::parse(args, &options, &[])?;
    args.none()?;
    let source = source_settings(&args)?;
    let public_key = read_public_key(&read_file(args.required("pub")?, "the public key")?)?;
    let code = join_code(
        args.required("org-id")?,
        args.required("name")?,
        source,
        &public_key,
    )?;
    let notes = [
        format!("org: {} ({})", code.name, code.org_id),
        format!(
            "source: {} at {}",
            code.source.kind(),
            code.source.address()
        ),
        format!(
            "policy key fingerprint: {}; Dots shows it on joining, so tell people to expect it",
            key_fingerprint(&code.policy_key).map_err(core_failed)?
        ),
    ];
    match args.value("file") {
        Some(path) => {
            write_file(path, &format!("{}\n", code.encode()))?;
            say(io.out, &format!("wrote {path}"))?;
            notes.iter().try_for_each(|note| say(io.out, note))
        }
        None => {
            say(io.out, &code.encode())?;
            notes.iter().try_for_each(|note| say(io.err, note))
        }
    }
}

/// The `SourceSettings` the options describe. Fields left out take `dots-core`'s defaults, as
/// they do in a join code: the settings are read with its own serde rules.
fn source_settings(args: &Args) -> Result<SourceSettings> {
    let kind_name = args.required("source")?;
    let kind = KINDS.iter().find(|k| k.name == kind_name).ok_or_else(|| {
        usage(format!(
            "--source must be openbao, infisical or sops, not '{kind_name}'"
        ))
    })?;
    for option in args.given() {
        let belongs = OPTIONS.contains(&option)
            || kind.required.contains(&option)
            || kind.optional.contains(&option);
        if !belongs {
            let owner = KINDS
                .iter()
                .find(|k| k.required.contains(&option) || k.optional.contains(&option))
                .map_or("another source", |k| k.name);
            return Err(usage(format!("--{option} is for --source {owner}")));
        }
    }
    let mut fields = Map::new();
    fields.insert("kind".into(), Value::from(kind.name));
    for &option in kind.required {
        let value = args
            .value(option)
            .ok_or_else(|| usage(format!("--source {} needs --{option}", kind.name)))?;
        fields.insert(option.replace('-', "_"), Value::from(value));
    }
    for &option in kind.optional {
        if let Some(value) = args.value(option) {
            fields.insert(option.replace('-', "_"), Value::from(value));
        }
    }
    if let Some(auth) = args.value("auth") {
        if !BaoAuth::ALL.iter().any(|a| a.as_str() == auth) {
            return Err(usage(format!(
                "--auth must be token, userpass or ldap, not '{auth}'"
            )));
        }
    }
    if args.value("auth-mount").is_some() && matches!(args.value("auth"), None | Some("token")) {
        return Err(usage("--auth-mount is for --auth userpass or ldap"));
    }
    serde_json::from_value(Value::Object(fields)).map_err(|e| {
        let why = e.to_string().replace('`', "'");
        failed(format!("the source options do not make a source: {why}"))
    })
}
```

```rust
//! The org's policy signing key: a minisign key pair. `policy.key` is the secret key, normally
//! protected by a password; `policy.pub` is the public key, whose `RW…` line goes into every
//! join code.

use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::io::{ErrorKind, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD;
use base64::Engine;
use dots_core::vault::org::key_fingerprint;
use minisign::{KeyPair, PublicKey, SecretKey, SecretKeyBox};

use crate::args::Args;
use crate::{core_failed, failed, say, Ask, Io, PasswordSource, Result};

/// The secret key's file name in `keygen --out <dir>`.
pub const SECRET_KEY_FILE: &str = "policy.key";
/// The public key's file name in `keygen --out <dir>`.
pub const PUBLIC_KEY_FILE: &str = "policy.pub";

/// A key pair `keygen` wrote.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct NewKeys {
    pub secret_path: PathBuf,
    pub public_path: PathBuf,
    /// The bare `RW…` public key, as a join code holds it.
    pub public_key: String,
    /// The key id as Dots shows it when someone joins.
    pub fingerprint: String,
}

/// Makes the org's key pair and writes `policy.key` and `policy.pub` into `dir`, creating `dir`
/// if needed. With `password` the secret key is encrypted with it (minisign's scrypt); `None`
/// writes an unprotected key. A file that is already there is never overwritten: the old key
/// may be the one every join code names.
pub fn keygen(dir: &Path, password: Option<&str>) -> Result<NewKeys> {
    let secret_path = dir.join(SECRET_KEY_FILE);
    let public_path = dir.join(PUBLIC_KEY_FILE);
    for path in [&secret_path, &public_path] {
        if path.exists() {
            return Err(exists(path));
        }
    }
    if password == Some("") {
        return Err(failed(
            "an empty password does not protect the key; give one, or use --no-password for \
             an unprotected key",
        ));
    }
    let keys = match password {
        Some(password) => KeyPair::generate_encrypted_keypair(Some(password.to_string())),
        None => KeyPair::generate_unencrypted_keypair(),
    }
    .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not make the key pair: {e}")))?;
    let comment = match password {
        Some(_) => "dots-admin policy secret key",
        None => "dots-admin policy secret key, not password-protected",
    };
    let boxed = |e: minisign::PError| failed(format!("could not encode the key pair: {e}"));
    let secret_text = keys.sk.to_box(Some(comment)).map_err(boxed)?.into_string();
    let public_text = keys.pk.to_box().map_err(boxed)?.into_string();
    let public_key = keys.pk.to_base64();
    let fingerprint = key_fingerprint(&public_key).map_err(core_failed)?;

    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not create {}: {e}", dir.display())))?;
    write_new(&secret_path, &secret_text, true)?;
    if let Err(e) = write_new(&public_path, &public_text, false) {
        // A secret key without its public key is of no use to anyone.
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&secret_path);
        return Err(e);
    }
    Ok(NewKeys {
        secret_path,
        public_path,
        public_key,
        fingerprint,
    })
}

/// `keygen --out <dir> [--no-password]`.
pub(crate) fn keygen_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse(args, &["out"], &["no-password"])?;
    args.none()?;
    let dir = Path::new(args.required("out")?);
    // Checked before the password is asked for, so nobody types one for a key that won't be
    // written.
    for name in [SECRET_KEY_FILE, PUBLIC_KEY_FILE] {
        if dir.join(name).exists() {
            return Err(exists(&dir.join(name)));
        }
    }
    let password = if args.switch("no-password") {
        say(
            io.err,
            "warning: policy.key is not password-protected; anyone who copies it can sign \
             policies for this org",
        )?;
        None
    } else {
        Some((io.password)(Ask::NewKey)?)
    };
    let keys = keygen(dir, password.as_deref())?;
    say(io.out, &format!("wrote {}", keys.secret_path.display()))?;
    say(io.out, &format!("wrote {}", keys.public_path.display()))?;
    say(io.out, &format!("public key: {}", keys.public_key))?;
    say(io.out, &format!("key fingerprint: {}", keys.fingerprint))?;
    say(
        io.out,
        "Keep policy.key offline. Join codes carry policy.pub; Dots shows the fingerprint.",
    )
}

/// The bare `RW…` public key from a `policy.pub` file's text, or from that line alone.
pub fn read_public_key(text: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let not_a_key = || {
        failed("the --pub file is not a minisign public key (policy.pub from 'dots-admin keygen')")
    };
    let lines: Vec<&str> = text
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())
        .collect();
    let key = match lines.as_slice() {
        [key] => *key,
        [comment, key] if comment.starts_with("untrusted comment:") => *key,
        _ => return Err(not_a_key()),
    };
    PublicKey::from_base64(key).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    Ok(key.to_string())
}

/// Reads a `policy.key` file's text. The password is asked for only when the key has one.
pub fn unlock_secret_key(text: &str, password: PasswordSource<'_>) -> Result<SecretKey> {
    let not_a_key = || {
        failed("the --key file is not a minisign secret key (policy.key from 'dots-admin keygen')")
    };
    // The box is a comment line, then the key's base64. Its header says whether it is
    // encrypted.
    let line = text.lines().nth(1).ok_or_else(not_a_key)?;
    let bytes = STANDARD.decode(line.trim()).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    let header = SecretKey::from_bytes(&bytes).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    let sk_box = SecretKeyBox::from_string(text).map_err(|_| not_a_key())?;
    if !header.is_encrypted() {
        return SecretKey::from_unencrypted_box(sk_box).map_err(|_| not_a_key());
    }
    let password = password(Ask::Unlock)?;
    SecretKey::from_box(sk_box, Some(password)).map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
        minisign::ErrorKind::Verify => failed("wrong password for the policy key"),
        _ => not_a_key(),
    })
}

/// Creates `path` with `text`, refusing to replace a file. The secret key is readable by its
/// owner only where the OS has such modes; on Windows it takes the folder's permissions.
fn write_new(path: &Path, text: &str, secret: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let mut options = OpenOptions::new();
    options.write(true).create_new(true);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    if secret {
        use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
        options.mode(0o600);
    }
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let _ = secret;
    let mut file = options.open(path).map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
        ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => exists(path),
        _ => failed(format!("could not write {}: {e}", path.display())),
    })?;
    file.write_all(text.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not write {}: {e}", path.display())))
}

fn exists(path: &Path) -> crate::AdminError {
    failed(format!(
        "{} already exists; dots-admin never overwrites a key. Move it away or choose another \
         --out",
        path.display()
    ))
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-admin/src/lib.rs`:**

```rust
//! `dots-admin`, the org admin's helper (env vault spec §12): the policy signing key, the policy
//! itself and the join codes people paste into Dots. It uses `dots-core`'s policy and join code
//! types and checks, so what it writes is what Dots reads.
//!
//! Every command is a function here, so tests call them without a terminal; `main` only wires
//! `run` to the console.

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::Path;

mod args;
pub mod join;
pub mod keys;
pub mod policy;

/// The environment variable a password is read from before asking on the terminal.
pub const PASSWORD_VAR: &str = "DOTS_ADMIN_PASSWORD";

/// Why a command did not run or did not succeed, in plain words. A secret key or password is
/// never part of the text.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum AdminError {
    /// The command line is wrong.
    #[error("{0}\nRun 'dots-admin help' to see the commands.")]
    Usage(String),
    /// The command ran and failed, or found the input invalid.
    #[error("{0}")]
    Failed(String),
}

impl AdminError {
    /// The process exit code: 2 for a wrong command line, 1 for a failure.
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> u8 {
        match self {
            Self::Usage(_) => 2,
            Self::Failed(_) => 1,
        }
    }
}

pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, AdminError>;

/// What a password is asked for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Ask {
    /// The password that will protect a new key: asked twice on the terminal.
    NewKey,
    /// The password of an existing key, to sign with it.
    Unlock,
}

/// A source of passwords: `console_password` in the binary, a closure in tests.
pub type PasswordSource<'a> = &'a mut dyn FnMut(Ask) -> Result<String>;

/// Where a command writes and how it gets a password.
pub struct Io<'a> {
    /// The command's result: a policy, a signed text, a join code, a summary.
    pub out: &'a mut dyn Write,
    /// Notes and warnings that should not end up in a redirected result.
    pub err: &'a mut dyn Write,
    pub password: PasswordSource<'a>,
}

const USAGE: &str = "\
dots-admin: the org admin's key, policy and join code helper for Dots.

Commands:
  dots-admin keygen --out <dir> [--no-password]
      Makes the policy signing key pair, <dir>/policy.key and <dir>/policy.pub.
  dots-admin policy new --org-id <id> [--out <file>]
      Writes a policy with every field at its default.
  dots-admin policy check <policy.json>
      Checks a policy as Dots does.
  dots-admin policy sign <policy.json> --key <policy.key> [--out <file>]
      Sets issued_at to now and writes the signed text, to store as DOTS_POLICY.
  dots-admin policy verify <signed> --pub <policy.pub> [--org-id <id>]
      Shows what a Dots client would accept.
  dots-admin join-code --org-id <id> --name <name> --source <openbao|infisical|sops>
                       [source options] --pub <policy.pub> [--file <out.dotsorg>]
      Prints a join code, or writes it to a .dotsorg file.
      openbao:   --address <url> --path <path> [--mount <kv mount>]
                 [--auth <token|userpass|ldap>] [--auth-mount <mount>] [--namespace <ns>]
      infisical: --site-url <url> --project-id <id> --environment <slug>
                 [--secret-path </path>]
      sops:      --location <full path or https:// url>

A key's password is read from DOTS_ADMIN_PASSWORD when it is set, else from the terminal.
";

/// Runs one command line, without the program name.
pub fn run(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let Some((command, rest)) = args.split_first() else {
        return Err(usage("no command given"));
    };
    match command.as_str() {
        "help" | "--help" | "-h" => say(io.out, USAGE.trim_end()),
        "keygen" => keys::keygen_command(rest, io),
        "policy" => {
            let Some((sub, rest)) = rest.split_first() else {
                return Err(usage("'policy' needs one of: new, check, sign, verify"));
            };
            match sub.as_str() {
                "new" => policy::new_command(rest, io),
                "check" => policy::check_command(rest, io),
                "sign" => policy::sign_command(rest, io),
                "verify" => policy::verify_command(rest, io),
                other => Err(usage(format!("unknown policy command '{other}'"))),
            }
        }
        "join-code" => join::join_code_command(rest, io),
        other => Err(usage(format!("unknown command '{other}'"))),
    }
}

/// The binary's password source: `DOTS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when it is set, else the terminal
/// without echo. A new key's password is asked twice.
pub fn console_password(ask: Ask) -> Result<String> {
    if let Some(value) = std::env::var_os(PASSWORD_VAR) {
        return value
            .into_string()
            .map_err(|_| failed(format!("{PASSWORD_VAR} is not valid text")));
    }
    let read = |prompt: &str| {
        rpassword::prompt_password(prompt).map_err(|e| {
            failed(format!(
                "could not read a password from the terminal ({e}); set {PASSWORD_VAR} instead"
            ))
        })
    };
    match ask {
        Ask::Unlock => read("Password for the policy key: "),
        Ask::NewKey => {
            let first = read("Password for the new policy key: ")?;
            let again = read("The same password again: ")?;
            if first != again {
                return Err(failed("the two passwords differ; nothing was written"));
            }
            Ok(first)
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn usage(message: impl Into<String>) -> AdminError {
    AdminError::Usage(message.into())
}

pub(crate) fn failed(message: impl Into<String>) -> AdminError {
    AdminError::Failed(message.into())
}

/// A `dots-core` error as plain words: its own message without the "invalid input: " prefix.
pub(crate) fn core_failed(error: dots_core::Error) -> AdminError {
    match error {
        dots_core::Error::Invalid(message) => failed(message),
        other => failed(other.to_string()),
    }
}

/// Writes `text` and a line end.
pub(crate) fn say(to: &mut dyn Write, text: &str) -> Result<()> {
    writeln!(to, "{text}").map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not write the output: {e}")))
}

pub(crate) fn read_file(path: &str, what: &str) -> Result<String> {
    std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not read {what} {path}: {e}")))
}

/// Writes a result file, replacing one that is there.
pub(crate) fn write_file(path: &str, text: &str) -> Result<()> {
    std::fs::write(Path::new(path), text)
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not write {path}: {e}")))
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-admin/src/main.rs`:**

```rust
//! `dots-admin`: see the library for the commands.

use std::process::ExitCode;

use dots_admin::{console_password, run, Io};

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Result<Vec<String>, _> = std::env::args_os()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|a| a.into_string())
        .collect();
    let Ok(args) = args else {
        eprintln!("dots-admin: an argument is not valid text");
        return ExitCode::from(2);
    };
    let (mut out, mut err) = (std::io::stdout(), std::io::stderr());
    let mut password = console_password;
    let mut io = Io {
        out: &mut out,
        err: &mut err,
        password: &mut password,
    };
    match run(&args, &mut io) {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("dots-admin: {e}");
            ExitCode::from(e.exit_code())
        }
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-admin/src/policy.rs`:**

```rust
//! The org's policy (env vault spec §6.3): a new one with every default, the same check Dots
//! makes, signing it into the text stored as `DOTS_POLICY`, and verifying that text as a Dots
//! client does.

use std::fs::OpenOptions;
use std::io::{Cursor, ErrorKind, Write};
use std::ops::Range;

use chrono::{DateTime, SecondsFormat, Utc};
use dots_core::vault::org::policy::POLICY_VERSION;
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    check_org_id, envelope, key_fingerprint, parse_policy, verify_policy, OrgPolicy, PersonalMode,
    PolicyError,
};
use minisign::PublicKey;
use serde_json::Value;

use crate::args::Args;
use crate::keys::{read_public_key, unlock_secret_key};
use crate::{core_failed, failed, read_file, say, write_file, Io, PasswordSource, Result};

/// The signature's untrusted comment. Nothing reads it; it tells a person what the box is.
const UNTRUSTED_COMMENT: &str = "dots policy signature from dots-admin";

/// `issued_at` as `policy new` and `policy sign` write it: UTC, to the second.
pub fn timestamp(now: DateTime<Utc>) -> String {
    now.to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Secs, true)
}

/// A new policy's text, with every field present at its default so the admin sees what can be
/// set, and `issued_at` set to `now`.
pub fn new_policy(org_id: &str, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> Result<String> {
    check_org_id(org_id).map_err(core_failed)?;
    Ok(format!(
        r#"{{
  "v": {POLICY_VERSION},
  "org_id": {org_id},
  "issued_at": {issued_at},
  "plain": [],
  "use": {{ "allow": ["*"], "deny": [] }},
  "personal": "deny",
  "shell_secrets": false,
  "refresh_minutes": 15,
  "offline_hours": 24,
  "audit": null
}}
"#,
        org_id = json_string(org_id),
        issued_at = json_string(&timestamp(now)),
    ))
}

/// The policy in plain words, one line per field.
pub fn summary(policy: &OrgPolicy) -> Vec<String> {
    let rules = &policy.use_rules;
    let plain = if policy.plain.is_empty() {
        "plain entries: none; every org entry is a secret".to_string()
    } else {
        format!(
            "plain entries, shown with their values: {}; every other org entry is a secret",
            policy.plain.join(", ")
        )
    };
    let granted = match (rules.allow.as_slice(), rules.deny.as_slice()) {
        ([], _) => "no org entry (use.allow is empty)".to_string(),
        ([all], []) if all == "*" => "every org entry".to_string(),
        ([all], deny) if all == "*" => {
            format!("every org entry except names matching {}", deny.join(", "))
        }
        (allow, []) => format!("names matching {}", allow.join(", ")),
        (allow, deny) => format!(
            "names matching {}, except names matching {}",
            allow.join(", "),
            deny.join(", ")
        ),
    };
    let personal = match policy.personal {
        PersonalMode::Deny => "personal entries: not used; only the org's entries resolve",
        PersonalMode::Fallback => "personal entries: used when the org has no entry of that name",
        PersonalMode::Override => "personal entries: win over the org's entry of the same name",
    };
    let shell = if policy.shell_secrets {
        "secrets in the shell: allowed"
    } else {
        "secrets in the shell: not allowed"
    };
    let offline = match policy.offline_hours {
        0 => "offline copy: none; offline, the org's entries are not available".to_string(),
        hours => format!(
            "offline copy: kept for {} after the last good fetch",
            count(hours, "hour")
        ),
    };
    let audit = match &policy.audit {
        None => "audit: off".to_string(),
        Some(audit) => format!(
            "audit: records go to {}, with the token in entry {}",
            audit.endpoint, audit.token_entry
        ),
    };
    vec![
        format!("org: {}", policy.org_id),
        format!("issued at: {}", policy.issued_at),
        plain,
        format!("dots may be granted: {granted}"),
        personal.to_string(),
        shell.to_string(),
        format!("refresh: every {}", count(policy.refresh_minutes, "minute")),
        offline,
        audit,
    ]
}

/// The policy text signed: the envelope to store as `DOTS_POLICY`, and the policy in it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Signed {
    pub text: String,
    pub policy: OrgPolicy,
    /// The signing key's fingerprint, which every join code for the org must carry.
    pub fingerprint: String,
}

/// Signs a policy, in this order:
///
/// 1. checks it as Dots does, before any password is asked for;
/// 2. sets `issued_at` to `now`, rewriting only that value, so the admin's layout stays;
/// 3. checks the result again;
/// 4. signs its exact text with the trusted comment `dots policy <org_id> <issued_at>`;
/// 5. verifies the envelope with `verify_policy`, as a Dots client will.
pub fn sign_policy(
    policy_text: &str,
    secret_key_text: &str,
    password: PasswordSource<'_>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Signed> {
    parse_policy(policy_text).map_err(refused)?;
    let text = set_issued_at(policy_text, &timestamp(now))?;
    let policy = parse_policy(&text).map_err(refused)?;

    let secret_key = unlock_secret_key(secret_key_text, password)?;
    let public_key = PublicKey::from_secret_key(&secret_key)
        .map_err(|_| failed("the --key file is not a minisign secret key"))?;
    let trusted = format!("dots policy {} {}", policy.org_id, policy.issued_at);
    let signature = minisign::sign(
        Some(&public_key),
        &secret_key,
        Cursor::new(text.as_bytes()),
        Some(&trusted),
        Some(UNTRUSTED_COMMENT),
    )
    .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not sign the policy: {e}")))?;
    let signed = envelope(&text, &signature.to_string());

    let public_key = public_key.to_base64();
    verify_policy(&signed, &public_key, &policy.org_id)
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("the signed policy does not verify: {e}")))?;
    Ok(Signed {
        text: signed,
        policy,
        fingerprint: key_fingerprint(&public_key).map_err(core_failed)?,
    })
}

/// Verifies a signed text as a Dots client in `org_id` does. `None` checks it against the org
/// the policy names. `public_key_text` is a `policy.pub` file's text or its `RW…` line.
pub fn verify_signed(
    signed: &str,
    public_key_text: &str,
    org_id: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<OrgPolicy> {
    let public_key = read_public_key(public_key_text)?;
    let org = match org_id {
        Some(org) => {
            check_org_id(org).map_err(core_failed)?;
            org.to_string()
        }
        // An unreadable text fails `verify_policy` before the org is compared.
        None => claimed_org(signed).unwrap_or_default(),
    };
    verify_policy(signed, &public_key, &org)
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("a Dots client would refuse it: {e}")))
}

/// `policy new --org-id <id> [--out <file>]`. The file is never replaced: it may hold edits.
pub(crate) fn new_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse(args, &["org-id", "out"], &[])?;
    args.none()?;
    let text = new_policy(args.required("org-id")?, Utc::now())?;
    let Some(path) = args.value("out") else {
        return write_all(io.out, &text);
    };
    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
        .write(true)
        .create_new(true)
        .open(path)
        .map_err(|e| match e.kind() {
            ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => {
                failed(format!("{path} already exists; choose another --out"))
            }
            _ => failed(format!("could not write {path}: {e}")),
        })?;
    file.write_all(text.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not write {path}: {e}")))?;
    say(io.out, &format!("wrote {path}"))
}

/// `policy check <policy.json>`: "ok" and the summary, or why Dots would refuse it.
pub(crate) fn check_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse(args, &[], &[])?;
    let path = args.one("the policy file")?;
    let policy = parse_policy(&read_file(path, "the policy")?).map_err(refused)?;
    say(io.out, "ok")?;
    for line in summary(&policy) {
        say(io.out, &format!("  {line}"))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `policy sign <policy.json> --key <policy.key> [--out <file>]`.
pub(crate) fn sign_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse(args, &["key", "out"], &[])?;
    let path = args.one("the policy file")?;
    let key_path = args.required("key")?;
    let policy = read_file(path, "the policy")?;
    let key = read_file(key_path, "the key")?;
    let signed = sign_policy(&policy, &key, &mut *io.password, Utc::now())?;
    let note = format!(
        "signed the policy for org '{}', issued_at {}, with key {}",
        signed.policy.org_id, signed.policy.issued_at, signed.fingerprint
    );
    match args.value("out") {
        Some(out) => {
            write_file(out, &format!("{}\n", signed.text))?;
            say(io.out, &note)?;
            say(
                io.out,
                &format!("wrote {out}; store its text as DOTS_POLICY"),
            )
        }
        None => {
            say(io.out, &signed.text)?;
            say(io.err, &note)
        }
    }
}

/// `policy verify <signed> --pub <policy.pub> [--org-id <id>]`.
pub(crate) fn verify_command(args: &[String], io: &mut Io<'_>) -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse(args, &["pub", "org-id"], &[])?;
    let path = args.one("the signed policy file")?;
    let public_key = read_file(args.required("pub")?, "the public key")?;
    let signed = read_file(path, "the signed policy")?;
    let policy = verify_signed(&signed, &public_key, args.value("org-id"))?;
    let fingerprint = key_fingerprint(&read_public_key(&public_key)?).map_err(core_failed)?;
    say(
        io.out,
        &format!(
            "ok: a Dots client in org '{}' accepts this policy, signed by key {fingerprint}",
            policy.org_id
        ),
    )?;
    for line in summary(&policy) {
        say(io.out, &format!("  {line}"))?;
    }
    say(
        io.out,
        "Dots refuses it all the same if it has accepted a policy issued later.",
    )
}

fn refused(error: PolicyError) -> crate::AdminError {
    failed(format!("policy invalid: {error}"))
}

fn write_all(to: &mut dyn Write, text: &str) -> Result<()> {
    to.write_all(text.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| failed(format!("could not write the output: {e}")))
}

fn json_string(text: &str) -> String {
    Value::String(text.to_string()).to_string()
}

fn count(n: u32, unit: &str) -> String {
    match n {
        1 => format!("1 {unit}"),
        n => format!("{n} {unit}s"),
    }
}

/// The org a signed text's policy names, read without any check, to verify it against.
fn claimed_org(signed: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let envelope: Value = serde_json::from_str(signed).ok()?;
    let policy: Value = serde_json::from_str(envelope.get("policy")?.as_str()?).ok()?;
    Some(policy.get("org_id")?.as_str()?.to_string())
}

/// Replaces the value of the top-level `issued_at` in a policy text that `parse_policy`
/// accepted, leaving every other byte as it was.
fn set_issued_at(text: &str, issued_at: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let span = issued_at_span(text)
        .ok_or_else(|| failed("policy invalid: could not find its issued_at"))?;
    let mut rewritten = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    rewritten.push_str(&text[..span.start]);
    rewritten.push_str(&json_string(issued_at));
    rewritten.push_str(&text[span.end..]);
    Ok(rewritten)
}

/// Where the top-level `issued_at` string value is, quotes included. It walks the JSON text
/// tracking depth and strings, so a nested `issued_at` or one inside a string is passed over,
/// and a key spelled with escapes still counts. `None` if there is none.
fn issued_at_span(text: &str) -> Option<Range<usize>> {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    // At depth 1: the next string is a key; the last key was `issued_at`; its value is next.
    let (mut key_next, mut is_issued_at, mut value_next) = (false, false, false);
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        match bytes[i] {
            b'"' => {
                let end = string_end(bytes, i)?;
                if depth == 1 && value_next {
                    return Some(i..end);
                }
                if depth == 1 && key_next {
                    let key: String = serde_json::from_str(&text[i..end]).ok()?;
                    is_issued_at = key == "issued_at";
                    key_next = false;
                }
                i = end;
                continue;
            }
            b'{' | b'[' => {
                depth += 1;
                key_next = depth == 1;
                value_next = false;
            }
            b'}' | b']' => depth = depth.checked_sub(1)?,
            b':' if depth == 1 => value_next = is_issued_at,
            b',' if depth == 1 => {
                key_next = true;
                value_next = false;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    None
}

/// The index just past the string that opens at `start`.
fn string_end(bytes: &[u8], start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut i = start + 1;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        match bytes[i] {
            b'\\' => i += 2,
            b'"' => return Some(i + 1),
            _ => i += 1,
        }
    }
    None
}
```

### Task 3: The `orgs` table, and the org a dot belongs to

Spec §5.2 and §6.4: migration `0013_orgs.sql` (the `orgs` table and `dots.org_id`, with no foreign key so a re-join re-attaches), the store's org rows, and `Dot.org_id`, fixed when the dot is made.

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/dots-core/migrations/0013_orgs.sql`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/row.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/store/orgs.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/store/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/store/dots.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/model.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/runtime.rs`, `crates/dots-core/examples/smoke.rs`, `apps/dots-app/src/{commands,contract,tray}.rs`, `ui/src/api/{types,commands}.ts`
- Regenerate: `ui/src/api/__fixtures__/contract.json`
- Tests: `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_orgs_store_test.rs` (new); `None` added to every `create_dot` call in the core tests, and `org_id: None` in `tests/common/mod.rs`'s `fake_dot`; `store_dots_test.rs` (+2); `ui/src/lib/dot-rules.test.ts`, `ui/src/screens/DotEditorScreen.test.tsx`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: Task 1's `SourceSettings`, `check_org_id`, `plain_serde`.
- Produces:
  - `vault::org::OrgRow { id, name, source: SourceSettings, policy_key, last_issued_at: Option<String>, last_fetch_at: Option<String>, joined_at }`.
  - `Store::{add_org(&OrgRow), get_org(id) -> Option<OrgRow>, list_orgs() -> Vec<OrgRow> (by name without case, then id), update_org_settings(id, name, source, policy_key), record_org_fetch(id, last_fetch_at, last_issued_at), remove_org(id)}`. A duplicate is `Conflict("the org 'acme-eng' is already joined on this PC")`; an unknown id `NotFound("no org 'x' is joined on this PC")`; a row whose `source` does not parse `Other("org 'acme-eng': its stored source settings are not readable: …")`.
  - `Dot.org_id: Option<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`, `None` is Personal); `Store::create_dot(&spec, org_id: Option<&str>)`; `Runtime::create_dot(spec, org_id: Option<String>)`, which refuses an org not joined with `Invalid("no org 'x' is joined on this PC")`.
  - The app's `create_dot(spec, org_id)`; UI `Dot.org_id: nullable(z.string())` and `commands.createDot(spec, orgId = null)`.

```rust
/// A dot's org is fixed when it is made (env vault spec §5.2): no change of the dot moves it.
#[tokio::test]
async fn no_change_of_a_dot_changes_its_org() {
    let (_d, store) = temp_store().await;
    let dot = store
        .create_dot(&spec("a"), Some("acme-eng"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(dot.org_id.as_deref(), Some("acme-eng"));
    let org = |d: Dot| d.org_id;
    let mut s = dot.spec.clone();
    s.name = "renamed".into();
    s.instructions = "New instructions".into();
    s.enabled = false;
    let updated = store.update_dot(&dot.id, &s).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(updated.spec.name, "renamed");
    assert_eq!(org(updated), dot.org_id);
    let enabled = store.set_dot_enabled(&dot.id, true).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(org(enabled), dot.org_id);
    assert_eq!(org(store.mark_dot_seen(&dot.id).await.unwrap()), dot.org_id);
    store.regenerate_webhook_token(&dot.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(org(store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap()), dot.org_id);
    // A Personal dot stays Personal.
    let personal = store.create_dot(&spec("b"), None).await.unwrap();
    let saved = store
        .update_dot(&personal.id, &personal.spec)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(org(saved), None);
}
```

```rust
/// Migration 0013 on a database Dots left at 0012: every stored dot is Personal, and no org is
/// joined (env vault spec §5.2).
#[tokio::test]
async fn migration_0013_leaves_every_stored_dot_in_personal() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = dir.path().join("dots.db");
    let opts = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
        .filename(&path)
        .create_if_missing(true);
    let pool = SqlitePool::connect_with(opts).await.unwrap();
    let mut before = sqlx::migrate!("./migrations");
    before.migrations = before
        .migrations
        .iter()
        .filter(|m| m.version < 13)
        .cloned()
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .into();
    before.run(&pool).await.unwrap();
    sqlx::query(
        "INSERT INTO dots (id, name, instructions, engine, model, workdir, workspace_mode, \
         webhook_token, policy, max_turns, timeout_secs, approval_wait_secs, \
         created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('D1', 'old', 'Do it.', 'claude', 'sonnet', \
         'C:/tmp/repo', 'worktree', '', ?, 40, 1800, 240, '2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z', \
         '2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z')",
    )
    .bind(serde_json::to_string(&Policy::preset(Preset::Sandboxed)).unwrap())
    .execute(&pool)
    .await
    .unwrap();
    pool.close().await;

    let store = Store::open(&path).await.unwrap();
    let old = store.get_dot("D1").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(old.org_id, None);
    assert_eq!(old.spec.name, "old");
    assert!(store.list_orgs().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    let made = store
        .create_dot(&spec("new"), Some("acme-eng"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(made.org_id.as_deref(), Some("acme-eng"));
    assert_eq!(store.get_dot("D1").await.unwrap(), old);
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_orgs_store_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The orgs joined on this PC, and the org each dot belongs to (env vault spec §5.2 and §6.4).

mod common;

use common::{spec, temp_store};
use dots_core::model::Dot;
use dots_core::store::Store;
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    BaoAuth, InfisicalSettings, OpenBaoSettings, OrgRow, SopsSettings, SourceSettings,
};
use dots_core::{Config, Error, Runtime};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use sqlx::sqlite::SqlitePool;
use tempfile::TempDir;

const KEY: &str = "RWQf6LRCGA9i53mlYecO4IzT51TGPpvWucNSCh1CBM0QTaLn73Y7GFO3";
const JOINED: &str = "2026-10-22T09:00:00.000Z";

fn openbao() -> SourceSettings {
    SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
        address: "https://bao.acme.example".into(),
        mount: "kv".into(),
        path: "teams/eng".into(),
        auth: BaoAuth::Userpass,
        auth_mount: Some("people".into()),
        namespace: Some("eng".into()),
    })
}

fn infisical() -> SourceSettings {
    SourceSettings::Infisical(InfisicalSettings {
        site_url: "https://app.infisical.com".into(),
        project_id: "6f1c0d7e".into(),
        environment: "prod".into(),
        secret_path: "/dots".into(),
    })
}

fn sops() -> SourceSettings {
    SourceSettings::Sops(SopsSettings {
        location: "https://files.acme.example/dots/env.sops.json".into(),
    })
}

fn org(id: &str, name: &str, source: SourceSettings) -> OrgRow {
    OrgRow {
        id: id.into(),
        name: name.into(),
        source,
        policy_key: KEY.into(),
        last_issued_at: None,
        last_fetch_at: None,
        joined_at: JOINED.into(),
    }
}

fn acme() -> OrgRow {
    org("acme-eng", "Acme Engineering", openbao())
}

async fn raw_pool(dir: &TempDir) -> SqlitePool {
    SqlitePool::connect(&format!(
        "sqlite://{}",
        dir.path().join("dots.db").display()
    ))
    .await
    .unwrap()
}

/// The `source` column of the org `id`, as stored.
async fn stored_source(dir: &TempDir, id: &str) -> Value {
    let pool = raw_pool(dir).await;
    let text: String = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT source FROM orgs WHERE id = ?")
        .bind(id)
        .fetch_one(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    pool.close().await;
    serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap()
}

fn names(orgs: &[OrgRow]) -> Vec<&str> {
    orgs.iter().map(|o| o.name.as_str()).collect()
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_of_each_kind_round_trips_with_its_source_as_json() {
    let (dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    assert_eq!(store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap(), None);
    let defaults = SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
        address: "https://bao.acme.example".into(),
        mount: "secret".into(),
        path: "ops".into(),
        auth: BaoAuth::Token,
        auth_mount: None,
        namespace: None,
    });
    let cases = [
        (
            org("acme-eng", "Acme Engineering", openbao()),
            json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://bao.acme.example", "mount": "kv",
                   "path": "teams/eng", "auth": "userpass", "auth_mount": "people",
                   "namespace": "eng"}),
        ),
        (
            org("acme-ops", "Acme Ops", defaults),
            json!({"kind": "openbao", "address": "https://bao.acme.example", "mount": "secret",
                   "path": "ops", "auth": "token"}),
        ),
        (
            org("beta", "Beta", infisical()),
            json!({"kind": "infisical", "site_url": "https://app.infisical.com",
                   "project_id": "6f1c0d7e", "environment": "prod", "secret_path": "/dots"}),
        ),
        (
            org("gamma-1", "Gamma", sops()),
            json!({"kind": "sops",
                   "location": "https://files.acme.example/dots/env.sops.json"}),
        ),
    ];
    for (row, json) in &cases {
        let mut row = row.clone();
        row.last_issued_at = Some("2026-10-22T08:00:00Z".into());
        row.last_fetch_at = Some("2026-10-22T09:00:05.000Z".into());
        store.add_org(&row).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.get_org(&row.id).await.unwrap().as_ref(), Some(&row));
        assert_eq!(&stored_source(&dir, &row.id).await, json, "{}", row.id);
    }
    assert_eq!(store.list_orgs().await.unwrap().len(), 4);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_id_already_joined_is_refused_and_the_first_row_stays() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    let again = org("acme-eng", "Acme Again", sops());
    let err = store.add_org(&again).await.unwrap_err();
    let want = "the org 'acme-eng' is already joined on this PC";
    assert!(matches!(&err, Error::Conflict(m) if m == want), "{err:?}");
    assert_eq!(store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap(), Some(acme()));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_id_that_breaks_the_rule_is_refused() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    for id in ["", "Acme", "acme_eng", "-acme", "../acme"] {
        let err = store
            .add_org(&org(id, "Acme", openbao()))
            .await
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Invalid(_)), "{id}: {err:?}");
    }
    assert!(store.list_orgs().await.unwrap().is_empty());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn orgs_are_listed_by_name_without_regard_to_case() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    assert!(store.list_orgs().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    for (id, name) in [
        ("z", "Zeta"),
        ("a2", "acme Design"),
        ("b", "beta"),
        ("a1", "Acme Engineering"),
        ("a0", "Acme Engineering"),
    ] {
        store.add_org(&org(id, name, sops())).await.unwrap();
    }
    let listed = store.list_orgs().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        names(&listed),
        [
            "acme Design",
            "Acme Engineering",
            "Acme Engineering",
            "beta",
            "Zeta"
        ]
    );
    // Two orgs of one name come by id.
    assert_eq!(listed[1].id, "a0");
    assert_eq!(listed[2].id, "a1");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn updating_the_settings_keeps_what_the_last_fetch_accepted() {
    let (dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    store
        .record_org_fetch(
            "acme-eng",
            "2026-10-22T09:00:05.000Z",
            "2026-10-22T08:00:00Z",
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let new_key = "RWTdnu2/6v8wB3XtPmO0VDUhd2DcHn1D5yN0FTcpUOFnnC6IbYTEQQts";
    store
        .update_org_settings("acme-eng", "Acme Eng", &infisical(), new_key)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let want = OrgRow {
        name: "Acme Eng".into(),
        source: infisical(),
        policy_key: new_key.into(),
        last_issued_at: Some("2026-10-22T08:00:00Z".into()),
        last_fetch_at: Some("2026-10-22T09:00:05.000Z".into()),
        ..acme()
    };
    assert_eq!(store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap(), Some(want));
    assert_eq!(stored_source(&dir, "acme-eng").await["kind"], "infisical");

    let err = store
        .update_org_settings("nope", "Nope", &sops(), KEY)
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        matches!(&err, Error::NotFound(m) if m == "no org 'nope' is joined on this PC"),
        "{err:?}"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_good_fetch_is_recorded_and_the_next_one_replaces_it() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    store.add_org(&org("beta", "Beta", sops())).await.unwrap();
    store
        .record_org_fetch(
            "acme-eng",
            "2026-10-22T09:00:05.000Z",
            "2026-10-22T08:00:00Z",
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let got = store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        got.last_fetch_at.as_deref(),
        Some("2026-10-22T09:00:05.000Z")
    );
    assert_eq!(got.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some("2026-10-22T08:00:00Z"));
    assert_eq!(got.joined_at, JOINED);

    store
        .record_org_fetch(
            "acme-eng",
            "2026-10-22T09:15:05.000Z",
            "2026-10-22T09:10:00Z",
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let got = store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        got.last_fetch_at.as_deref(),
        Some("2026-10-22T09:15:05.000Z")
    );
    assert_eq!(got.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some("2026-10-22T09:10:00Z"));
    // Another org's row is untouched.
    let beta = store.get_org("beta").await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!((beta.last_fetch_at, beta.last_issued_at), (None, None));

    let err = store
        .record_org_fetch("nope", "2026-10-22T09:15:05.000Z", "2026-10-22T09:10:00Z")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, Error::NotFound(_)), "{err:?}");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_removed_orgs_dots_keep_its_id_and_a_re_join_attaches_them_again() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    let dot = store
        .create_dot(&spec("deploy"), Some("acme-eng"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(dot.org_id.as_deref(), Some("acme-eng"));

    store.remove_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap(), None);
    assert!(store.list_orgs().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap(), dot);
    let err = store.remove_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        matches!(&err, Error::NotFound(m) if m == "no org 'acme-eng' is joined on this PC"),
        "{err:?}"
    );

    // Joining it again finds the dot where it was: the column has no foreign key.
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    let org_id = store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap().org_id.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(store.get_org(&org_id).await.unwrap(), Some(acme()));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_stored_source_that_no_longer_reads_is_an_error_naming_the_org() {
    let (dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    store.add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    store.add_org(&org("beta", "Beta", sops())).await.unwrap();
    let pool = raw_pool(&dir).await;
    sqlx::query("UPDATE orgs SET source = ? WHERE id = 'acme-eng'")
        .bind(json!({"kind": "dropbox", "folder": "x"}).to_string())
        .execute(&pool)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    pool.close().await;

    let err = store.get_org("acme-eng").await.unwrap_err();
    let text = err.to_string();
    assert!(
        text.starts_with("org 'acme-eng': its stored source settings are not readable: "),
        "{text}"
    );
    assert!(text.contains("dropbox"), "{text}");
    assert!(store.list_orgs().await.is_err());
    // The other org still reads.
    assert!(store.get_org("beta").await.unwrap().is_some());
}
```
