```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_runtime_stores_the_org_of_a_dot_in_a_joined_org() {
    let (_dir, rt) = runtime().await;
    rt.store().add_org(&acme()).await.unwrap();
    let dot = rt
        .create_dot(spec("deploy"), Some("acme-eng".into()))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(dot.org_id.as_deref(), Some("acme-eng"));

    let personal = rt.create_dot(spec("notes"), None).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(personal.org_id, None);
    rt.shutdown();
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_shows_its_org_as_org_id() {
    let (_dir, store) = temp_store().await;
    let in_org = store
        .create_dot(&spec("deploy"), Some("acme-eng"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let personal = store.create_dot(&spec("notes"), None).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&in_org).unwrap()["org_id"], "acme-eng");
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(&personal).unwrap()["org_id"],
        Value::Null
    );
    // A dot written without the field, as before plan B, reads as Personal.
    let mut old = serde_json::to_value(&personal).unwrap();
    old.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("org_id");
    let read: Dot = serde_json::from_value(old).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read, personal);
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/migrations/0013_orgs.sql`:**

```sql
-- Orgs (spec 2026-10-21-env-vault-design.md, sections 5.2 and 6).

-- Each org joined on this PC, with the settings of its join code and never a secret. `source` is
-- the `SourceSettings` JSON. The source's credentials are in Credential Manager, and the org's
-- entries are held in memory and in its offline copy. `last_issued_at` is the `issued_at` of the
-- last policy accepted, kept here so an older policy is refused even after the offline copy
-- expires (section 6.4). `last_fetch_at` is the last good fetch. Leaving the org deletes the row.
CREATE TABLE orgs (
    id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    source TEXT NOT NULL,
    policy_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_issued_at TEXT,
    last_fetch_at TEXT,
    joined_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- The org a dot belongs to, set when it is created and never changed. NULL is Personal. There is
-- no foreign key: a removed org's dots keep its id, and joining it again re-attaches them
-- (section 6.4).
ALTER TABLE dots ADD COLUMN org_id TEXT;
```

```rust
    /// on this PC; it is fixed from then on (env vault spec §5.2).
    pub async fn create_dot(&self, spec: DotSpec, org_id: Option<String>) -> Result<Dot> {
        if let Some(org) = &org_id {

                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "no org '{org}' is joined on this PC"
                )));

        self.sync_schedule(&dot, false).await?;
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/store/orgs.rs`:**

```rust
//! The orgs joined on this PC (env vault spec §5.2): their settings, never a secret.

use sqlx::sqlite::SqliteRow;
use sqlx::Row;

use super::Store;
use crate::vault::org::policy::plain_serde;
use crate::vault::org::{check_org_id, OrgRow, SourceSettings};
use crate::{Error, Result};

const ORG_COLUMNS: &str = "id, name, source, policy_key, last_issued_at, last_fetch_at, joined_at";

fn org_from_row(row: &SqliteRow) -> Result<OrgRow> {
    let id: String = row.try_get("id")?;
    let source = serde_json::from_str(&row.try_get::<String, _>("source")?).map_err(|e| {
        Error::Other(format!(
            "org '{id}': its stored source settings are not readable: {}",
            plain_serde(&e)
        ))
    })?;
    Ok(OrgRow {
        name: row.try_get("name")?,
        source,
        policy_key: row.try_get("policy_key")?,
        last_issued_at: row.try_get("last_issued_at")?,
        last_fetch_at: row.try_get("last_fetch_at")?,
        joined_at: row.try_get("joined_at")?,
        id,
    })
}

fn not_joined(id: &str) -> Error {
    Error::NotFound(format!("no org '{id}' is joined on this PC"))
}

impl Store {
    /// Adds a joined org. An id already joined is a `Conflict`.
    pub async fn add_org(&self, org: &OrgRow) -> Result<()> {
        check_org_id(&org.id)?;
        let added = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO orgs ({ORG_COLUMNS}) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)"
        ))
        .bind(&org.id)
        .bind(&org.name)
        .bind(serde_json::to_string(&org.source)?)
        .bind(&org.policy_key)
        .bind(&org.last_issued_at)
        .bind(&org.last_fetch_at)
        .bind(&org.joined_at)
        .execute(&self.pool)
        .await;
        if let Err(sqlx::Error::Database(db)) = &added {
            if db.is_unique_violation() {
                return Err(Error::Conflict(format!(
                    "the org '{}' is already joined on this PC",
                    org.id
                )));
            }
        }
        added?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The org `id`, if it is joined.
    pub async fn get_org(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<OrgRow>> {
        let row = sqlx::query(&format!("SELECT {ORG_COLUMNS} FROM orgs WHERE id = ?"))
            .bind(id)
            .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
            .await?;
        row.as_ref().map(org_from_row).transpose()
    }

    /// Every joined org, by name without regard to case.
    pub async fn list_orgs(&self) -> Result<Vec<OrgRow>> {
        let rows = sqlx::query(&format!(
            "SELECT {ORG_COLUMNS} FROM orgs ORDER BY name COLLATE NOCASE, id"
        ))
        .fetch_all(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        rows.iter().map(org_from_row).collect()
    }

    /// Replaces the org's settings with those of a new join code for the same id (§6.4,
    /// **Update**). What the last fetch accepted stays.
    pub async fn update_org_settings(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        name: &str,
        source: &SourceSettings,
        policy_key: &str,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let done = sqlx::query("UPDATE orgs SET name = ?, source = ?, policy_key = ? WHERE id = ?")
            .bind(name)
            .bind(serde_json::to_string(source)?)
            .bind(policy_key)
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&self.pool)
            .await?;
        if done.rows_affected() == 0 {
            return Err(not_joined(id));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Records a good fetch at `last_fetch_at`, whose policy was issued at `last_issued_at`.
    pub async fn record_org_fetch(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        last_fetch_at: &str,
        last_issued_at: &str,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let done =
            sqlx::query("UPDATE orgs SET last_fetch_at = ?, last_issued_at = ? WHERE id = ?")
                .bind(last_fetch_at)
                .bind(last_issued_at)
                .bind(id)
                .execute(&self.pool)
                .await?;
        if done.rows_affected() == 0 {
            return Err(not_joined(id));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Removes the org's row. Its dots keep their `org_id` (§6.4).
    pub async fn remove_org(&self, id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        let done = sqlx::query("DELETE FROM orgs WHERE id = ?")
            .bind(id)
            .execute(&self.pool)
            .await?;
        if done.rows_affected() == 0 {
            return Err(not_joined(id));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

```rust
//! its join code and what the last good fetch accepted. It holds no secrets.

use super::join::SourceSettings;

/// One row of `orgs`. `store/orgs.rs` reads and writes it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OrgRow {
    /// The join code's `org_id`; `join::check_org_id` holds for it.

    /// When the last good fetch was, RFC 3339 UTC. `None` before the first.
    pub last_fetch_at: Option<String>,
    /// When the org was joined, RFC 3339 UTC.
    pub joined_at: String,
}
```

### Task 4: The org's offline copy, encrypted with DPAPI

Spec §5.2 and §6.4: the last good fetch kept on disk, protected for the signed-in Windows user with the org id as entropy, written by temp file and rename.

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/offline.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/Cargo.toml` (`zeroize` gains `serde`; `windows-sys` gains `Win32_Security_Cryptography`), `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`
- Create: `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_offline_test.rs`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: Task 1's `check_org_id`.
- Produces, re-exported from `vault::org`:
  - `OFFLINE_DIR = "vault"`; `Protector` (`protect(data, entropy) -> Result<Vec<u8>>`, `unprotect(data, entropy) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>`); `Dpapi` (Windows), `TestProtector` (tests only: a `DOTSTEST` prefix, the entropy's hash, the data XORed), `NoProtector` (refuses: "no offline copy on this platform"); `os_protector() -> Arc<dyn Protector>`.
  - `OfflineCopy { fetched_at, entries: BTreeMap<String, Zeroizing<String>>, policy }`, JSON `{"v":1,…}`, `Debug` without values.
  - `offline_path(dir, org_id) -> Result<PathBuf>` (`dir/<org_id>.bin`), `write_offline(dir, protector, org_id, &copy) -> Result<()>`, `read_offline(dir, protector, org_id) -> Result<Option<OfflineCopy>>`, `delete_offline(dir, org_id) -> Result<()>` (also removes that org's temp files). They block: async callers use `spawn_blocking`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_offline_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The org's offline copy (env vault spec §5.2 and §6.4): protected on disk, one org's file never
//! opening as another's, and a failed write leaving the old copy.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::Path;

use dots_core::vault::org::{
    delete_offline, offline_path, read_offline, write_offline, NoProtector, OfflineCopy, Protector,
    TestProtector, OFFLINE_DIR,
};
use dots_core::{Error, Result};
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

const NAME: &str = "OFFLINE_NAME_4b1e";
const VALUE: &str = "offline-value-7f3a9c";
const FETCHED: &str = "2026-10-23T09:00:00.000Z";

fn copy(value: &str) -> OfflineCopy {
    let mut entries = BTreeMap::new();
    entries.insert(NAME.to_string(), Zeroizing::new(value.to_string()));
    entries.insert(
        "REGION".to_string(),
        Zeroizing::new("eu-west-1".to_string()),
    );
    OfflineCopy {
        fetched_at: FETCHED.into(),
        entries,
        policy: r#"{"v":1,"policy":"{}","signature":"sig"}"#.into(),
    }
}

fn contains(haystack: &[u8], needle: &str) -> bool {
    haystack
        .windows(needle.len())
        .any(|w| w == needle.as_bytes())
}

/// The names of the files in `dir`, sorted.
fn files(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(dir)
        .unwrap()
        .map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

fn message(e: Error) -> String {
    e.to_string()
}

/// Fails every call, as a protector that cannot reach DPAPI would.
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Failing;

impl Protector for Failing {
    fn protect(&self, _data: &[u8], _entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        Err(Error::Other("protector down".into()))
    }

    fn unprotect(&self, _data: &[u8], _entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>> {
        Err(Error::Other("protector down".into()))
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_copy_round_trips_under_the_data_folders_vault() {
    let data = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let dir = data.path().join(OFFLINE_DIR);
    write_offline(&dir, &TestProtector, "acme-eng", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        offline_path(&dir, "acme-eng").unwrap(),
        data.path().join("vault").join("acme-eng.bin")
    );
    let read = read_offline(&dir, &TestProtector, "acme-eng").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read, Some(copy(VALUE)));
    // No temp file is left beside it.
    assert_eq!(files(&dir), vec!["acme-eng.bin".to_string()]);
}

#[test]
fn a_new_copy_replaces_the_old_one() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy("first")).unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy("second")).unwrap();
    let read = read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read, Some(copy("second")));
    assert_eq!(files(dir.path()), vec!["acme.bin".to_string()]);
}

#[test]
fn the_file_holds_neither_the_value_nor_the_name() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    let bytes = std::fs::read(offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert!(bytes.starts_with(b"DOTSTEST"));
    assert!(!contains(&bytes, VALUE));
    assert!(!contains(&bytes, NAME));
    assert!(!contains(&bytes, "eu-west-1"));
}

#[test]
fn another_orgs_entropy_does_not_open_the_file() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    let path = offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
    assert!(TestProtector.unprotect(&bytes, b"beta").is_err());
    assert!(TestProtector.unprotect(&bytes, b"acme").is_ok());

    // A file renamed to another org's name is unprotected with that org's id, and fails.
    std::fs::rename(&path, offline_path(dir.path(), "beta").unwrap()).unwrap();
    let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "beta").unwrap_err());
    assert!(err.contains("org 'beta'"), "{err}");
    assert!(err.contains("other entropy"), "{err}");
    assert!(!err.contains(VALUE), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn a_missing_copy_reads_none_and_deletes_quietly() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap(),
        None
    );
    delete_offline(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
    // A data folder without the vault folder yet is the same.
    let absent = dir.path().join(OFFLINE_DIR);
    assert_eq!(read_offline(&absent, &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap(), None);
    delete_offline(&absent, "acme").unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn delete_removes_the_copy_and_its_temp_files_only() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme-eng", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    // Temp files a crash left behind.
    std::fs::write(dir.path().join(".acme.01JBXYZ.tmp"), b"x").unwrap();
    std::fs::write(dir.path().join(".acme-eng.01JBXYZ.tmp"), b"x").unwrap();
    delete_offline(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap(),
        None
    );
    assert_eq!(
        files(dir.path()),
        vec![
            ".acme-eng.01JBXYZ.tmp".to_string(),
            "acme-eng.bin".to_string()
        ]
    );
    delete_offline(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn a_corrupt_copy_is_an_error_naming_the_org() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();

    std::fs::write(&path, b"not protected at all").unwrap();
    let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap_err());
    assert!(err.contains("org 'acme'"), "{err}");

    // Protected, but not JSON.
    std::fs::write(&path, TestProtector.protect(b"{\"v\":1,", b"acme").unwrap()).unwrap();
    let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap_err());
    assert!(err.contains("org 'acme'"), "{err}");
    assert!(err.contains("damaged"), "{err}");

    // An unknown field.
    let json =
        format!(r#"{{"v":1,"fetched_at":"{FETCHED}","entries":{{}},"policy":"p","extra":true}}"#);
    std::fs::write(
        &path,
        TestProtector.protect(json.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").is_err());

    // A time that is not RFC 3339.
    let json = r#"{"v":1,"fetched_at":"yesterday","entries":{},"policy":"p"}"#;
    std::fs::write(
        &path,
        TestProtector.protect(json.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap_err());
    assert!(err.contains("RFC 3339"), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn a_damaged_copy_never_quotes_a_value_in_its_error() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
    for json in [
        format!(r#"{{"v":"{VALUE}"}}"#),
        format!(r#"{{"v":1,"fetched_at":"{FETCHED}","entries":{{"{VALUE}":5}},"policy":"p"}}"#),
        format!(r#"{{"v":1,"fetched_at":"{FETCHED}","entries":["{VALUE}"],"policy":"p"}}"#),
    ] {
        std::fs::write(
            &path,
            TestProtector.protect(json.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap_err());
        assert!(err.contains("org 'acme'"), "{err}");
        assert!(!err.contains(VALUE), "{err}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn an_unknown_format_version_is_refused() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap();
    for json in [
        format!(r#"{{"v":2,"fetched_at":"{FETCHED}","entries":{{}},"policy":"p"}}"#),
        r#"{"v":2,"shape":"new"}"#.to_string(),
    ] {
        std::fs::write(
            &path,
            TestProtector.protect(json.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap_err());
        assert!(err.contains("org 'acme'"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("format v2"), "{err}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_json_form_carries_its_version() {
    let json = serde_json::to_value(copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["v"], 1);
    assert_eq!(json["fetched_at"], FETCHED);
    assert_eq!(json["entries"][NAME], VALUE);
    let back: OfflineCopy = serde_json::from_value(json.clone()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(back, copy(VALUE));
    let mut later = json;
    later["v"] = 2.into();
    assert!(serde_json::from_value::<OfflineCopy>(later).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn a_failed_write_leaves_the_old_copy() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy("old-value")).unwrap();
    let err = write_offline(dir.path(), &Failing, "acme", &copy("new-value")).unwrap_err();
    assert!(message(err).contains("protector down"));
    let read = read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read, Some(copy("old-value")));
    assert_eq!(files(dir.path()), vec!["acme.bin".to_string()]);
}

#[test]
fn a_failed_rename_leaves_no_temp_file() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    // A folder where the copy goes: the rename over it fails.
    std::fs::create_dir(offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap()).unwrap();
    let err = write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap_err();
    assert!(message(err).contains("org 'acme'"));
    assert_eq!(files(dir.path()), vec!["acme.bin".to_string()]);
    assert!(offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap().is_dir());
}

#[test]
fn a_copy_with_a_bad_time_is_not_written() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let mut bad = copy(VALUE);
    bad.fetched_at = "yesterday".into();
    let err = write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme", &bad).unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Invalid(_)), "{err}");
    assert!(files(dir.path()).is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn a_bad_org_id_is_refused_before_any_file_is_touched() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    for id in ["../x", "Acme", "", "a/b", "acme.bin"] {
        assert!(
            matches!(offline_path(dir.path(), id), Err(Error::Invalid(_))),
            "{id:?}"
        );
        assert!(write_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, id, &copy(VALUE)).is_err());
        assert!(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, id).is_err());
        assert!(delete_offline(dir.path(), id).is_err());
    }
    assert!(files(dir.path()).is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn debug_shows_the_time_and_names_but_no_value() {
    let shown = format!("{:?}", copy(VALUE));
    assert!(shown.contains(FETCHED), "{shown}");
    assert!(shown.contains(NAME), "{shown}");
    assert!(!shown.contains(VALUE), "{shown}");
    assert!(!shown.contains("eu-west-1"), "{shown}");
}

#[test]
fn the_test_protector_refuses_data_it_did_not_protect() {
    assert!(TestProtector.unprotect(b"plain text", b"acme").is_err());
    assert!(TestProtector.unprotect(b"DOTSTEST", b"acme").is_err());
    let sealed = TestProtector.protect(VALUE.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap();
    assert!(!contains(&sealed, VALUE));
    let plain = TestProtector.unprotect(&sealed, b"acme").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(plain.as_slice(), VALUE.as_bytes());
}

#[test]
fn no_protector_writes_nothing() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let vault = dir.path().join(OFFLINE_DIR);
    let err = write_offline(&vault, &NoProtector, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap_err();
    assert!(message(err).contains("no offline copy on this platform"));
    assert!(!vault.exists());
    assert!(NoProtector.unprotect(b"x", b"acme").is_err());
}

#[cfg(windows)]
mod dpapi {
    use super::*;
    use dots_core::vault::org::{os_protector, Dpapi};

    #[test]
    fn the_os_protector_is_dpapi() {
        assert_eq!(format!("{:?}", os_protector()), "Dpapi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_copy_round_trips_under_this_user() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_offline(dir.path(), &Dpapi, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
        let bytes = std::fs::read(offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(!contains(&bytes, VALUE));
        assert!(!contains(&bytes, NAME));
        assert_eq!(
            read_offline(dir.path(), &Dpapi, "acme").unwrap(),
            Some(copy(VALUE))
        );
        // The test protector cannot read DPAPI's file.
        assert!(read_offline(dir.path(), &TestProtector, "acme").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn protected_bytes_hold_no_value_and_open_only_with_their_entropy() {
        let sealed = Dpapi.protect(VALUE.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap();
        assert!(!contains(&sealed, VALUE));
        let plain = Dpapi.unprotect(&sealed, b"acme").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(plain.as_slice(), VALUE.as_bytes());

        let err = message(Dpapi.unprotect(&sealed, b"beta").unwrap_err());
        assert!(err.starts_with("DPAPI: unprotecting data failed"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("with other entropy"), "{err}");
        assert!(Dpapi.unprotect(&sealed, b"").is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_renamed_dpapi_file_does_not_open_as_another_org() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write_offline(dir.path(), &Dpapi, "acme", &copy(VALUE)).unwrap();
        std::fs::rename(
            offline_path(dir.path(), "acme").unwrap(),
            offline_path(dir.path(), "beta").unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let err = message(read_offline(dir.path(), &Dpapi, "beta").unwrap_err());
        assert!(err.contains("org 'beta'"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("DPAPI"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn data_dpapi_did_not_protect_is_an_error_not_a_panic() {
        assert!(Dpapi.unprotect(b"not a DPAPI blob", b"acme").is_err());
        assert!(Dpapi.unprotect(b"", b"acme").is_err());
        let sealed = Dpapi.protect(VALUE.as_bytes(), b"acme").unwrap();
        assert!(Dpapi
            .unprotect(&sealed[..sealed.len() / 2], b"acme")
            .is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_data_round_trips() {
        let sealed = Dpapi.protect(b"", b"acme").unwrap();
        assert!(Dpapi.unprotect(&sealed, b"acme").unwrap().is_empty());
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/offline.rs`:**

```rust
//! The org's offline copy (env vault spec §5.2 and §6.4): the last fetched entries and the signed
//! policy, kept so an org still resolves while its source is unreachable, until the policy's
//! `offline_hours` run out. The copy is JSON, protected with DPAPI for the signed-in Windows user
//! with the org id as entropy, and written to `data_dir/vault/<org_id>.bin`. Nothing in it is
//! ever on disk in the clear (spec §2).

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::io::Write as _;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

use super::check_org_id;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The folder of the offline copies, under the data folder.
pub const OFFLINE_DIR: &str = "vault";

/// The offline copy's format. A copy of another version is refused, never guessed at.
const FORMAT: u32 = 1;

const RENAME_ATTEMPTS: u32 = 5;
const RENAME_PAUSE: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_millis(100);

/// Encrypts bytes so that only this Windows user on this PC can read them back. `entropy` must be
/// the same on both sides: the offline copy passes its org id, so one org's file never opens as
/// another's. Its `Debug` never shows data.
pub trait Protector: Send + Sync + std::fmt::Debug {
    /// `data`, encrypted.
    fn protect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>>;
    /// The bytes `protect` was given. Data from another user, another entropy or another
    /// protector is an error.
    fn unprotect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>>;
}

/// DPAPI (`CryptProtectData`), in the signed-in user's scope, never asking for a prompt.
#[cfg(windows)]
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Dpapi;

#[cfg(windows)]
mod dpapi {
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{LocalFree, ERROR_INVALID_DATA};
    use windows_sys::Win32::Security::Cryptography::{
        CryptProtectData, CryptUnprotectData, CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB,
    };
    use zeroize::{Zeroize, Zeroizing};

    use super::{Dpapi, Protector};
    use crate::{Error, Result};

    /// A blob that borrows `bytes`. DPAPI only reads an input blob.
    fn blob(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB> {
        let len = u32::try_from(bytes.len())
            .map_err(|_| Error::Invalid("DPAPI protects at most 4 GiB at a time".into()))?;
        Ok(CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB {
            cbData: len,
            pbData: bytes.as_ptr() as *mut u8,
        })
    }

    fn empty() -> CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB {
        CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB {
            cbData: 0,
            pbData: std::ptr::null_mut(),
        }
    }

    fn failed(what: &str) -> Error {
        let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();
        let why = if err.raw_os_error() == Some(ERROR_INVALID_DATA as i32) {
            " (it was protected by another Windows user, with other entropy, or is damaged)"
        } else {
            ""
        };
        Error::Other(format!("DPAPI: {what} failed: {err}{why}"))
    }

    /// Copies a blob DPAPI returned, wipes it and frees it.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// `out` must be a blob a successful DPAPI call filled: `pbData` is null or holds `cbData`
    /// bytes allocated with `LocalAlloc`, owned by the caller.
    unsafe fn take(out: CRYPT_INTEGER_BLOB) -> Vec<u8> {
        if out.pbData.is_null() {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let bytes = std::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(out.pbData, out.cbData as usize);
        let copy = bytes.to_vec();
        bytes.zeroize();
        LocalFree(out.pbData.cast());
        copy
    }

    impl Protector for Dpapi {
        fn protect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
            let input = blob(data)?;
            let entropy = blob(entropy)?;
            let mut out = empty();
            // SAFETY: `input` and `entropy` borrow slices that live until the call ends, and
            // `out` receives a buffer that `take` frees.
            let ok = unsafe {
                CryptProtectData(
                    &input,
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    &entropy,
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
                    &mut out,
                )
            };
            if ok == 0 {
                return Err(failed("protecting data"));
            }
            // SAFETY: the call succeeded, so `out` is a blob it allocated.
            Ok(unsafe { take(out) })
        }

        fn unprotect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>> {
            let input = blob(data)?;
            let entropy = blob(entropy)?;
            let mut out = empty();
            // SAFETY: as in `protect`. No description is asked for, so none needs freeing.
            let ok = unsafe {
                CryptUnprotectData(
                    &input,
                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
                    &entropy,
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    std::ptr::null(),
                    CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN,
                    &mut out,
                )
            };
            if ok == 0 {
                return Err(failed("unprotecting data"));
            }
            // SAFETY: the call succeeded, so `out` is a blob it allocated. `take` wipes it.
            Ok(Zeroizing::new(unsafe { take(out) }))
        }
    }
}

/// For tests only: it hides nothing from anyone. It XORs with a fixed key behind a `DOTSTEST`
/// prefix and the SHA-256 of the entropy, so a test can check that a file holds no plain value
/// and that one org's copy does not open as another's, as under DPAPI.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct TestProtector;

const TEST_MAGIC: &[u8] = b"DOTSTEST";
const TEST_KEY: &[u8] = b"dots-test-protector-key";

fn xor(data: &[u8]) -> impl Iterator<Item = u8> + '_ {
    data.iter().zip(TEST_KEY.iter().cycle()).map(|(b, k)| b ^ k)
}

impl Protector for TestProtector {
    fn protect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(TEST_MAGIC.len() + 32 + data.len());
        out.extend_from_slice(TEST_MAGIC);
        out.extend_from_slice(&Sha256::digest(entropy));
        out.extend(xor(data));
        Ok(out)
    }

    fn unprotect(&self, data: &[u8], entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>> {
        let rest = data
            .strip_prefix(TEST_MAGIC)
            .filter(|rest| rest.len() >= 32)
            .ok_or_else(|| Error::Other("test protector: this is not its data".into()))?;
        let (hash, body) = rest.split_at(32);
        if hash != Sha256::digest(entropy).as_slice() {
            return Err(Error::Other(
                "test protector: the data was protected with other entropy".into(),
            ));
        }
        let mut plain = Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(body.len()));
        plain.extend(xor(body));
        Ok(plain)
    }
}

/// Refuses everything, on a system without DPAPI: there is no offline copy rather than one in
/// the clear.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct NoProtector;

impl NoProtector {
    fn refuse<T>() -> Result<T> {
        Err(Error::Other("no offline copy on this platform".into()))
    }
}

impl Protector for NoProtector {
    fn protect(&self, _data: &[u8], _entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
        NoProtector::refuse()
    }

    fn unprotect(&self, _data: &[u8], _entropy: &[u8]) -> Result<Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>> {
        NoProtector::refuse()
    }
}

/// The protector of the signed-in user: DPAPI on Windows, none elsewhere (Dots ships on
/// Windows), so an offline copy is never written in the clear.
pub fn os_protector() -> Arc<dyn Protector> {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        Arc::new(Dpapi)
    }
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    {
        tracing::warn!("no DPAPI on this system: orgs keep no offline copy");
        Arc::new(NoProtector)
    }
}

/// An org's last good fetch, as kept on disk. Its JSON carries `"v": 1`, and another version is
/// refused. Its `Debug` shows only `fetched_at` and the names.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
#[serde(try_from = "Stored")]
pub struct OfflineCopy {
    /// When the entries were fetched, RFC 3339. The copy expires `offline_hours` after it.
    pub fetched_at: String,
    /// The org's entries by name, plain values and secrets alike.
    pub entries: BTreeMap<String, Zeroizing<String>>,
    /// The signed policy text the entries came with.
    pub policy: String,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for OfflineCopy {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("OfflineCopy")
            .field("fetched_at", &self.fetched_at)
            .field("names", &self.entries.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>())
            .finish()
    }
}

/// The JSON form, read.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Stored {
    v: u32,
    fetched_at: String,
    entries: BTreeMap<String, Zeroizing<String>>,
    policy: String,
}

/// The JSON form, written.
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct StoredRef<'a> {
    v: u32,
    fetched_at: &'a str,
    entries: &'a BTreeMap<String, Zeroizing<String>>,
    policy: &'a str,
}

/// Only the version, read first so a copy of a later format says so rather than naming a field.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Head {
    v: u32,
}

fn check_version(v: u32) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
    if v != FORMAT {
        return Err(format!("it has format v{v}, and this Dots reads v{FORMAT}"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl OfflineCopy {
    fn check(&self) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
        chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&self.fetched_at)
            .map(|_| ())
            .map_err(|_| "its fetched_at is not an RFC 3339 time".to_string())
    }
}

impl TryFrom<Stored> for OfflineCopy {
    type Error = String;

    fn try_from(stored: Stored) -> std::result::Result<OfflineCopy, String> {
        check_version(stored.v)?;
        let copy = OfflineCopy {
            fetched_at: stored.fetched_at,
            entries: stored.entries,
            policy: stored.policy,
        };
        copy.check()?;
        Ok(copy)
    }
}

impl Serialize for OfflineCopy {
    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, s: S) -> std::result::Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        StoredRef {
            v: FORMAT,
            fetched_at: &self.fetched_at,
            entries: &self.entries,
            policy: &self.policy,
        }
        .serialize(s)
    }
}

/// Where the offline copy of `org_id` lives in `dir`: `dir/<org_id>.bin`. The id must be a valid
/// org id, since it names a file.
pub fn offline_path(dir: &Path, org_id: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
    check_org_id(org_id)?;
    Ok(dir.join(format!("{org_id}.bin")))
}

/// Counts the bytes written to it, to size the plain buffer once: a buffer that grows would leave
/// copies of the values behind in memory it gave back.
struct Count(usize);

impl std::io::Write for Count {
    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
        self.0 += buf.len();
        Ok(buf.len())
    }

    fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Saves `copy` as the offline copy of `org_id` in `dir`, replacing the one there. The file is
/// written beside the target and renamed over it, so a write that fails leaves the old copy.
pub fn write_offline(
    dir: &Path,
    protector: &dyn Protector,
    org_id: &str,
    copy: &OfflineCopy,
) -> Result<()> {
    let path = offline_path(dir, org_id)?;
    copy.check()
        .map_err(|why| Error::Invalid(format!("org '{org_id}': an offline copy: {why}")))?;
    let mut count = Count(0);
    serde_json::to_writer(&mut count, copy)?;
    let mut plain = Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(count.0));
    serde_json::to_writer(&mut *plain, copy)?;
    let sealed = protector.protect(&plain, org_id.as_bytes())?;
    drop(plain);

    let failed = |e: std::io::Error| {
        Error::Other(format!(
            "org '{org_id}': saving its offline copy failed: {e}"
        ))
    };
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(failed)?;
    let tmp = dir.join(format!(".{org_id}.{}.tmp", crate::util::new_id()));
    let written = write_synced(&tmp, &sealed).and_then(|()| rename(&tmp, &path));
    if let Err(e) = written {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&tmp);
        return Err(failed(e));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_synced(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut file = std::fs::File::create_new(path)?;
    file.write_all(bytes)?;
    file.sync_all()
}

/// Renames `from` over `to`. A file just written may be held for a moment (antivirus, the
/// indexer), and Windows then refuses the rename: try again a few times.
fn rename(from: &Path, to: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let mut attempt = 1;
    loop {
        match std::fs::rename(from, to) {
            Err(_) if attempt < RENAME_ATTEMPTS => {
                attempt += 1;
                std::thread::sleep(RENAME_PAUSE);
            }
            other => return other,
        }
    }
}

/// The offline copy of `org_id` in `dir`, or `None` if there is none. A copy that does not
/// unprotect or parse is an error naming the org; the error never holds a value.
pub fn read_offline(
    dir: &Path,
    protector: &dyn Protector,
    org_id: &str,
) -> Result<Option<OfflineCopy>> {
    let path = offline_path(dir, org_id)?;
    let sealed = match std::fs::read(&path) {
        Ok(bytes) => bytes,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
        Err(e) => {
            return Err(Error::Other(format!(
                "org '{org_id}': reading its offline copy failed: {e}"
            )))
        }
    };
    let unreadable = |why: String| {
        Error::Other(format!(
            "org '{org_id}': its offline copy cannot be read: {why}"
        ))
    };
    let plain = protector
        .unprotect(&sealed, org_id.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|e| unreadable(e.to_string()))?;
    // serde_json's messages may quote the text they choke on, which could be a value: name only
    // the place.
    let damaged = |e: serde_json::Error| {
        unreadable(format!(
            "it is damaged (line {}, column {})",
            e.line(),
            e.column()
        ))
    };
    let head: Head = serde_json::from_slice(&plain).map_err(damaged)?;
    check_version(head.v).map_err(unreadable)?;
    let stored: Stored = serde_json::from_slice(&plain).map_err(damaged)?;
    OfflineCopy::try_from(stored).map(Some).map_err(unreadable)
}

/// Deletes the offline copy of `org_id` in `dir`, with any temp file a crash left behind. A copy
/// that is not there is not an error.
pub fn delete_offline(dir: &Path, org_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let path = offline_path(dir, org_id)?;
    let failed = |e: std::io::Error| {
        Error::Other(format!(
            "org '{org_id}': deleting its offline copy failed: {e}"
        ))
    };
    match std::fs::remove_file(&path) {
        Err(e) if e.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Err(failed(e)),
        _ => {}
    }
    let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
        Ok(entries) => entries,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
        Err(e) => return Err(failed(e)),
    };
    // An org id has no '.', so `.acme.` never matches a temp file of `acme-eng`.
    let prefix = format!(".{org_id}.");
    for entry in entries {
        let name = entry.map_err(failed)?.file_name();
        let name = name.to_string_lossy();
        if name.starts_with(&prefix) && name.ends_with(".tmp") {
            match std::fs::remove_file(dir.join(&*name)) {
                Err(e) if e.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Err(failed(e)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

### Task 5: The source trait, and reading an org from OpenBao or Vault

Spec §6.2 and §6.1: one `Source` trait and the rules every adapter shares, the sign-in details kept in the secret store, and the OpenBao (KV v2) adapter with token, userpass and ldap sign-in.

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/openbao.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/Cargo.toml` (reqwest's TLS features), `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`
- Create: `crates/dots-core/tests/common/fake_openbao.rs`, `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_openbao_test.rs`; modify `crates/dots-core/tests/common/mod.rs`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: Task 1's `SourceSettings`, `OpenBaoSettings`; plan A's `SecretStore`, `MAX_SECRET_BYTES`, `check_variable_name`.

```rust
//! A fake OpenBao (or Vault) server for the org source tests, on a port of its own: KV v2 reads,
//! `userpass` and `ldap` login, and a token's `lookup-self` and `renew-self`, with the shapes and
//! errors `research.md` §1 gives. It is programmed through `FakeOpenBao` and records every
//! request it sees. It stops when dropped.

use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use axum::body::Bytes;
use axum::extract::State;
use axum::http::{HeaderMap, Method, StatusCode, Uri};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use axum::{Json, Router};
use serde_json::{json, Value};

/// What the next KV reads answer instead of the data.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Failure {
    /// This status, with `{"errors":[…]}`. A 3xx also gets a `Location` to `/v1/elsewhere`.
    Status(u16),
    /// A 200 whose body is not JSON.
    NotJson,
    /// No answer for a minute, so the client's timeout fires first.
    Hang,
}

/// One request the fake saw.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Seen {
    pub method: String,
    /// The path as sent, still percent-encoded.
    pub path: String,
    /// `X-Vault-Token`.
    pub token: Option<String>,
    /// `X-Vault-Namespace`.
    pub namespace: Option<String>,
    /// The body, when it was JSON.
    pub body: Option<Value>,
}

struct User {
    password: String,
    lease_seconds: u64,
}

#[derive(Default)]
struct Fake {
    /// KV v2 secrets by `<mount>/data/<path>`, decoded: the object of `data.data`.
    kv: HashMap<String, Value>,
    /// Tokens it accepts, and whether each is renewable.
    tokens: HashMap<String, bool>,
    /// Users by `(auth mount, username)`.
    users: HashMap<(String, String), User>,
    failures: VecDeque<Failure>,
    refuse_renewals: bool,
    issued: usize,
    seen: Vec<Seen>,
}

/// The fake server.
pub struct FakeOpenBao {
    address: String,
    state: Arc<Mutex<Fake>>,
    task: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
}

impl Drop for FakeOpenBao {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.task.abort();
    }
}

impl FakeOpenBao {
    /// Starts the fake on `127.0.0.1` and a free port. It holds nothing and accepts no token.
    pub async fn start() -> FakeOpenBao {
        let state = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Fake::default()));
        let app = Router::new().fallback(handle).with_state(state.clone());
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let address = format!("http://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
        });
        FakeOpenBao {
            address,
            state,
            task,
        }
    }

    /// `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, the join code's `address`.
    pub fn address(&self) -> String {
        self.address.clone()
    }

    fn fake(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Fake> {
        self.state.lock().unwrap()
    }

    /// Writes the KV v2 secret `<mount>/<path>`: `data` is the object `data.data` reads.
    pub fn put(&self, mount: &str, path: &str, data: Value) {
        self.fake().kv.insert(format!("{mount}/data/{path}"), data);
    }

    /// Writes the org's entries, at `<mount>/<path>/env`.
    pub fn put_env(&self, mount: &str, path: &str, entries: Value) {
        self.put(mount, &format!("{path}/env"), entries);
    }

    /// Writes the org's signed policy text, as key `DOTS_POLICY` of `<mount>/<path>/policy`.
    pub fn put_policy(&self, mount: &str, path: &str, signed: &str) {
        self.put(
            mount,
            &format!("{path}/policy"),
            json!({ "DOTS_POLICY": signed }),
        );
    }

    /// Deletes the KV v2 secret `<mount>/<path>`: reading it is a 404.
    pub fn remove(&self, mount: &str, path: &str) {
        self.fake().kv.remove(&format!("{mount}/data/{path}"));
    }

    /// Accepts `token` from now on. `lookup-self` says whether it is `renewable`.
    pub fn allow_token(&self, token: &str, renewable: bool) {
        self.fake().tokens.insert(token.to_string(), renewable);
    }

    /// Stops accepting `token`, as a revoked or expired one: every call with it is a 403.
    pub fn revoke_token(&self, token: &str) {
        self.fake().tokens.remove(token);
    }

    /// Stops accepting every token, those logins gave included.
    pub fn revoke_all_tokens(&self) {
        self.fake().tokens.clear();
    }

    /// Adds a user to the `userpass` or `ldap` mount `auth_mount`. A login gives a new token
    /// with a lease of `lease_seconds` (0: it does not expire), renewable if the lease is not 0.
    pub fn add_user(&self, auth_mount: &str, username: &str, password: &str, lease_seconds: u64) {
        self.fake().users.insert(
            (auth_mount.to_string(), username.to_string()),
            User {
                password: password.to_string(),
                lease_seconds,
            },
        );
    }

    /// The next `count` KV reads answer `failure`. Logins and token calls are not affected.
    pub fn fail_next(&self, failure: Failure, count: usize) {
        let mut fake = self.fake();
        for _ in 0..count {
            fake.failures.push_back(failure);
        }
    }

    /// Makes `renew-self` fail with a 500 even for a renewable token.
    pub fn refuse_renewals(&self) {
        self.fake().refuse_renewals = true;
    }

    /// Every request so far, oldest first.
    pub fn requests(&self) -> Vec<Seen> {
        self.fake().seen.clone()
    }

    /// Every request so far as `METHOD /path`, oldest first.
    pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.requests()
            .iter()
            .map(|s| format!("{} {}", s.method, s.path))
            .collect()
    }

    /// How many requests went to `path` (as sent), with any method.
    pub fn count(&self, path: &str) -> usize {
        self.requests().iter().filter(|s| s.path == path).count()
    }

    /// How many logins were tried, on any mount.
    pub fn logins(&self) -> usize {
        self.requests()
            .iter()
            .filter(|s| s.path.starts_with("/v1/auth/") && s.path.contains("/login/"))
            .count()
    }

    /// How many `renew-self` calls were made.
    pub fn renewals(&self) -> usize {
        self.count("/v1/auth/token/renew-self")
    }

    /// Forgets the requests seen so far.
    pub fn clear_requests(&self) {
        self.fake().seen.clear();
    }
}

fn header(headers: &HeaderMap, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    headers
        .get(name)
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
        .map(str::to_string)
}

/// `%XX` decoded, as a server reads a path.
fn decode(path: &str) -> String {
    let bytes = path.as_bytes();
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let hex = bytes
            .get(i + 1..i + 3)
            .and_then(|h| std::str::from_utf8(h).ok())
            .and_then(|h| u8::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok());
        match (bytes[i], hex) {
            (b'%', Some(b)) => {
                out.push(b);
                i += 3;
            }
            (b, _) => {
                out.push(b);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()
}

fn errors(status: u16, messages: &[&str]) -> Response {
    let status = StatusCode::from_u16(status).unwrap();
    (status, Json(json!({ "errors": messages }))).into_response()
}

fn denied() -> Response {
    errors(403, &["permission denied"])
}

/// The envelope every answer has, around `data` and `auth`.
fn envelope(data: Value, auth: Value) -> Response {
    Json(json!({
        "request_id": "8d3c2a6e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
        "lease_id": "",
        "renewable": false,
        "lease_duration": 0,
        "data": data,
        "wrap_info": null,
        "warnings": null,
        "auth": auth,
    }))
    .into_response()
}

fn auth_answer(token: &str, username: &str, lease_seconds: u64) -> Value {
    json!({
        "client_token": token,
        "accessor": "acc-0001",
        "policies": ["default", "dots-read"],
        "token_policies": ["default", "dots-read"],
        "metadata": { "username": username },
        "lease_duration": lease_seconds,
        "renewable": lease_seconds > 0,
        "entity_id": "ent-0001",
        "token_type": "service",
        "orphan": true,
    })
}

async fn handle(
    State(state): State<Arc<Mutex<Fake>>>,
    method: Method,
    uri: Uri,
    headers: HeaderMap,
    body: Bytes,
) -> Response {
    let token = header(&headers, "x-vault-token");
    let path = decode(uri.path());
    let failure = {
        let mut fake = state.lock().unwrap();
        fake.seen.push(Seen {
            method: method.to_string(),
            path: uri.path().to_string(),
            token: token.clone(),
            namespace: header(&headers, "x-vault-namespace"),
            body: serde_json::from_slice(&body).ok(),
        });
        let kv_read = method == Method::GET && !path.starts_with("/v1/auth/");
        if kv_read {
            fake.failures.pop_front()
        } else {
            None
        }
    };
    match failure {
        Some(Failure::Hang) => {
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(60)).await;
            return errors(503, &["Vault is sealed"]);
        }
        Some(Failure::NotJson) => {
            return (StatusCode::OK, "<html>a proxy page</html>").into_response()
        }
        Some(Failure::Status(code)) if (300..400).contains(&code) => {
            let mut response = errors(code, &[]);
            response
                .headers_mut()
                .insert("location", "/v1/elsewhere".parse().unwrap());
            return response;
        }
        Some(Failure::Status(403)) => return denied(),
        Some(Failure::Status(503)) => return errors(503, &["Vault is sealed"]),
        Some(Failure::Status(code)) => return errors(code, &["internal error"]),
        None => {}
    }

    let mut fake = state.lock().unwrap();
    let Some(rest) = path.strip_prefix("/v1/") else {
        return errors(404, &[]);
    };
    if let Some(login) = rest
        .strip_prefix("auth/")
        .and_then(|r| r.rsplit_once("/login/"))
    {
        if method != Method::POST {
            return errors(405, &[]);
        }
        let (mount, username) = (login.0.to_string(), login.1.to_string());
        let password = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body)
            .ok()
            .and_then(|b| b["password"].as_str().map(str::to_string));
        let lease = match fake.users.get(&(mount, username.clone())) {
            Some(user) if Some(&user.password) == password.as_ref() => user.lease_seconds,
            _ => return errors(400, &["invalid username or password"]),
        };
        fake.issued += 1;
        let issued = format!("hvs.issued-{}", fake.issued);
        fake.tokens.insert(issued.clone(), lease > 0);
        return envelope(Value::Null, auth_answer(&issued, &username, lease));
    }
    let renewable = match token.as_ref().and_then(|t| fake.tokens.get(t)) {
        Some(renewable) => *renewable,
        None => return denied(),
    };
    match (method.clone(), rest) {
        (Method::GET, "auth/token/lookup-self") => envelope(
            json!({ "renewable": renewable, "ttl": 3600, "policies": ["default"] }),
            Value::Null,
        ),
        (Method::POST, "auth/token/renew-self") if fake.refuse_renewals => {
            errors(500, &["internal error"])
        }
        (Method::POST, "auth/token/renew-self") if !renewable => {
            errors(400, &["lease is not renewable"])
        }
        (Method::POST, "auth/token/renew-self") => envelope(
            Value::Null,
            auth_answer(token.as_deref().unwrap(), "", 3600),
        ),
        (Method::GET, kv) => match fake.kv.get(kv) {
            Some(data) => envelope(
                json!({
                    "data": data,
                    "metadata": {
                        "created_time": "2026-10-23T09:00:00.000000000Z",
                        "custom_metadata": null,
                        "deletion_time": "",
                        "destroyed": false,
                        "version": 1,
                    },
                }),
                Value::Null,
            ),
            None => errors(404, &[]),
        },
        _ => errors(405, &[]),
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Reading an org from OpenBao or Vault (env vault spec §6.1 to §6.3), against a fake server:
//! the entries and the policy, the headers, token and login sign-in, what each failure means,
//! and the sign-in details kept in the secret store. No error ever holds a value.

mod common;

use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use common::fake_openbao::{Failure, FakeOpenBao};
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    http_client, http_client_with_timeout, source_for, BaoAuth, Fetched, InfisicalSettings,
    OpenBao, OpenBaoSettings, SopsSettings, Source, SourceCreds, SourceError, SourceSettings,
};
use dots_core::vault::{MemorySecrets, SecretStore, MAX_SECRET_BYTES};
use dots_core::Error;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

const TOKEN: &str = "hvs.tok-4d9e1b7a";
const PASSWORD: &str = "pw-8c2f5e01aa";
const WRONG_PASSWORD: &str = "pw-wrong-61d0c3";
const SECRET: &str = "val-secret-3b6a9f";
const NESTED: &str = "val-nested-5e0d";
const NUMBER: u64 = 734911;
const POLICY: &str = "signed-policy-71e2c0";

/// Every value a test hands the fake, and the prefix of the tokens its logins give.
const VALUES: &[&str] = &[
    TOKEN,
    PASSWORD,
    WRONG_PASSWORD,
    SECRET,
    NESTED,
    "734911",
    POLICY,
    "hvs.issued",
];

fn assert_clean(e: &SourceError) {
    let text = format!("{e} {e:?}");
    for value in VALUES {
        assert!(!text.contains(value), "{text:?} holds {value:?}");
    }
}

fn z(s: &str) -> Zeroizing<String> {
    Zeroizing::new(s.to_string())
}

fn token() -> SourceCreds {
    SourceCreds::Token { token: z(TOKEN) }
}

fn login(username: &str, password: &str) -> SourceCreds {
    SourceCreds::Login {
        username: z(username),
        password: z(password),
    }
}

fn settings(fake: &FakeOpenBao) -> OpenBaoSettings {
    OpenBaoSettings {
        address: fake.address(),
        mount: "secret".into(),
        path: "dots".into(),
        auth: BaoAuth::Token,
        auth_mount: None,
        namespace: None,
    }
}

fn login_settings(fake: &FakeOpenBao, auth: BaoAuth) -> OpenBaoSettings {
    OpenBaoSettings {
        auth,
        ..settings(fake)
    }
}

fn bao(settings: OpenBaoSettings) -> OpenBao {
    OpenBao::new(settings, http_client())
}

/// A fake with the org's entries and policy at `secret/dots`, the token `TOKEN` (not
/// renewable), and the `userpass` user `alice`, whose logins last an hour.
async fn seeded() -> FakeOpenBao {
    let fake = FakeOpenBao::start().await;
    fake.put_env(
        "secret",
        "dots",
        json!({ "API_KEY": SECRET, "LOG_LEVEL": "debug" }),
    );
    fake.put_policy("secret", "dots", POLICY);
    fake.allow_token(TOKEN, false);
    fake.add_user("userpass", "alice", PASSWORD, 3600);
    fake
}

fn names(fetched: &Fetched) -> Vec<&str> {
    fetched.entries.keys().map(String::as_str).collect()
}

fn invalid(e: SourceError) -> String {
    match e {
        SourceError::Invalid(why) => why,
        other => panic!("expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

// Reading.

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_token_read_gives_the_entries_and_the_policy() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let fetched = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(names(&fetched), ["API_KEY", "LOG_LEVEL"]);
    assert_eq!(fetched.entries["API_KEY"].as_str(), SECRET);
    assert_eq!(fetched.entries["LOG_LEVEL"].as_str(), "debug");
    assert_eq!(fetched.policy, POLICY);
    assert_eq!(
        fake.calls(),
        [
            "GET /v1/secret/data/dots/env",
            "GET /v1/secret/data/dots/policy",
            "GET /v1/auth/token/lookup-self",
        ]
    );
    for seen in fake.requests() {
        assert_eq!(seen.token.as_deref(), Some(TOKEN), "{seen:?}");
        assert_eq!(seen.namespace, None, "{seen:?}");
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_namespace_header_is_sent_only_when_set() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        namespace: Some("team-a/".into()),
        ..settings(&fake)
    });
    source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        namespace: Some("team-a/".into()),
        ..login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass)
    });
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    let seen = fake.requests();
    assert_eq!(seen.len(), 6, "{:?}", fake.calls());
    for seen in seen {
        assert_eq!(seen.namespace.as_deref(), Some("team-a/"), "{seen:?}");
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_address_may_end_with_a_slash() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        address: format!("{}/", fake.address()),
        ..settings(&fake)
    });
    source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.calls()[0], "GET /v1/secret/data/dots/env");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn each_path_segment_is_percent_encoded() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.put_env("kv/team", "eng ops/q?x#y", json!({ "API_KEY": SECRET }));
    fake.put_policy("kv/team", "eng ops/q?x#y", POLICY);
    fake.add_user("userpass", "a/b c", PASSWORD, 3600);
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        mount: "kv/team".into(),
        path: "/eng ops//q?x#y/".into(),
        ..login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass)
    });
    let fetched = source.fetch(&login("a/b c", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(names(&fetched), ["API_KEY"]);
    assert_eq!(
        fake.calls(),
        [
            "POST /v1/auth/userpass/login/a%2Fb%20c",
            "GET /v1/kv/team/data/eng%20ops/q%3Fx%23y/env",
            "GET /v1/kv/team/data/eng%20ops/q%3Fx%23y/policy",
        ]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn fetched_debug_shows_only_the_names() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let fetched = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();
    let debug = format!("{fetched:?}");
    assert!(debug.contains("API_KEY"), "{debug}");
    assert!(!debug.contains(SECRET), "{debug}");
    assert!(!debug.contains(POLICY), "{debug}");
}

// Logging in.

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_userpass_login_then_a_read_and_the_token_is_kept() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    let first = source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    let second = source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(names(&first), ["API_KEY", "LOG_LEVEL"]);
    assert_eq!(first, second);
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 1, "{:?}", fake.calls());
    let seen = fake.requests();
    assert_eq!(seen[0].method, "POST");
    assert_eq!(seen[0].path, "/v1/auth/userpass/login/alice");
    assert_eq!(seen[0].token, None);
    assert_eq!(seen[0].body, Some(json!({ "password": PASSWORD })));
    for read in &seen[1..] {
        assert_eq!(read.token.as_deref(), Some("hvs.issued-1"), "{read:?}");
    }
    assert_eq!(fake.count("/v1/auth/token/lookup-self"), 0);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_ldap_login_uses_its_mount() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.add_user("ldap", "alice", PASSWORD, 3600);
    fake.add_user("corp-ldap", "alice", PASSWORD, 3600);

    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Ldap));
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        auth_mount: Some("corp-ldap".into()),
        ..login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Ldap)
    });
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    let logins: Vec<String> = fake
        .calls()
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|c| c.starts_with("POST"))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        logins,
        [
            "POST /v1/auth/ldap/login/alice",
            "POST /v1/auth/corp-ldap/login/alice",
        ]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_token_close_to_its_expiry_is_not_kept() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.add_user("userpass", "bob", PASSWORD, 5);
    fake.add_user("userpass", "carol", PASSWORD, 0);
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));

    source.fetch(&login("bob", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    source.fetch(&login("bob", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 2, "a 5-second lease is too close to its end");

    fake.clear_requests();
    source.fetch(&login("carol", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    source.fetch(&login("carol", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 1, "a lease of 0 does not expire");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn other_sign_in_details_log_in_again() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.add_user("userpass", "bob", PASSWORD, 3600);
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    source.fetch(&login("bob", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 2);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_403_on_the_kept_token_logs_in_again_once() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(403), 1);
    let fetched = source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(names(&fetched), ["API_KEY", "LOG_LEVEL"]);
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 2, "{:?}", fake.calls());

    // The new token is kept.
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 2);

    // A token the source no longer accepts works the same way.
    fake.revoke_all_tokens();
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 3);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn two_403s_in_a_row_are_denied() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();

    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(403), 2);
    let e = source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, SourceError::Denied(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert!(e.to_string().contains("HTTP 403"), "{e}");
    assert_clean(&e);
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 2);

    // Nothing refused is kept: the next fetch logs in again.
    source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 3);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_403_right_after_a_login_is_denied_without_another() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(403), 1);
    let e = source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, SourceError::Denied(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert_eq!(fake.logins(), 1);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_bad_password_is_denied() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    for creds in [login("alice", WRONG_PASSWORD), login("nobody", PASSWORD)] {
        let e = source.fetch(&creds).await.unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(e, SourceError::Denied(_)), "{e:?}");
        assert!(
            e.to_string()
                .contains("refused the username or password (HTTP 400)"),
            "{e}"
        );
        assert_clean(&e);
    }

}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_bad_token_is_denied() {

    assert_eq!(
        e.to_string(),
        format!(
            "{} refused access to secret/dots/env (HTTP 403)",

        )
    );

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_wrong_kind_of_sign_in_details_is_invalid() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let by_token = bao(settings(&fake));
    for creds in [
        login("alice", PASSWORD),
        SourceCreds::Token { token: z("") },
    ] {
        let why = invalid(by_token.fetch(&creds).await.unwrap_err());
        assert_eq!(
            why,
            "this org's OpenBao signs in with a token, so it needs a token"
        );
    }
    let by_login = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Ldap));
    for creds in [
        token(),
        login("alice", ""),
        login("", PASSWORD),
        SourceCreds::Age {
            identity: z("AGE-SECRET-KEY-1"),
        },
    ] {
        let why = invalid(by_login.fetch(&creds).await.unwrap_err());
        assert_eq!(
            why,
            "this org's OpenBao signs in with ldap, so it needs a username and password"
        );
    }
    assert!(fake.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fake.calls());
}

// Renewing a token.

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_renewable_token_is_renewed_once_an_hour() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.allow_token(TOKEN, true);
    let source = bao(settings(&fake));
    source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();
    source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(fake.count("/v1/auth/token/lookup-self"), 1);
    assert_eq!(fake.renewals(), 1);
    let renew = fake
        .requests()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|s| s.path == "/v1/auth/token/renew-self")
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(renew.method, "POST");
    assert_eq!(renew.token.as_deref(), Some(TOKEN));
}

}

// What each failure means.

#[tokio::test]
async fn sealed_a_server_error_or_rate_limiting_is_unreachable() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);
    let e = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        e,
        SourceError::Unreachable(format!(
            "{} is sealed or not ready (HTTP 503)",
            fake.address()
        ))
    );

    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(502), 1);
    let e = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, SourceError::Unreachable(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert!(e.to_string().contains("HTTP 502"), "{e}");

    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(500), 1);
    let e = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        e,
        SourceError::Unreachable(format!("{} is not available (HTTP 500)", fake.address()))
    );

    fake.fail_next(Failure::Status(429), 1);
    let e = bao(settings(&fake)).fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        e,
        SourceError::Unreachable(format!(
            "{} is rate limiting Dots (HTTP 429)",
            fake.address()
        ))
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_refused_connection_is_unreachable() {
    let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
    drop(listener);
    let source = OpenBao::new(
        OpenBaoSettings {
            address: format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}"),
            mount: "secret".into(),
            path: "dots".into(),
            auth: BaoAuth::Token,
            auth_mount: None,
            namespace: None,
        },
        http_client(),
    );
    let e = source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, SourceError::Unreachable(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert!(
        e.to_string()
            .starts_with(&format!("cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:{port}")),
        "{e}"
    );
    assert_clean(&e);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_source_that_hangs_is_unreachable() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    fake.fail_next(Failure::Hang, 1);
    let source = OpenBao::new(
        settings(&fake),
        http_client_with_timeout(Duration::from_millis(300)),
    );
    let started = Instant::now();
    let e = source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        e,
        SourceError::Unreachable(format!("{} did not answer in time", fake.address()))
    );
    assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_path_leaving_its_mount_is_refused_before_any_request() {
    let fake = seeded().await;
    let paths = [
        "../x", "dots/..", "a/./b", "%2e%2e/x", "%2E.", ".%2e", "", "/", "//", "a\nb",
    ];
    for path in paths {
        let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
            path: path.into(),
            ..settings(&fake)
        });
        let why = invalid(source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err());
        assert!(why.starts_with("the source's path "), "{path:?}: {why}");
    }
    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        mount: "..".into(),
        ..settings(&fake)
    });
    let why = invalid(source.fetch(&token()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        "the source's mount '..' must not hold a '.' or '..' segment"
    );

    let source = bao(OpenBaoSettings {
        auth_mount: Some("userpass/../token".into()),
        ..login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass)
    });
    let why = invalid(source.fetch(&login("alice", PASSWORD)).await.unwrap_err());
    assert!(why.starts_with("the source's auth_mount "), "{why}");

    let source = bao(login_settings(&fake, BaoAuth::Userpass));
    for username in ["..", ".", "%2e%2E"] {
        let why = invalid(source.fetch(&login(username, PASSWORD)).await.unwrap_err());
        assert!(why.starts_with("the username cannot be"), "{why}");
    }
    assert!(fake.calls().is_empty(), "{:?}", fake.calls());
}

// The sign-in details in the secret store.

fn every_kind() -> Vec<SourceCreds> {
    vec![
        token(),
        login("alice", PASSWORD),
        SourceCreds::Machine {
            client_id: z("client-id-0c1d"),
            client_secret: z(SECRET),
        },
        SourceCreds::Age {
            identity: z("AGE-SECRET-KEY-1QYQSZQGPQYQSZQGPQYQSZQGPQYQSZQGP"),
        },
    ]
}

#[test]
fn sign_in_details_round_trip_through_the_secret_store() {
    let secrets = MemorySecrets::new();
    assert_eq!(SourceCreds::store_key("acme-eng"), "org/acme-eng/source");
    assert_eq!(SourceCreds::load(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap(), None);

    for creds in every_kind() {
        creds.save(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            SourceCreds::load(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap(),
            Some(creds)
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(secrets.keys("org/").unwrap(), ["org/acme-eng/source"]);

    SourceCreds::forget(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(SourceCreds::load(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap(), None);
    SourceCreds::forget(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn sign_in_details_are_tagged_json() {
    let secrets = MemorySecrets::new();
    login("alice", PASSWORD).save(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();
    let stored = secrets.get("org/acme-eng/source").unwrap().unwrap();
    let json: Value = serde_json::from_str(&stored).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        json,
        json!({ "kind": "login", "username": "alice", "password": PASSWORD })
    );

    let kinds: Vec<&str> = every_kind().iter().map(SourceCreds::kind).collect();
    assert_eq!(kinds, ["token", "login", "machine", "age"]);
    for creds in every_kind() {
        let json = serde_json::to_value(&creds).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(json["kind"], creds.kind());
    }
}

#[test]
fn sign_in_details_debug_shows_the_kind_only() {
    for creds in every_kind() {
        let debug = format!("{creds:?}");
        assert_eq!(debug, format!("SourceCreds({:?})", creds.kind()));
    }
}

#[test]
fn sign_in_details_too_long_to_keep_are_refused() {
    let secrets = MemorySecrets::new();
    // `{"kind":"token","token":""}` is 27 bytes.
    let fits = "t".repeat(MAX_SECRET_BYTES - 27);
    let creds = SourceCreds::Token { token: z(&fits) };
    creds.save(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        SourceCreds::load(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap(),
        Some(creds)
    );
    SourceCreds::forget(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap();

    let long = format!("{SECRET}{}", "t".repeat(MAX_SECRET_BYTES));
    let e = SourceCreds::Token { token: z(&long) }
        .save(&secrets, "acme-eng")
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, Error::Invalid(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert_eq!(
        e.to_string(),
        "invalid input: these sign-in details are too long to keep: at most 2560 bytes in all"
    );
    assert!(secrets.keys("").unwrap().is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn damaged_sign_in_details_are_an_error_without_their_text() {
    let secrets = MemorySecrets::new();
    let damaged = [
        format!(r#"{{"kind":"token","token":{NUMBER}}}"#),
        format!(r#"{{"kind":"bearer","token":"{SECRET}"}}"#),
        format!(r#"{{"kind":"token","token":"{SECRET}","extra":"{NESTED}"}}"#),
        format!("not json {SECRET}"),
    ];
    for text in damaged {
        secrets.put("org/acme-eng/source", &text).unwrap();
        let e = SourceCreds::load(&secrets, "acme-eng").unwrap_err();
        let shown = format!("{e} {e:?}");
        assert!(shown.contains("org 'acme-eng'"), "{shown}");
        for value in VALUES {
            assert!(!shown.contains(value), "{shown:?} holds {value:?}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn sign_in_details_need_a_good_org_id() {
    let secrets = MemorySecrets::new();
    for org_id in ["../x", "Acme", "", "a/b"] {
        assert!(token().save(&secrets, org_id).is_err(), "{org_id:?}");
        assert!(SourceCreds::load(&secrets, org_id).is_err(), "{org_id:?}");
        assert!(SourceCreds::forget(&secrets, org_id).is_err(), "{org_id:?}");
    }
    assert!(secrets.keys("").unwrap().is_empty());
}
```
