**Create `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/infisical.rs`:**

```rust
//! Infisical, self-hosted or cloud (env vault spec §6.1). The entries are the shared secrets of
//! one folder, `secret_path` in the join code's project and environment, and the signed policy
//! is secret `DOTS_POLICY` of its `policy` sub-folder (§6.3). The person signs in with a
//! Universal Auth machine identity. The access token a login gives is kept in memory until it
//! expires, and a login again replaces it: there is no renewal.
//!
//! Only the folder's own secrets are read. Imported secrets come from other folders and
//! environments an admin controls, so `includeImports=false` is sent, and an `imports` list in
//! the answer is ignored all the same: v1 keeps an org's entries to one folder. A personal
//! override (`type: personal`) is skipped, since an org's entries are the shared ones only.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use async_trait::async_trait;
use reqwest::header::{HeaderValue, AUTHORIZATION, CONTENT_TYPE};
use reqwest::{StatusCode, Url};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use tokio::sync::Mutex;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

use super::{
    collect_entries, endpoint, is_dot_segment, read_json, request_failed, status_failed, Fetched,
    Field, Source, SourceCreds, SourceError, POLICY_ENTRY,
};
use crate::vault::entries::check_variable_name;
use crate::vault::org::InfisicalSettings;

/// An access token this close to its expiry is not used: the next fetch logs in again.
const EXPIRY_MARGIN: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

/// What the login is called in messages.
const LOGIN: &str = "the Universal Auth login";

/// An org's Infisical source. It keeps, in memory only, the access token of the last login.
pub struct Infisical {
    settings: InfisicalSettings,
    http: reqwest::Client,
    /// `site_url` without a slash at the end, for URLs and messages.
    site: String,
    login: Mutex<Option<CachedToken>>,
}

struct CachedToken {
    token: Zeroizing<String>,
    /// The SHA-256 of the client id and client secret the token was given for.
    creds: [u8; 32],
    /// `None` when the login gave no lifetime.
    expires: Option<Instant>,
}

impl CachedToken {
    fn usable(&self, creds: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
        &self.creds == creds
            && self
                .expires
                .is_none_or(|at| Instant::now() + EXPIRY_MARGIN < at)
    }
}

/// The two reads of a fetch, and the names they go by in messages: `dev:/dots`.
struct Reads {
    env: Url,
    env_name: String,
    policy: Url,
    policy_name: String,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct LoginBody<'a> {
    #[serde(rename = "clientId")]
    client_id: &'a str,
    #[serde(rename = "clientSecret")]
    client_secret: &'a str,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct LoginAnswer {
    #[serde(rename = "accessToken", default)]
    access_token: Option<Zeroizing<String>>,
    /// Seconds until the token expires.
    #[serde(rename = "expiresIn", default)]
    expires_in: Option<u64>,
}

/// The answer of `GET /api/v4/secrets`. Every other field, `imports` included, is skipped
/// without being copied.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ListAnswer {
    #[serde(default)]
    secrets: Option<Vec<RawSecret>>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawSecret {
    #[serde(rename = "secretKey", default)]
    key: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "secretValue", default)]
    value: Option<Field>,
    /// True when the identity may list the secret but not read its value.
    #[serde(rename = "secretValueHidden", default)]
    hidden: Option<bool>,
    /// `shared` or `personal`. A secret without one is taken as shared.
    #[serde(rename = "type", default)]
    kind: Option<String>,
}

impl RawSecret {
    fn is_personal(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|k| k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("personal"))
    }
}

impl Infisical {
    pub fn new(settings: InfisicalSettings, http: reqwest::Client) -> Infisical {
        let site = settings.site_url.trim_end_matches('/').to_string();
        Infisical {
            settings,
            http,
            site,
            login: Mutex::new(None),
        }
    }

    /// The URLs of the two reads, checked before any request is sent.
    fn reads(&self) -> Result<Reads, SourceError> {
        let folder = folder_path(&self.settings.secret_path)?;
        let policy = policy_folder(&folder);
        let environment = &self.settings.environment;
        Ok(Reads {
            env: self.list_url(&folder)?,
            env_name: format!("{environment}:{folder}"),
            policy: self.list_url(&policy)?,
            policy_name: format!("{environment}:{policy}"),
        })
    }

    /// `GET /api/v4/secrets` for one folder, without its sub-folders or imports.
    fn list_url(&self, folder: &str) -> Result<Url, SourceError> {
        let mut url = endpoint(&self.site, ["api", "v4", "secrets"])?;
        url.query_pairs_mut()
            .append_pair("projectId", &self.settings.project_id)
            .append_pair("environment", &self.settings.environment)
            .append_pair("secretPath", folder)
            .append_pair("recursive", "false")
            .append_pair("includeImports", "false")
            .append_pair("viewSecretValue", "true");
        Ok(url)
    }

    /// Logs in with the machine identity. A refusal (401 or 403) is `Denied`.
    async fn log_in(
        &self,
        url: &Url,
        client_id: &str,
        client_secret: &str,
        creds: [u8; 32],
    ) -> Result<CachedToken, SourceError> {
        let body = serde_json::to_vec(&LoginBody {
            client_id,
            client_secret,
        })
        .expect("a login body serializes");
        let response = self
            .http
            .post(url.clone())
            .header(CONTENT_TYPE, "application/json")
            .body(body)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| request_failed(&self.site, e))?;
        let status = response.status();
        if matches!(status.as_u16(), 401 | 403) {
            return Err(SourceError::Denied(format!(
                "{} refused the client id or client secret (HTTP {})",
                self.site,
                status.as_u16()
            )));
        }
        if !status.is_success() {
            return Err(status_failed(&self.site, LOGIN, status));
        }
        let answer: LoginAnswer = read_json(response, &self.site, LOGIN).await?;
        let token = answer
            .access_token
            .filter(|t| !t.is_empty())
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                SourceError::Invalid(format!("{} gave no access token for {LOGIN}", self.site))
            })?;
        let expires = match answer.expires_in.unwrap_or(0) {
            0 => None,
            seconds => Instant::now().checked_add(Duration::from_secs(seconds)),
        };
        Ok(CachedToken {
            token,
            creds,
            expires,
        })
    }

    /// Reads the entries, then the policy, with `token`.
    async fn read(&self, reads: &Reads, token: &str) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
        let Some(secrets) = self.list(&reads.env, &reads.env_name, token).await? else {
            return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                "no secrets at {}: the project, environment or folder does not exist",
                reads.env_name
            )));
        };
        let entries = shared_entries(secrets, &reads.env_name)?;

        let policy = self
            .list(&reads.policy, &reads.policy_name, token)
            .await?
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .into_iter()
            .find(|s| !s.is_personal() && s.key.as_deref() == Some(POLICY_ENTRY))
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                SourceError::Invalid(format!("no {POLICY_ENTRY} at {}", reads.policy_name))
            })?;
        let mut policy = match (policy.hidden, policy.value) {
            (Some(true), _) => return Err(hidden(POLICY_ENTRY)),
            (_, None) => return Err(no_value(POLICY_ENTRY)),
            (_, Some(Field::NotText)) => return Err(not_text(POLICY_ENTRY)),
            (_, Some(Field::Text(text))) => text,
        };
        Ok(Fetched {
            entries,
            policy: std::mem::take(&mut *policy),
        })
    }

    /// One folder's secrets, or `None` when the folder is not there (404).
    async fn list(
        &self,
        url: &Url,
        name: &str,
        token: &str,
    ) -> Result<Option<Vec<RawSecret>>, SourceError> {
        let bearer = Zeroizing::new(format!("Bearer {token}"));
        let mut bearer = HeaderValue::from_str(&bearer).map_err(|_| {
            SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                "the access token from {} holds characters a header cannot carry",
                self.site
            ))
        })?;
        bearer.set_sensitive(true);
        let response = self
            .http
            .get(url.clone())
            .header(AUTHORIZATION, bearer)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| request_failed(&self.site, e))?;
        match response.status() {
            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND => Ok(None),
            s if s.is_success() => {
                let answer: ListAnswer = read_json(response, &self.site, name).await?;
                let secrets = answer.secrets.ok_or_else(|| {
                    SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                        "the answer from {} for {name} has no list of secrets",
                        self.site
                    ))
                })?;
                Ok(Some(secrets))
            }
            s => Err(status_failed(&self.site, name, s)),
        }
    }

    /// A fetch with the machine identity. The token of the last login is used while it is
    /// good; if the source refuses it, the fetch logs in once more and tries again.
    async fn fetch_with(
        &self,
        reads: &Reads,
        client_id: &str,
        client_secret: &str,
    ) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
        let url = endpoint(&self.site, ["api", "v1", "auth", "universal-auth", "login"])?;
        let creds = creds_hash(client_id, client_secret);
        let mut cached = self.login.lock().await;
        let reused = match cached.as_ref() {
            Some(c) if c.usable(&creds) => Some(c.token.clone()),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let Some(token) = reused {
            match self.read(reads, &token).await {
                Err(SourceError::Denied(_)) => {}
                done => return done,
            }
            tracing::debug!(
                "{}: the access token was refused; logging in again",
                self.site
            );
        }
        *cached = None;
        let token = self.log_in(&url, client_id, client_secret, creds).await?;
        let fetched = self.read(reads, &token.token).await;
        if !matches!(fetched, Err(SourceError::Denied(_))) {
            *cached = Some(token);
        }
        fetched
    }
}

/// `secret_path` as Infisical names a folder: `/`, or `/team/dots` with no slash at the end. It
/// must start with `/`, and an empty segment (`/a//b`), a `.` or `..` segment (also written with
/// `%2e`) or a control character is refused. One slash at the end is dropped.
fn folder_path(value: &str) -> Result<String, SourceError> {
    let refuse = |why: &str| {
        SourceError::Invalid(format!(
            "the source's secret_path '{}' {why}",
            value.escape_debug()
        ))
    };
    if value.chars().any(char::is_control) {
        return Err(refuse("holds a control character"));
    }
    if value == "/" {
        return Ok(value.to_string());
    }
    let Some(rest) = value.strip_prefix('/') else {
        return Err(refuse("must start with '/'"));
    };
    let rest = rest.strip_suffix('/').unwrap_or(rest);
    let segments: Vec<&str> = rest.split('/').collect();
    if segments.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()) {
        return Err(refuse("has an empty segment"));
    }
    if segments.iter().any(|s| is_dot_segment(s)) {
        return Err(refuse("must not hold a '.' or '..' segment"));
    }
    Ok(format!("/{}", segments.join("/")))
}

/// The policy's sub-folder of `folder`: `/policy` under the root, `/dots/policy` under `/dots`.
fn policy_folder(folder: &str) -> String {
    match folder {
        "/" => "/policy".to_string(),
        _ => format!("{folder}/policy"),
    }
}

/// The entries of a folder's shared secrets.
fn shared_entries(
    secrets: Vec<RawSecret>,
    name: &str,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Zeroizing<String>>, SourceError> {
    let mut raw = BTreeMap::new();
    for secret in secrets {
        if secret.is_personal() {
            continue;
        }
        let Some(key) = secret.key else {
            return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                "a secret at {name} has no name"
            )));
        };
        let field = match (secret.hidden, secret.value) {
            // `collect_entries` skips these names whatever their value.
            _ if skipped(&key) => Field::NotText,
            (Some(true), _) => return Err(hidden(&key)),
            (_, None) => return Err(no_value(&key)),
            (_, Some(field)) => field,
        };
        if raw.contains_key(&key) {
            return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!("{key} is at {name} twice")));
        }
        raw.insert(key, field);
    }
    collect_entries(raw)
}

/// Whether `collect_entries` skips `name`: the policy key, or not a variable name.
fn skipped(name: &str) -> bool {
    name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(POLICY_ENTRY) || check_variable_name(name).is_err()
}

fn hidden(name: &str) -> SourceError {
    SourceError::Invalid(format!(
        "the value of {name} is hidden from this machine identity"
    ))
}

fn no_value(name: &str) -> SourceError {
    SourceError::Invalid(format!("{name} has no value"))
}

fn not_text(name: &str) -> SourceError {
    SourceError::Invalid(format!("{name} is not text"))
}

/// The SHA-256 of a client id and secret, to tell whether a kept token is theirs.
fn creds_hash(client_id: &str, client_secret: &str) -> [u8; 32] {
    let mut hash = Sha256::new();
    hash.update(client_id.as_bytes());
    hash.update([0]);
    hash.update(client_secret.as_bytes());
    hash.finalize().into()
}

#[async_trait]
impl Source for Infisical {
    async fn fetch(&self, creds: &SourceCreds) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
        let reads = self.reads()?;
        match creds {
            SourceCreds::Machine {
                client_id,
                client_secret,
            } if !client_id.is_empty() && !client_secret.is_empty() => {
                self.fetch_with(&reads, client_id, client_secret).await
            }
            _ => Err(SourceError::Invalid(
                "this org's Infisical signs in with a machine identity, so it needs a client id \
                 and client secret"
                    .into(),
            )),
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 7: Reading an org from a SOPS file encrypted with age

Spec §6.1: a SOPS file in JSON format, local or at an `https://` URL, opened natively with this PC's age key, its MAC checked before anything in it is used. The fixtures were made with the real `sops` 3.13.3 and `age` 1.3.2; their README holds the commands.

**Files:**

- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/sops.rs` (with 12 unit tests)
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/Cargo.toml` (`age`, `aes-gcm`, `subtle`), `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/mod.rs` (the SOPS arm; the not-built stub goes), `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`
- Create: `crates/dots-core/tests/common/fake_files.rs`, `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_sops_test.rs`, `crates/dots-core/tests/fixtures/sops/` (a README, 2 test identities, 5 plain inputs and 12 encrypted files); modify `crates/dots-core/tests/common/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_openbao_test.rs` (its `source_for` test no longer expects the SOPS stub)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: Task 5's `Source`, `SourceCreds::Age`, the shared helpers.
- Produces: `Sops::new(SopsSettings, reqwest::Client)`, re-exported from `vault::org`; `sources::sops::{new_identity() -> (Zeroizing<String>, String), public_key(identity) -> Result<String>, NOT_A_RECIPIENT}` (the text "this PC's key is not a recipient of the file"; Task 8 makes it `pub`). The file is `{"env": {NAME: value}, "policy": "<signed text>", "sops": {…}}`. One key group at most, no `shamir_threshold` above 1, no comment rules; every age stanza is tried, a key twice in an object is refused, the MAC is compared in constant time, and a location's query is never shown. The test server `common::fake_files::FakeFiles`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/common/fake_files.rs`:**

```rust
//! A fake web server for files, such as an org's SOPS file published over HTTPS: it answers
//! `GET <path>` with the file put there, a 404 for any other path, or the status a test sets.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use axum::body::Bytes;
use axum::extract::State;
use axum::http::{StatusCode, Uri};
use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};
use axum::Router;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;

#[derive(Default)]
struct Fake {
    files: HashMap<String, Bytes>,
    /// A status to answer with, and how many more requests get it.
    failing: Option<(u16, usize)>,
    /// The paths asked for, with their query, in order.
    requests: Vec<String>,
}

type Shared = Arc<Mutex<Fake>>;

/// The fake. It stops when dropped.
pub struct FakeFiles {
    address: String,
    state: Shared,
    task: JoinHandle<()>,
}

impl Drop for FakeFiles {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.task.abort();
    }
}

impl FakeFiles {
    /// Starts an empty fake on `127.0.0.1` and a free port.
    pub async fn start() -> FakeFiles {
        let state: Shared = Arc::default();
        let app = Router::new().fallback(handle).with_state(state.clone());
        let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let address = format!("http://{}", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
        });
        FakeFiles {
            address,
            state,
            task,
        }
    }

    /// The URL of `path`, which starts with `/`.
    pub fn url(&self, path: &str) -> String {
        format!("{}{path}", self.address)
    }

    /// Serves `body` at `path`.
    pub fn put(&self, path: &str, body: impl Into<Bytes>) {
        self.fake().files.insert(path.to_string(), body.into());
    }

    /// Answers the next `count` requests with `status` and a short text body.
    pub fn fail_next(&self, status: u16, count: usize) {
        self.fake().failing = Some((status, count));
    }

    /// The paths asked for, with their query, in order.
    pub fn requests(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.fake().requests.clone()
    }

    fn fake(&self) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, Fake> {
        self.state.lock().unwrap()
    }
}

async fn handle(State(state): State<Shared>, uri: Uri) -> Response {
    let mut fake = state.lock().unwrap();
    let asked = uri
        .path_and_query()
        .map_or(uri.path().to_string(), |p| p.to_string());
    fake.requests.push(asked);
    if let Some((status, count)) = fake.failing {
        fake.failing = (count > 1).then_some((status, count - 1));
        let status = StatusCode::from_u16(status).unwrap();
        return (status, "the fake is failing on purpose").into_response();
    }
    match fake.files.get(uri.path()) {
        Some(body) => body.clone().into_response(),
        None => (StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "404 page not found").into_response(),
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/fixtures/sops/README.md`:**

````markdown
# SOPS fixtures

Test files for the SOPS + age org source (`src/vault/org/sources/sops.rs`, tested by
`tests/vault_org_sops_test.rs`). The real tools made every `*.enc.json` here. No file holds a
real secret.

- **Tools:** sops 3.13.3 and age v1.3.2 (`age-keygen` from the same release), installed on
  Windows with `winget install SecretsOPerationS.SOPS` and `winget install FiloSottile.age`.
- **Shell:** Git Bash, run in this folder. No `.sops.yaml` applies here, so the flags below are
  the whole configuration.
- **The `policy` value** in every file is a placeholder string, not a signed policy. The SOPS
  source hands the text on without checking it; the `Orgs` service verifies it.

## Files

- `test-identity.txt`: the test-only age identity the tests open the files with.
- `other-identity.txt`: a second test-only identity, not a recipient of most files.
- `*.plain.json`: the plain inputs.
- `good.enc.json`: `good.plain.json`, for `test-identity.txt`.
- `mac-only.enc.json`: the same, made with `--mac-only-encrypted`.
- `two-recipients.enc.json`: the same, for both identities.
- `not-recipient.enc.json`: the same, for `other-identity.txt` only.
- `encrypted-regex.enc.json`: the same, encrypting only `env` and `policy`. Its other values
  stay plain, and the MAC still covers them.
- `tampered.enc.json`: `good.enc.json` with the first two values of `extra.replicas` swapped.
  Both have the AAD `extra:replicas:`, so each still decrypts, and only the MAC catches it.
- `unencrypted-changed.enc.json`: `good.enc.json` with `note_unencrypted` edited, which fails
  the MAC.
- `not-text.enc.json`: an `env` value that is a number.
- `no-policy.enc.json`: no `policy`.
- `names.enc.json`: names the source skips: `DOTS_POLICY`, `dots_policy`, `1BAD` and
  `has-dash`.
- `case-clash.enc.json`: `API_KEY` and `Api_Key`.

The tests make the other bad files they need in a temporary folder, by changing the text of
`good.enc.json`.

## Making them again

The identities. `age-keygen` prints each public key. The tests check the public keys, so after
making new identities, also update `TEST_RECIPIENT` and `OTHER_RECIPIENT` in the test file.

```bash
age-keygen -o test-identity.txt
age-keygen -o other-identity.txt
```

Then add this as the first line of both files:

```text
# For tests only: a throwaway key that protects no real secret. Never use it elsewhere.
```

Add this as the second line of `other-identity.txt`:

```text
# It is not a recipient of the files encrypted to test-identity.txt alone.
```

The encrypted files:

```bash
T=$(age-keygen -y test-identity.txt)
O=$(age-keygen -y other-identity.txt)
enc() { sops --encrypt --input-type json --output-type json "$@"; }

enc --age "$T" good.plain.json > good.enc.json
enc --mac-only-encrypted --age "$T" good.plain.json > mac-only.enc.json
enc --age "$T,$O" good.plain.json > two-recipients.enc.json
enc --age "$O" good.plain.json > not-recipient.enc.json
enc --encrypted-regex '^(env|policy)$' --age "$T" good.plain.json > encrypted-regex.enc.json
for f in not-text no-policy names case-clash; do
  enc --age "$T" $f.plain.json > $f.enc.json
done
```

The two changed files, edited with Python so that nothing else changes:

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import json

def change(name, edit):
    with open('good.enc.json') as f:
        file = json.load(f)
    edit(file)
    with open(name, 'w', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump(file, f, indent='\t')
        f.write('\n')

def swap_replicas(file):
    replicas = file['extra']['replicas']
    replicas[0], replicas[1] = replicas[1], replicas[0]

def edit_note(file):
    file['note_unencrypted'] = 'visible text, edited by hand'

change('tampered.enc.json', swap_replicas)
change('unencrypted-changed.enc.json', edit_note)
EOF
```

To check them with sops itself: `good`, `mac-only`, `two-recipients` and `encrypted-regex`
decrypt; `tampered` and `unencrypted-changed` fail with "MAC mismatch"; `not-recipient` fails to
get the data key.

```bash
for f in *.enc.json; do
  echo "== $f"
  SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE=test-identity.txt sops --decrypt $f > /dev/null && echo ok
done
```

The tests that use the files read the text exactly as written above, such as `"sops": {` and
the tab indents, so remake a file with these commands rather than by hand.
````

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_sops_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! Reading an org from a SOPS file encrypted with age (env vault spec §6.1 and §6.2), against
//! fixtures the real `sops` and `age` tools made (`tests/fixtures/sops/README.md`): the entries
//! and the policy, the MAC, the recipients, the metadata Dots refuses, a file on disk and one
//! over HTTP, and the identity a PC makes for an org. No error ever holds a value.

mod common;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;

use common::fake_files::FakeFiles;
use dots_core::vault::org::sources::sops::{new_identity, public_key};
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    http_client, source_for, Fetched, Sops, SopsSettings, Source, SourceCreds, SourceError,
    SourceSettings,
};
use dots_core::Error;
use serde_json::Value;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

const API_KEY: &str = "fixture-api-key-9d27b3";
const DATABASE_URL: &str = "postgres://dots:fixture-db-pass-4e1c@db.example.test:5432/app";
const POLICY: &str = "placeholder-signed-policy-5a8e: the SOPS source does not check it";

/// The public keys of `test-identity.txt` and `other-identity.txt`.
const TEST_RECIPIENT: &str = "age1a03d7rmd3zc7lpcxldf24f2g2gyhgphdwesczxmtf0vfvcjtcshseuswgt";
const OTHER_RECIPIENT: &str = "age16fa053f93s48cuu70erfpw7yygxuwkns96x5ptg2ldsrlceqgf8qw8r74u";

/// Values in the fixtures, and pieces of them, that no error may hold.
const VALUES: &[&str] = &[
    API_KEY,
    "fixture-db-pass-4e1c",
    "placeholder-signed-policy",
    "fixture-skipped-1f0a",
    "eu-west-1",
    "secret-sig-77",
];

const MIB: usize = 1024 * 1024;

fn assert_clean(e: &SourceError) {
    let text = format!("{e} {e:?}");
    for value in VALUES {
        assert!(!text.contains(value), "{text:?} holds {value:?}");
    }
    for file in ["test-identity.txt", "other-identity.txt"] {
        let identity = identity(file);
        assert!(
            !text.contains(identity.as_str()),
            "{text:?} holds an identity"
        );
    }
}

fn invalid(e: SourceError) -> String {
    assert_clean(&e);
    match e {
        SourceError::Invalid(why) => why,
        other => panic!("expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

fn denied(e: SourceError) -> String {
    assert_clean(&e);
    match e {
        SourceError::Denied(why) => why,
        other => panic!("expected Denied, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

fn unreachable(e: SourceError) -> String {
    assert_clean(&e);
    match e {
        SourceError::Unreachable(why) => why,
        other => panic!("expected Unreachable, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

fn fixture(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("tests/fixtures/sops")
        .join(name)
}

/// A fixture's text, with the line ends git may have changed made `\n` again.
fn fixture_text(name: &str) -> String {
    std::fs::read_to_string(fixture(name))
        .unwrap()
        .replace("\r\n", "\n")
}

/// The `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…` line of an identity file.
fn identity(file: &str) -> Zeroizing<String> {
    let text = Zeroizing::new(fixture_text(file));
    let line = text
        .lines()
        .find(|line| line.starts_with("AGE-SECRET-KEY-1"))
        .expect("an identity line");
    Zeroizing::new(line.to_string())
}

fn age(file: &str) -> SourceCreds {
    SourceCreds::Age {
        identity: identity(file),
    }
}

fn mine() -> SourceCreds {
    age("test-identity.txt")
}

fn sops_at(location: &str) -> Sops {
    Sops::new(
        SopsSettings {
            location: location.to_string(),
        },
        http_client(),
    )
}

fn local(path: &Path) -> Sops {
    sops_at(&path.display().to_string())
}

async fn open(name: &str, creds: &SourceCreds) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
    local(&fixture(name)).fetch(creds).await
}

/// Writes `text` to a new file in `dir` and gives its path.
fn write(dir: &tempfile::TempDir, text: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let path = dir.path().join("org.sops.json");
    std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
    path
}

/// `good.enc.json` with `from` replaced by `to`, which must be there once, opened.
async fn open_changed(from: &str, to: &str) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
    let text = fixture_text("good.enc.json");
    assert_eq!(text.matches(from).count(), 1, "{from:?}");
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = write(&dir, &text.replace(from, to));
    local(&path).fetch(&mine()).await
}

/// The `ENC[…]` text of `env.<name>` in `good.enc.json`.
fn encrypted(name: &str) -> String {
    let file: Value = serde_json::from_str(&fixture_text("good.enc.json")).unwrap();
    file["env"][name].as_str().unwrap().to_string()
}

fn entries(fetched: &Fetched) -> Vec<(&str, &str)> {
    fetched
        .entries
        .iter()
        .map(|(name, value)| (name.as_str(), value.as_str()))
        .collect()
}

fn good_entries() -> Vec<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    vec![
        ("API_KEY", API_KEY),
        ("DATABASE_URL", DATABASE_URL),
        ("LOG_LEVEL", "debug"),
    ]
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_file_that_encrypts_by_regex_hashes_its_plain_numbers_and_bools_too() {
    // Only `env` and `policy` are encrypted, so `extra`'s ints, floats, bools, empty text and
    // null stay plain and are hashed as SOPS hashes them.
    let text = fixture_text("encrypted-regex.enc.json");
    assert!(text.contains("\"encrypted_regex\": \"^(env|policy)$\""));
    assert!(text.contains("\"weight\": 0.25"));
    let fetched = open("encrypted-regex.enc.json", &mine()).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(entries(&fetched), good_entries());
    assert_eq!(fetched.policy, POLICY);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn one_key_group_opens_like_the_top_level_age_list() {
    let text = fixture_text("good.enc.json");
    assert!(text.contains("\n\t\t],\n\t\t\"lastmodified\""));
    let changed = text
        .replace(
            "\"sops\": {\n\t\t\"age\": [",
            "\"sops\": {\n\t\t\"key_groups\": [{\"age\": [",
        )
        .replace(
            "\n\t\t],\n\t\t\"lastmodified\"",
            "\n\t\t]}],\n\t\t\"lastmodified\"",
        );
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let fetched = local(&write(&dir, &changed)).fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(entries(&fetched), good_entries());

    // Two groups would split the key, which Dots does not read.
    let two = changed.replace("\"key_groups\": [{", "\"key_groups\": [{\"age\": []}, {");
    let e = local(&write(&dir, &two)).fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "the file has 2 key groups, which is not supported"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_file_with_two_values_swapped_in_a_list_fails_the_mac() {
    // Both values have the AAD `extra:replicas:`, so each decrypts; only the MAC sees it.
    let e = open("tampered.enc.json", &mine()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "the file's MAC does not match");
}

        .await
        .unwrap_err();

}

#[tokio::test]

    let api_key = encrypted("API_KEY");
    let e = open_changed(
        &format!("\"API_KEY\": \"{api_key}\""),
        &format!("\"API_KEY\": \"{}\"", encrypted("LOG_LEVEL")),
    )
    .await
    .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        denied(e),
        "the file's value at env:API_KEY does not decrypt: the file was changed"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_file_with_no_mac_or_a_damaged_one_is_denied() {
    let text = fixture_text("good.enc.json");
    let file: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
    let mac = file["sops"]["mac"].as_str().unwrap();

    let e = open_changed(&format!("\t\t\"mac\": \"{mac}\",\n"), "")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "the file's MAC does not match");

    // The MAC of another file, made with another data key.
    let other: Value = serde_json::from_str(&fixture_text("mac-only.enc.json")).unwrap();
    let other_mac = other["sops"]["mac"].as_str().unwrap();
    let e = open_changed(mac, other_mac).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "the file's MAC does not match");

    // The right MAC, with a changed `lastmodified`, its AAD.
    let modified = file["sops"]["lastmodified"].as_str().unwrap();
    let e = open_changed(modified, "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "the file's MAC does not match");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_key_that_is_not_a_recipient_is_denied() {
    let e = open("not-recipient.enc.json", &mine()).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "this PC's key is not a recipient of the file");

    let e = open("good.enc.json", &age("other-identity.txt"))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "this PC's key is not a recipient of the file");

    // A file with no age entries at all, such as one for PGP keys only.
    let e = open_changed("\"sops\": {\n\t\t\"age\": [", "\"sops\": {\n\t\t\"pgp\": [")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(denied(e), "this PC's key is not a recipient of the file");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_value_that_is_not_sops_syntax_is_refused() {
    let api_key = encrypted("API_KEY");
    for bad in [
        "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:zz".to_string(),
        api_key.replace("type:str]", "type:str"),

    ] {
        let e = open_changed(&api_key, &bad).await.unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            invalid(e),

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_key_split_with_shamir_is_not_supported() {
    let e = open_changed(
        "\t\t\"lastmodified\":",
        "\t\t\"shamir_threshold\": 2,\n\t\t\"lastmodified\":",
    )
    .await
    .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "the file splits its data key with shamir_threshold 2, which is not supported"
    );

    // A threshold of 1 is what SOPS writes for one group: nothing is split.
    let fetched = open_changed(
        "\t\t\"lastmodified\":",
        "\t\t\"shamir_threshold\": 1,\n\t\t\"lastmodified\":",
    )
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(entries(&fetched), good_entries());
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn more_than_one_rule_or_a_comment_rule_is_refused() {
    let rule = "\t\t\"unencrypted_suffix\": \"_unencrypted\",\n";
    let e = open_changed(
        rule,
        &format!("{rule}\t\t\"encrypted_suffix\": \"_secret\",\n"),
    )
    .await
    .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "the file's sops metadata sets more than one of unencrypted_suffix, encrypted_suffix, \
         unencrypted_regex, encrypted_regex, unencrypted_comment_regex, encrypted_comment_regex"
    );

    let e = open_changed(rule, "\t\t\"encrypted_comment_regex\": \"sops:enc\",\n")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "the file's encrypted_comment_regex is not supported: a JSON file has no comments"
    );

    let e = open_changed(rule, "\t\t\"encrypted_regex\": \"(\",\n")
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "the file's sops metadata is damaged: encrypted_regex is not a regular expression"
    );
}

        .await

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_wrong_kind_of_creds_or_a_bad_key_is_refused_before_reading() {
    // The location does not exist: a read would be Unreachable.
    let source = sops_at("C:/nowhere/org.sops.json");
    let token = SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new("hvs.tok-4d9e1b7a".into()),
    };
    let e = source.fetch(&token).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "this org's SOPS file is opened with this PC's age key, so it needs one"
    );

    for bad in [
        "",
        "AGE-SECRET-KEY-1NOTAKEY",
        "age1a03d7rmd3zc7lpcxldf24f2g2gyhgph",
    ] {
        let creds = SourceCreds::Age {
            identity: Zeroizing::new(bad.into()),
        };
        let e = source.fetch(&creds).await.unwrap_err();
        let text = format!("{e} {e:?}");
        assert!(bad.is_empty() || !text.contains(bad), "{text}");
        assert_eq!(
            invalid(e),
            "this PC's age key is not an age identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…)"
        );
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_server_error_or_rate_limiting_is_unreachable_and_a_refusal_is_denied() {
    let fake = FakeFiles::start().await;
    fake.put("/org.sops.json", fixture_text("good.enc.json"));
    let source = sops_at(&fake.url("/org.sops.json"));
    let shown = fake.url("/org.sops.json");

    fake.fail_next(503, 1);
    let why = unreachable(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(why, format!("{shown} is not available (HTTP 503)"));

    fake.fail_next(500, 1);
    let why = unreachable(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(why, format!("{shown} is not available (HTTP 500)"));

    fake.fail_next(429, 1);
    let why = unreachable(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(why, format!("{shown} is rate limiting Dots (HTTP 429)"));

    fake.fail_next(403, 1);
    let why = denied(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        format!("{shown} refused access to the SOPS file (HTTP 403)")
    );

    // A redirect is not followed.
    fake.fail_next(302, 1);
    let why = invalid(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(why, format!("{shown} answered HTTP 302 for the SOPS file"));

    // The file is there once the server is back.
    assert!(source.fetch(&mine()).await.is_ok());
}

async fn a_refused_connection_is_unreachable() {
    let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").unwrap();
    let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
    drop(listener);
    let source = sops_at(&format!("http://127.0.0.1:{port}/org.sops.json"));
    let why = unreachable(source.fetch(&mine()).await.unwrap_err());
    assert!(
        why.starts_with(&format!(
            "cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:{port}/org.sops.json: "
        )),
        "{why}"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]

// This PC's identity for an org.

#[test]
fn the_test_identities_give_the_recipients_in_the_fixtures() {
    assert_eq!(
        public_key(&identity("test-identity.txt")).unwrap(),
        TEST_RECIPIENT
    );
    assert_eq!(
        public_key(&identity("other-identity.txt")).unwrap(),
        OTHER_RECIPIENT
    );
    // age-keygen wrote the same public key into each file's comment.
    let text = fixture_text("test-identity.txt");
    assert!(text.contains(&format!("# public key: {TEST_RECIPIENT}")));
    let good: Value = serde_json::from_str(&fixture_text("good.enc.json")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(good["sops"]["age"][0]["recipient"], TEST_RECIPIENT);
}

#[test]
fn a_new_identity_matches_its_public_key() {
    let (secret, public) = new_identity();
    assert!(secret.starts_with("AGE-SECRET-KEY-1"), "an age identity");
    assert!(public.starts_with("age1"), "{public}");
    assert_eq!(public_key(&secret).unwrap(), public);
    assert_eq!(
        public_key(&format!("  {}\n", secret.as_str())).unwrap(),
        public
    );

    let (other, other_public) = new_identity();
    assert_ne!(other.as_str(), secret.as_str());
    assert_ne!(other_public, public);
}

#[test]
fn a_bad_identity_has_no_public_key() {
    for bad in [
        "",
        "age1a03d7rmd3zc7lpcxldf24f2g2gyhgph",
        "AGE-SECRET-KEY-1NOTAKEY",
    ] {
        match public_key(bad) {
            Err(Error::Invalid(why)) => {
                assert_eq!(
                    why,
                    "this PC's age key is not an age identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…)"
                );
            }
            other => panic!("expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
}

/// The real `age-keygen`, from `DOTS_TEST_AGE_KEYGEN` or the PATH, if it is installed.
fn age_keygen() -> Option<Command> {
    let program = std::env::var_os("DOTS_TEST_AGE_KEYGEN").unwrap_or("age-keygen".into());
    let found = Command::new(&program).arg("--version").output().is_ok();
    found.then(|| Command::new(program))
}

#[test]
fn the_age_cli_reads_a_new_identity() {
    let Some(mut keygen) = age_keygen() else {
        eprintln!("skipped: age-keygen is not installed (set DOTS_TEST_AGE_KEYGEN)");
        return;
    };
    let (secret, public) = new_identity();
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let path = dir.path().join("identity.txt");
    std::fs::write(&path, format!("{}\n", secret.as_str())).unwrap();
    // `-y` reads the identity file and prints its public key.
    let out = keygen.arg("-y").arg(&path).output().unwrap();
    assert!(
        out.status.success(),
        "{}",
        String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr)
    );
    assert_eq!(String::from_utf8(out.stdout).unwrap().trim(), public);
}
```
