```rust
//! A SOPS file encrypted with age (env vault spec §6.1): the file at the join code's
//! `location`, a local path synced by git or IT, or an `https://` URL. Only SOPS's JSON format
//! is read. The file holds `{"env": {NAME: value, …}, "policy": "<signed policy text>"}`, and
//! may hold other keys, which are ignored but covered by the MAC.
//!
//! This PC holds its own age identity for the org, and the admin adds its public key as a
//! recipient. Opening the file follows SOPS 3.13 exactly:
//!
//! 1. The JSON is read with every object's keys in the file's order, since the MAC hashes the
//!    values in that order. (`serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature is off in this workspace,
//!    and turning it on would change the order of every map other code writes, so the file is
//!    read into a small tree of its own.)
//! 2. The `sops` metadata gives the age entries, `lastmodified`, the MAC and the rule for which
//!    values are encrypted. One key group at most; a key split with Shamir is refused.
//! 3. The 32-byte data key is unwrapped from an age entry with this PC's identity.
//! 4. Every leaf, in the file's order, is decrypted with AES-256-GCM and a 32-byte IV. Its AAD
//!    is its path of keys joined with `:`, plus a trailing `:`. An array adds nothing to the
//!    path. Each plain value is hashed into the MAC with SHA-512, unencrypted ones too unless
//!    the file says `mac_only_encrypted`.
//! 5. The MAC in the file, decrypted with `lastmodified` as its AAD, must match, compared in
//!    constant time. Nothing is read from the values before it does.
//!
//! A file that can't be read, or a server error, is `Unreachable`, since a synced file may not
//! have arrived yet. A key that is not a recipient, a value that does not decrypt and a MAC that
//! does not match are `Denied`: a failed MAC counts as revoked (§6.2). Anything that is not a
//! SOPS file Dots can open is `Invalid`. No message holds a value.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashSet};
use std::io::Read;
use std::str::FromStr;
use std::sync::LazyLock;

use aes_gcm::aead::consts::U32;
use aes_gcm::aead::{AeadInPlace, KeyInit};
use aes_gcm::aes::Aes256;
use aes_gcm::{AesGcm, Key, Nonce, Tag};
use age::armor::ArmoredReader;
use age::secrecy::ExposeSecret;
use age::x25519;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD;
use base64::Engine;
use chrono::{DateTime, FixedOffset, Timelike};
use regex::{Regex, RegexBuilder};
use reqwest::{StatusCode, Url};
use serde::de::{self, Deserializer, MapAccess, SeqAccess, Visitor};
use serde::Deserialize;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha512};
use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
use tokio::io::AsyncReadExt;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

use super::{
    collect_entries, read_json, request_failed, status_failed, Fetched, Field, Source, SourceCreds,
    SourceError, MAX_ANSWER_BYTES,
};
use crate::vault::org::SopsSettings;
use crate::{Error, Result};

/// The key that holds the file's metadata.
const METADATA: &str = "sops";

/// SOPS's default rule: a key ending with this, or under one that does, is not encrypted.
const DEFAULT_UNENCRYPTED_SUFFIX: &str = "_unencrypted";

/// The bytes a `mac_only_encrypted` MAC starts from: SHA-256 of `sops`, as SOPS sets it.
const MAC_ONLY_ENCRYPTED_INIT: [u8; 32] = [
    0x8a, 0x3f, 0xd2, 0xad, 0x54, 0xce, 0x66, 0x52, 0x7b, 0x10, 0x34, 0xf3, 0xd1, 0x47, 0xbe, 0x0b,
    0x0b, 0x97, 0x5b, 0x3b, 0xf4, 0x4f, 0x72, 0xc6, 0xfd, 0xad, 0xec, 0x81, 0x76, 0xf2, 0x7d, 0x69,
];

/// The six rules SOPS allows, at most one per file.
const RULES: [&str; 6] = [
    "unencrypted_suffix",
    "encrypted_suffix",
    "unencrypted_regex",
    "encrypted_regex",
    "unencrypted_comment_regex",
    "encrypted_comment_regex",
];

/// What `fetch` says when this PC's key opens none of the file's age entries.
const NOT_A_RECIPIENT: &str = "this PC's key is not a recipient of the file";

/// What `fetch` says when the MAC is missing, does not decrypt, or does not match.
const MAC_MISMATCH: &str = "the file's MAC does not match";

/// AES-256-GCM with the 32-byte IV SOPS uses.
type Aes256Gcm32 = AesGcm<Aes256, U32>;

/// An encrypted value: `ENC[AES256_GCM,data:…,iv:…,tag:…,type:…]`, as SOPS matches it.
static ENCRYPTED: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"^ENC\[AES256_GCM,data:(.+),iv:(.+),tag:(.+),type:(.+)\]").expect("the pattern")
});

/// Makes a new age identity for an org: the secret `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…`, kept in the secret
/// store, and its public key `age1…`, which the person sends to the admin.
pub fn new_identity() -> (Zeroizing<String>, String) {
    let identity = x25519::Identity::generate();
    let secret = Zeroizing::new(identity.to_string().expose_secret().to_string());
    (secret, identity.to_public().to_string())
}

/// The public key `age1…` of an age identity.
pub fn public_key(identity: &str) -> Result<String> {
    let identity = parse_identity(identity).map_err(|_| Error::Invalid(bad_identity()))?;
    Ok(identity.to_public().to_string())
}

fn bad_identity() -> String {
    "this PC's age key is not an age identity (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…)".to_string()
}

fn parse_identity(text: &str) -> std::result::Result<x25519::Identity, ()> {
    x25519::Identity::from_str(text.trim()).map_err(|_| ())
}

/// The SOPS source: reads the file, then opens it with this PC's age identity.
pub struct Sops {
    settings: SopsSettings,
    http: reqwest::Client,
}

impl Sops {
    pub fn new(settings: SopsSettings, http: reqwest::Client) -> Sops {
        Sops { settings, http }
    }

    /// Reads and parses the file, from disk or over HTTPS.
    async fn read(&self) -> std::result::Result<Node, SourceError> {
        let location = self.settings.location.as_str();
        if location.contains("://") {
            self.download(location).await
        } else {
            read_file(location).await
        }
    }

    /// GETs the file. A 404 means the URL is wrong, so it is `Invalid`; other statuses follow
    /// the shared rules.
    async fn download(&self, location: &str) -> std::result::Result<Node, SourceError> {
        // The location is not quoted: its query could carry an access token.
        let url = Url::parse(location)
            .map_err(|_| SourceError::Invalid("the source's location is not a URL".into()))?;
        let shown = shown_url(&url);
        let response = self
            .http
            .get(url)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| request_failed(&shown, e))?;
        match response.status() {
            s if s.is_success() => read_json(response, &shown, "the SOPS file").await,
            StatusCode::NOT_FOUND => Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                "there is no file at {shown} (HTTP 404)"
            ))),
            s => Err(status_failed(&shown, "the SOPS file", s)),
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Source for Sops {
    async fn fetch(&self, creds: &SourceCreds) -> std::result::Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
        let SourceCreds::Age { identity } = creds else {
            return Err(SourceError::Invalid(
                "this org's SOPS file is opened with this PC's age key, so it needs one".into(),
            ));
        };
        let identity =
            parse_identity(identity).map_err(|_| SourceError::Invalid(bad_identity()))?;
        let file = self.read().await?;
        open(&file, &identity)
    }
}

/// A URL as messages show it: no query or fragment, which could carry an access token.
fn shown_url(url: &Url) -> String {
    let mut shown = url.clone();
    shown.set_query(None);
    shown.set_fragment(None);
    shown.to_string()
}

/// Reads a local file of at most `MAX_ANSWER_BYTES`. A file that is missing or can't be read is
/// `Unreachable`: it may not be synced yet.
async fn read_file(path: &str) -> std::result::Result<Node, SourceError> {
    let unreadable =
        |e: std::io::Error| SourceError::Unreachable(format!("cannot read {path}: {e}"));
    let file = tokio::fs::File::open(path).await.map_err(unreadable)?;
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(MAX_ANSWER_BYTES as u64 + 1)
        .read_to_end(&mut bytes)
        .await
        .map_err(unreadable)?;
    if bytes.len() > MAX_ANSWER_BYTES {
        return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!("{path} is larger than 1 MiB")));
    }
    serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| {
        SourceError::Invalid(format!(
            "{path} is not readable as JSON (line {}, column {})",
            e.line(),
            e.column()
        ))
    })
}

/// Opens a parsed SOPS file with `identity`: the entries and the policy, once the MAC matches.
fn open(file: &Node, identity: &x25519::Identity) -> std::result::Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
    let Node::Object(top) = file else {
        return Err(not_sops());
    };
    check_keys(file)?;
    let metadata = top
        .iter()
        .find(|(key, _)| key == METADATA)
        .ok_or_else(not_sops)?;
    let metadata = Metadata::read(&metadata.1)?;
    let data_key = data_key(&metadata.age, identity)?;
    let mut run = Decrypting::new(&data_key, &metadata);

    let mut env = Part::Missing;
    let mut policy = Part::Missing;
    let mut path = Vec::new();
    for (key, node) in top {
        if key == METADATA {
            continue;
        }
        path.push(key.as_str());
        match (key.as_str(), node) {
            ("env", Node::Object(fields)) => {
                let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
                for (name, value) in fields {
                    path.push(name.as_str());
                    values.push((name.as_str(), run.walk(value, &mut path)?));
                    path.pop();
                }
                env = Part::Found(values);
            }
            ("env", other) => {
                run.walk(other, &mut path)?;
                env = Part::NotItsShape;
            }
            ("policy", other) => {
                policy = match run.walk(other, &mut path)? {
                    Some(plain) => Part::Found(plain),
                    None => Part::NotItsShape,
                }
            }
            (_, other) => {
                run.walk(other, &mut path)?;
            }
        }
        path.pop();
    }
    run.check_mac(&metadata)?;

    // The MAC matches: only now is anything read from the values.
    let policy = match policy {
        Part::Missing => return Err(SourceError::Invalid("the file has no policy".into())),
        Part::NotItsShape => None,
        Part::Found(plain) => plain.into_text(),
    };
    let policy =
        policy.ok_or_else(|| SourceError::Invalid("the file's policy is not text".into()))?;
    let env = match env {
        Part::Missing => return Err(SourceError::Invalid("the file has no env object".into())),
        Part::NotItsShape => {
            return Err(SourceError::Invalid(
                "the file's env is not an object".into(),
            ))
        }
        Part::Found(env) => env,
    };
    let raw: BTreeMap<String, Field> = env
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(name, plain)| {
            let field = match plain.and_then(Plain::into_text) {
                Some(text) => Field::Text(text),
                None => Field::NotText,
            };
            (name.to_string(), field)
        })
        .collect();
    Ok(Fetched {
        entries: collect_entries(raw)?,
        policy: policy.to_string(),
    })
}

/// What the file's `env` or `policy` held: nothing, a value of the wrong shape (`env` must be
/// an object, `policy` a leaf), or its values, not yet read.
enum Part<T> {
    Missing,
    NotItsShape,
    Found(T),
}

fn not_sops() -> SourceError {
    SourceError::Invalid("the file is not a SOPS file: it has no sops metadata".into())
}

fn damaged(why: &str) -> SourceError {
    SourceError::Invalid(format!("the file's sops metadata is damaged: {why}"))
}

/// Refuses an object with the same key twice anywhere in the file: which one counts would be
/// a guess.
fn check_keys(node: &Node) -> std::result::Result<(), SourceError> {
    match node {
        Node::Object(fields) => {
            let mut seen = HashSet::with_capacity(fields.len());
            for (key, value) in fields {
                if !seen.insert(key.as_str()) {
                    return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                        "the file has the key \"{}\" twice in one object",
                        key.escape_debug()
                    )));
                }
                check_keys(value)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        Node::Array(items) => items.iter().try_for_each(check_keys),
        _ => Ok(()),
    }
}

/// What the `sops` object says, as far as an age-encrypted JSON file needs.
struct Metadata<'n> {
    /// `lastmodified` as SOPS formats it for the MAC's AAD.
    mac_aad: String,
    mac: Option<&'n str>,
    /// The armored `enc` of each age entry.
    age: Vec<&'n str>,
    rule: Rule,
    mac_only_encrypted: bool,
}

impl<'n> Metadata<'n> {
    fn read(node: &'n Node) -> std::result::Result<Metadata<'n>, SourceError> {
        let Node::Object(fields) = node else {
            return Err(not_sops());
        };
        match field(fields, "shamir_threshold") {
            None | Some(Node::Null) | Some(Node::Int(0 | 1)) => {}
            Some(Node::Int(n)) => {
                return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                    "the file splits its data key with shamir_threshold {n}, which is not \
                     supported"
                )))
            }
            Some(_) => return Err(damaged("shamir_threshold is not a number")),
        }
        let groups = match field(fields, "key_groups") {
            None | Some(Node::Null) => &[][..],
            Some(Node::Array(groups)) => groups.as_slice(),
            Some(_) => return Err(damaged("key_groups is not a list")),
        };
        let age = match groups {
            [] => field(fields, "age"),
            [Node::Object(group)] => field(group, "age"),
            [_] => return Err(damaged("its key group is not an object")),
            _ => {
                return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                    "the file has {} key groups, which is not supported",
                    groups.len()
                )))
            }
        };
        let last_modified =
            text(fields, "lastmodified")?.ok_or_else(|| damaged("it has no lastmodified"))?;
        let mac_only_encrypted = match field(fields, "mac_only_encrypted") {
            None | Some(Node::Null) => false,
            Some(Node::Bool(b)) => *b,
            Some(_) => return Err(damaged("mac_only_encrypted is not true or false")),
        };
        Ok(Metadata {
            mac_aad: mac_aad(last_modified)
                .ok_or_else(|| damaged("lastmodified is not an RFC 3339 time"))?,
            mac: text(fields, "mac")?,
            age: age_entries(age)?,
            rule: Rule::read(fields)?,
            mac_only_encrypted,
        })
    }
}

fn field<'n>(fields: &'n [(String, Node)], name: &str) -> Option<&'n Node> {
    fields
        .iter()
        .find(|(key, _)| key == name)
        .map(|(_, value)| value)
}

/// A text field of the metadata, if it is set. An empty one counts as not set, as in SOPS.
fn text<'n>(
    fields: &'n [(String, Node)],
    name: &str,
) -> std::result::Result<Option<&'n str>, SourceError> {
    match field(fields, name) {
        None | Some(Node::Null) => Ok(None),
        Some(Node::Str(s)) if s.is_empty() => Ok(None),
        Some(Node::Str(s)) => Ok(Some(s)),
        Some(_) => Err(damaged(&format!("{name} is not text"))),
    }
}

fn age_entries(list: Option<&Node>) -> std::result::Result<Vec<&str>, SourceError> {
    let entries = match list {
        None | Some(Node::Null) => return Ok(Vec::new()),
        Some(Node::Array(entries)) => entries,
        Some(_) => return Err(damaged("age is not a list")),
    };
    entries
        .iter()
        .map(|entry| match entry {
            Node::Object(fields) => {
                text(fields, "enc")?.ok_or_else(|| damaged("an age entry has no enc"))
            }
            _ => Err(damaged("an age entry is not an object")),
        })
        .collect()
}

/// `lastmodified` as SOPS writes it into the MAC's AAD: Go's RFC 3339, whole seconds, `Z` for
/// UTC. A file SOPS wrote holds exactly that already.
fn mac_aad(last_modified: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let time = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(last_modified).ok()?;
    go_rfc3339(&time, false)
}

/// A time as Go formats it: `RFC3339`, or with `nanos` `RFC3339Nano`, whose fraction has no
/// trailing zeros. A zero offset is `Z`. A leap second, which Go refuses, is `None`.
fn go_rfc3339(time: &DateTime<FixedOffset>, nanos: bool) -> Option<String> {
    if time.nanosecond() >= 1_000_000_000 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut text = time.format("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S").to_string();
    if nanos && time.nanosecond() != 0 {
        let fraction = format!("{:09}", time.nanosecond());
        text.push('.');
        text.push_str(fraction.trim_end_matches('0'));
    }
    let offset = time.offset().local_minus_utc();
    if offset == 0 {
        text.push('Z');
    } else {
        let sign = if offset < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        let minutes = offset.abs() / 60;
        text.push_str(&format!("{sign}{:02}:{:02}", minutes / 60, minutes % 60));
    }
    Some(text)
}

/// Which values the file encrypts. A rule is checked against every key on a value's path, its
/// parents' included.
enum Rule {
    UnencryptedSuffix(String),
    EncryptedSuffix(String),
    UnencryptedRegex(Regex),
    EncryptedRegex(Regex),
}

impl Rule {
    fn read(fields: &[(String, Node)]) -> std::result::Result<Rule, SourceError> {
        let mut set = Vec::new();
        for name in RULES {
            if let Some(value) = text(fields, name)? {
                set.push((name, value));
            }
        }
        let (name, value) = match set.as_slice() {
            [] => return Ok(Rule::UnencryptedSuffix(DEFAULT_UNENCRYPTED_SUFFIX.into())),
            [one] => *one,
            _ => {
                return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                    "the file's sops metadata sets more than one of {}",
                    RULES.join(", ")
                )))
            }
        };
        let regex = || {
            RegexBuilder::new(value)
                .size_limit(1 << 20)
                .build()
                .map_err(|_| damaged(&format!("{name} is not a regular expression")))
        };
        match name {
            "unencrypted_suffix" => Ok(Rule::UnencryptedSuffix(value.into())),
            "encrypted_suffix" => Ok(Rule::EncryptedSuffix(value.into())),
            "unencrypted_regex" => Ok(Rule::UnencryptedRegex(regex()?)),
            "encrypted_regex" => Ok(Rule::EncryptedRegex(regex()?)),
            _ => Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                "the file's {name} is not supported: a JSON file has no comments"
            ))),
        }
    }

    fn encrypts(&self, path: &[&str]) -> bool {
        match self {
            Rule::UnencryptedSuffix(s) => !path.iter().any(|key| key.ends_with(s.as_str())),
            Rule::EncryptedSuffix(s) => path.iter().any(|key| key.ends_with(s.as_str())),
            Rule::UnencryptedRegex(r) => !path.iter().any(|key| r.is_match(key)),
            Rule::EncryptedRegex(r) => path.iter().any(|key| r.is_match(key)),
        }
    }
}

/// Unwraps the 32-byte data key from the first age entry this identity opens.
fn data_key(
    entries: &[&str],
    identity: &x25519::Identity,
) -> std::result::Result<Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>, SourceError> {
    let mut wrong_size = false;
    for enc in entries {
        let Ok(decryptor) = age::Decryptor::new_buffered(ArmoredReader::new(enc.as_bytes())) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(reader) = decryptor.decrypt(std::iter::once(identity as &dyn age::Identity)) else {
            continue;
        };
        // One byte more than a key, to see a longer one, and no more: the buffer never grows.
        let mut plain = Zeroizing::new(Vec::with_capacity(33));
        if reader.take(33).read_to_end(&mut plain).is_err() {
            continue;
        }
        if plain.len() != 32 {
            wrong_size = true;
            continue;
        }
        let mut key = Zeroizing::new([0u8; 32]);
        key.copy_from_slice(&plain);
        return Ok(key);
    }
    if wrong_size {
        return Err(SourceError::Invalid(
            "the file's data key is not 32 bytes".into(),
        ));
    }
    Err(SourceError::Denied(NOT_A_RECIPIENT.into()))
}

/// The AAD of the value at `path`: its keys joined with `:`, plus a trailing `:`.
fn aad(path: &[&str]) -> String {
    let mut aad = path.join(":");
    aad.push(':');
    aad
}

/// A path as messages show it, `env:API_KEY`.
fn shown_path(path: &[&str]) -> String {
    path.join(":").escape_debug().to_string()
}

/// One plain leaf, kept only as far as the layout needs: text, or something else.
enum Plain {
    Text(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>),
    Other,
}

impl Plain {
    /// The text, if it is UTF-8 text.
    fn into_text(self) -> Option<Zeroizing<String>> {
        let Plain::Text(mut bytes) = self else {
            return None;
        };
        std::str::from_utf8(&bytes).ok()?;
        let text = String::from_utf8(std::mem::take(&mut *bytes)).expect("checked UTF-8");
        Some(Zeroizing::new(text))
    }
}

/// A value as SOPS types it, plain.
enum Value {
    Str(Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>),
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    Bool(bool),
    /// The time as Go's `RFC3339Nano` text.
    Time(String),
}

/// The bytes SOPS hashes into the MAC for a value (Go's `ToBytes`): the text, the number in
/// decimal (a float as short as it round-trips, never with an exponent), or `True`/`False`.
fn mac_bytes(value: &Value) -> Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> {
    Zeroizing::new(match value {
        Value::Str(bytes) => bytes.to_vec(),
        Value::Int(n) => n.to_string().into_bytes(),
        Value::Float(f) => go_float(*f).into_bytes(),
        Value::Bool(true) => b"True".to_vec(),
        Value::Bool(false) => b"False".to_vec(),
        Value::Time(text) => text.clone().into_bytes(),
    })
}

/// A float as Go's `strconv.FormatFloat(f, 'f', -1, 64)` writes it. Rust's `Display` gives the
/// same shortest digits with no exponent.
fn go_float(f: f64) -> String {
    if f.is_nan() {
        "NaN".into()
    } else if f.is_infinite() {
        if f > 0.0 { "+Inf" } else { "-Inf" }.into()
    } else {
        f.to_string()
    }
}

/// Go's `strconv.ParseBool`.
fn go_bool(text: &str) -> Option<bool> {
    match text {
        "1" | "t" | "T" | "TRUE" | "true" | "True" => Some(true),
        "0" | "f" | "F" | "FALSE" | "false" | "False" => Some(false),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Why one encrypted value could not be used.
enum ValueError {
    /// It is not `ENC[AES256_GCM,…]` with base64 parts of the right sizes.
    NotSops,
    /// AES-GCM refused it: changed, moved or made with another key.
    DoesNotDecrypt,
    /// Its type is one Dots does not read, or no type at all.
    Unsupported,
    /// The plain text is not a value of its type.
    NotItsType,
}

/// Decrypts one `ENC[…]` value with `aad`.
fn decrypt_value(
    cipher: &Aes256Gcm32,
    text: &str,
    aad: &[u8],
) -> std::result::Result<Value, ValueError> {
    let parts = ENCRYPTED.captures(text).ok_or(ValueError::NotSops)?;
    let decode = |i: usize| STANDARD.decode(&parts[i]).map_err(|_| ValueError::NotSops);
    let mut plain = Zeroizing::new(decode(1)?);
    let iv = decode(2)?;
    let tag = decode(3)?;
    if iv.len() != 32 || tag.len() != 16 {
        return Err(ValueError::NotSops);
    }
    cipher
        .decrypt_in_place_detached(
            Nonce::<U32>::from_slice(&iv),
            aad,
            &mut plain,
            Tag::from_slice(&tag),
        )
        .map_err(|_| ValueError::DoesNotDecrypt)?;
    let as_text = || std::str::from_utf8(&plain).map_err(|_| ValueError::NotItsType);
    Ok(match &parts[4] {
        "str" => Value::Str(plain),
        "int" => Value::Int(as_text()?.parse().map_err(|_| ValueError::NotItsType)?),
        "float" => Value::Float(as_text()?.parse().map_err(|_| ValueError::NotItsType)?),
        "bool" => Value::Bool(go_bool(as_text()?).ok_or(ValueError::NotItsType)?),
        "time" => {
            let time =
                DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(as_text()?).map_err(|_| ValueError::NotItsType)?;
            Value::Time(go_rfc3339(&time, true).ok_or(ValueError::NotItsType)?)
        }
        _ => return Err(ValueError::Unsupported),
    })
}

/// The walk over the file's values: decrypts each leaf and feeds the MAC.
struct Decrypting<'m> {
    cipher: Aes256Gcm32,
    metadata: &'m Metadata<'m>,
    hash: Sha512,
}

impl<'m> Decrypting<'m> {
    fn new(data_key: &[u8; 32], metadata: &'m Metadata<'m>) -> Decrypting<'m> {
        let mut hash = Sha512::new();
        if metadata.mac_only_encrypted {
            hash.update(MAC_ONLY_ENCRYPTED_INIT);
        }
        Decrypting {
            cipher: Aes256Gcm32::new(Key::<Aes256Gcm32>::from_slice(data_key)),
            metadata,
            hash,
        }
    }

    /// Walks `node` at `path`, in the file's order. A leaf gives its plain value; an object,
    /// an array or `null` gives `None`. `null` is not part of the MAC.
    fn walk<'n>(
        &mut self,
        node: &'n Node,
        path: &mut Vec<&'n str>,
    ) -> std::result::Result<Option<Plain>, SourceError> {
        match node {
            Node::Null => Ok(None),
            Node::Array(items) => {
                for item in items {
                    self.walk(item, path)?;
                }
                Ok(None)
            }
            Node::Object(fields) => {
                for (key, value) in fields {
                    path.push(key.as_str());
                    self.walk(value, path)?;
                    path.pop();
                }
                Ok(None)
            }
            leaf => self.leaf(leaf, path).map(Some),
        }
    }

    fn leaf(&mut self, node: &Node, path: &[&str]) -> std::result::Result<Plain, SourceError> {
        let encrypted = self.metadata.rule.encrypts(path);
        let value = match node {
            // SOPS leaves an empty string as it is, encrypted or not.
            Node::Str(s) if s.is_empty() => Value::Str(Zeroizing::new(Vec::new())),
            Node::Str(s) if encrypted => decrypt_value(&self.cipher, s, aad(path).as_bytes())
                .map_err(|e| {
                    let at = shown_path(path);
                    match e {
                        ValueError::NotSops => SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                            "the file's value at {at} is not a SOPS value"
                        )),
                        ValueError::DoesNotDecrypt => SourceError::Denied(format!(
                            "the file's value at {at} does not decrypt: the file was changed"
                        )),
                        ValueError::Unsupported => SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                            "the file's value at {at} has a type Dots does not read"
                        )),
                        ValueError::NotItsType => SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                            "the file's value at {at} does not match its type"
                        )),
                    }
                })?,
            _ if encrypted => {
                return Err(SourceError::Invalid(format!(
                    "the file's value at {} is not encrypted",
                    shown_path(path)
                )))
            }
            Node::Str(s) => Value::Str(Zeroizing::new(s.as_bytes().to_vec())),
            Node::Int(n) => Value::Int(*n),
            Node::Float(f) => Value::Float(*f),
            Node::Bool(b) => Value::Bool(*b),
            Node::Null | Node::Array(_) | Node::Object(_) => unreachable!("walk gives leaves"),
        };
        if encrypted || !self.metadata.mac_only_encrypted {
            self.hash.update(&*mac_bytes(&value));
        }
        Ok(match value {
            Value::Str(bytes) => Plain::Text(bytes),
            _ => Plain::Other,
        })
    }

    /// Checks the walk's MAC against the file's, in constant time.
    fn check_mac(self, metadata: &Metadata) -> std::result::Result<(), SourceError> {
        let mismatch = || SourceError::Denied(MAC_MISMATCH.into());
        let digest = self.hash.finalize();
        let mut computed = Zeroizing::new(String::with_capacity(128));
        for byte in digest {
            computed.push_str(&format!("{byte:02X}"));
        }
        let mac = metadata.mac.ok_or_else(mismatch)?;
        let file_mac = match decrypt_value(&self.cipher, mac, metadata.mac_aad.as_bytes()) {
            Ok(Value::Str(bytes)) => bytes,
            Ok(_) => return Err(SourceError::Invalid("the file's MAC is not text".into())),
            Err(ValueError::NotSops) => {
                return Err(SourceError::Invalid(
                    "the file's MAC is not a SOPS value".into(),
                ))
            }
            Err(_) => return Err(mismatch()),
        };
        if bool::from(file_mac.as_slice().ct_eq(computed.as_bytes())) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(mismatch())
        }
    }
}

/// The file's JSON, keeping every object's keys in the file's order. A number is an `Int` when
/// it fits an `i64`, else a `Float`, as SOPS reads it.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Node {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Int(i64),
    Float(f64),
    Str(String),
    Array(Vec<Node>),
    Object(Vec<(String, Node)>),
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Node {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> std::result::Result<Node, D::Error> {
        d.deserialize_any(NodeVisitor)
    }
}

struct NodeVisitor;

impl<'de> Visitor<'de> for NodeVisitor {
    type Value = Node;

    fn expecting(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("JSON")
    }

    fn visit_unit<E: de::Error>(self) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Null)
    }

    fn visit_bool<E: de::Error>(self, v: bool) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Bool(v))
    }

    fn visit_i64<E: de::Error>(self, v: i64) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Int(v))
    }

    fn visit_u64<E: de::Error>(self, v: u64) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(i64::try_from(v).map_or(Node::Float(v as f64), Node::Int))
    }

    fn visit_f64<E: de::Error>(self, v: f64) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Float(v))
    }

    fn visit_str<E: de::Error>(self, v: &str) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Str(v.to_string()))
    }

    fn visit_string<E: de::Error>(self, v: String) -> std::result::Result<Node, E> {
        Ok(Node::Str(v))
    }

    fn visit_seq<A: SeqAccess<'de>>(self, mut seq: A) -> std::result::Result<Node, A::Error> {
        let mut items = Vec::new();
        while let Some(item) = seq.next_element()? {
            items.push(item);
        }
        Ok(Node::Array(items))
    }

    fn visit_map<A: MapAccess<'de>>(self, mut map: A) -> std::result::Result<Node, A::Error> {
        let mut fields = Vec::new();
        while let Some(field) = map.next_entry()? {
            fields.push(field);
        }
        Ok(Node::Object(fields))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use aes_gcm::aead::AeadInPlace;

    use super::*;

    const KEY: [u8; 32] = [7; 32];

    fn cipher() -> Aes256Gcm32 {
        Aes256Gcm32::new(Key::<Aes256Gcm32>::from_slice(&KEY))
    }

    /// Encrypts `plain` as SOPS would, with a fixed IV.
    fn seal(plain: &str, kind: &str, aad: &str) -> String {
        let iv = [9u8; 32];
        let mut data = plain.as_bytes().to_vec();
        let tag = cipher()
            .encrypt_in_place_detached(Nonce::<U32>::from_slice(&iv), aad.as_bytes(), &mut data)
            .unwrap();
        format!(
            "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:{},iv:{},tag:{},type:{kind}]",
            STANDARD.encode(&data),
            STANDARD.encode(iv),
            STANDARD.encode(tag)
        )
    }

    fn metadata(rule: Rule) -> Metadata<'static> {
        Metadata {
            mac_aad: "2026-10-23T18:52:25Z".into(),
            mac: None,
            age: Vec::new(),
            rule,
            mac_only_encrypted: false,
        }
    }

    fn default_rule() -> Rule {
        Rule::UnencryptedSuffix(DEFAULT_UNENCRYPTED_SUFFIX.into())
    }

    fn walk(json: &str, rule: Rule) -> std::result::Result<(), SourceError> {
        let node: Node = serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap();
        let metadata = metadata(rule);
        let mut run = Decrypting::new(&KEY, &metadata);
        run.walk(&node, &mut Vec::new()).map(|_| ())
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_aad_is_the_path_joined_with_colons_and_a_trailing_colon() {
        assert_eq!(aad(&["env", "API_KEY"]), "env:API_KEY:");
        assert_eq!(aad(&["foo"]), "foo:");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_nested_leaf_and_an_array_leaf_decrypt_with_their_aad() {
        let json = format!(
            r#"{{"a": {{"b": {{"c": "{}"}}, "list": ["{}", {{"d": "{}"}}, ["{}"]]}}}}"#,
            seal("x", "str", "a:b:c:"),
            seal("y", "str", "a:list:"),
            seal("z", "str", "a:list:d:"),
            seal("w", "str", "a:list:"),
        );
        assert!(walk(&json, default_rule()).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_array_index_in_the_aad_does_not_decrypt() {
        let json = format!(r#"{{"list": ["{}"]}}"#, seal("y", "str", "list:0:"));
        let e = walk(&json, default_rule()).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(
            e,
            SourceError::Denied(
                "the file's value at list does not decrypt: the file was changed".into()
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_value_moved_to_another_key_does_not_decrypt() {
        let json = format!(r#"{{"a": "{}"}}"#, seal("x", "str", "b:"));
        assert!(matches!(
            walk(&json, default_rule()),
            Err(SourceError::Denied(_))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_mac_bytes_follow_go() {
        let bytes = |v: Value| String::from_utf8(mac_bytes(&v).to_vec()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Bool(true)), "True");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Bool(false)), "False");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Int(7)), "7");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Int(-42)), "-42");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), "-9223372036854775808");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(1.5)), "1.5");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(0.25)), "0.25");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(1.0)), "1");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(-0.0)), "-0");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(0.1 + 0.2)), "0.30000000000000004");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(1e21)), "1000000000000000000000");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(1e-7)), "0.0000001");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(f64::INFINITY)), "+Inf");
        assert_eq!(bytes(Value::Float(f64::NAN)), "NaN");
        let text = Value::Str(Zeroizing::new(b"plain".to_vec()));
        assert_eq!(bytes(text), "plain");
    }

    #[test]
    fn decrypted_values_are_typed_as_sops_types_them() {
        let open =
            |plain: &str, kind: &str| decrypt_value(&cipher(), &seal(plain, kind, "k:"), b"k:");
        assert!(matches!(open("12", "int"), Ok(Value::Int(12))));
        assert!(matches!(open("1.5", "float"), Ok(Value::Float(f)) if f == 1.5));
        assert!(matches!(open("True", "bool"), Ok(Value::Bool(true))));
        assert!(matches!(open("false", "bool"), Ok(Value::Bool(false))));
        assert!(matches!(open("x", "int"), Err(ValueError::NotItsType)));
        assert!(matches!(open("yes", "bool"), Err(ValueError::NotItsType)));
        assert!(matches!(open("x", "bytes"), Err(ValueError::Unsupported)));
        assert!(matches!(open("x", "comment"), Err(ValueError::Unsupported)));
        assert!(matches!(open("x", "other"), Err(ValueError::Unsupported)));
        match open("2026-10-23T20:52:25.500+02:00", "time") {
            Ok(Value::Time(t)) => assert_eq!(t, "2026-10-23T20:52:25.5+02:00"),
            _ => panic!("a time"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_value_that_is_not_sops_syntax_is_refused_as_such() {
        let c = cipher();
        for text in [
            "plain",
            "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:abc",
            "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:@@@,iv:AAAA,tag:AAAA,type:str]",
            // An IV of 12 bytes, not 32.
            "ENC[AES256_GCM,data:AAAA,iv:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA,tag:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==,type:str]",
        ] {
            assert!(
                matches!(decrypt_value(&c, text, b"k:"), Err(ValueError::NotSops)),
                "{text}"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn go_parses_bools_this_way() {
        for t in ["1", "t", "T", "TRUE", "true", "True"] {
            assert_eq!(go_bool(t), Some(true), "{t}");
        }
        for f in ["0", "f", "F", "FALSE", "false", "False"] {
            assert_eq!(go_bool(f), Some(false), "{f}");
        }
        assert_eq!(go_bool("yes"), None);
        assert_eq!(go_bool("tRUE"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn last_modified_is_formatted_as_go_does_for_the_mac() {
        assert_eq!(
            mac_aad("2026-10-23T18:52:25Z").unwrap(),
            "2026-10-23T18:52:25Z"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mac_aad("2026-10-23T18:52:25+00:00").unwrap(),
            "2026-10-23T18:52:25Z"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mac_aad("2026-10-23T18:52:25.75Z").unwrap(),
            "2026-10-23T18:52:25Z"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            mac_aad("2026-10-23T14:52:25-04:00").unwrap(),
            "2026-10-23T14:52:25-04:00"
        );
        assert_eq!(mac_aad("yesterday"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_rules_check_every_key_on_the_path() {
        let path = ["db_unencrypted", "password"];
        assert!(!default_rule().encrypts(&path));
        assert!(default_rule().encrypts(&["db", "password"]));
        let suffix = Rule::EncryptedSuffix("_secret".into());
        assert!(suffix.encrypts(&["db_secret", "password"]));
        assert!(!suffix.encrypts(&["db", "password"]));
        let only = Rule::EncryptedRegex(Regex::new("^(env|policy)$").unwrap());
        assert!(only.encrypts(&["env", "API_KEY"]));
        assert!(!only.encrypts(&["extra", "env_x"]));
        let not = Rule::UnencryptedRegex(Regex::new("^public").unwrap());
        assert!(!not.encrypts(&["public_notes", "x"]));
        assert!(not.encrypts(&["notes", "x"]));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_mac_only_encrypted_start_is_sha256_of_sops() {
        use sha2::Sha256;
        assert_eq!(Sha256::digest(b"sops").as_slice(), MAC_ONLY_ENCRYPTED_INIT);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_tree_keeps_the_files_order_and_number_kinds() {
        let node: Node =
            serde_json::from_str(r#"{"b": 1, "a": [1.5, 18446744073709551615, true, null]}"#)
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            node,
            Node::Object(vec![
                ("b".into(), Node::Int(1)),
                (
                    "a".into(),
                    Node::Array(vec![
                        Node::Float(1.5),
                        Node::Float(18446744073709551615u64 as f64),
                        Node::Bool(true),
                        Node::Null,
                    ])
                ),
            ])
        );
    }
}
```

### Task 8: The org service: join, update, remove, refresh and status

Spec §6.1 and §6.4: the `Orgs` service holds each joined org's state. It joins and updates only on a fetch whose policy verifies, maps each fetch outcome to a status, keeps and expires the offline copy, and loads it at start.

- Create: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/service.rs`
- Modify: `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/mod.rs`, `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/policy.rs` (`OrgPolicy::summary`), `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/sources/sops.rs` (`NOT_A_RECIPIENT` made `pub`), `crates/dots-core/src/store/orgs.rs` (`list_org_names`), `crates/dots-admin/src/policy.rs` (calls `policy.summary()`)

```rust
//! A harness for the `Orgs` service (env vault spec §6): a store and secrets in memory, the test
//! protector, a clock the test moves by hand, a fake OpenBao, and an org key that signs real
//! policies with minisign. `Scripted` is a source that answers what a test tells it to, for
//! the cases a real server can't be made to give.

use std::io::Cursor;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration as StdDuration;

use async_trait::async_trait;
use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use dots_core::store::Store;
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    envelope, http_client_with_timeout, BaoAuth, Fetched, JoinCode, OpenBaoSettings, OrgSummary,
    Orgs, Protector, SopsSettings, Source, SourceCreds, SourceError, SourceFactory, SourceSettings,
    TestProtector, OFFLINE_DIR,
};
use dots_core::vault::MemorySecrets;
use minisign::KeyPair;
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use tempfile::TempDir;
use tokio::sync::{Notify, Semaphore};
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

use super::clock::FakeClock;
use super::fake_openbao::FakeOpenBao;

pub const ACME: &str = "acme-eng";
pub const ACME_NAME: &str = "Acme Engineering";
/// The person's OpenBao token, which the fake accepts.
pub const TOKEN: &str = "hvs.org-test-token-51c2e0";
/// Where the harness's clock stands until a test moves it.
pub const START: &str = "2026-10-22T09:00:00Z";
/// The `issued_at` of the policies the harness serves.
pub const ISSUED: &str = "2026-10-22T08:00:00Z";

pub fn at(text: &str) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(text)
        .unwrap()
        .with_timezone(&Utc)
}

/// A time as the service writes it: RFC 3339, UTC, milliseconds.
pub fn stamp(at: DateTime<Utc>) -> String {
    at.to_rfc3339_opts(chrono::SecondsFormat::Millis, true)
}

/// A new org key pair, as `dots-admin keygen` makes one.
pub fn keys() -> KeyPair {
    KeyPair::generate_unencrypted_keypair().unwrap()
}

/// The join code's `policy_key`: the bare `RW…` line.
pub fn public_key(keys: &KeyPair) -> String {
    keys.pk.to_base64()
}

/// The signed text of `policy`, as `dots-admin policy sign` writes it.
pub fn sign(keys: &KeyPair, policy: &str) -> String {
    let signature = minisign::sign(Some(&keys.pk), &keys.sk, Cursor::new(policy), None, None)
        .unwrap()
        .to_string();
    envelope(policy, &signature)
}

/// A policy for `org_id` issued at `issued_at`: the defaults, with `extra`'s fields over them.
pub fn policy(org_id: &str, issued_at: &str, extra: Value) -> String {
    let mut policy = json!({"v": 1, "org_id": org_id, "issued_at": issued_at});
    for (key, value) in extra.as_object().unwrap() {
        policy[key] = value.clone();
    }
    policy.to_string()
}

pub fn token() -> SourceCreds {
    SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new(TOKEN.into()),
    }
}

/// OpenBao with token sign-in, the `secret` mount and `path`.
pub fn openbao(address: &str, path: &str) -> SourceSettings {
    SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
        address: address.into(),
        mount: "secret".into(),
        path: path.into(),
        auth: BaoAuth::Token,
        auth_mount: None,
        namespace: None,
    })
}

pub fn sops_at(location: &str) -> SourceSettings {
    SourceSettings::Sops(SopsSettings {
        location: location.into(),
    })
}

/// The join code an admin hands out for `org_id`.
pub fn code(org_id: &str, name: &str, source: SourceSettings, keys: &KeyPair) -> String {
    JoinCode {
        v: 1,
        org_id: org_id.into(),
        name: name.into(),
        source,
        policy_key: public_key(keys),
    }
    .encode()
}

/// One service on a data folder of its own, with its fake OpenBao and org key.
pub struct OrgsHarness {
    pub data: TempDir,
    pub store: Store,
    pub secrets: Arc<MemorySecrets>,
    pub protector: Arc<dyn Protector>,
    pub clock: Arc<FakeClock>,
    pub bao: FakeOpenBao,
    pub keys: KeyPair,
    pub orgs: Orgs,
}

impl OrgsHarness {
    pub async fn new() -> OrgsHarness {
        OrgsHarness::with_protector(Arc::new(TestProtector)).await
    }

    pub async fn with_protector(protector: Arc<dyn Protector>) -> OrgsHarness {
        let data = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let store = Store::open(&data.path().join("dots.db")).await.unwrap();
        let bao = FakeOpenBao::start().await;
        bao.allow_token(TOKEN, false);
        let secrets = Arc::new(MemorySecrets::new());
        let clock = FakeClock::new(at(START));
        let orgs = service(&store, &secrets, &protector, &data, &clock);
        OrgsHarness {
            data,
            store,
            secrets,
            protector,
            clock,
            bao,
            keys: keys(),
            orgs,
        }
    }

    /// Another service on the same data, secrets and clock, as after a restart. It has loaded
    /// nothing yet.
    pub fn service(&self) -> Orgs {
        service(
            &self.store,
            &self.secrets,
            &self.protector,
            &self.data,
            &self.clock,
        )
    }

    /// `data_dir/vault`.
    pub fn vault_dir(&self) -> PathBuf {
        self.data.path().join(OFFLINE_DIR)
    }

    /// Where the offline copy of `org_id` is.
    pub fn copy_path(&self, org_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.vault_dir().join(format!("{org_id}.bin"))
    }

    pub fn now(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> {
        dots_core::scheduler::Clock::now(self.clock.as_ref())
    }

    /// Moves the clock on by `by`.
    pub fn advance(&self, by: Duration) {
        self.clock.set(self.now() + by);
    }

    /// Serves `entries` and the signed `policy` at `secret/<path>` of the fake.
    pub fn serve(&self, path: &str, entries: Value, signed: &str) {
        self.bao.put_env("secret", path, entries);
        self.bao.put_policy("secret", path, signed);
    }

    /// Serves Acme's `entries` at `secret/dots`, with a policy issued at `ISSUED` and `extra`.
    pub fn serve_acme(&self, entries: Value, extra: Value) {
        let signed = sign(&self.keys, &policy(ACME, ISSUED, extra));
        self.serve("dots", entries, &signed);
    }

    /// Acme's join code: the fake at `secret/dots`, and the harness's key.
    pub fn acme_code(&self) -> String {
        self.code_at(ACME, ACME_NAME, "dots")
    }

    /// The join code of `org_id` at `secret/<path>` of the fake, with the harness's key.
    pub fn code_at(&self, org_id: &str, name: &str, path: &str) -> String {
        code(org_id, name, openbao(&self.bao.address(), path), &self.keys)
    }

    /// Serves Acme and joins it with the token.
    pub async fn join_acme(&self, entries: Value, extra: Value) -> OrgSummary {
        self.serve_acme(entries, extra);
        self.orgs
            .join(&self.acme_code(), Some(token()))
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }

    /// How many times the fake was asked for `secret/<path>/env`.
    pub fn env_reads(&self, path: &str) -> usize {
        self.bao.count(&format!("/v1/secret/data/{path}/env"))
    }
}

fn service(
    store: &Store,
    secrets: &Arc<MemorySecrets>,
    protector: &Arc<dyn Protector>,
    data: &TempDir,
    clock: &Arc<FakeClock>,
) -> Orgs {
    Orgs::new(
        store.clone(),
        secrets.clone(),
        protector.clone(),
        data.path().join(OFFLINE_DIR),
        http_client_with_timeout(StdDuration::from_secs(5)),
        clock.clone(),
    )
}

/// A source that answers what the test sets, after a gate the test may hold shut. It records
/// the sign-in details of every fetch.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Scripted(Arc<ScriptedState>);

#[derive(Default)]
struct ScriptedState {
    answer: Mutex<Option<Result<Fetched, SourceError>>>,
    creds: Mutex<Vec<SourceCreds>>,
    gate: Mutex<Option<Arc<Semaphore>>>,
    entered: Notify,
}

impl Scripted {
    pub fn new() -> Scripted {
        Scripted::default()
    }

    /// What every fetch gives from now on.
    pub fn answer(&self, answer: Result<Fetched, SourceError>) {
        *self.0.answer.lock().unwrap() = Some(answer);
    }

    /// Every fetch gives `entries` and the signed `policy`.
    pub fn serve(&self, entries: &[(&str, &str)], signed: &str) {
        self.answer(Ok(Fetched {
            entries: entries
                .iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), Zeroizing::new(v.to_string())))
                .collect(),
            policy: signed.to_string(),
        }));
    }

    /// The sign-in details each fetch was given, in order.
    pub fn creds(&self) -> Vec<SourceCreds> {
        self.0.creds.lock().unwrap().clone()
    }

    /// Shuts the gate: each fetch from now on waits for a permit added to the semaphore.
    pub fn hold(&self) -> Arc<Semaphore> {
        let gate = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(0));
        *self.0.gate.lock().unwrap() = Some(gate.clone());
        gate
    }

    /// Returns once a fetch has begun (or had begun since the last call).
    pub async fn entered(&self) {
        tokio::time::timeout(StdDuration::from_secs(10), self.0.entered.notified())
            .await
            .expect("no fetch began");
    }

    /// Every org's source is this one.
    pub fn factory(&self) -> SourceFactory {
        let this = self.clone();
        Arc::new(move |_: &SourceSettings| Box::new(this.clone()) as Box<dyn Source>)
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl Source for Scripted {
    async fn fetch(&self, creds: &SourceCreds) -> Result<Fetched, SourceError> {
        self.0.creds.lock().unwrap().push(creds.clone());
        self.0.entered.notify_one();
        let gate = self.0.gate.lock().unwrap().clone();
        if let Some(gate) = gate {
            gate.acquire().await.unwrap().forget();
        }
        self.0
            .answer
            .lock()
            .unwrap()
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Err(SourceError::Unreachable("no answer is set".into())))
    }
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_orgs_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The `Orgs` service (env vault spec §6.1, §6.2 and §6.4): joining an org, changing its
//! settings, leaving it, and what each outcome of a fetch does to its status, its values and
//! its offline copy. The fetches go to the fake OpenBao and the SOPS fixtures, and the policies
//! are signed with minisign. No error or summary ever holds a value.

mod common;

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::thread::ThreadId;
use std::time::Duration as StdDuration;

use chrono::Duration;
use common::fake_openbao::{Failure, FakeOpenBao};
use common::orgs::{
    at, code, keys, openbao, policy, public_key, sign, sops_at, stamp, token, OrgsHarness,
    Scripted, ACME, ACME_NAME, ISSUED, START, TOKEN,
};
use common::spec;
use dots_core::model::DotSpec;
use dots_core::vault::entries::EntryKind;
use dots_core::vault::org::sources::sops::public_key as age_public_key;
use dots_core::vault::org::{
    key_fingerprint, parse_policy, read_offline, verify_policy, write_offline, OfflineCopy,
    OrgEntry, OrgLookup, OrgRow, OrgStatus, OrgSummary, Orgs, Protector, SourceCreds, SourceError,
    TestProtector, RETRY_AFTER,
};
use dots_core::vault::{redact, Grants};
use dots_core::{Error, Result};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use sqlx::sqlite::SqlitePool;
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

const API_KEY: &str = "org-secret-api-key-3f9a1c";
const LOG_LEVEL: &str = "org-plain-log-level-77d2";
const ROTATED: &str = "org-secret-rotated-key-8c41e5";
const OTHER_TOKEN: &str = "hvs.other-person-token-6d0f";

/// Every value a test serves, which no error, summary or listing may hold.
const VALUES: &[&str] = &[API_KEY, LOG_LEVEL, ROTATED, TOKEN, OTHER_TOKEN];

fn entries() -> Value {
    json!({"API_KEY": API_KEY, "LOG_LEVEL": LOG_LEVEL})
}

/// `LOG_LEVEL` is plain; Personal entries fill in where the org has no entry.
fn acme_policy() -> Value {
    json!({"plain": ["LOG_LEVEL"], "personal": "fallback"})
}

fn value(value: &str, is_plain: bool) -> OrgLookup {
    OrgLookup::Value {
        value: Zeroizing::new(value.into()),
        is_plain,
    }
}

fn assert_clean(text: &str) {
    for value in VALUES {
        assert!(!text.contains(value), "{text:?} holds {value:?}");
    }
}

/// The error's text, checked for values both ways it can be printed.
fn error_text(e: &Error) -> String {
    assert_clean(&format!("{e:?}"));
    let text = e.to_string();
    assert_clean(&text);
    text
}

fn other(e: Error) -> String {
    error_text(&e);
    match e {
        Error::Other(why) => why,
        e => panic!("expected Error::Other, got {e:?}"),
    }
}

fn invalid(e: Error) -> String {
    let text = error_text(&e);
    match e {
        Error::Invalid(why) => why,
        e => panic!("expected Error::Invalid ({text}), got {e:?}"),
    }
}

fn status(summary: &OrgSummary) -> OrgStatus {
    assert_clean(&serde_json::to_string(summary).unwrap());
    summary.status.clone()
}

async fn status_of(orgs: &Orgs, org_id: &str) -> OrgStatus {
    status(&orgs.summary(org_id).await.expect("the org is listed"))
}

fn copy_of(h: &OrgsHarness, org_id: &str) -> Option<OfflineCopy> {
    read_offline(&h.vault_dir(), &TestProtector, org_id).unwrap()
}

fn names(copy: &OfflineCopy) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
    copy.entries
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), v.to_string()))
        .collect()
}

fn stored_creds(h: &OrgsHarness, org_id: &str) -> Option<SourceCreds> {
    SourceCreds::load(h.secrets.as_ref(), org_id).unwrap()
}

/// `START` plus `hours`, as the service writes it.
fn start_plus(hours: i64) -> String {
    stamp(at(START) + Duration::hours(hours))
}

fn fixture(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("tests/fixtures/sops")
        .join(name)
}

/// The secret line of a fixture identity file.
fn fixture_identity(file: &str) -> String {
    std::fs::read_to_string(fixture(file))
        .unwrap()
        .lines()
        .find(|line| line.starts_with("AGE-SECRET-KEY-1"))
        .unwrap()
        .to_string()
}

fn dot_spec(name: &str) -> DotSpec {
    let mut spec = spec(name);
    spec.variables = Grants(BTreeMap::from([
        ("shell".to_string(), vec!["LOG_LEVEL".to_string()]),
        ("mcp:github".to_string(), vec!["API_KEY".to_string()]),
    ]));
    spec
}

// Join

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_join_fetches_verifies_and_keeps_the_row_the_copy_and_the_creds() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    let summary = h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;

    let accepted = parse_policy(&policy(ACME, ISSUED, acme_policy())).unwrap();
    let expected = OrgSummary {
        id: ACME.into(),
        name: ACME_NAME.into(),
        source_kind: "openbao".into(),
        address: h.bao.address(),
        key_fingerprint: key_fingerprint(&public_key(&h.keys)).unwrap(),
        status: OrgStatus::Connected,
        status_text: "connected".into(),
        last_fetch_at: Some(start_plus(0)),
        copy_until: Some(start_plus(24)),
        policy_summary: accepted.summary(),
    };
    assert_eq!(summary, expected);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.summaries().await, vec![expected.clone()]);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.policy(ACME), Some(accepted));
    let json = serde_json::to_value(&summary).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(json["status"], "connected");
    assert_clean(&json.to_string());

    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        row,
        OrgRow {
            id: ACME.into(),
            name: ACME_NAME.into(),
            source: openbao(&h.bao.address(), "dots"),
            policy_key: public_key(&h.keys),
            last_issued_at: Some(ISSUED.into()),
            last_fetch_at: Some(start_plus(0)),
            joined_at: start_plus(0),
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), Some(token()));
    let copy = copy_of(&h, ACME).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(copy.fetched_at, start_plus(0));
    assert_eq!(
        names(&copy),
        BTreeMap::from([
            ("API_KEY".to_string(), API_KEY.to_string()),
            ("LOG_LEVEL".to_string(), LOG_LEVEL.to_string()),
        ])
    );
    verify_policy(&copy.policy, &public_key(&h.keys), ACME).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
    assert_eq!(
        h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "log_level").await,
        value(LOG_LEVEL, true)
    );
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "MISSING").await, OrgLookup::NotDefined);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup("beta", "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Removed);
}

/// After a failed join, nothing of the org is kept.
async fn assert_nothing_kept(h: &OrgsHarness) {
    assert_eq!(h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap(), None);
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(h, ACME), None);
    assert!(!h.copy_path(ACME).exists());
    assert!(h.orgs.summaries().await.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.summary(ACME).await, None);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Removed);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_join_whose_fetch_or_policy_fails_keeps_nothing() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.serve_acme(entries(), acme_policy());

    // The source refuses the token.
    let wrong = SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new(OTHER_TOKEN.into()),
    };
    let e = h.orgs.join(&h.acme_code(), Some(wrong)).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        other(e),
        format!(
            "could not join Acme Engineering: {} refused access to secret/dots/env (HTTP 403)",
            h.bao.address()
        )
    );
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;

    // The source can't be reached.
    let gone = FakeOpenBao::start().await;
    let address = gone.address();
    drop(gone);
    let dead = code(ACME, ACME_NAME, openbao(&address, "dots"), &h.keys);
    let why = other(h.orgs.join(&dead, Some(token())).await.unwrap_err());
    assert!(
        why.starts_with(&format!(
            "could not join Acme Engineering: cannot reach {address}"
        )),
        "{why}"
    );
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;

    // The source has nothing at the path.
    let empty = h.code_at(ACME, ACME_NAME, "nothing");
    let why = other(h.orgs.join(&empty, Some(token())).await.unwrap_err());
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        "could not join Acme Engineering: no secrets at secret/nothing/env"
    );
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;

    // The policy is signed by another key.
    let signed = sign(&keys(), &policy(ACME, ISSUED, json!({})));
    h.serve("dots", entries(), &signed);
    let why = other(
        h.orgs
            .join(&h.acme_code(), Some(token()))
            .await
            .unwrap_err(),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        "could not join Acme Engineering: policy invalid: signature does not match"
    );
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;

    // The policy is for another org.
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy("other-org", ISSUED, json!({})));
    h.serve("dots", entries(), &signed);
    let why = other(
        h.orgs
            .join(&h.acme_code(), Some(token()))
            .await
            .unwrap_err(),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        why,
        "could not join Acme Engineering: policy invalid: for org 'other-org', not 'acme-eng'"
    );
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;

    // Once the source and the policy are right, the join works.
    h.serve_acme(entries(), acme_policy());
    let summary = h.orgs.join(&h.acme_code(), Some(token())).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn joining_an_org_already_joined_is_refused_and_keeps_its_creds() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let reads = h.env_reads("dots");

    let other_token = SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new(OTHER_TOKEN.into()),
    };
    let e = h
        .orgs
        .join(&h.acme_code(), Some(other_token))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, Error::Conflict(_)), "{e:?}");
    assert_eq!(
        error_text(&e),
        "conflict: the org 'acme-eng' is already joined on this PC; use Update to change its \
         settings"
    );
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), reads, "nothing is fetched");
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), Some(token()));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn creds_must_fit_the_source_and_none_is_only_for_sops() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.serve_acme(entries(), acme_policy());

    let e = h.orgs.join(&h.acme_code(), None).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "joining Acme Engineering needs your sign-in details for its OpenBao"
    );
    let login = SourceCreds::Login {
        username: Zeroizing::new("ana".into()),
        password: Zeroizing::new(OTHER_TOKEN.into()),
    };
    let e = h.orgs.join(&h.acme_code(), Some(login)).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(invalid(e), "this org's OpenBao signs in with a token");
    assert!(h.bao.calls().is_empty(), "nothing is fetched");
    assert_nothing_kept(&h).await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn rejoining_a_removed_org_re_attaches_its_dots() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let dot = h
        .store
        .create_dot(&dot_spec("Triage"), Some(ACME))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(h.store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap(), dot);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Removed);

    h.orgs.join(&h.acme_code(), Some(token())).await.unwrap();
    let again = h.store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(again, dot);
    let org_id = again.org_id.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        h.orgs.lookup(&org_id, "API_KEY").await,
        value(API_KEY, false)
    );
}

// Remove

#[tokio::test]
async fn remove_wipes_the_copy_the_creds_and_the_row_and_the_dots_stay() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let dot = h
        .store
        .create_dot(&dot_spec("Triage"), Some(ACME))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(h.copy_path(ACME).exists());

    h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert!(!h.copy_path(ACME).exists());
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), None);
    assert_eq!(h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap(), None);
    assert!(h.orgs.summaries().await.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.policy(ACME), None);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Removed);
    assert!(matches!(
        h.orgs.entries(ACME).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    let kept = h.store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(kept.org_id.as_deref(), Some(ACME));

    let e = h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        error_text(&e),
        "not found: no org 'acme-eng' is joined on this PC"
    );
    let e = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap_err();
    assert!(matches!(e, Error::NotFound(_)), "{e:?}");
}

// Update

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_preview_shows_a_new_org_or_what_an_update_changes() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    let preview = h.orgs.preview_join(&h.acme_code()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(preview.org_id, ACME);
    assert_eq!(preview.name, ACME_NAME);
    assert_eq!(preview.source_kind, "openbao");
    assert_eq!(preview.address, h.bao.address());
    assert_eq!(
        preview.key_fingerprint,
        key_fingerprint(&public_key(&h.keys)).unwrap()
    );
    assert!(!preview.existing);
    assert!(preview.changes.is_empty());

    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let calls = h.bao.calls().len();
    let unchanged = h.orgs.preview_join(&h.acme_code()).unwrap();
    assert!(unchanged.existing);
    assert!(unchanged.changes.is_empty(), "{:?}", unchanged.changes);

    let new_keys = keys();
    let moved = code(
        ACME,
        "Acme Eng",
        openbao(&h.bao.address(), "dots2"),
        &new_keys,
    );
    let preview = h.orgs.preview_join(&moved).unwrap();
    assert!(preview.existing);
    assert_eq!(
        preview.changes,
        vec![
            "name changes from Acme Engineering to Acme Eng".to_string(),
            "path changes from dots to dots2".to_string(),
            format!(
                "the policy key changes from {} to {}: the key that signs the org's policy is \
                 new, so accept this code only if your admin told you the key changed",
                key_fingerprint(&public_key(&h.keys)).unwrap(),
                key_fingerprint(&public_key(&new_keys)).unwrap()
            ),
        ]
    );

    let file = fixture("good.enc.json").display().to_string();
    let to_sops = code(ACME, ACME_NAME, sops_at(&file), &h.keys);
    let preview = h.orgs.preview_join(&to_sops).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        preview.changes,
        vec![format!(
            "source changes from OpenBao at {} to SOPS file at {file}",
            h.bao.address()
        )]
    );
    assert_eq!(h.bao.calls().len(), calls, "a preview fetches nothing");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_failed_update_leaves_the_old_settings_and_values_working() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();

    // Nothing at the new path.
    let empty = h.code_at(ACME, ACME_NAME, "nothing");
    let e = h.orgs.update(ACME, &empty, None).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        other(e),
        "could not update Acme Engineering: no secrets at secret/nothing/env"
    );

    // A policy at the new path signed by another key.
    let signed = sign(&keys(), &policy(ACME, "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z", json!({})));
    h.serve("dots2", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let moved = h.code_at(ACME, ACME_NAME, "dots2");
    let e = h.orgs.update(ACME, &moved, None).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        other(e),
        "could not update Acme Engineering: policy invalid: signature does not match"
    );

    // A policy older than the one accepted.
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy(ACME, "2026-10-21T08:00:00Z", json!({})));
    h.serve("dots2", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let e = h.orgs.update(ACME, &moved, None).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        other(e),
        "could not update Acme Engineering: policy invalid: issued before the last accepted \
         policy (2026-10-21T08:00:00Z, last 2026-10-22T08:00:00Z)"
    );

    // New creds that the new source refuses are not kept.
    let refused = SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new(OTHER_TOKEN.into()),
    };
    let e = h
        .orgs
        .update(ACME, &moved, Some(refused))
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(other(e).contains("refused access"));

    // A code for another org.
    let beta = h.code_at("beta", "Beta", "dots");
    let e = h.orgs.update(ACME, &beta, None).await.unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        invalid(e),
        "this join code is for org 'beta', not 'acme-eng'"
    );

    assert_eq!(h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap(), row);
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), Some(token()));
    assert_eq!(status_of(&h.orgs, ACME).await, OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
    assert_eq!(names(&copy_of(&h, ACME).unwrap())["API_KEY"], API_KEY);
    let reads = h.env_reads("dots");
    h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        h.env_reads("dots"),
        reads + 1,
        "a refresh still reads the old path"
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_update_replaces_the_settings_and_leaves_dots_and_grants_alone() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let dot = h
        .store
        .create_dot(&dot_spec("Triage"), Some(ACME))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    // A new path and a new key, with the stored token.
    let new_keys = keys();
    let issued = "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z";
    let signed = sign(
        &new_keys,
        &policy(ACME, issued, json!({"offline_hours": 48})),
    );
    h.serve("dots2", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let moved = code(
        ACME,
        "Acme Eng",
        openbao(&h.bao.address(), "dots2"),
        &new_keys,
    );
    h.advance(Duration::hours(1));
    let summary = h.orgs.update(ACME, &moved, None).await.unwrap();

    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(summary.name, "Acme Eng");
    assert_eq!(
        summary.key_fingerprint,
        key_fingerprint(&public_key(&new_keys)).unwrap()
    );
    assert_eq!(summary.copy_until, Some(start_plus(49)));
    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.name, "Acme Eng");
    assert_eq!(row.source, openbao(&h.bao.address(), "dots2"));
    assert_eq!(row.policy_key, public_key(&new_keys));
    assert_eq!(row.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some(issued));
    assert_eq!(row.last_fetch_at, Some(start_plus(1)));
    assert_eq!(row.joined_at, start_plus(0));
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), Some(token()));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(ROTATED, false));
    assert_eq!(
        h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "LOG_LEVEL").await,
        OrgLookup::NotDefined
    );
    assert_eq!(names(&copy_of(&h, ACME).unwrap())["API_KEY"], ROTATED);
    assert_eq!(h.store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap(), dot);

    // New creds are kept once the new settings work with them.
    h.bao.allow_token(OTHER_TOKEN, false);
    let other_token = SourceCreds::Token {
        token: Zeroizing::new(OTHER_TOKEN.into()),
    };
    h.orgs
        .update(ACME, &moved, Some(other_token.clone()))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(stored_creds(&h, ACME), Some(other_token));
    assert_eq!(h.store.get_dot(&dot.id).await.unwrap(), dot);

    // The refresh reads the new path with the new key.
    let reads = h.env_reads("dots2");
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots2"), reads + 1);
}

// Refresh

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_denied_refresh_wipes_the_copy_and_the_values() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    h.bao.revoke_token(TOKEN);

    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Revoked);
    assert_eq!(
        summary.status_text,
        format!(
            "access revoked ({} refused access to secret/dots/env (HTTP 403))",
            h.bao.address()
        )
    );
    assert_eq!(summary.copy_until, None);
    assert!(!h.copy_path(ACME).exists());
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Revoked);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "LOG_LEVEL").await, OrgLookup::Revoked);
    assert!(h.orgs.entries(ACME).await.unwrap().is_empty());

    // A load after it has no copy to read.
    let restarted = h.service();
    restarted.load().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status_of(&restarted, ACME).await,
        OrgStatus::Offline { until: None }
    );
    assert_eq!(restarted.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Offline);

    // Access given back: the next refresh connects again.
    h.bao.allow_token(TOKEN, false);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_unreachable_refresh_keeps_the_copy_until_offline_hours() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    h.advance(Duration::hours(1));
    h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);

    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status(&summary),
        OrgStatus::Offline {
            until: Some(start_plus(24))
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        summary.status_text,
        format!(
            "offline ({} is sealed or not ready (HTTP 503)); using the saved copy until {}",
            h.bao.address(),
            start_plus(24)
        )
    );
    assert_eq!(summary.last_fetch_at, Some(start_plus(0)));
    assert_eq!(summary.copy_until, Some(start_plus(24)));
    assert_eq!(copy_of(&h, ACME).unwrap().fetched_at, start_plus(0));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));

    // Back online, with a rotated value: the next fetch brings it.
    h.serve_acme(json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), acme_policy());
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(summary.copy_until, Some(start_plus(25)));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(ROTATED, false));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_invalid_answer_or_a_bad_signature_keeps_the_last_good_copy() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;
    let bytes = std::fs::read(h.copy_path(ACME)).unwrap();

    h.bao.remove("secret", "dots/env");
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status(&summary),
        OrgStatus::PolicyInvalid {
            error: "no secrets at secret/dots/env".into()
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        summary.status_text,
        format!(
            "policy invalid: no secrets at secret/dots/env; using the saved copy until {}",
            start_plus(24)
        )
    );
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));

    // New values under a policy signed by another key are not taken.
    let signed = sign(
        &keys(),
        &policy(ACME, "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z", acme_policy()),
    );
    h.serve("dots", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status(&summary),
        OrgStatus::PolicyInvalid {
            error: "signature does not match".into()
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(h.copy_path(ACME)).unwrap(), bytes);
    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some(ISSUED));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_rolled_back_policy_is_refused_and_the_copy_kept() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(entries(), acme_policy()).await;

    let older = "2026-10-21T08:00:00Z";
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy(ACME, older, acme_policy()));
    h.serve("dots", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status(&summary),
        OrgStatus::PolicyInvalid {
            error: "issued before the last accepted policy (2026-10-21T08:00:00Z, last \
                    2026-10-22T08:00:00Z)"
                .into()
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some(ISSUED));

    // A newer policy is taken, and recorded.
    let newer = "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z";
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy(ACME, newer, acme_policy()));
    h.serve("dots", json!({"API_KEY": ROTATED}), &signed);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(ROTATED, false));
    let row = h.store.get_org(ACME).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(row.last_issued_at.as_deref(), Some(newer));
}

// Expiry

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_copy_expires_offline_hours_after_the_last_good_fetch() {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    let extra = json!({"plain": ["LOG_LEVEL"], "offline_hours": 2});
    h.join_acme(entries(), extra.clone()).await;
    h.advance(Duration::hours(1));
    h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        status(&summary),
        OrgStatus::Offline {
            until: Some(start_plus(2))
        }
    );

    h.advance(Duration::minutes(59));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
    h.advance(Duration::minutes(1));
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, OrgLookup::Expired);
    assert!(!h.copy_path(ACME).exists());
    let summary = h.orgs.summary(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Expired);
    assert_eq!(
        summary.status_text,
        "secrets expired offline; reconnect to refresh"
    );
    assert_eq!(summary.copy_until, None);
    assert!(h.orgs.entries(ACME).await.unwrap().is_empty());

    // Still offline: still expired.
    h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Expired);

    // Reconnected: values again.
    let summary = h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(status(&summary), OrgStatus::Connected);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.lookup(ACME, "API_KEY").await, value(API_KEY, false));
}
```
