```rust
// The store's confirmed origins

#[tokio::test]
async fn confirmed_origins_are_kept_per_scope_once_each() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, _vault, _lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let store = &h.store;
    assert!(store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await.unwrap().is_empty());
    for (scope, origin) in [
        (PERSONAL_SCOPE, "https://api.github.com"),
        (ACME, "https://ghe.acme.example:8443"),
        (PERSONAL_SCOPE, "http://127.0.0.1:9"),
        (PERSONAL_SCOPE, "https://api.github.com"),
        (ACME, "https://ghe.acme.example:8443"),
    ] {
        store
            .add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, scope, origin)
            .await
            .unwrap();
    }
    assert_eq!(
        store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await.unwrap(),
        origins(&[
            (ACME, &["https://ghe.acme.example:8443"]),
            (
                PERSONAL_SCOPE,
                &["https://api.github.com", "http://127.0.0.1:9"]
            ),
        ])
    );
    // A scope is checked as a catalog's is; an origin is one `http_origin` gives.
    for scope in ["Acme", "", "acme_eng"] {
        let err = store
            .add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, scope, "https://api.github.com")
            .await
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Invalid(_)), "{scope}: {err:?}");
    }
    for origin in [
        "https://api.github.com/",
        "https://API.github.com",
        "https://api.github.com:443",
        "https://api.github.com/mcp",
        "ftp://files.example",
        "api.github.com",
        "",
    ] {
        match store
            .add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, PERSONAL_SCOPE, origin)
            .await
        {
            Err(Error::Invalid(why)) => assert_eq!(
                why,
                format!(
                    "{origin:?} is not an origin: it reads like https://host or \
                     https://host:8443"
                )
            ),
            other => panic!("{origin:?}: expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }
    // Only an MCP server has origins.
    let skill = store
        .add_library_item(
            "pdf",
            &LibraryConfig::Skill(SkillConfig {
                path: "C:/skills/pdf".into(),
            }),
            None,
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
    for id in [skill.id.as_str(), "01NOSUCHSERVER"] {
        assert!(matches!(
            store
                .add_confirmed_origin(id, PERSONAL_SCOPE, "https://api.github.com")
                .await,
            Err(Error::NotFound(_))
        ));
        assert!(matches!(
            store.confirmed_origins(id).await,
            Err(Error::NotFound(_))
        ));
    }
}

/// Deleting a server deletes its origins: one added again under its name starts with none.
#[tokio::test]
async fn deleting_a_server_deletes_its_confirmed_origins() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, _vault, _lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    h.store
        .add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, ACME, "https://ghe.acme.example")
        .await
        .unwrap();
    h.store.remove_library_item(&item.id).await.unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        h.store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
    let again = h
        .store
        .add_library_item("gh", &pinned_config(), None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(h
        .store
        .confirmed_origins(&again.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
}

// At spawn

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_personal_dots_server_starts_only_where_its_origin_was_confirmed() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let origin = served.origin("127.0.0.1");

    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(notices, [not_confirmed("gh", &origin)]);
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty(), "nothing was sent");

    // The origin a Personal run reaches, as the server form shows it.
    assert_eq!(
        lib.origin_in(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal).await.unwrap(),
        Ok(HttpOrigin {
            ascii: origin.clone(),
            unicode: None
        })
    );
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &origin)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await;
    assert_eq!((opened, notices), (1, Vec::<String>::new()));
    assert_eq!(served.auths(), [format!("Bearer {PERSONAL_KEY}")]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_personal_value_that_moves_the_host_is_refused() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &served.origin("127.0.0.1"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    vault
        .set_value("MCP_HOST", &served.at("localhost"))
        .await
        .unwrap();

    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(notices, [not_confirmed("gh", &served.origin("localhost"))]);
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty(), "nothing was sent");
    // Moved back, it starts again.
    vault
        .set_value("MCP_HOST", &served.at("127.0.0.1"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await.0, 1);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_dots_server_starts_once_the_orgs_origin_is_confirmed() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    // Confirmed for Personal only: the org's value reaches another origin.
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &served.origin("127.0.0.1"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let in_org = served.origin("localhost");
    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &acme(), "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(notices, [not_confirmed("gh", &in_org)]);
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty(), "nothing was sent");

    // The origin the org's values reach, as if all were granted, as its Check would.
    let shown = lib.origin_in(&item.id, &acme()).await.unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(shown.ascii, in_org);
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &acme(), &shown.ascii)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        h.store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await.unwrap(),
        origins(&[
            (ACME, &[in_org.as_str()]),
            (PERSONAL_SCOPE, &[served.origin("127.0.0.1").as_str()]),
        ])
    );
    assert_eq!(run(&h, &vault, &acme(), "gh").await, (1, Vec::new()));
    assert_eq!(
        run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await,
        (1, Vec::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        served.auths(),
        [
            format!("Bearer {ORG_KEY}"),
            format!("Bearer {PERSONAL_KEY}")
        ]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_orgs_value_moving_the_host_is_refused_while_personal_stays_confirmed() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &served.origin("127.0.0.1"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &acme(), &served.origin("localhost"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run(&h, &vault, &acme(), "gh").await.0, 1);

    // The org's next fetch moves its host.
    let extra = json!({"personal": "deny", "plain": ["MCP_HOST"]});
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy(ACME, "2026-10-22T08:30:00Z", extra));
    h.serve("dots", org_entries(&served, "127.0.0.2"), &signed);
    h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();

    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &acme(), "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(notices, [not_confirmed("gh", &served.origin("127.0.0.2"))]);
    assert_eq!(
        run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await,
        (1, Vec::new())
    );
    assert_eq!(
        served.auths(),
        [
            format!("Bearer {ORG_KEY}"),
            format!("Bearer {PERSONAL_KEY}")
        ]
    );
}

/// A change keeps the origins: one that keeps the origin still starts, one that moves it no
/// longer matches, and the old origin stays confirmed for when the URL comes back to it.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_changed_server_keeps_its_origins_and_a_moved_one_does_not_match() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let here = served.origin("127.0.0.1");
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &here)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let with = |url: &str, extra: &str| {
        LibraryConfig::McpServer(McpServerConfig::Http {
            url: url.into(),
            headers: BTreeMap::from([
                ("Authorization".into(), "Bearer ${API_KEY}".into()),
                ("X-Client".into(), extra.into()),
            ]),
        })
    };
    // A header changed, the origin the same.
    h.store
        .update_library_item(&item.id, &with("http://${MCP_HOST}/mcp", "dots"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await.0, 1);
    // Moved to another origin, its URL still reading a variable: the stored one does not match.
    let moved = format!("{}/mcp?via=${{MCP_HOST}}", served.origin("localhost"));
    h.store
        .update_library_item(&item.id, &with(&moved, "dots"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        h.store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await.unwrap(),
        origins(&[(PERSONAL_SCOPE, &[here.as_str()])])
    );
    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(notices, [not_confirmed("gh", &served.origin("localhost"))]);
    // Back on the first origin, it starts without a new confirmation.
    h.store
        .update_library_item(&item.id, &with("http://${MCP_HOST}/mcp", "dots-2"))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await.0, 1);
}

/// `origin_in` says why there is no origin, naming the variable and the scope, never a value.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_origin_that_cannot_be_computed_says_why_without_a_value() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    // The org lacks `MCP_HOST`, and `personal: deny` takes nothing from Personal.
    let (h, vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, json!({"API_KEY": ORG_KEY})).await;
    let why = lib.origin_in(&item.id, &acme()).await.unwrap().unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(why, "MCP_HOST: not in Acme Engineering");
    vault.remove("MCP_HOST").await.unwrap();
    let why = lib
        .origin_in(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(why, "MCP_HOST is not set");
    // A run in either scope leaves it out for the variable, as before.
    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &DotScope::Personal, "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(
        notices,
        ["MCP_HOST: not in Personal (dot 'triage', mcp:gh)"]
    );
    let (opened, notices) = run(&h, &vault, &acme(), "gh").await;
    assert_eq!(opened, 0);
    assert_eq!(
        notices,
        ["MCP_HOST: not in Acme Engineering (dot 'triage', mcp:gh)"]
    );
}

// Values Dots moves itself

/// A server added with a secret typed into a header sends a variable once Dots moves the value
/// into Personal. Its URL reads none, so its origin cannot move: it is not pinned, nothing is
/// confirmed, and the server starts as before. A URL that reads a variable is pinned, and
/// confirming it is the form's question.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_typed_secret_that_dots_moves_leaves_a_fixed_url_unpinned() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, vault, lib, _) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let typed = LibraryConfig::McpServer(served.http.config(BTreeMap::from([(
        "Authorization".into(),
        format!("Bearer {LITERAL}"),
    )])));
    let item = lib.add("typed", typed, None).await.unwrap();
    let LibraryConfig::McpServer(saved) = &item.config else {
        unreachable!()
    };
    assert!(!saved.variables().is_empty(), "{saved:?}");
    assert!(!saved.origin_pinned(), "{saved:?}");
    assert_clean(&serde_json::to_string(saved).unwrap());
    assert!(h
        .store
        .confirmed_origins(&item.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
    let grants = Grants(
        [(
            "mcp:typed".to_string(),
            saved.variables().into_iter().collect(),
        )]
        .into(),
    );
    let uses = Uses {
        mcp_servers: vec!["typed".into()],
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let (tools, notices) = RunTools::open(OpenRequest {
        store: &h.store,
        bus: &new_bus(),
        run_id: "01RUN",
        uses: &uses,
        workspace: h.data.path(),
        plugins_dir: None,
        cancel: &CancellationToken::new(),
        vault: &vault,
        scope: &DotScope::Personal,
        grants: &grants,
        dot_name: "triage",
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(tools.servers().len(), 1, "{notices:?}");
    tools.close().await;
    assert_eq!(served.auths(), [format!("Bearer {LITERAL}")]);

    // With a variable in the URL it is pinned, and nothing is confirmed by the move.
    let mixed = LibraryConfig::McpServer(McpServerConfig::Http {
        url: "http://${MCP_HOST}/mcp".into(),
        headers: BTreeMap::from([("Authorization".into(), format!("Bearer {LITERAL}"))]),
    });
    let item = lib.add("mixed", mixed, None).await.unwrap();
    assert!(h
        .store
        .confirmed_origins(&item.id)
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .is_empty());
}
```

```rust
/// What the person allowed in `confirm_library`'s question: the origins it named, each in ASCII
/// as the HTTP client reaches it with Personal's values, and those values. Empty when nothing
/// was asked, or the question named no origin that could be computed.
struct Allowed {
    origins: Vec<String>,
    personal: Resolved,
}

impl Allowed {
    /// The Personal origin of `config` when the question named it.
    fn origin_of(&self, config: &LibraryConfig) -> Option<String> {
        let LibraryConfig::McpServer(server @ McpServerConfig::Http { url, .. }) = config else {
            return None;
        };
        if !server.origin_pinned() {
            return None;
        }
        let origin = http_origin(url, &|k| self.personal.get(k)).ok()?.ascii;
        self.origins.contains(&origin).then_some(origin)
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// The origins confirmed in Personal for the item `id`.
    async fn confirmed(rt: &Runtime, id: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        rt.store()
            .confirmed_origins(id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .remove("personal")
            .unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Every question asked, and the answer `answer` to each.
    fn answering(
        asked: &std::cell::RefCell<Vec<String>>,
        answer: bool,
    ) -> impl FnOnce(String) -> std::future::Ready<bool> + '_ {
        move |q| {
            asked.borrow_mut().push(q);
            std::future::ready(answer)
        }
    }

            .await

            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        // A secret typed into a header asks nothing. Dots moves it into Personal, so the server
        // sends a variable, to the one origin its fixed URL has: it is not pinned, and nothing
        // is confirmed.
        let typed = http_with("https://typed.example/mcp", "typed-secret-value-81f3");
        let item = add_confirmed(&rt, "typed", typed, None, answering(&asked, false))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(asked.borrow().len(), 5);
        assert!(rt
            .store()
            .confirmed_origins(&item.id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        // A fixed URL whose header reads a variable asks, and a yes confirms nothing: there is
        // no pin to record.
        let fixed = http_with("https://fixed.example/mcp", "Bearer ${TOK}");
        let item = add_confirmed(&rt, "fixed", fixed, None, answering(&asked, true))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert!(asked.borrow()[5].contains(r#"values of TOK to "https://fixed.example""#));
        assert!(rt
            .store()
            .confirmed_origins(&item.id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        // A server that sends no variables asks nothing and has nothing to confirm.
        let item = add_confirmed(&rt, "plain", http(), None, answering(&asked, false))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(asked.borrow().len(), 6);
        assert!(rt
            .store()
            .confirmed_origins(&item.id)
            .await
            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        for question in asked.borrow().iter() {
            assert!(!question.contains("Mcp.Example") && !question.contains("typed-secret"));
        }
        rt.shutdown();
    }

    async fn an_allowed_plugin_confirms_the_origins_of_its_servers_whose_url_reads_a_variable() {

        rt.vault()
```

```rust
impl McpServerConfig {
    /// Whether the server's origin is pinned (env vault spec §8): an http server whose `url`
    /// reads a `${VAR}`, so a value can move the host its requests go to. A run starts it only
    /// when the origin it reaches with the run's values was confirmed for the dot's scope. A
    /// fixed URL has one origin, which the add and change dialog already names with the
    /// variables its headers send, so it starts as before.
    pub fn origin_pinned(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Self::Http { url, .. } if !url_variables(url).is_empty())
    }
}

/// The variables an http URL reads, sorted, each once: the ones its origin depends on.
pub(crate) fn url_variables(url: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    McpServerConfig::Http {
        url: url.to_string(),
        headers: BTreeMap::new(),
    }
    .variables()
}
```

```rust
/// was opened is closed.
/// Why the server `item` does not start in `scope` with the values `env`: its origin is pinned
/// (`McpServerConfig::origin_pinned`) and the origin its URL reaches with them is not confirmed
/// there, or it reaches none. `None` when it may start. The notice names the server and the
/// origin in ASCII, never a value.
async fn unconfirmed_origin(
    store: &Store,
    item: &LibraryItem,
    config: &McpServerConfig,
    env: &Resolved,
    scope: &DotScope,
) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    let McpServerConfig::Http { url, .. } = config else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    if !config.origin_pinned() {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    let origin = match http_origin(url, &|k| env.get(k)) {
        Ok(origin) => origin.ascii,
        Err(why) => return Ok(Some(format!("{}: could not start: {why}", item.name))),
    };
    let confirmed = store.confirmed_origins(&item.id).await?;
    if confirmed
        .get(scope.key())
        .is_some_and(|list| list.contains(&origin))
    {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "{}: {origin} is not a confirmed origin; open the server in the Library to confirm it",
        item.name
    )))
}
```

```rust
/// Refuses text that is not an origin as `http_origin` gives it: `scheme://host[:port]`, lower
/// case, the host in ASCII, no default port, no path.
fn check_origin(origin: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let canonical = reqwest::Url::parse(origin)
        .ok()
        .filter(|u| matches!(u.scheme(), "http" | "https") && u.host_str().is_some())
        .map(|u| u.origin().ascii_serialization());
    if canonical.as_deref() == Some(origin) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
        "{origin:?} is not an origin: it reads like https://host or https://host:8443"
    )))
}

/// Adds `origin` to the list of `scope` in a server's `confirmed_origins`, unless it is there:
/// one statement, so two confirmations at once both land. `path` is the scope's JSON path.
fn add_origin<'q>(
    server_id: &'q str,
    path: &'q str,
    origin: &'q str,
) -> sqlx::query::Query<'q, sqlx::Sqlite, sqlx::sqlite::SqliteArguments<'q>> {
    sqlx::query(
        "UPDATE library_items SET confirmed_origins = json_set(\
         COALESCE(confirmed_origins, '{}'), ?, json_insert(COALESCE(\
         json_extract(confirmed_origins, ?), '[]'), '$[#]', ?)) \
         WHERE id = ? AND kind = 'mcp_server' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM \
         json_each(COALESCE(confirmed_origins, '{}'), ?) WHERE value = ?)",
    )
    .bind(path)
    .bind(path)
    .bind(origin)
    .bind(server_id)
    .bind(path)
    .bind(origin)
}

/// The JSON path of a scope's list in `confirmed_origins`. A checked scope holds only `a-z`,
/// `0-9` and `-`, so it needs no escaping.
fn scope_path(scope: &str) -> String {
    format!("$.\"{scope}\"")
}

/// Records, inside the caller's transaction, `origin` as confirmed in `scope` for `server_id`
/// (`finish_0013`).
pub(super) async fn add_origin_in(
    conn: &mut SqliteConnection,
    server_id: &str,
    scope: &str,
    origin: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    check_scope(scope)?;
    check_origin(origin)?;
    let path = scope_path(scope);
    add_origin(server_id, &path, origin)
        .execute(&mut *conn)
        .await?;
    Ok(())
}
```

```rust
    /// The origins confirmed for the http MCP server `server_id`, by scope (env vault spec §8):
    /// each list in the order the origins were confirmed. Empty when none is. `NotFound` when
    /// there is no such MCP server.
    pub async fn confirmed_origins(
        &self,
        server_id: &str,
    ) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>> {
        let stored: Option<Option<String>> = sqlx::query_scalar(
            "SELECT confirmed_origins FROM library_items WHERE id = ? AND kind = 'mcp_server'",
        )
        .bind(server_id)
        .fetch_optional(&self.pool)
        .await?;
        match stored {
            None => Err(Error::NotFound(format!("MCP server {server_id}"))),
            Some(None) => Ok(BTreeMap::new()),
            Some(Some(text)) => Ok(serde_json::from_str(&text)?),
        }
    }

    /// Records `origin` (`HttpOrigin::ascii`) as confirmed for the http MCP server `server_id`
    /// in `scope` (`personal`, or an org id): a run of a dot in that scope then starts the
    /// server when its URL reaches that origin. Recording it again changes nothing. Refused for
    /// a server whose URL reads no variable: its one origin needs no confirmation.
    pub async fn add_confirmed_origin(
        &self,
        server_id: &str,
        scope: &str,
        origin: &str,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        check_scope(scope)?;
        check_origin(origin)?;
        let item = self.get_library_item(server_id).await.ok();
        let config = match item.as_ref().map(|i| &i.config) {
            Some(LibraryConfig::McpServer(config)) => config,
            _ => return Err(Error::NotFound(format!("MCP server {server_id}"))),
        };
        if !config.origin_pinned() {
            return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                "the MCP server {:?} has no variable in its http URL: its origin needs no \
                 confirmation",
                item.map(|i| i.name).unwrap_or_default()
            )));
        }
        let path = scope_path(scope);
        add_origin(server_id, &path, origin)
            .execute(&self.pool)
            .await?;
        Ok(())
    }
```

```rust
/// Confirms in Personal, for each MCP server that migration 0013 listed and whose origin is
/// pinned (`McpServerConfig::origin_pinned`), the origin its URL reaches with Personal's values
/// now, so nothing that worked before stops (env vault spec §8); then drops the list. An origin
/// that cannot be computed (a variable Personal does not set, a URL that is no http one) is not
/// recorded: that server asks to be confirmed again. It runs once the vault is open, since a
/// URL may read a Personal secret. A value that cannot be read fails it with nothing written,
/// and the next start tries again. Returns how many origins were recorded.
pub(super) async fn finish_0013(store: &super::Store, vault: &Vault) -> Result<usize> {
    let waiting: i64 = sqlx::query_scalar(
        "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'upgrade_0013'",
    )
    .fetch_one(&store.pool)
    .await?;
    if waiting == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }
    let ids: Vec<String> = sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT server_id FROM upgrade_0013")
        .fetch_all(&store.pool)
        .await?;
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for id in ids {
        let item = match store.get_library_item(&id).await {
            Ok(item) => item,
            Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => continue,
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let LibraryConfig::McpServer(config @ McpServerConfig::Http { url, .. }) = &item.config
        else {
            continue;
        };
        if !config.origin_pinned() {
            continue;
        }
        let personal = vault.personal_values(&url_variables(url)).await?;
        match http_origin(url, &|k| personal.get(k)) {
            Ok(origin) => found.push((id, origin.ascii)),
            Err(why) => tracing::warn!(
                "migration 0013: the MCP server {:?} has no origin to confirm ({why}); it asks \
                 to be confirmed again",
                item.name
            ),
        }
    }
    let mut tx = store.pool.begin().await?;
    for (id, origin) in &found {
        super::library::add_origin_in(&mut tx, id, PERSONAL_SCOPE, origin).await?;
    }
    sqlx::query("DROP TABLE upgrade_0013")
        .execute(&mut *tx)
        .await?;
    tx.commit().await?;
    Ok(found.len())
}
```

- per-scope catalogs and "Tools changed" in the app's answers;
- a Check that asks before it sends a scope's values to an unconfirmed origin.

- Consumes: Tasks 8 to 11.
- Produces:
  - In `vault::org`:
    - `OrgTimers::new(orgs, clock, bus, shutdown)`, with `start_up()`, `start(org_id)`, `retime(org_id)`, `stop(org_id)`, `running() -> Vec<String>` and `starting_up() -> bool`. Each timer sleeps on the clock, at most `scheduler::MAX_SLEEP` at a time. When due, it refreshes, publishes `OrgUpdated`, and re-times from the policy the fetch left.
    - `KEY_CHANGE = "the policy key changes"`, `DEFAULT_REFRESH_MINUTES = 15`.
  - `RuntimeEvent::OrgUpdated { org_id }`, JSON `{"type": "org_updated", "org_id": …}`. It goes out after each join, update, refresh, remove, timer fetch and start-up fetch.

    - `LibraryEntry.catalogs` (Personal, then each joined org) and `.confirmed_origins`; `ToolsChanged.scope`.
    - `LibraryService::{check_and_accept(id, scope, fingerprint), origin_to_confirm(id, scope)}`.
    - `check` refuses an unconfirmed origin: `Conflict("gh: http://127.0.0.1:61234 is not a confirmed origin in Personal")`.
  - Commands:
    - `org_list`, `org_preview(code)`, `org_sops_key(orgId)`, `org_join(code, creds)`
    - `org_update(orgId, code, creds)`: a new key asks the native "Accept the new policy key?"
    - `org_refresh(orgId)`, `org_remove(orgId)`, `org_entries(orgId)`
    - `confirm_origin(serverId, scope?)`
    - `library_check(id, scope?)`, which asks on an unconfirmed origin, and `library_accept(id, fingerprint, scope?)`. A missing `scope` is Personal.
    - Creds that do not parse: "these sign-in details are not ones Dots reads: give a token, a username and password, a machine identity's client id and secret, or an age key".
  - `dots_app::confirm::{scope_of, origin_question, check_confirmed, origin_confirmed, KEY_TITLE, key_question, update_org_confirmed}`.
  - UI types: `T.{SourceCreds, OrgSummary, JoinPreview, OrgEntry, ScopedCatalog}`, `ToolsChanged.scope`, `LibraryEntry.{catalogs, confirmed_origins}`, and the `org_updated` event.
  - UI commands: `commands.{orgList, orgPreview, orgSopsKey, orgJoin, orgUpdate, orgRefresh, orgRemove, orgEntries, confirmOrigin}`, `libraryCheck(id, scope?)` and `libraryAccept(id, fingerprint, scope?)`.

```rust
/// Waits (at most 10 real seconds) for `check` to hold.
async fn eventually(what: &str, check: impl Fn() -> bool) {
    for _ in 0..1000 {
        if check() {
            return;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(StdDuration::from_millis(10)).await;
    }
    panic!("{what} did not happen");
}

/// The runtime's org commands keep one timer per joined org: a join starts it, an Update and a
/// Refresh keep it, a remove stops it, and the runtime's shutdown stops every one. Each change
/// is published as `OrgUpdated`.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_runtime_keeps_one_timer_per_joined_org() {
    let t = Rt::start().await;
    let mut events = t.rt.subscribe();
    let timers = t.rt.org_timers();
    t.serve(LEVEL_ONE);
    t.rt.join_org(&t.acme_code(), Some(token())).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);
    assert_eq!(t.env_reads(), 1);
    let updated = |event: Result<RuntimeEvent, _>| match event {
        Ok(RuntimeEvent::OrgUpdated { org_id }) => Some(org_id),
        _ => None,
    };
    assert_eq!(updated(events.try_recv()).as_deref(), Some(ACME));

    // Its timer fetches after `refresh_minutes`.
    t.clock.set(at(START) + Duration::minutes(15));
    eventually("the timer's fetch", || t.env_reads() == 2).await;

    t.rt.update_org(ACME, &t.acme_code(), None).await.unwrap();
    t.rt.refresh_org(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.env_reads(), 4);
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);

    t.rt.remove_org(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert!(timers.running().is_empty());
    let mut said = Vec::new();
    while let Some(org_id) = updated(events.try_recv()) {
        said.push(org_id);
    }
    assert!(
        said.len() >= 3 && said.iter().all(|id| id == ACME),
        "{said:?}"
    );
    t.clock.set(at(START) + Duration::hours(2));
    tokio::time::sleep(StdDuration::from_millis(200)).await;
    assert_eq!(t.env_reads(), 4, "a removed org is not fetched");
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.remove_org(ACME).await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));

    t.rt.join_org(&t.acme_code(), Some(token())).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
    eventually("the timers' end", || timers.running().is_empty()).await;
}

/// A restarted runtime fetches every joined org once, and starts its timer.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_restarted_runtime_fetches_each_org_and_starts_its_timer() {
    let t = Rt::start().await;
    t.join_acme().await;
    assert!(t.rt.close(StdDuration::from_secs(10)).await);
    let Rt {
        dir,
        rt,
        bao,
        keys,
        secrets,
        ..
    } = t;
    drop(rt);
    let t = Rt::on(dir, secrets, bao, keys).await;
    let timers = t.rt.org_timers();
    eventually("the start-up fetch", || {
        t.env_reads() == 2 && !timers.starting_up()
    })
    .await;
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);
    t.rt.shutdown();
}
```

```rust
// The Library's listing and the Inbox, per scope

/// The listing gives each server's catalog in Personal and in each joined org, and the Inbox's
/// "Tools changed" names the scope whose list changed, with the dots of that scope. A removed
/// org's catalogs are left out of both.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_library_and_the_inbox_show_each_scopes_catalog() {
    use dots_core::model::{DotRef, ToolsChanged};
    let (h, _vault, lib) = setup(json!({"personal": "deny"})).await;
    let (_fake, item) = server_reading(&h.store, "sf", "API_KEY").await;
    let mut spec = common::spec("mine");
    spec.uses.mcp_servers = vec!["sf".into()];
    let mine = h.store.create_dot(&spec, None).await.unwrap();
    spec.name = "theirs".into();
    let theirs = h.store.create_dot(&spec, Some(ACME)).await.unwrap();
    let entry = |entries: Vec<dots_core::library_service::LibraryEntry>| {
        entries.into_iter().find(|e| e.item.id == item.id).unwrap()
    };
    let scopes = |e: &dots_core::library_service::LibraryEntry| -> Vec<(String, CatalogStatus)> {
        e.catalogs
            .iter()
            .map(|c| (c.scope.clone(), c.catalog.status))
            .collect()
    };

    let listed = entry(lib.list().await.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        scopes(&listed),
        [
            (PERSONAL_SCOPE.to_string(), CatalogStatus::Unchecked),
            (ACME.to_string(), CatalogStatus::Unchecked)
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(listed.catalog, Some(McpCatalog::unchecked(&item.id)));
    assert!(listed.confirmed_origins.is_empty());
    assert!(lib.tools_changed().await.unwrap().is_empty());

    let changed = |scope: &str, dot: &dots_core::model::Dot| ToolsChanged {
        server_id: item.id.clone(),
        name: "sf".into(),
        scope: scope.into(),
        dots: vec![DotRef {
            id: dot.id.clone(),
            name: dot.spec.name.clone(),
        }],
    };
    lib.check(&item.id, &acme()).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(lib.tools_changed().await.unwrap(), [changed(ACME, &theirs)]);
    lib.check(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        lib.tools_changed().await.unwrap(),
        [changed(PERSONAL_SCOPE, &mine), changed(ACME, &theirs)]
    );
    let listed = entry(lib.list().await.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        scopes(&listed),
        [
            (PERSONAL_SCOPE.to_string(), CatalogStatus::Changed),
            (ACME.to_string(), CatalogStatus::Changed)
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(listed.catalog.as_ref(), Some(&listed.catalogs[0].catalog));

    h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    let listed = entry(lib.list().await.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        scopes(&listed),
        [(PERSONAL_SCOPE.to_string(), CatalogStatus::Changed)]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        lib.tools_changed().await.unwrap(),
        [changed(PERSONAL_SCOPE, &mine)]
    );
}
```

```rust
// The Library's Check

/// The refusal of a Check whose origin is not confirmed in the scope named `scope_name`.
fn check_refused(origin: &str, scope_name: &str) -> String {
    format!("gh: {origin} is not a confirmed origin in {scope_name}")
}

/// A Check sends a scope's values only to an origin confirmed for that scope: otherwise it is
/// refused with the server, the origin and the scope's name, nothing is sent, and the catalog
/// is not touched. `origin_to_confirm` says what to ask, and nothing once it is confirmed.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_check_is_refused_until_the_origin_is_confirmed_in_its_scope() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, _vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let (here, in_org) = (served.origin("127.0.0.1"), served.origin("localhost"));
    for (scope, origin, name) in [
        (DotScope::Personal, &here, "Personal"),
        (acme(), &in_org, "Acme Engineering"),
    ] {
        match lib.check(&item.id, &scope).await {
            Err(Error::Conflict(why)) => assert_eq!(why, check_refused(origin, name)),
            other => panic!("expected Conflict, got {other:?}"),
        }
        match lib.check_and_accept(&item.id, &scope, "fp").await {
            Err(Error::Conflict(why)) => assert_eq!(why, check_refused(origin, name)),
            other => panic!("expected Conflict, got {other:?}"),
        }
        let asked = lib.origin_to_confirm(&item.id, &scope).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            asked,
            Some(dots_core::library_service::OriginToConfirm {
                server: "gh".into(),
                origin: HttpOrigin {
                    ascii: origin.clone(),
                    unicode: None
                },
                variables: vec!["API_KEY".into(), "MCP_HOST".into()],
                scope_name: name.into(),
            })
        );
    }
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty(), "nothing was sent");
    for scope in [PERSONAL_SCOPE, ACME] {
        let catalog = h.store.get_catalog(&item.id, scope).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(catalog.checked_at, None, "{scope}: {catalog:?}");
    }

    // Confirmed in Personal: Personal's Check sends Personal's token; the org's is still
    // refused.
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal, &here)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        lib.origin_to_confirm(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal)
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        None
    );
    let checked = lib.check(&item.id, &DotScope::Personal).await.unwrap();
    assert!(checked.checked_at.is_some(), "{checked:?}");
    assert!(matches!(
        lib.check(&item.id, &acme()).await,
        Err(Error::Conflict(_))
    ));
    lib.add_confirmed_origin(&item.id, &acme(), &in_org)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let fp = lib
        .check(&item.id, &acme())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .seen_fingerprint
        .unwrap();
    let accepted = lib.check_and_accept(&item.id, &acme(), &fp).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(accepted.accepted_fingerprint.as_deref(), Some(fp.as_str()));
    assert_eq!(
        served.auths(),
        [
            format!("Bearer {PERSONAL_KEY}"),
            format!("Bearer {ORG_KEY}"),
            format!("Bearer {ORG_KEY}")
        ]
    );
    // The listing shows what is confirmed, by scope.
    let entry = lib
        .list()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .into_iter()
        .find(|e| e.item.id == item.id)
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        entry.confirmed_origins,
        origins(&[
            (ACME, &[in_org.as_str()]),
            (PERSONAL_SCOPE, &[here.as_str()])
        ])
    );
}

/// With no origin to confirm, `origin_to_confirm` says why, naming the scope and the variable,
/// and the Check fails on the variable as before, sending nothing.
#[tokio::test]
async fn an_origin_that_cannot_be_computed_is_not_asked_about() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, _vault, lib, item) = setup(&served, json!({"API_KEY": ORG_KEY})).await;
    match lib.origin_to_confirm(&item.id, &acme()).await {
        Err(Error::Invalid(why)) => assert_eq!(
            why,
            "gh: there is no origin to confirm in Acme Engineering: MCP_HOST: not in Acme \
             Engineering"
        ),
        other => panic!("expected Invalid, got {other:?}"),
    }
    let catalog = lib.check(&item.id, &acme()).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        catalog.error.as_deref(),
        Some("MCP_HOST: not in Acme Engineering")
    );
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty());
    // A server that is not pinned has nothing to confirm.
    let plain = LibraryConfig::McpServer(served.http.config(BTreeMap::new()));
    let plain = h
        .store
        .add_library_item("plain", &plain, None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        lib.origin_to_confirm(&plain.id, &DotScope::Personal).await,
        Err(Error::Invalid(_))
    ));
}

/// `add` with a fingerprint to accept checks the server first. A pinned one whose origin is not
/// confirmed is saved unchecked, and nothing is sent.
#[tokio::test]
async fn adding_a_pinned_server_with_accept_sends_nothing_to_an_unconfirmed_origin() {
    let served = Served::start().await;
    let (h, _vault, lib, _) = setup(&served, org_entries(&served, "localhost")).await;
    let item = lib.add("gh2", pinned_config(), Some("fp")).await.unwrap();
    let catalog = h.store.get_catalog(&item.id, PERSONAL_SCOPE).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(catalog.checked_at, None, "{catalog:?}");
    assert!(served.auths().is_empty());
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_org_timers_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The org timers (env vault spec §6.4): each joined org is fetched every `refresh_minutes` of
//! its accepted policy, a policy that changes the interval re-times the org from its next
//! fetch, and **Refresh** or **Update** count from now. A stopped timer fetches no more, and
//! every timer and the start-up fetch stop with the shutdown token. The clock is the fake the
//! scheduler's tests use: a timer sleeps at most a minute at a time, and a test knows the timer
//! is idle once it sleeps until the deadline the test expects.

mod common;

use std::time::Duration as StdDuration;

use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use common::clock::FakeClock;
use common::fake_openbao::Failure;
use common::orgs::{at, policy, sign, token, OrgsHarness, ACME, START};
use dots_core::events::{new_bus, Bus, RuntimeEvent};
use dots_core::vault::org::OrgTimers;
use serde_json::json;
use tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

const ORG_VALUE: &str = "org-secret-timer-value-5b2c71";

/// `START` and `minutes` more.
fn plus(minutes: i64) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    at(START) + Duration::minutes(minutes)
}

/// Waits (at most 10 real seconds) until the newest sleep of `clock` has `deadline`: the timer
/// has done what the time asked of it and waits again.
async fn sleeping_until(clock: &FakeClock, deadline: DateTime<Utc>) {
    let waited = tokio::time::timeout(StdDuration::from_secs(10), async {
        loop {
            let n = clock.sleeps();
            if n > 0 && clock.nth_sleep(n).await == deadline {
                return;
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(StdDuration::from_millis(5)).await;
        }
    })
    .await;
    assert!(waited.is_ok(), "no timer began to sleep until {deadline}");
}

/// Waits (at most 10 real seconds) for `check` to hold.
async fn eventually(what: &str, check: impl Fn() -> bool) {
    for _ in 0..1000 {
        if check() {
            return;
        }
        tokio::time::sleep(StdDuration::from_millis(10)).await;
    }
    panic!("{what} did not happen");
}

/// The next `OrgUpdated`'s org, skipping other events.
async fn next_org_updated(events: &mut Receiver<RuntimeEvent>) -> String {
    let next = tokio::time::timeout(StdDuration::from_secs(10), async {
        loop {
            if let RuntimeEvent::OrgUpdated { org_id } = events.recv().await.unwrap() {
                return org_id;
            }
        }
    });
    next.await.expect("no OrgUpdated was published")
}

/// Acme joined at `START` with a policy of `extra`, and timers on the harness's clock.
async fn joined(extra: serde_json::Value) -> (OrgsHarness, OrgTimers, Bus, CancellationToken) {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    h.join_acme(json!({"API_KEY": ORG_VALUE}), extra).await;
    let bus = new_bus();
    let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
    let timers = OrgTimers::new(
        h.orgs.clone(),
        h.clock.clone(),
        bus.clone(),
        shutdown.clone(),
    );
    (h, timers, bus, shutdown)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_is_fetched_every_refresh_minutes_of_its_policy() {
    let (h, timers, bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    let mut events = bus.subscribe();
    timers.start(ACME);
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);
    // At most a minute at a time, as the scheduler sleeps.
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(1)).await;
    h.clock.set(plus(14) + Duration::seconds(59));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(15)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 1, "only the join's fetch so far");

    h.clock.set(plus(15));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(16)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 2);
    assert_eq!(next_org_updated(&mut events).await, ACME);
    h.clock.set(plus(30));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(31)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 3);
    assert_eq!(next_org_updated(&mut events).await, ACME);
}

/// A fetch that brings a policy with another `refresh_minutes` re-times the org from there.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_policy_that_changes_the_interval_retimes_the_org_at_its_next_fetch() {
    let (h, timers, _bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    timers.start(ACME);
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(1)).await;
    let every_five = json!({"refresh_minutes": 5});
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy(ACME, "2026-10-22T08:30:00Z", every_five));
    h.serve("dots", json!({"API_KEY": ORG_VALUE}), &signed);

    h.clock.set(plus(15));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(16)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 2);
    assert_eq!(h.orgs.policy(ACME).unwrap().refresh_minutes, 5);
    h.clock.set(plus(19) + Duration::seconds(59));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(20)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 2, "not before five minutes");
    h.clock.set(plus(20));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(21)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 3);
}

/// **Refresh** and **Update** fetch now, so the next fetch counts from now. Starting a running
/// timer again keeps that one timer, re-timed.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_refresh_counts_from_now_and_a_second_start_keeps_one_timer() {
    let (h, timers, _bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    timers.start(ACME);
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(1)).await;
    h.clock.set(plus(10));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(11)).await;
    h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    // The new time holds from the call on, whenever the timer's task next runs.
    timers.retime(ACME);
    timers.start(ACME);
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);

    h.clock.set(plus(15));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(16)).await;
    assert_eq!(
        h.env_reads("dots"),
        2,
        "the refresh, and no timer fetch at 15 minutes"
    );
    h.clock.set(plus(24) + Duration::seconds(59));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(25)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 2);
    h.clock.set(plus(25));
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(26)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 3, "one fetch: one timer");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_stopped_timer_fetches_no_more() {
    let (h, timers, _bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    timers.start(ACME);
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(1)).await;
    timers.stop(ACME);
    eventually("the timer's end", || timers.running().is_empty()).await;
    let sleeps = h.clock.sleeps();
    h.clock.set(plus(60));
    tokio::time::sleep(StdDuration::from_millis(200)).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 1);
    assert_eq!(h.clock.sleeps(), sleeps, "no timer sleeps again");
    // A stopped org can be started again.
    timers.start(ACME);
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME]);
}

/// An org removed without its timer being stopped ends the timer at its next fetch.
#[tokio::test]
async fn a_timer_ends_when_its_org_is_no_longer_joined() {
    let (h, timers, _bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    timers.start(ACME);
    sleeping_until(&h.clock, plus(1)).await;
    h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    h.clock.set(plus(15));
    eventually("the timer's end", || timers.running().is_empty()).await;
    assert_eq!(h.env_reads("dots"), 1);
}

/// The start-up fetch starts every joined org's timer, fetches each org once, and says so.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_start_up_fetch_fetches_every_org_once_and_starts_its_timer() {
    let (h, timers, bus, _shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    let signed = sign(&h.keys, &policy("beta", "2026-10-22T08:00:00Z", json!({})));
    h.serve("beta", json!({"API_KEY": ORG_VALUE}), &signed);
    h.orgs
        .join(&h.code_at("beta", "Beta", "beta"), Some(token()))
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let mut events = bus.subscribe();
    timers.start_up();
    let mut said = vec![
        next_org_updated(&mut events).await,
        next_org_updated(&mut events).await,
    ];
    said.sort();
    assert_eq!(said, [ACME, "beta"]);
    assert_eq!((h.env_reads("dots"), h.env_reads("beta")), (2, 2));
    assert_eq!(timers.running(), [ACME, "beta"]);
    eventually("the start-up fetch's end", || !timers.starting_up()).await;
}

/// Every timer, and a start-up fetch that hangs, stop with the shutdown token.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_timers_and_the_start_up_fetch_stop_with_the_shutdown_token() {
    let (h, timers, _bus, shutdown) = joined(json!({})).await;
    h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Hang, 1);
    timers.start_up();
    eventually("the timer's start", || timers.running() == [ACME]).await;
    eventually("the hanging fetch", || h.env_reads("dots") == 2).await;
    assert!(timers.starting_up());
    shutdown.cancel();
    eventually("the end of every task", || {
        timers.running().is_empty() && !timers.starting_up()
    })
    .await;
}
```

```rust
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn org_update(

    state: State<'_, AppState>,

    code: String,
    creds: Option<serde_json::Value>,
) -> Res<OrgSummary> {

    confirm::update_org_confirmed(&rt, &org_id, &code, creds, |message| {
        confirm::ask(&app, confirm::KEY_TITLE, message)
    })
```

```rust
}

/// The sign-in details a command was given, read as `SourceCreds`. The words of a failure name
/// no part of them: serde's messages can quote the text they fail on.
fn creds_of(creds: Option<serde_json::Value>) -> Res<Option<SourceCreds>> {
    creds
        .map(|value| {
            serde_json::from_value(value).map_err(|_| {
                CmdError::from(dots_core::Error::Invalid(
                    "these sign-in details are not ones Dots reads: give a token, a username \
                     and password, a machine identity's client id and secret, or an age key"
                        .into(),
                ))
            })
        })
        .transpose()
}
```

```rust
/// An origin for a dialog: quoted in ASCII, with the Unicode host in parentheses when it
/// differs.
fn shown_origin(origin: &HttpOrigin) -> String {
    match &origin.unicode {
        Some(u) => format!("{} ({u})", quoted(&origin.ascii)),
        None => quoted(&origin.ascii),
    }
}

/// The question before an http MCP server may send a scope's values to the origin its URL
/// reaches there: the words of the server form's question, naming the org whose values they
/// are. Names, never values.
pub fn origin_question(asked: &OriginToConfirm, scope: &DotScope) -> String {
    let whose = match scope {
        DotScope::Personal => String::new(),
        DotScope::Org(_) => format!(" in {}", asked.scope_name),
    };
    format!(
        "Dots will send the values of {}{whose} to {}. Send them?\n\nAllow this only for a \
         server you trust.",
        asked.variables.join(", "),
        shown_origin(&asked.origin)
    )
}

/// The scope a command names: an org id, or none for Personal.
pub fn scope_of(scope: Option<String>) -> DotScope {
    scope.map_or(DotScope::Personal, DotScope::Org)
}
```

```rust
/// Asks `asked`'s question for the server `id` in `scope`, and records the origin after a yes.
/// A no answers `cancelled`, with nothing sent or recorded.
async fn confirm_asked<F, Fut>(
    rt: &Runtime,
    id: &str,
    scope: &DotScope,
    asked: &OriginToConfirm,
    ask: F,
) -> Result<(), CmdError>
where
    F: FnOnce(String) -> Fut,
    Fut: Future<Output = bool>,
{
    if !ask(origin_question(asked, scope)).await {
        return Err(CmdError::cancelled("declined: nothing was sent or saved"));
    }
    rt.library()
        .add_confirmed_origin(id, scope, &asked.origin.ascii)
        .await?;
    Ok(())
}

/// `library_check` in `scope` (env vault spec §8). The core refuses to check a pinned server
/// whose origin in that scope is not confirmed; then this asks, with that origin and the
/// server's variables, and a yes records the origin and checks. A no answers `cancelled`, and
/// nothing is sent.
pub async fn check_confirmed<F, Fut>(
    rt: &Runtime,
    id: &str,
    scope: &DotScope,
    ask: F,
) -> Result<McpCatalog, CmdError>
where
    F: FnOnce(String) -> Fut,
    Fut: Future<Output = bool>,
{
    let library = rt.library();
    let refused = match library.check(id, scope).await {
        Err(dots_core::Error::Conflict(why)) => why,
        other => return Ok(other?),
    };
    // Any other conflict, or one that no longer holds, is answered as it came.
    let Ok(Some(asked)) = library.origin_to_confirm(id, scope).await else {
        return Err(dots_core::Error::Conflict(refused).into());
    };
    confirm_asked(rt, id, scope, &asked, ask).await?;
    Ok(library.check(id, scope).await?)
}

/// `confirm_origin`: the question of `check_confirmed` and its record, without the Check. It
/// works for a plugin's own server, which the server form cannot change. An origin confirmed
/// already asks nothing.
pub async fn origin_confirmed<F, Fut>(
    rt: &Runtime,
    id: &str,
    scope: &DotScope,
    ask: F,
) -> Result<(), CmdError>
where
    F: FnOnce(String) -> Fut,
    Fut: Future<Output = bool>,
{
    match rt.library().origin_to_confirm(id, scope).await? {
        Some(asked) => confirm_asked(rt, id, scope, &asked, ask).await,
        None => Ok(()),
    }
}

/// The title of the question before an Update that brings a new policy key.
pub const KEY_TITLE: &str = "Accept the new policy key?";

/// The question before an Update that brings a new policy key: the preview's warning.
pub fn key_question(org: &str, warning: &str) -> String {
    format!("{org}: {warning}.\n\nUpdate {org} with this code?")
}

/// `org_update`, after the person's yes when the code brings a new policy key (env vault spec
/// §6.4): the key that signs the org's policy decides what Dots trusts, so the warning of
/// `org_preview` is asked in a dialog the webview cannot answer. A no answers `cancelled` and
/// nothing is fetched or changed. A code for another org is the core's refusal, unasked.
pub async fn update_org_confirmed<F, Fut>(
    rt: &Runtime,
    org_id: &str,
    code: &str,
    creds: Option<SourceCreds>,
    ask: F,
) -> Result<OrgSummary, CmdError>
where
    F: FnOnce(String) -> Fut,
    Fut: Future<Output = bool>,
{
    let preview = rt.preview_org(code)?;
    let warning = preview.changes.iter().find(|c| c.starts_with(KEY_CHANGE));
    if let Some(warning) = warning.filter(|_| preview.org_id == org_id) {
        if !ask(key_question(&preview.name, warning)).await {
            return Err(CmdError::cancelled("the org was not updated"));
        }
    }
    Ok(rt.update_org(org_id, code, creds).await?)
}
```

```rust
    /// A server whose host comes from `${MCP_HOST}`, which Personal sets to a port nothing
    /// listens on, so a check that runs records `unreachable`. Added as the store adds it,
    /// with nothing confirmed.
    async fn pinned(rt: &Runtime, name: &str) -> LibraryItem {
        let config = http_with("http://${MCP_HOST}/mcp", "Bearer ${TOK}");
        rt.store()
            .add_library_item(name, &config, None)
            .await
            .unwrap()
    }

        rt.vault()
            .add("MCP_HOST", EntryKind::Plain, "127.0.0.1:1")
            .await
            .unwrap();
        rt.vault()

            .await
            .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(catalog.checked_at, None, "not checked: {catalog:?}");

        // A yes records the origin, then checks.

            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(asked.borrow().len(), 2);
        assert!(catalog.checked_at.is_some(), "{catalog:?}");
        assert_eq!(confirmed(&rt, &item.id).await, ["http://127.0.0.1:1"]);
        // Confirmed: no question again (a no would refuse it).

    /// Two policy keys, `0101010101010101` and `0202020202020202` by fingerprint.
    const KEY_A: &str = "RWQBAQEBAQEBARERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERERER";
    const KEY_B: &str = "RWQCAgICAgICAhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhISEhIS";

    /// The join code of `org_id` signed with `key`, its OpenBao on a port nothing listens on.
    fn org_code(org_id: &str, path: &str, key: &str) -> String {
        use dots_core::vault::org::{BaoAuth, JoinCode, OpenBaoSettings, SourceSettings};
        JoinCode {
            v: 1,
            org_id: org_id.into(),
            name: "Acme Engineering".into(),
            source: SourceSettings::OpenBao(OpenBaoSettings {
                address: "http://127.0.0.1:1".into(),
                mount: "secret".into(),
                path: path.into(),
                auth: BaoAuth::Token,
                auth_mount: None,
                namespace: None,
            }),
            policy_key: key.into(),
        }
        .encode()
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn an_update_that_brings_a_new_policy_key_asks_first() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        // Acme is joined with key A: its row, as a join leaves it, with no copy.
        let data = dir.path().join("data");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&data).unwrap();
        let store = dots_core::store::Store::open(&data.join(dots_core::store::DB_FILE))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        let joined = org_code("acme-eng", "dots", KEY_A);
        let code = dots_core::vault::org::parse_join_code(&joined).unwrap();
        store
            .add_org(&dots_core::vault::org::OrgRow {
                id: code.org_id,
                name: code.name,
                source: code.source,
                policy_key: code.policy_key,
                last_issued_at: None,
                last_fetch_at: None,
                joined_at: "2026-10-22T09:00:00.000Z".into(),
            })
            .await
            .unwrap();
        store.close().await;
        let rt = runtime(&dir).await;
        let token: SourceCreds =
            serde_json::from_value(serde_json::json!({"kind": "token", "token": "hvs.t"})).unwrap();
        let asked = std::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new());
        let new_key = org_code("acme-eng", "dots", KEY_B);

        // A no fetches and changes nothing.
        let err = update_org_confirmed(
            &rt,
            "acme-eng",
            &new_key,
            Some(token.clone()),
            answering(&asked, false),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err, CmdError::cancelled("the org was not updated"));
        assert_eq!(
            *asked.borrow(),
            [key_question(
                "Acme Engineering",
                "the policy key changes from 0101010101010101 to 0202020202020202: the key that \
                 signs the org's policy is new, so accept this code only if your admin told you \
                 the key changed"
            )]
        );
        assert!(asked.borrow()[0].starts_with("Acme Engineering: the policy key changes from"));
        let summary = rt.orgs().summary("acme-eng").await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(summary.key_fingerprint, "0101010101010101");

        // A yes goes on to the Update, which fetches with the new settings (and fails here).
        let err = update_org_confirmed(
            &rt,
            "acme-eng",
            &new_key,
            Some(token.clone()),
            answering(&asked, true),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.kind, CmdErrorKind::Internal);
        assert!(
            err.message.starts_with("could not update Acme Engineering"),
            "{err:?}"
        );
        assert_eq!(asked.borrow().len(), 2);

        // The same key asks nothing; a code for another org is the core's refusal, unasked.
        let same_key = org_code("acme-eng", "dots2", KEY_A);
        let err = update_org_confirmed(
            &rt,
            "acme-eng",
            &same_key,
            Some(token.clone()),
            answering(&asked, false),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.message.starts_with("could not update"), "{err:?}");
        let other = org_code("beta", "dots", KEY_B);
        let err = update_org_confirmed(
            &rt,
            "acme-eng",
            &other,
            Some(token),
            answering(&asked, true),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.kind, CmdErrorKind::Invalid);
        assert_eq!(asked.borrow().len(), 2);
        rt.shutdown();
    }
}
```

```rust
/// A changed tool list in Personal, with the dot that uses it, and the same server's in an
/// org, used by no dot of that org.
fn tools_changed() -> Vec<ToolsChanged> {

        server_id: "01J0SRV".into(),

}

/// An org of every status (`org_list`, and what `org_join`, `org_update` and `org_refresh`
/// answer): every optional field is set in one of them.
fn org_summaries() -> Vec<OrgSummary> {
    let connected = OrgSummary {
        id: "acme-eng".into(),
        name: "Acme Engineering".into(),
        source_kind: "openbao".into(),
        address: "https://bao.acme.internal".into(),
        key_fingerprint: "6E2F0A1B9C3D4E5F".into(),
        status: OrgStatus::Connected,
        status_text: "connected".into(),
        last_fetch_at: Some(TS.into()),
        copy_until: Some("2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z".into()),
        policy_summary: vec![
            "org: acme-eng".into(),
            "personal: fallback (a personal entry is used when the org has none)".into(),
        ],
    };
    let status = |status: OrgStatus, text: &str| OrgSummary {
        status,
        status_text: text.into(),
        ..connected.clone()
    };
    vec![
        connected.clone(),
        status(
            OrgStatus::Offline {
                until: Some("2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z".into()),
            },
            "offline (connection refused); using the saved copy until 2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z",
        ),
        OrgSummary {
            copy_until: None,
            ..status(
                OrgStatus::Offline { until: None },
                "offline, with no saved copy",
            )
        },
        OrgSummary {
            copy_until: None,
            ..status(OrgStatus::Revoked, "access revoked (permission denied)")
        },
        status(
            OrgStatus::PolicyInvalid {
                error: "signature does not match".into(),
            },
            "policy invalid: signature does not match; using the saved copy until \
             2026-10-10T12:00:00.000Z",
        ),
        OrgSummary {
            copy_until: None,
            ..status(
                OrgStatus::Expired,
                "secrets expired offline; reconnect to refresh",
            )
        },
        OrgSummary {
            id: "design".into(),
            name: "Design".into(),
            source_kind: "sops".into(),
            address: "C:/Users/u/Sync/acme/design.enc.json".into(),
            last_fetch_at: None,
            copy_until: None,
            policy_summary: vec![],
            ..status(
                OrgStatus::Pending,
                "waiting for the admin to add this PC's key",
            )
        },
    ]
}

/// A code for a new org, and one that changes a joined org's path and key (`org_preview`).
fn join_previews() -> Vec<JoinPreview> {
    let new = JoinPreview {
        org_id: "acme-eng".into(),
        name: "Acme Engineering".into(),
        source_kind: "openbao".into(),
        address: "https://bao.acme.internal".into(),
        key_fingerprint: "6E2F0A1B9C3D4E5F".into(),
        existing: false,
        changes: vec![],
    };
    vec![
        new.clone(),
        JoinPreview {
            existing: true,
            key_fingerprint: "0A1B2C3D4E5F6071".into(),
            changes: vec![
                "path changes from dots to dots2".into(),
                "the policy key changes from 6E2F0A1B9C3D4E5F to 0A1B2C3D4E5F6071: the key that \
                 signs the org's policy is new, so accept this code only if your admin told you \
                 the key changed"
                    .into(),
            ],
            ..new
        },
    ]
}

/// Sign-in details of every kind, as `org_join` and `org_update` take them. Read through the
/// core's type, so a sample in a form the core does not accept fails here. No value is real.
fn source_creds() -> Value {
    let samples = [
        json!({"kind": "token", "token": "hvs.sample-token"}),
        json!({"kind": "login", "username": "jdoe", "password": "sample-password"}),
        json!({"kind": "machine", "client_id": "sample-id", "client_secret": "sample-secret"}),
        json!({"kind": "age", "identity": "AGE-SECRET-KEY-1SAMPLE"}),
    ];
    let read: Vec<SourceCreds> = samples
        .into_iter()
        .map(|v| serde_json::from_value(v).expect("sample sign-in details"))
        .collect();
    to(read)
}
```

```rust
    /// Checks the MCP server `id` in `scope`, as `check` does, and accepts the list it gives
    /// when its fingerprint is `fingerprint`, the one the person was shown by `probe`
    /// (`library_add` with `accept`). Otherwise the list waits for review.
    pub async fn check_and_accept(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        scope: &DotScope,
        fingerprint: &str,
    ) -> Result<McpCatalog> {
        let item = self.server(id).await?;
        let catalog = self.check_item(&item, scope).await?;
        if catalog.seen_fingerprint.as_deref() != Some(fingerprint) {
            return Ok(catalog);
        }
        let accepted = self
            .store
            .accept_catalog(id, scope.key(), fingerprint)
            .await?;
        publish(&self.bus, id);
        Ok(accepted)
    }

    /// What to ask before the http MCP server `id` may send `scope`'s values to the origin its
    /// URL reaches there (`origin_in`): that origin, the variables the server sends and the
    /// scope's name. `None` when that origin is confirmed for the scope already. `Invalid` for
    /// a server whose URL reads no variable, or with why no origin can be computed. A plugin's
    /// own server is asked about too: nothing else can confirm it.
    pub async fn origin_to_confirm(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        scope: &DotScope,
    ) -> Result<Option<OriginToConfirm>> {
        let item = self.server(id).await?;
        let scope_name = self.scope_name(scope).await;
        let origin = match self.origin_in(id, scope).await? {
            Ok(origin) => origin,
            Err(why) => {
                return Err(Error::Invalid(format!(
                    "{}: there is no origin to confirm in {scope_name}: {why}",
                    item.name
                )))
            }
        };
        if self.is_confirmed(id, scope, &origin).await? {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let LibraryConfig::McpServer(config) = &item.config else {
            unreachable!("origin_in takes only an http MCP server")
        };
        Ok(Some(OriginToConfirm {
            server: item.name.clone(),
            origin,
            variables: config.variables(),
            scope_name,
        }))
    }
```

```rust
    /// The scopes the Library shows a server's catalog in: `personal`, then the id of each org
    /// joined on this PC, by name.
    async fn scopes(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut scopes = vec![PERSONAL_SCOPE.to_string()];
        if let Some(orgs) = self.vault.orgs() {
            scopes.extend(orgs.summaries().await.into_iter().map(|s| s.id));
        }
        scopes
    }

    /// "Personal", or the org's name; its id when it is not joined.
    async fn scope_name(&self, scope: &DotScope) -> String {
        let DotScope::Org(id) = scope else {
            return "Personal".into();
        };
        match self.vault.orgs() {
            Some(orgs) => orgs
                .summary(id)
                .await
                .map_or_else(|| id.clone(), |s| s.name),
            None => id.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether `origin` is confirmed for the server `id` in `scope`.
    async fn is_confirmed(&self, id: &str, scope: &DotScope, origin: &HttpOrigin) -> Result<bool> {
        let confirmed = self.store.confirmed_origins(id).await?;
        Ok(confirmed
            .get(scope.key())
            .is_some_and(|list| list.contains(&origin.ascii)))
    }

    /// The origin the pinned http server `item` reaches in `scope`, when it is not confirmed
    /// there. `None` when it is, when the server is not pinned, or when no origin can be
    /// computed: the check then fails on its own, for the variable or the URL, and sends
    /// nothing.
    async fn unconfirmed(
        &self,
        item: &LibraryItem,
        config: &McpServerConfig,
        scope: &DotScope,
    ) -> Result<Option<HttpOrigin>> {
        let McpServerConfig::Http { url, .. } = config else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        if !config.origin_pinned() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let consumer = Consumer::Mcp(item.name.clone());
        let names = url_variables(url);
        let Ok(values) = self.vault.check_values(scope, &consumer, &names).await? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let Ok(origin) = http_origin(url, &|k| values.get(k)) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        Ok((!self.is_confirmed(&item.id, scope, &origin).await?).then_some(origin))
    }
```

```rust
/// Orgs (env vault spec §6.1 and §6.4). The app changes an org through these, not through
/// `Orgs` itself, so that its timer stays in step and the screens hear of it (`OrgUpdated`).
impl Runtime {
    /// The orgs joined on this PC, for what only reads them: the list, a join code's preview,
    /// an org's entries, and a SOPS org's key.
    pub fn orgs(&self) -> &Orgs {
        &self.orgs
    }

    /// The orgs' timers.
    pub fn org_timers(&self) -> &OrgTimers {
        &self.org_timers
    }

    /// What `code` would join, or change for an org joined already. Nothing is fetched.
    pub fn preview_org(&self, code: &str) -> Result<JoinPreview> {
        self.orgs.preview_join(code)
    }

    /// Joins the org of `code` (**Join**), then starts its timer.
    pub async fn join_org(&self, code: &str, creds: Option<SourceCreds>) -> Result<OrgSummary> {
        let summary = self.orgs.join(code, creds).await?;
        self.org_timers.start(&summary.id);
        self.org_updated(&summary.id);
        Ok(summary)
    }

    /// Replaces a joined org's settings with a new join code's (**Update**). It fetched just
    /// now, so its timer counts from now, with the new policy's `refresh_minutes`.
    pub async fn update_org(
        &self,
        org_id: &str,
        code: &str,
        creds: Option<SourceCreds>,
    ) -> Result<OrgSummary> {
        let summary = self.orgs.update(org_id, code, creds).await?;
        self.org_timers.retime(org_id);
        self.org_updated(org_id);
        Ok(summary)
    }

    /// Fetches the org now (**Refresh**); its timer counts from now.
    pub async fn refresh_org(&self, org_id: &str) -> Result<OrgSummary> {
        let summary = self.orgs.refresh(org_id).await?;
        self.org_timers.retime(org_id);
        self.org_updated(org_id);
        Ok(summary)
    }

    /// Leaves the org (**Remove**): its timer stops first, so no fetch of it starts while its
    /// copy, sign-in details and row go. If the remove fails with the org still joined, its
    /// timer starts again.
    pub async fn remove_org(&self, org_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        self.org_timers.stop(org_id);
        if let Err(e) = self.orgs.remove(org_id).await {
            if self.orgs.is_joined(org_id) {
                self.org_timers.start(org_id);
            }
            return Err(e);
        }
        self.org_updated(org_id);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn org_updated(&self, org_id: &str) {
        let _ = self.bus.send(RuntimeEvent::OrgUpdated {
            org_id: org_id.to_string(),
        });
    }
}

/// Browser use (browser spec sections 7 and 8).
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/src/vault/org/timers.rs`:**

```rust
//! The org timers (env vault spec §6.4): each joined org is fetched every `refresh_minutes` of
//! its accepted policy, and once at start. There is one task per org. Its next fetch is
//! `refresh_minutes` after its last one, read from the policy that fetch left, so a policy that
//! changes the interval re-times the org from its next fetch on. A join starts the org's timer,
//! an Update or a **Refresh** re-times it from now, and a remove stops it. Every timer, and the
//! start-up fetch, stops with the runtime's shutdown token.
//!
//! The timers sleep on the runtime's `Clock`, at most `scheduler::MAX_SLEEP` at a time, as the
//! scheduler does: a timer does not follow the wall clock across a system sleep, so each one
//! looks at the clock again at least that often. After each fetch a timer publishes
//! `OrgUpdated`, so the screens read the org's status again.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, PoisonError};

use chrono::{DateTime, Duration, Utc};
use tokio::sync::Notify;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use super::policy::DEFAULT_REFRESH_MINUTES;
use super::service::Orgs;
use crate::events::{Bus, RuntimeEvent};
use crate::scheduler::{Clock, MAX_SLEEP};
use crate::Error;

/// The timers of the joined orgs. Cheap to clone: every clone shares one set of timers.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct OrgTimers {
    inner: Arc<Inner>,
}

struct Inner {
    orgs: Orgs,
    clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
    bus: Bus,
    shutdown: CancellationToken,
    timers: Mutex<HashMap<String, Timer>>,
    /// The start-up fetch of every org, while it runs.
    startup: Mutex<Option<JoinHandle<()>>>,
}

struct Timer {
    stop: CancellationToken,
    /// When the org is fetched next. Set by whoever moves it, then `moved` wakes the task, so
    /// the time holds from the call on, whenever the task runs.
    due: Due,
    moved: Arc<Notify>,
    task: JoinHandle<()>,
}

type Due = Arc<Mutex<DateTime<Utc>>>;

impl std::fmt::Debug for OrgTimers {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("OrgTimers")
            .field("running", &self.running())
            .finish()
    }
}

impl OrgTimers {
    /// No timer runs yet: `start_up` starts one per joined org. They all stop with `shutdown`.
    pub fn new(
        orgs: Orgs,
        clock: Arc<dyn Clock>,
        bus: Bus,
        shutdown: CancellationToken,
    ) -> OrgTimers {
        OrgTimers {
            inner: Arc::new(Inner {
                orgs,
                clock,
                bus,
                shutdown,
                timers: Mutex::default(),
                startup: Mutex::default(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// At start, after `Orgs::load`: starts every joined org's timer, then fetches every org
    /// once (`Orgs::refresh_all`) without holding the start up, and publishes `OrgUpdated` for
    /// each. A source that is slow or down must not keep the app from opening; until it
    /// answers, an org resolves from its offline copy.
    pub fn start_up(&self) {
        let this = self.clone();
        let stop = self.inner.shutdown.clone();
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            tokio::select! {
                _ = stop.cancelled() => {}
                _ = this.fetch_all() => {}
            }
        });
        *lock(&self.inner.startup) = Some(task);
    }

    /// Starts the timer of `org_id`, whose first fetch is `refresh_minutes` from now: it was
    /// fetched just now, by its join or the start-up fetch. An org whose timer runs already
    /// keeps that one, re-timed from now.
    pub fn start(&self, org_id: &str) {
        let next = next_fetch(&self.inner, org_id);
        let mut timers = lock(&self.inner.timers);
        if let Some(timer) = timers.get(org_id).filter(|t| !t.task.is_finished()) {
            *lock(&timer.due) = next;
            timer.moved.notify_one();
            return;
        }
        let stop = self.inner.shutdown.child_token();
        let due = Arc::new(Mutex::new(next));
        let moved = Arc::new(Notify::new());
        let task = tokio::spawn(tick(
            self.inner.clone(),
            org_id.to_string(),
            stop.clone(),
            due.clone(),
            moved.clone(),
        ));
        let timer = Timer {
            stop,
            due,
            moved,
            task,
        };
        timers.insert(org_id.to_string(), timer);
    }

    /// The org was fetched just now (**Update**, **Refresh**): its next fetch is
    /// `refresh_minutes` of its policy from now. An org without a timer gets one.
    pub fn retime(&self, org_id: &str) {
        self.start(org_id);
    }

    /// Stops the timer of `org_id` (**Remove**). A fetch it has begun runs to its end.
    pub fn stop(&self, org_id: &str) {
        if let Some(timer) = lock(&self.inner.timers).remove(org_id) {
            timer.stop.cancel();
        }
    }

    /// The orgs whose timer runs, sorted.
    pub fn running(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut ids: Vec<String> = lock(&self.inner.timers)
            .iter()
            .filter(|(_, timer)| !timer.task.is_finished())
            .map(|(id, _)| id.clone())
            .collect();
        ids.sort();
        ids
    }

    /// Whether the start-up fetch is still going.
    pub fn starting_up(&self) -> bool {
        lock(&self.inner.startup)
            .as_ref()
            .is_some_and(|task| !task.is_finished())
    }

    async fn fetch_all(&self) {
        let orgs = &self.inner.orgs;
        let ids: Vec<String> = orgs.summaries().await.into_iter().map(|s| s.id).collect();
        for id in &ids {
            self.start(id);
        }
        orgs.refresh_all().await;
        for id in ids {
            published(&self.inner.bus, id);
        }
    }
}

/// One org's timer: fetches it once `due` has come, and then `refresh_minutes` of its policy
/// after each fetch, until `stop`. A move of `due` wakes it to sleep anew. An org that is no
/// longer joined ends it.
async fn tick(
    inner: Arc<Inner>,
    org_id: String,
    stop: CancellationToken,
    due: Due,
    moved: Arc<Notify>,
) {
    loop {
        let next = *lock(&due);
        let wake = next.min(inner.clock.now() + MAX_SLEEP);
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            _ = stop.cancelled() => return,
            _ = moved.notified() => continue,
            _ = inner.clock.sleep_until(wake) => {}
        }
        if inner.clock.now() < *lock(&due) {
            continue;
        }
        match inner.orgs.refresh(&org_id).await {
            Ok(_) => published(&inner.bus, org_id.clone()),
            Err(Error::NotFound(_)) => return,
            // A store failure; the next fetch tries again.
            Err(e) => tracing::warn!("org {org_id:?} was not refreshed by its timer: {e}"),
        }
        *lock(&due) = next_fetch(&inner, &org_id);
    }
}

/// `refresh_minutes` of the org's accepted policy from now; the policy's default while it has
/// none.
fn next_fetch(inner: &Inner, org_id: &str) -> DateTime<Utc> {
    let minutes = inner
        .orgs
        .policy(org_id)
        .map_or(DEFAULT_REFRESH_MINUTES, |p| p.refresh_minutes);
    inner.clock.now() + Duration::minutes(minutes.into())
}

fn published(bus: &Bus, org_id: String) {
    let _ = bus.send(RuntimeEvent::OrgUpdated { org_id });
}

fn lock<T>(mutex: &Mutex<T>) -> std::sync::MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    mutex.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
```
