**Create `ui/src/screens/library/ServerScopes.tsx`:**

```tsx
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useState } from "react";

import { commands } from "@/api/commands";
import type { McpCatalog } from "@/api/types";
import { Field } from "@/components/Field";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { NativeSelect } from "@/components/ui/native-select";
import { errorMessage } from "@/lib/notify";
import { invalidate, keys } from "@/lib/query";

import { isDeclined, PERSONAL, useScopes, type ServerEntry } from "./parts";
import { variablesIn } from "./text";

/// What a Check found, in words.
function checked(name: string, catalog: McpCatalog): { text: string; failed: boolean } {
  switch (catalog.status) {
    case "accepted":
      return { text: `Checked as ${name}: the tools are the ones you accepted.`, failed: false };
    case "changed":
      return {
        text: `Checked as ${name}: the tools changed. Review them in the list.`,
        failed: false,
      };
    case "unreachable":
      return { text: `Checked as ${name}: ${catalog.error ?? "unreachable"}`, failed: true };
    case "unchecked":
      return { text: `Checked as ${name}.`, failed: false };
  }
}

/// A saved server's Check in a scope the person picks ("Check as": Personal or a joined org,
/// env vault spec §8), and, for a server whose URL reads a variable, the origins confirmed in
/// each scope, with "Confirm origin in <scope>" where there is none yet. Both ask in a native
/// dialog before a scope's values go to an origin not confirmed there; a no changes nothing. A
/// plugin's own server has these too, though its settings are the plugin's.
export function ServerScopes({ entry }: { entry: ServerEntry }) {
  const qc = useQueryClient();
  const { orgs, nameOf } = useScopes();
  // "" is Personal, which the commands take as a scope left out.
  const [picked, setPicked] = useState("");
  const scopeOf = (key: string) => (key === "" || key === PERSONAL ? undefined : key);
  const check = useMutation({
    mutationFn: async (scope: string | undefined) => ({
      scope,
      catalog: await commands.libraryCheck(entry.id, scope),
    }),
    onSuccess: () => invalidate(qc, keys.library),
  });
  const confirm = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (scope: string | undefined) => commands.confirmOrigin(entry.id, scope),
    onSuccess: () => invalidate(qc, keys.library),
  });

  const config = entry.config;
  const pinned = config.transport === "http" && variablesIn([config.url]).length > 0;
  const scopes = [PERSONAL, ...orgs.map((org) => org.id)];
  const result = check.data && checked(nameOf(check.data.scope), check.data.catalog);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 rounded-md border p-3">
      <div className="flex items-end gap-3">
        <Field
          label="Check as"
          htmlFor="server-check-as"
          hint="Lists the tools with the values of this scope, as a run of a dot in it would."
        >
          <NativeSelect
            id="server-check-as"
            value={picked}
            onChange={(e) => {
              setPicked(e.target.value);
              check.reset();
            }}
          >
            <option value="">Personal</option>
            {orgs.map((org) => (
              <option key={org.id} value={org.id}>
                {org.name}
              </option>
            ))}
          </NativeSelect>
        </Field>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          disabled={check.isPending}
          onClick={() => check.mutate(scopeOf(picked))}
        >
          {check.isPending ? "Checking…" : "Check"}
        </Button>
      </div>
      {result && (
        <p role="status" className={`text-xs ${result.failed ? "text-destructive" : ""}`}>
          {result.text}
        </p>
      )}
      {check.isError &&
        (isDeclined(check.error) ? (
          <p role="status" className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
            Not checked: you did not confirm the origin.
          </p>
        ) : (
          <p role="alert" className="text-xs text-destructive">
            {errorMessage(check.error)}
          </p>
        ))}

      {pinned && (
        <>
          <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
            This server's URL reads a variable, so where it sends values can differ by scope.
            Dots sends a scope's values only to an origin confirmed in that scope.
          </p>
          <ul aria-label="Confirmed origins" className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-xs">
            {scopes.map((scope) => {
              const origins = entry.confirmed_origins[scope] ?? [];
              return (
                <li key={scope} aria-label={nameOf(scope)} className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
                  <span className="font-medium">{`${nameOf(scope)}:`}</span>
                  {origins.length > 0 ? (
                    <span className="font-mono">{origins.join(", ")}</span>
                  ) : (
                    <span className="text-muted-foreground">None yet</span>
                  )}
                </li>
              );
            })}
          </ul>
          <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
            {scopes
              .filter((scope) => (entry.confirmed_origins[scope] ?? []).length === 0)
              .map((scope) => (
                <Button
                  key={scope}
                  type="button"
                  variant="outline"
                  size="sm"
                  disabled={confirm.isPending}
                  onClick={() => confirm.mutate(scopeOf(scope))}
                >
                  {`Confirm origin in ${nameOf(scope)}`}
                </Button>
              ))}
          </div>
          {confirm.isError &&
            (isDeclined(confirm.error) ? (
              <p role="status" className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                You declined. Nothing was confirmed.
              </p>
            ) : (
              <p role="alert" className="text-xs text-destructive">
                {errorMessage(confirm.error)}
              </p>
            ))}
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```rust
/// The dot editor's status of a dot's variables (`dot_variables`) is read without the fetch a
/// run's start makes of a stale org, and holds no value. A dot whose org was removed gets the
/// reason for each grant.
#[tokio::test]
async fn the_status_of_a_dots_variables_fetches_nothing_and_holds_no_value() {
    let t = Rt::start().await;
    t.join_acme().await;
    let dot =
        t.rt.create_dot(t.triage(), Some(ACME.into()))
            .await
            .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.env_reads(), 1);
    // Stale: a run's start would fetch now.
    t.clock
        .set(at(START) + Duration::minutes(15) + Duration::seconds(1));
    let statuses = t.rt.dot_variables(&dot.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(statuses.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(
        (statuses[0].consumer.as_str(), statuses[0].name.as_str()),
        ("shell", "DOTS_TEST_LEVEL")
    );
    assert_eq!(statuses[0].status, GrantState::Ok);
    assert_eq!(statuses[0].source, Some(ValueSource::Org));
    assert!(!statuses[0].secret);
    let json = serde_json::to_string(&statuses).unwrap();
    assert!(!json.contains(LEVEL_ONE), "{json}");
    assert_eq!(t.env_reads(), 1, "no fetch");

    t.orgs().remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    let statuses = t.rt.dot_variables(&dot.id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(statuses[0].status, GrantState::OrgRemoved);
    assert_eq!(statuses[0].text.as_deref(), Some(REMOVED));
    assert!(matches!(
        t.rt.dot_variables("01J0NODOT").await,
        Err(Error::NotFound(_))
    ));
}
```

**Create `crates/dots-core/tests/vault_dot_status_test.rs`:**

```rust
//! The status of a dot's grants (env vault spec §9, the dot editor's Variables): each name
//! granted to each consumer, resolved in the dot's scope by the resolver's own steps, with
//! where its value comes from and why it does not resolve. No value is in the answer, no
//! Personal secret's value is read, and the org is not fetched.

mod common;

use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;

use chrono::Duration;
use common::fake_openbao::Failure;
use common::orgs::{keys, policy, sign, OrgsHarness, ACME, TOKEN};
use common::spec;
use dots_core::library::{LibraryConfig, McpServerConfig};
use dots_core::model::Dot;
use dots_core::vault::org::{OrgStatus, PersonalMode, UseRules};
use dots_core::vault::{
    Consumer, DotScope, EntryKind, GrantState, GrantStatus, Grants, MemorySecrets, SecretStore,
    ValueSource, Vault,
};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use zeroize::Zeroizing;

const ORG_TOKEN: &str = "org-secret-gh-token-7c41e9";
const ORG_PROD: &str = "org-secret-prod-db-0b5d22";
const ORG_LEVEL: &str = "org-plain-level-e83f10";
const PERSONAL_KEY: &str = "personal-secret-key-4a90cd";
const PERSONAL_REGION: &str = "personal-plain-region-61b7";

/// Every value a test serves or stores, which no answer may hold.
const VALUES: &[&str] = &[
    ORG_TOKEN,
    ORG_PROD,
    ORG_LEVEL,
    PERSONAL_KEY,
    PERSONAL_REGION,
    TOKEN,
];

fn assert_clean(text: &str) {
    for value in VALUES {
        assert!(!text.contains(value), "{text:?} holds {value:?}");
    }
}

/// A secret store that counts the values read from it.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct Counting {
    inner: MemorySecrets,
    gets: AtomicUsize,
}

impl SecretStore for Counting {
    fn put(&self, key: &str, value: &str) -> dots_core::Result<()> {
        self.inner.put(key, value)
    }
    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> dots_core::Result<Option<Zeroizing<String>>> {
        self.gets.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
        self.inner.get(key)
    }
    fn delete(&self, key: &str) -> dots_core::Result<()> {
        self.inner.delete(key)
    }
    fn keys(&self, prefix: &str) -> dots_core::Result<Vec<String>> {
        self.inner.keys(prefix)
    }
}

/// The org's entries: the secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `PROD_DB`, and the plain `LOG_LEVEL`.
fn org_entries() -> Value {
    json!({"GITHUB_TOKEN": ORG_TOKEN, "PROD_DB": ORG_PROD, "LOG_LEVEL": ORG_LEVEL})
}

struct Setup {
    h: OrgsHarness,
    vault: Vault,
    secrets: Arc<Counting>,
}

/// Acme joined with `org_entries` under a policy of `extra` (`LOG_LEVEL` plain), and Personal
/// holding the secret `API_KEY` and the plain `REGION`, in a store that counts reads.
async fn setup(extra: Value) -> Setup {
    let h = OrgsHarness::new().await;
    let mut extra = extra;
    extra["plain"] = json!(["LOG_LEVEL"]);
    h.join_acme(org_entries(), extra).await;
    let secrets = Arc::new(Counting::default());
    let vault = Vault::new(h.store.clone(), secrets.clone()).with_orgs(h.orgs.clone());
    vault
        .add("API_KEY", EntryKind::Secret, PERSONAL_KEY)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    vault
        .add("REGION", EntryKind::Plain, PERSONAL_REGION)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // A server that reads no variable, so ticking it grants nothing beyond what a test gives.
    let github = McpServerConfig::Stdio {
        command: "gh-mcp".into(),
        args: Vec::new(),
        cwd: None,
        env: Default::default(),
    };
    h.store
        .add_library_item("github", &LibraryConfig::McpServer(github), None)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    Setup { h, vault, secrets }
}

impl Setup {
    /// A dot named `triage` in `org`, using the server `github`, granted `grants` (consumer
    /// key, names).
    async fn dot(&self, org: Option<&str>, grants: &[(&str, &[&str])]) -> Dot {
        let mut s = spec("triage");
        s.uses.mcp_servers = vec!["github".into()];
        s.variables = Grants(
            grants
                .iter()
                .map(|(key, names)| {
                    (
                        key.to_string(),
                        names.iter().map(|n| n.to_string()).collect(),
                    )
                })
                .collect(),
        );
        self.h.store.create_dot(&s, org).await.unwrap()
    }

    /// The statuses of `dot`, none of which holds a value, read without reading a Personal
    /// secret's value.
    async fn statuses(&self, dot: &Dot) -> Vec<GrantStatus> {
        let gets = self.secrets.gets.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        let statuses = self.vault.grant_statuses(dot).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            self.secrets.gets.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
            gets,
            "no value was read"
        );
        assert_clean(&format!("{statuses:?}"));
        assert_clean(&serde_json::to_string(&statuses).unwrap());
        statuses
    }
}

/// A status that resolves.
fn ok(consumer: &str, name: &str, source: ValueSource, secret: bool) -> GrantStatus {
    GrantStatus {
        consumer: consumer.into(),
        name: name.into(),
        status: GrantState::Ok,
        text: None,
        source: Some(source),
        secret,
    }
}

/// A status that does not resolve, with its text.
fn not(consumer: &str, name: &str, status: GrantState, text: &str) -> GrantStatus {
    GrantStatus {
        consumer: consumer.into(),
        name: name.into(),
        status,
        text: Some(text.into()),
        source: None,
        secret: false,
    }
}

/// Each status agrees with what `resolve` gives for that grant: the same names resolve, and
/// the same text is given for those that don't.
async fn agrees_with_resolve(vault: &Vault, dot: &Dot, statuses: &[GrantStatus]) {
    let scope = DotScope::of(dot);
    for status in statuses {
        let consumer = Consumer::parse(&status.consumer).unwrap();
        let names = vec![status.name.clone()];
        let resolved = vault
            .resolve(&scope, &dot.spec.variables, &consumer, &names)
            .await
            .unwrap();
        match resolved {
            Ok(_) => assert_eq!(status.status, GrantState::Ok, "{status:?}"),
            Err(missing) => {
                assert_eq!(
                    status.text,
                    Some(missing.text(&dot.spec.name)),
                    "{status:?}"
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_grant_resolves_from_the_org_or_from_personal_under_fallback() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "fallback"})).await;
    let dot = t
        .dot(
            Some(ACME),
            &[
                ("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN", "API_KEY", "REGION"]),
                ("shell", &["LOG_LEVEL", "region"]),
            ],
        )
        .await;
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        [
            ok("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN", ValueSource::Org, true),
            ok("mcp:github", "API_KEY", ValueSource::Personal, true),
            ok("mcp:github", "REGION", ValueSource::Personal, false),
            ok("shell", "LOG_LEVEL", ValueSource::Org, false),
            // As granted, in any case.
            ok("shell", "region", ValueSource::Personal, false),
        ]
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn under_override_a_name_both_have_comes_from_personal() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "override", "shell_secrets": true})).await;
    // The org's summary tells the editor both rules, for its name pickers.
    let summary = t.h.orgs.summary(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(summary.personal_mode, Some(PersonalMode::Override));
    assert!(summary.shell_secrets);
    t.vault
        .add("LOG_LEVEL", EntryKind::Plain, PERSONAL_REGION)
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let dot = t
        .dot(Some(ACME), &[("shell", &["LOG_LEVEL", "GITHUB_TOKEN"])])
        .await;
    assert_eq!(
        t.statuses(&dot).await,
        [
            ok("shell", "LOG_LEVEL", ValueSource::Personal, false),
            // `shell_secrets: true`: the shell may have the org's secret.
            ok("shell", "GITHUB_TOKEN", ValueSource::Org, true),
        ]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn each_reason_a_grant_does_not_resolve_has_its_status_and_text() {
    let t = setup(json!({
        "personal": "fallback",
        "use": {"allow": ["*"], "deny": ["PROD_*"]},
    }))
    .await;
    // The summary gives the editor the `use` globs, so its shell picker leaves out PROD_*.
    let summary = t.h.orgs.summary(ACME).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        summary.use_rules,
        Some(UseRules {
            allow: vec!["*".into()],
            deny: vec!["PROD_*".into()],
        })
    );
    let dot = t
        .dot(
            Some(ACME),
            &[
                ("mcp:github", &["NOWHERE", "PROD_DB"]),
                ("shell", &["GITHUB_TOKEN", "API_KEY", "LOG_LEVEL"]),
            ],
        )
        .await;
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    let forbidden = |name: &str, source: ValueSource| GrantStatus {
        source: Some(source),
        secret: true,
        ..not(
            "shell",
            name,
            GrantState::ShellSecretsForbidden,
            &format!("{name}: Acme Engineering does not allow secrets in the shell (dot 'triage')"),
        )
    };
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        [
            not(
                "mcp:github",
                "NOWHERE",
                GrantState::NotDefined,
                "NOWHERE: not in Acme Engineering (dot 'triage', mcp:github)"
            ),
            not(
                "mcp:github",
                "PROD_DB",
                GrantState::DeniedByPolicy,
                "PROD_DB: Acme Engineering's policy does not allow it (dot 'triage')"
            ),
            // A secret of the org's, and a Personal one `fallback` would give.
            forbidden("GITHUB_TOKEN", ValueSource::Org),
            forbidden("API_KEY", ValueSource::Personal),
            // A plain value is no secret.
            ok("shell", "LOG_LEVEL", ValueSource::Org, false),
        ]
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;
}

/// Serves Acme's entries under a policy signed with a key that is not the org's.
fn serve_badly_signed(h: &OrgsHarness) {
    let signed = sign(&keys(), &policy(ACME, "2026-10-22T10:00:00Z", json!({})));
    h.serve("dots", org_entries(), &signed);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_org_that_gives_no_values_is_the_status_of_every_grant() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "override", "offline_hours": 0})).await;
    let dot = t
        .dot(Some(ACME), &[("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN", "REGION"])])
        .await;
    let each = |status: GrantState, text: &str| {
        vec![
            not("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN", status, text),
            not("mcp:github", "REGION", status, text),
        ]
    };

    t.h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);
    assert_eq!(
        t.h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap().status,
        OrgStatus::Offline { until: None }
    );
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        each(
            GrantState::OrgOffline,
            "Acme Engineering: offline, with no saved copy"
        )
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;

    serve_badly_signed(&t.h);
    let OrgStatus::PolicyInvalid { error } = t.h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap().status else {
        panic!("the policy is refused");
    };
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        each(
            GrantState::PolicyInvalid,
            &format!("Acme Engineering: policy invalid: {error}")
        )
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;

    t.h.bao.revoke_token(TOKEN);
    assert_eq!(
        t.h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap().status,
        OrgStatus::Revoked
    );
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        each(GrantState::OrgRevoked, "Acme Engineering: access revoked")
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;

    t.h.orgs.remove(ACME).await.unwrap();
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        each(
            GrantState::OrgRemoved,
            "dot 'triage': its org 'acme-eng' was removed"
        )
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_expired_copy_is_the_status_of_every_grant() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "fallback", "offline_hours": 2})).await;
    let dot = t.dot(Some(ACME), &[("shell", &["LOG_LEVEL"])]).await;
    t.h.bao.fail_next(Failure::Status(503), 1);
    t.h.orgs.refresh(ACME).await.unwrap();
    t.h.advance(Duration::hours(2));
    assert_eq!(
        t.statuses(&dot).await,
        [not(
            "shell",
            "LOG_LEVEL",
            GrantState::OrgExpired,
            "Acme Engineering: secrets expired offline; reconnect to refresh"
        )]
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_status_fetches_nothing_even_when_the_org_is_stale() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "deny"})).await;
    let dot = t
        .dot(Some(ACME), &[("mcp:github", &["GITHUB_TOKEN"])])
        .await;
    assert_eq!(t.h.env_reads("dots"), 1);
    // Past `refresh_minutes` (15): a run's start would fetch now.
    t.h.advance(Duration::minutes(16));
    assert_eq!(
        t.statuses(&dot).await,
        [ok("mcp:github", "GITHUB_TOKEN", ValueSource::Org, true)]
    );
    assert_eq!(t.h.env_reads("dots"), 1, "no fetch");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_personal_dot_shows_personal_only() {
    let t = setup(json!({"personal": "fallback"})).await;
    let dot = t
        .dot(None, &[("shell", &["API_KEY", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "REGION"])])
        .await;
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses,
        [
            // A Personal dot's shell may have a Personal secret.
            ok("shell", "API_KEY", ValueSource::Personal, true),
            not(
                "shell",
                "GITHUB_TOKEN",
                GrantState::NotDefined,
                "GITHUB_TOKEN: not in Personal (dot 'triage', shell)"
            ),
            ok("shell", "REGION", ValueSource::Personal, false),
        ]
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;

    // A secret whose value is gone from the store does not resolve, as at a run.
    t.secrets.inner.delete("personal/API_KEY").unwrap();
    let statuses = t.statuses(&dot).await;
    assert_eq!(
        statuses[0],
        not(
            "shell",
            "API_KEY",
            GrantState::NotDefined,
            "API_KEY: not in Personal (dot 'triage', shell)"
        )
    );
    agrees_with_resolve(&t.vault, &dot, &statuses).await;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_dot_with_no_grants_has_no_status() {
    let t = setup(json!({})).await;
    let dot = t.dot(Some(ACME), &[]).await;
    assert_eq!(t.statuses(&dot).await, []);
}

#[test]
fn the_states_serialize_in_snake_case() {
    let names: Vec<Value> = GrantState::ALL
        .iter()
        .map(|s| serde_json::to_value(s).unwrap())
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        names,
        [
            "ok",
            "not_granted",
            "not_defined",
            "denied_by_policy",
            "shell_secrets_forbidden",
            "org_offline",
            "org_expired",
            "org_revoked",
            "policy_invalid",
            "org_removed"
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        serde_json::to_value(ValueSource::Personal).unwrap(),
        json!("personal")
    );
}
```

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import type { Dot, OrgSummary } from "@/api/types";
import { backend } from "@/test/backend";
import { blankSpec, sample } from "@/test/fixtures";
import { renderApp } from "@/test/render";

const [acme] = sample.orgs as [OrgSummary]; // Acme Engineering, connected
const gamma: OrgSummary = { ...acme, id: "gamma", name: "Gamma" };
// A dot of Acme Engineering, and the contract's Personal dot.
const release: Dot = { ...sample.dot, id: "D2", name: "acme-release", org_id: "acme-eng" };
const personal = sample.dot;
const REMOVED = "Its org 'acme-eng' was removed. Join it again to run this dot.";
const basics = { name: "nightly", instructions: "Run the tests.", workdir: "C:/dev/app" };

/// Opens the new-dot form with `orgs` joined and fills in what a dot needs.
async function newDot(orgs: OrgSummary[]) {
  backend.on("org_list", () => orgs);
  backend.on("create_dot", (args) => ({
    ...sample.dot,
    ...(args.spec as object),
    id: "dot-new",
    org_id: (args.orgId as string | null) ?? null,
  }));
  const rendered = renderApp("/dots/new");
  const { user } = rendered;
  await user.type(await screen.findByLabelText("Name"), basics.name);
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Instructions"), basics.instructions);
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Folder"), basics.workdir);
  return rendered;
}

/// The editor of `dot`, with `orgs` joined.
function editor(dot: Dot, orgs: OrgSummary[]) {
  const held = { dot };
  backend.on("org_list", () => orgs);
  backend.on("get_dot", () => held.dot);
  backend.on("update_dot", (args) => {
    held.dot = { ...held.dot, ...(args.spec as object) };
    return held.dot;
  });
  backend.on("set_dot_enabled", (args) => {
    held.dot = { ...held.dot, enabled: args.enabled as boolean };
    return held.dot;
  });
  backend.on("delete_dot", () => null);
  return { held, ...renderApp(`/dots/${dot.id}`) };
}

describe("the org of a new dot", () => {
  it("offers Personal and each joined org, and creates the dot in the one chosen", async () => {
    const { user, router } = await newDot([acme, gamma]);
    const picker = screen.getByLabelText("Org");
    expect(within(picker).getAllByRole("option").map((o) => o.textContent)).toEqual([
      "Personal",
      "Acme Engineering",
      "Gamma",
    ]);
    expect(picker).toHaveValue("");
    await user.selectOptions(picker, "Acme Engineering");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Create dot" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(router.state.location.pathname).toBe("/dots/dot-new"));
    expect(backend.callsTo("create_dot")).toEqual([
      { spec: { ...blankSpec, ...basics }, orgId: "acme-eng" },
    ]);
  });

  it("makes a Personal dot with no org", async () => {
    const { user, router } = await newDot([acme]);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Create dot" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(router.state.location.pathname).toBe("/dots/dot-new"));
    expect(backend.callsTo("create_dot")).toEqual([
      { spec: { ...blankSpec, ...basics }, orgId: null },
    ]);
  });

  it("offers no picker when no org is joined", async () => {
    await newDot([]);
    await waitFor(() => expect(backend.callsTo("org_list").length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Org")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("shows the org as text once the dot is made, with no picker", async () => {
    const { user } = await newDot([acme]);
    await user.selectOptions(screen.getByLabelText("Org"), "Acme Engineering");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Create dot" }));
    const org = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Org" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(org).toHaveTextContent("Org: Acme Engineering"));
    expect(screen.queryByRole("combobox", { name: "Org" })).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("a dot whose org was removed", () => {
  it("says so in the editor, and keeps Save and Run off with the reason", async () => {
    editor(release, []);
    const org = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Org" });
    expect(await within(org).findByText("org removed")).toBeVisible();
    expect(org).toHaveTextContent("Org: acme-eng");

    const save = screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" });

    expect(run).toHaveAttribute("title", REMOVED);
  });

    const { user, router } = editor({ ...release, enabled: true }, []);
    await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Org" });

    await user.click(screen.getByLabelText("Enabled"));
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(backend.callsTo("set_dot_enabled")).toEqual([{ id: "D2", enabled: false }]),
    );
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Enabled")).not.toBeChecked();
    expect(backend.callsTo("update_dot")).toEqual([]);

    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete" }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(router.state.location.pathname).toBe("/home"));
    expect(backend.callsTo("delete_dot")).toEqual([{ id: "D2" }]);
  });

  it("shows the core's refusal when the org went away after the list was read", async () => {
    const { user } = editor(release, [acme]);
    const org = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Org" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(org).toHaveTextContent("Org: Acme Engineering"));
    backend.on("update_dot", () => {
      throw { kind: "conflict", message: "dot 'acme-release': its org 'acme-eng' was removed" };
    });
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(
      "dot 'acme-release': its org 'acme-eng' was removed",
    );
  });

  it("is marked on its card at home, and can't be run from there", async () => {
    backend.on("org_list", () => []);
    backend.on("dot_overview", () => [
      { ...sample.overview, dot: release },
      { ...sample.overview, dot: personal },
    ]);
    backend.on("set_dot_enabled", (args) => ({ ...release, enabled: args.enabled as boolean }));
    const { user } = renderApp(`/home/${release.id}`);
    const card = await screen.findByRole("listitem", { name: "acme-release" });
    const mark = await within(card).findByText("org removed");
    expect(mark).toHaveClass("text-destructive");
    expect(mark).toHaveAttribute("title", REMOVED);
    const other = screen.getByRole("listitem", { name: personal.name });
    expect(within(other).queryByText("org removed")).toBeNull();

    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Dot settings" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("menuitem", { name: "Run now" })).toHaveAttribute(
      "data-disabled",
    );
    // Turning it off still works.
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("menuitemcheckbox", { name: "Enabled" }));
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(backend.callsTo("set_dot_enabled")).toEqual([{ id: "D2", enabled: false }]),
    );
  });

  it("can't be sent a message from the chat at home, which says why", async () => {
    backend.on("org_list", () => []);
    backend.on("dot_overview", () => [{ ...sample.overview, dot: release }]);
    renderApp(`/home/${release.id}`);
    const why = await screen.findByText(`org removed: ${REMOVED}`);
    expect(why).toHaveClass("text-destructive");
    const box = screen.getByLabelText("Message");
    expect(box).toBeDisabled();
    expect(box).toHaveAttribute("placeholder", "org removed");
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send" })).toBeDisabled();
    expect(backend.callsTo("chat")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("can be sent a message from the chat while its org is joined", async () => {
    backend.on("org_list", () => [acme]);
    backend.on("dot_overview", () => [{ ...sample.overview, dot: release }]);
    const { user } = renderApp(`/home/${release.id}`);
    const box = await screen.findByLabelText("Message");
    await waitFor(() => expect(backend.callsTo("org_list").length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
    expect(box).toBeEnabled();
    expect(screen.queryByText(/org removed/)).toBeNull();
    await user.type(box, "Ship it{Enter}");
    await waitFor(() => expect(backend.callsTo("chat")).toHaveLength(1));
  });

  it("is not marked while its org is joined", async () => {
    backend.on("org_list", () => [acme]);
    backend.on("dot_overview", () => [{ ...sample.overview, dot: release }]);
    renderApp(`/home/${release.id}`);
    await screen.findByRole("listitem", { name: "acme-release" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(backend.callsTo("org_list").length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
    expect(screen.queryByText("org removed")).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe("a Personal dot", () => {
  it("shows no org, asks for none, and saves and runs as before", async () => {
    backend.on("dot_overview", () => [{ ...sample.overview, dot: personal }]);
    editor(personal, [acme]);
    expect(await screen.findByLabelText("Name")).toHaveValue(personal.name);
    expect(screen.queryByRole("group", { name: "Org" })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Save" })).toBeEnabled();
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Run now" })).toBeEnabled();
    expect(screen.queryByText("org removed")).toBeNull();
    expect(backend.callsTo("org_list")).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```tsx
const [acme] = sample.orgs as [OrgSummary]; // Acme Engineering, connected, personal: fallback
// GITHUB_TOKEN from the org, LOG_LEVEL from Personal, API_KEY not in the org, PROD_DB_URL
// denied, GITHUB_TOKEN refused to the shell, and LOG_LEVEL of a dot whose org was removed.
const [fromOrg, fromPersonal, notInOrg, denied, forbidden, removed] =
  sample.grantStatuses as GrantStatus[];
const github: Uses = { ...none, mcp_servers: ["github"] };
const inAcme = { orgId: "acme-eng", dotId: "D2", uses: github, before: github };

/// The names the shell's picker offers.
function offered(): string[] {
  const input = within(screen.getByRole("group", { name: "Shell" })).getByLabelText(
    "Variable for the shell",
  );
  const list = document.getElementById(input.getAttribute("list")!)!;
  return [...list.querySelectorAll("option")].map((o) => o.value);
}

describe("the Variables section of a dot in an org", () => {
  it("shows each grant's status in the org: its source, or the core's reason", async () => {
    setup({
      ...inAcme,
      orgs: [acme],
      variables: {
        "mcp:github": ["GITHUB_TOKEN", "API_KEY", "PROD_DB_URL"],
        shell: ["LOG_LEVEL", "GITHUB_TOKEN"],
      },
      statuses: [fromOrg!, fromPersonal!, notInOrg!, denied!, forbidden!],
    });
    const server = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "github" });
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(within(server).getByText("GITHUB_TOKEN")).toHaveTextContent(
        "GITHUB_TOKEN · from Acme Engineering",
      ),
    );
    const missing = within(server).getByText(notInOrg!.text!);
    expect(missing).toHaveClass("text-needs");
    expect(within(server).getByText(denied!.text!)).toHaveClass("text-needs");
    const shell = screen.getByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    expect(within(shell).getByText("LOG_LEVEL")).toHaveTextContent("LOG_LEVEL · from Personal");
    expect(within(shell).getByText(forbidden!.text!)).toHaveClass("text-needs");
    expect(backend.callsTo("dot_variables")).toEqual([{ dotId: "D2" }]);
  });

  it("shows the grants of a dot whose org was removed in the error tone", async () => {
    setup({ ...inAcme, orgs: [], variables: { shell: ["LOG_LEVEL"] }, statuses: [removed!] });
    const shell = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    const text = await within(shell).findByText(removed!.text!);
    expect(text).toHaveTextContent("dot 'acme-release': its org 'acme-eng' was removed");
    expect(text).toHaveClass("text-destructive");
    // Nothing of the org is offered: it is not joined.
    expect(offered()).toEqual([]);
    expect(backend.callsTo("org_entries")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("says a grant not saved yet is checked when the dot is saved", async () => {
    const { user } = setup({ ...inAcme, orgs: [acme], entries: sample.orgEntries });
    const shell = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    await user.type(within(shell).getByLabelText("Variable for the shell"), "API_BASE_URL");
    await user.click(within(shell).getByRole("button", { name: "Grant to the shell" }));
    expect(within(shell).getByText("API_BASE_URL")).toHaveTextContent(
      "API_BASE_URL · checked when you save",
    );
  });

  it("hides the org's secrets from the shell while shell_secrets is false", async () => {
    const keeps = { ...acme, personal_mode: "deny" as const, shell_secrets: false };
    const { user, variables } = setup({ ...inAcme, orgs: [keeps], entries: sample.orgEntries });
    const shell = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(offered()).toEqual(["API_BASE_URL"]));
    const hint =
      "Acme Engineering does not allow secrets in the shell, so its secrets are not offered here.";
    expect(within(shell).getByText(hint)).toBeVisible();
    // Typed in anyway, it is not granted.
    await user.type(within(shell).getByLabelText("Variable for the shell"), "github_token");
    await user.click(within(shell).getByRole("button", { name: "Grant to the shell" }));
    expect(
      within(shell).getByText(
        "github_token is a secret, and Acme Engineering does not allow secrets in the shell.",
      ),
    ).toBeVisible();
    expect(variables()).toEqual({});
  });

  it("offers the org's secrets to the shell when shell_secrets is true", async () => {
    const lets = { ...acme, personal_mode: "deny" as const, shell_secrets: true };
    setup({ ...inAcme, orgs: [lets], entries: sample.orgEntries });
    await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(offered()).toEqual(["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN"]));
    expect(screen.queryByText(/does not allow secrets in the shell/)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("adds Personal's names as the org's personal mode allows", async () => {
    // Personal: GITHUB_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN (secrets), LOG_LEVEL (plain). The org:
    // API_BASE_URL (plain) and GITHUB_TOKEN (secret).
    const mode = (personal_mode: OrgSummary["personal_mode"], shell_secrets = true) => ({
      ...acme,
      personal_mode,
      shell_secrets,
    });
    const cases: [OrgSummary, string[]][] = [
      [mode("deny"), ["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN"]],
      // No accepted policy reads as deny.
      [mode(null), ["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN"]],
      [mode("fallback"), ["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "LOG_LEVEL", "NPM_TOKEN"]],
      [mode("override"), ["GITHUB_TOKEN", "LOG_LEVEL", "NPM_TOKEN", "API_BASE_URL"]],
      // A Personal secret is kept from the shell too.
      [mode("fallback", false), ["API_BASE_URL", "LOG_LEVEL"]],
      [mode("override", false), ["LOG_LEVEL", "API_BASE_URL"]],
    ];
    for (const [org, names] of cases) {
      const { unmount } = setup({
        ...inAcme,
        orgs: [org],
        entries: sample.orgEntries,
        env: sample.env,
      });
      await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
      await waitFor(() => expect(offered(), String(org.personal_mode)).toEqual(names));
      unmount();
    }
  });

  it("leaves out the names the org's use rules deny, from either side", async () => {
    // Under fallback the scope has API_BASE_URL and GITHUB_TOKEN (the org), then LOG_LEVEL and
    // NPM_TOKEN (Personal). The globs match without regard to case, and deny wins.
    const rules = (use_rules: OrgSummary["use_rules"]) => ({
      ...acme,
      personal_mode: "fallback" as const,
      shell_secrets: true,
      use_rules,
    });
    const cases: [OrgSummary, string[]][] = [
      [
        rules({ allow: ["*"], deny: [] }),
        ["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "LOG_LEVEL", "NPM_TOKEN"],
      ],
      [rules({ allow: ["*"], deny: ["github_*", "npm*"] }), ["API_BASE_URL", "LOG_LEVEL"]],
      [rules({ allow: ["api_*", "*_TOKEN"], deny: ["GITHUB_*"] }), ["API_BASE_URL", "NPM_TOKEN"]],
      // No accepted policy: nothing may be granted.
      [rules(null), []],
    ];
    for (const [org, names] of cases) {
      const { unmount } = setup({
        ...inAcme,
        orgs: [org],
        entries: sample.orgEntries,
        env: sample.env,
      });
      await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
      await waitFor(() => expect(offered(), JSON.stringify(org.use_rules)).toEqual(names));
      unmount();
    }
    // A denied name typed in by hand is still granted; its status then says why it is not set.
    const { user, variables } = setup({
      ...inAcme,
      orgs: [rules({ allow: ["*"], deny: ["NPM_*"] })],
      entries: sample.orgEntries,
      env: sample.env,
    });
    const shell = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(offered()).toEqual(["API_BASE_URL", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "LOG_LEVEL"]));
    await user.type(within(shell).getByLabelText("Variable for the shell"), "NPM_TOKEN");
    await user.click(within(shell).getByRole("button", { name: "Grant to the shell" }));
    expect(variables()).toEqual({ shell: ["NPM_TOKEN"] });
  });
});

describe("the Variables section of a Personal dot", () => {
  it("offers every Personal name, secrets too, and asks for no org", async () => {
    setup({ uses: none, before: none, env: sample.env, dotId: "D1" });
    await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(offered()).toEqual(["GITHUB_TOKEN", "LOG_LEVEL", "NPM_TOKEN"]));
    expect(screen.queryByText(/does not allow secrets/)).toBeNull();
    expect(backend.callsTo("org_list")).toEqual([]);
    expect(backend.callsTo("org_entries")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("shows only what Personal lacks, as before, from the core's status", async () => {
    const lacks: GrantStatus = {
      consumer: "shell",
      name: "NPM_TOKEN",
      status: "not_defined",
      text: "NPM_TOKEN: not in Personal (dot 'nightly-tests', shell)",
      source: null,
      secret: false,
    };
    const resolves: GrantStatus = {
      ...lacks,
      name: "LOG_LEVEL",
      status: "ok",
      text: null,
      source: "personal",
    };
    setup({
      uses: none,
      before: none,
      env: sample.env,
      dotId: "D1",
      variables: { shell: ["LOG_LEVEL", "NPM_TOKEN"] },
      statuses: [resolves, lacks],
    });
    const shell = await screen.findByRole("group", { name: "Shell" });
    // NPM_TOKEN is listed in Personal, but its value is gone: the core's status says so.
    await waitFor(() =>
      expect(within(shell).getByText("NPM_TOKEN")).toHaveTextContent("NPM_TOKEN · not in Personal"),
    );
    expect(within(shell).getByText("LOG_LEVEL")).toHaveTextContent(/^LOG_LEVEL$/);
    expect(within(shell).queryByText(/from Personal/)).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```rust
/// The status of each of the dot's grants in its scope, for its editor's Variables: whether
/// it resolves now, from where, and why not. No value is in it, and no org is fetched.
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn dot_variables(state: State<'_, AppState>, dot_id: String) -> Res<Vec<GrantStatus>> {
    Ok(state.rt()?.dot_variables(&dot_id).await?)
}
```

```rust
/// What `dot_variables` answers for acme-release, a dot of Acme Engineering (`personal:
/// fallback`, `shell_secrets: false`): a secret from the org; a plain value from Personal; a
/// name the org lacks; a name its `use` rules deny; a secret its shell may not have. Then a
/// grant of a dot whose org was removed. The texts are the core's own.
fn grant_statuses() -> Vec<GrantStatus> {
    let text = |name: &str, consumer: Consumer, why: Unresolved, org: &str| {
        Missing {
            name: name.into(),
            consumer,
            why,
            org: Some(org.into()),
        }
        .text("acme-release")
    };
    let acme = "Acme Engineering";
    let github = || Consumer::Mcp("github".into());
    let status = |consumer: &Consumer, name: &str, status: GrantState| GrantStatus {
        consumer: consumer.key(),
        name: name.into(),
        status,
        text: None,
        source: None,
        secret: false,
    };
    vec![
        GrantStatus {
            source: Some(ValueSource::Org),
            secret: true,
            ..status(&github(), "GITHUB_TOKEN", GrantState::Ok)
        },
        GrantStatus {
            source: Some(ValueSource::Personal),
            ..status(&Consumer::Shell, "LOG_LEVEL", GrantState::Ok)
        },
        GrantStatus {
            text: Some(text("API_KEY", github(), Unresolved::NotDefined, acme)),
            ..status(&github(), "API_KEY", GrantState::NotDefined)
        },
        GrantStatus {
            text: Some(text(
                "PROD_DB_URL",
                github(),
                Unresolved::DeniedByPolicy,
                acme,
            )),
            ..status(&github(), "PROD_DB_URL", GrantState::DeniedByPolicy)
        },
        GrantStatus {
            text: Some(text(
                "GITHUB_TOKEN",
                Consumer::Shell,
                Unresolved::ShellSecretsForbidden,
                acme,
            )),
            source: Some(ValueSource::Org),
            secret: true,
            ..status(
                &Consumer::Shell,
                "GITHUB_TOKEN",
                GrantState::ShellSecretsForbidden,
            )
        },
        GrantStatus {
            text: Some(text(
                "LOG_LEVEL",
                Consumer::Shell,
                Unresolved::OrgRemoved,
                "acme-eng",
            )),
            ..status(&Consumer::Shell, "LOG_LEVEL", GrantState::OrgRemoved)
        },
    ]
}
```

```rust
    /// The status of each of the dot's stored grants in its scope (the editor's Variables),
    /// as a run's start would resolve them now, without its fetch of a stale org. It holds no
    /// value (`Vault::grant_statuses`).
    pub async fn dot_variables(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Vec<GrantStatus>> {

        self.vault.grant_statuses(&dot).await
    }
```

```rust
/// Resolved values by the name they were asked for. Its `Debug` shows the names only.
```

**with:**

```rust

str_enum!(ValueSource {
    Org => "org",
    Personal => "personal",
});

/// What resolving one name found: its value, where it comes from, and whether it is a secret.
/// Its `Debug` leaves the value out.
pub(super) struct Found {
    /// `None` when only the entries that are there were read (`Reading::Presence`).
    pub(super) value: Option<Zeroizing<String>>,
    pub(super) source: ValueSource,
    pub(super) secret: bool,
}

impl std::fmt::Debug for Found {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("Found")
            .field("source", &self.source)
            .field("secret", &self.secret)
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

/// One name's answer: what it resolves to, or why it does not, with what was found for it.
pub(super) type Answer = std::result::Result<Found, (Missing, Option<Found>)>;

/// How resolving reads Personal: its values, for a run or a Check; or only which entries are
/// there (the status of a dot's grants), so no secret's value is read. `Presence` holds the
```

```rust
    /// What resolving in `scope` reads once for `names`: the org's name, and its policy and
    /// answers for those names from one read of the org.
    pub(super) async fn in_scope(&self, scope: &DotScope, names: &[String]) -> InScope {
        let DotScope::Org(org_id) = scope else {
            return InScope {
                org: None,
                view: None,
            };
        };
        let name = self.org_name(org_id).await;
        // The org's policy and values, from one read of the org.
        let view = match self.orgs() {
            Some(orgs) => Some(orgs.view(org_id, names).await),
            None => None,
        };
        InScope {
            org: Some((org_id.clone(), name)),
            view,
        }
    }

    /// The `i`th of the names `read` was made for, for `consumer`, in the spec's order (§8):
    /// the grant (`granted`); for an org, its state, then its `use` rules, then its `personal`
    /// mode, then the shell's secrets rule. A Personal scope reads Personal only. What does
    /// not resolve comes with what was found for it, if anything: a secret the shell may not
    /// have. `reading` says whether values are read, or only which entries are there.
    pub(super) async fn resolve_one(
        &self,
        read: &InScope,
        i: usize,
        name: &str,
        granted: bool,
        consumer: &Consumer,
        reading: &Reading,
    ) -> Result<Answer> {
        let missing = |why: Unresolved| Missing {
            name: name.to_string(),
            consumer: consumer.clone(),
            org: read.org.as_ref().map(|(id, org_name)| match why {
                Unresolved::OrgRemoved => id.clone(),
                _ => org_name.clone(),
            }),
            why,
        };
        if !granted {
            return Ok(Err((missing(Unresolved::NotGranted), None)));
        }
        let found = match (&read.org, &read.view) {
            (None, _) => self
                .personal_found(reading, name)
                .await?
                .ok_or((Unresolved::NotDefined, None)),
            (Some(_), Some(view)) => {
                let (lookup, policy) = (&view.lookups[i], view.policy.as_ref());
                self.org_value(lookup, policy, consumer, name, reading)
                    .await?
            }
            (Some(_), None) => Err((Unresolved::OrgRemoved, None)),
        };
        Ok(found.map_err(|(why, found)| (missing(why), found)))
    }
```

```rust
    /// The secret store's keys of the Personal secrets, lower-cased, so whether a secret has
    /// a value is known without reading it. `None`, logged, when they can't be listed.
    pub(crate) fn personal_secret_keys(&self) -> Option<HashSet<String>> {
        match self.secrets.keys(PERSONAL_PREFIX) {
            // Credential Manager compares targets without regard to case.
            Ok(keys) => Some(keys.iter().map(|k| k.to_ascii_lowercase()).collect()),
            Err(e) => {
```

```rust
//! The status of a dot's grants (env vault spec §9, the dot editor's Variables): for each name
//! granted to each consumer, whether it resolves in the dot's scope now, from where, and why
//! not. It is worked out by the resolver's own steps, but no value is kept and no Personal
//! secret's value is read, and the org is not fetched first.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use super::grants::Consumer;
use super::resolve::{DotScope, Found, Reading, Unresolved, ValueSource};
use super::service::Vault;
use crate::model::Dot;
use crate::Result;

str_enum!(GrantState {
    Ok => "ok",
    NotGranted => "not_granted",
    NotDefined => "not_defined",
    DeniedByPolicy => "denied_by_policy",
    ShellSecretsForbidden => "shell_secrets_forbidden",
    OrgOffline => "org_offline",
    OrgExpired => "org_expired",
    OrgRevoked => "org_revoked",
    PolicyInvalid => "policy_invalid",
    OrgRemoved => "org_removed",
});

impl GrantState {
    /// The state of a name that does not resolve for `why`.
    fn of(why: &Unresolved) -> GrantState {
        match why {
            Unresolved::NotGranted => GrantState::NotGranted,
            Unresolved::NotDefined => GrantState::NotDefined,
            Unresolved::DeniedByPolicy => GrantState::DeniedByPolicy,
            Unresolved::ShellSecretsForbidden => GrantState::ShellSecretsForbidden,
            Unresolved::OrgOffline => GrantState::OrgOffline,
            Unresolved::OrgExpired => GrantState::OrgExpired,
            Unresolved::OrgRevoked => GrantState::OrgRevoked,
            Unresolved::PolicyInvalid(_) => GrantState::PolicyInvalid,
            Unresolved::OrgRemoved => GrantState::OrgRemoved,
        }
    }
}

/// One grant of a dot as its editor shows it. It never holds a value.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct GrantStatus {
    /// `mcp:<server>` or `shell`.
    pub consumer: String,
    /// The name as it is granted.
    pub name: String,
    pub status: GrantState,
    /// Why it does not resolve, in the words of the run event (`Missing::text`); `None` when
    /// it resolves.
    pub text: Option<String>,
    /// Where its value comes from, or would but for the shell's secrets rule; `None` when
    /// nothing was found.
    pub source: Option<ValueSource>,
    /// The value that resolves, or would but for the shell's secrets rule, is a secret: an
    /// org entry not in `plain`, or a Personal secret.
    pub secret: bool,
}

impl Vault {
    /// The status of each of `dot`'s grants in its scope, by consumer (servers by name, then
    /// the shell), each in the order granted. Each name goes through `resolve`'s steps
    /// (`resolve_one`) as at a run's start, but reads only which entries are there: no value
    /// is kept, and no Personal secret's value is read. The org is not fetched first, so a
    /// stale org answers from what it holds now. A dot whose org is not joined gets
    /// `org_removed` for every grant.
    pub async fn grant_statuses(&self, dot: &Dot) -> Result<Vec<GrantStatus>> {
        let mut granted: Vec<(Consumer, String)> = Vec::new();
        for (key, names) in &dot.spec.variables.0 {
            // A stored dot's grants were validated when it was saved.
            let Ok(consumer) = Consumer::parse(key) else {
                tracing::warn!("dot {:?} grants to {key:?}, which is no consumer", dot.id);
                continue;
            };
            granted.extend(names.iter().map(|name| (consumer.clone(), name.clone())));
        }
        let names: Vec<String> = granted.iter().map(|(_, name)| name.clone()).collect();
        let read = self.in_scope(&DotScope::of(dot), &names).await;
        let reading = Reading::Presence(self.personal_secret_keys());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (i, (consumer, name)) in granted.into_iter().enumerate() {
            let answer = self
                .resolve_one(&read, i, &name, true, &consumer, &reading)
                .await?;
            let (status, text, found) = match answer {
                Ok(found) => (GrantState::Ok, None, Some(found)),
                Err((missing, found)) => (
                    GrantState::of(&missing.why),
                    Some(missing.text(&dot.spec.name)),
                    found,
                ),
            };
            let found = found.as_ref();
            out.push(GrantStatus {
                consumer: consumer.key(),
                name,
                status,
                text,
                source: found.map(|f: &Found| f.source),
                secret: found.is_some_and(|f| f.secret),
            });
        }
        Ok(out)
    }
}
```

**Create `ui/src/lib/dot-org.ts`:**

```ts
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";

import { commands } from "@/api/commands";
import type { OrgSummary, UseRules } from "@/api/types";
import { keys } from "@/lib/query";

/// What a dot whose org is not joined on this PC says, on its card and in its editor, and why
/// it can't be saved or run.
export function orgRemovedText(orgId: string): string {
  return `Its org '${orgId}' was removed. Join it again to run this dot.`;
}

/// Whether `dot`'s org is not joined on this PC, told from the joined orgs (`org_list`), as the
/// core tells it (`Vault::org_removed`): the list holds every joined org, a damaged one too,
/// and not a SOPS join that still waits for its key. False for a Personal dot, and while the
/// list is not loaded, so nothing is marked before the answer.
export function orgRemoved(dot: { org_id: string | null }, orgs: OrgSummary[] | undefined) {
  return dot.org_id !== null && orgs !== undefined && !orgs.some((org) => org.id === dot.org_id);
}

/// The orgs joined on this PC, asked for only when `enabled`: a screen with no dot of an org
/// makes no call. `undefined` until they are loaded.
export function useOrgList(enabled: boolean): OrgSummary[] | undefined {
  return useQuery({ queryKey: keys.orgs, queryFn: commands.orgList, enabled }).data;
}

/// A dot's org (`orgId`, null for Personal): the joined org, its name for the screen (the id
/// while the list loads, or when it was removed), and whether it was removed.
export function useDotOrg(orgId: string | null) {
  const orgs = useOrgList(orgId !== null);
  const org = orgs?.find((o) => o.id === orgId);
  const removed = orgRemoved({ org_id: orgId }, orgs);
  return { org, name: org?.name ?? orgId ?? "Personal", removed };
}

/// Whether an org's `use` rules let its dots be granted `name`, as the core decides it
/// (`OrgPolicy::may_use`): an `allow` glob matches and no `deny` glob does. No rules (no
/// accepted policy) allow nothing.
export function mayUse(rules: UseRules | null, name: string): boolean {
  if (rules === null) return false;
  const matches = (globs: string[]) => globs.some((glob) => globMatches(glob, name));
  return !matches(rules.deny) && matches(rules.allow);
}

/// A `use` glob against a name: `*` stands for any run of characters, and case does not
/// matter, since names compare that way.
function globMatches(glob: string, name: string): boolean {
  const [g, n] = [glob.toLowerCase(), name.toLowerCase()];
  let [gi, ni] = [0, 0];
  let star: [number, number] | null = null;
  while (ni < n.length) {
    if (gi < g.length && g[gi] === "*") {
      star = [gi, ni];
      gi += 1;
    } else if (gi < g.length && g[gi] === n[ni]) {
      gi += 1;
      ni += 1;
    } else if (star !== null) {
      gi = star[0] + 1;
      ni = star[1] + 1;
      star = [star[0], star[1] + 1];
    } else {
      return false;
    }
  }
  return [...g.slice(gi)].every((c) => c === "*");
}
```

**Create `ui/src/screens/dot-editor/DotOrg.tsx`:**

```tsx
import { Field } from "@/components/Field";
import { Badge } from "@/components/ui/badge";
import { NativeSelect } from "@/components/ui/native-select";
import { orgRemovedText, useDotOrg, useOrgList } from "@/lib/dot-org";

/// The org a new dot belongs to (env vault spec §9): Personal, or one of the orgs joined on
/// this PC. Fixed once the dot is made. With no org joined there is nothing to choose, and
/// nothing shows.
export function OrgPicker(props: { value: string | null; onChange: (org: string | null) => void }) {
  const orgs = useOrgList(true) ?? [];
  if (orgs.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <Field
      label="Org"
      htmlFor="dot-org"
      hint="Where the dot's variables come from. It can't be changed once the dot is made."
    >
      <NativeSelect
        id="dot-org"
        value={props.value ?? ""}
        onChange={(e) => props.onChange(e.target.value === "" ? null : e.target.value)}
      >
        <option value="">Personal</option>
        {orgs.map((org) => (
          <option key={org.id} value={org.id}>
            {org.name}
          </option>
        ))}
      </NativeSelect>
    </Field>
  );
}

/// The org of a dot that was made in one, as read-only text; when the org is no longer joined,
/// "org removed" and why the dot can't be saved or run.
export function OrgLine({ orgId }: { orgId: string }) {
  const { name, removed } = useDotOrg(orgId);
  return (
    <div role="group" aria-label="Org" className="flex flex-col gap-1">
      <p className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
        <span>
          Org: <span className="font-medium">{name}</span>
        </span>
        {removed && <Badge variant="destructive">org removed</Badge>}
      </p>
      {removed ? (
        <p className="text-xs text-destructive">{orgRemovedText(orgId)}</p>
      ) : (
        <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
          Its variables come from this org. It was set when the dot was made.
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx

/// A dot's grants (env vault spec §7): what each server it uses may read, and what its shell
```

**with:**

```tsx

/// The names a dot of the org `orgId` reads, each with the kind of the value that would
/// resolve: the org's entries, and Personal's where the org's `personal` mode lets its dots
/// read them, the side the mode puts first winning a name both have (env vault spec §8). No
/// accepted policy reads as `deny`, and an org not joined (`org` null) gives nothing. A
/// Personal dot (`orgId` null) reads Personal's.
function scopeEntries(
  orgId: string | null,
  org: OrgSummary | null,
  personal: Entry[],
  inOrg: Entry[],
): Entry[] {
  if (orgId === null) return personal;
  if (org === null) return [];
  const lacking = (from: Entry[], have: Entry[]) =>
    from.filter((e) => !have.some((h) => same(h.name, e.name)));
  switch (org.personal_mode ?? "deny") {
    case "deny":
      return inOrg;
    case "fallback":
      return [...inOrg, ...lacking(personal, inOrg)];
    case "override":
      return [...personal, ...lacking(inOrg, personal)];
  }
}

/// A granted name with its status in the dot's scope. A Personal dot shows, as before, only
/// that Personal lacks it. An org dot's resolves "from" the org or Personal, or gives the
/// core's reason: in the attention tone, or the error tone when the org was removed. A grant
/// the stored dot does not have yet has no status until the dot is saved.
function GrantLine(props: {
  name: string;
  status: GrantStatus | undefined;
  orgName: string | null;
  lacksInPersonal: boolean;
}) {
  const { name, status, orgName } = props;
  const plain = (note: string) => (
    <span className="font-mono text-xs">
      {name}
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">{note}</span>
    </span>
  );
  if (orgName === null) {
    const lacks = status ? status.status !== "ok" : props.lacksInPersonal;
    return plain(lacks ? " · not in Personal" : "");
  }
  if (!status) return plain(" · checked when you save");
  if (status.status === "ok") {
    return plain(` · from ${status.source === "personal" ? "Personal" : orgName}`);
  }
  const tone = status.status === "org_removed" ? "text-destructive" : "text-needs";
  return (
    <span className="flex flex-col">
      <span className="font-mono text-xs">{name}</span>
      <span className={`text-xs ${tone}`}>{status.text}</span>
    </span>
  );
}

/// A dot's grants (env vault spec §7): what each server it uses may read, and what its shell
```
